texts.exo.38.21: Estas son las cuentas del tabernáculo, del tabernáculo del testimonio, lo que fué contado de orden de Moisés por mano de Ithamar, hijo de Aarón sacerdote, para el ministerio de los Levitas.
texts.exo.38.22: Y Bezaleel, hijo de Uri, hijo de Hur, de la tribu de Judá, hizo todas las cosas que Jehová mandó á Moisés.
texts.exo.38.23: Y con él estaba Aholiab, hijo de Ahisamac, de la tribu de Dan, artífice, y diseñador, y recamador en jacinto, y púrpura, y carmesí, y lino fino.
texts.exo.38.24: Todo el oro empleado en la obra, en toda la obra del santuario, el cual fué oro de ofrenda, fué veintinueve talentos, y setecientos y treinta siclos, según el siclo del santuario.
texts.exo.38.25: Y la plata de los contados de la congregación fué cien talentos, y mil setecientos setenta y cinco siclos, según el siclo del santuario:
texts.exo.38.26: Medio por cabeza, medio siclo, según el siclo del santuario, á todos los que pasaron por cuenta de edad de veinte años y arriba, que fueron seiscientos tres mil quinientos cincuenta.
texts.exo.38.27: Hubo además cien talentos de plata para hacer de fundición las basas del santuario y las basas del velo: en cien basas cien talentos, á talento por basa.
texts.exo.38.28: Y de los mil setecientos setenta y cinco siclos hizo los capiteles de las columnas, y cubrió los capiteles de ellas, y las ciñó.
texts.exo.38.29: Y el metal de la ofrenda fue setenta talentos, y dos mil cuatrocientos siclos;
texts.exo.38.30: Del cual hizo las basas de la puerta del tabernáculo del testimonio, y el altar de metal, y su enrejado de metal, y todos los vasos del altar.
texts.exo.38.31: Y las basas del atrio alrededor, y las basas de la puerta del atrio, y todas las estacas del tabernáculo, y todas las estacas del atrio alrededor.
texts.exo.39.1: Y DEL jacinto, y púrpura, y carmesí, hicieron las vestimentas del ministerio para ministrar en el santuario, y asimismo hicieron las vestiduras sagradas para Aarón; como Jehová lo había mandado á Moisés.
texts.exo.39.2: Hizo también el ephod de oro, de cárdeno y púrpura y carmesí, y lino torcido.
texts.exo.39.3: Y extendieron las planchas de oro, y cortaron hilos para tejerlos entre el jacinto, y entre la púrpura, y entre el carmesí, y entre el lino, con delicada obra.
texts.exo.39.4: Hiciéronle las hombreras que se juntasen; y uníanse en sus dos lados.
texts.exo.39.5: Y el cinto del ephod que estaba sobre él, era de lo mismo, conforme á su obra; de oro, jacinto, y púrpura, y carmesí, y lino torcido; como Jehová lo había mandado á Moisés.
texts.exo.39.6: Y labraron las piedras oniquinas cercadas de engastes de oro, grabadas de grabadura de sello con los nombres de los hijos de Israel:
texts.exo.39.7: Y púsolas sobre las hombreras del ephod, por piedras de memoria á los hijos de Israel; como Jehová lo había á Moisés mandado.
texts.exo.39.8: Hizo también el racional de primorosa obra, como la obra del ephod, de oro, jacinto, y púrpura, y carmesí, y lino torcido.
texts.exo.39.9: Era cuadrado: doblado hicieron el racional: su longitud era de un palmo, y de un palmo su anchura, doblado.
texts.exo.39.10: Y engastaron en él cuatro órdenes de piedras. El primer orden era un sardio, un topacio, y un carbunclo: este el primer orden.
texts.exo.39.11: El segundo orden, una esmeralda, un zafiro, y un diamante.
texts.exo.39.12: El tercer orden, un ligurio, un ágata, y un amatista.
texts.exo.39.13: Y el cuarto orden, un berilo, un onix, y un jaspe: cercadas y encajadas en sus engastes de oro.
texts.exo.39.14: Las cuales piedras eran conforme á los nombres de los hijos de Israel, doce según los nombres de ellos; como grabaduras de sello, cada una con su nombre según las doce tribus.
texts.exo.39.15: Hicieron también sobre el racional las cadenas pequeñas de hechura de trenza, de oro puro.
texts.exo.39.16: Hicieron asimismo los dos engastes y los dos anillos, de oro; los cuales dos anillos de oro pusieron en los dos cabos del racional.
texts.exo.39.17: Y pusieron las dos trenzas de oro en aquellos dos anillos á los cabos del racional.
texts.exo.39.18: Y fijaron los dos cabos de las dos trenzas en los dos engastes, que pusieron sobre las hombreras del ephod, en la parte delantera de él.
texts.exo.39.19: E hicieron dos anillos de oro, que pusieron en los dos cabos del racional, en su orilla, á la parte baja del ephod.
texts.exo.39.20: Hicieron además dos anillos de oro, los cuales pusieron en las dos hombreras del ephod, abajo en la parte delantera, delante de su juntura, sobre el cinto del ephod.
texts.exo.39.21: Y ataron el racional de sus anillos á los anillos del ephod con un cordón de jacinto, para que estuviese sobre el cinto del mismo ephod, y no se apartase el racional del ephod; como Jehová lo había mandado á Moisés.
texts.exo.39.22: Hizo también el manto del ephod de obra de tejedor, todo de jacinto.
texts.exo.39.23: Con su abertura en medio de él, como el cuello de un coselete, con un borde en derredor de la abertura, porque no se rompiese.
texts.exo.39.24: E hicieron en las orillas del manto las granadas de jacinto, y púrpura, y carmesí, y lino torcido.
texts.exo.39.25: Hicieron también las campanillas de oro puro, las cuales campanillas pusieron entre las granadas por las orillas del manto alrededor entre las granadas:
texts.exo.39.26: Una campanilla y una granada, una campanilla y una granada alrededor, en las orillas del manto, para ministrar; como Jehová lo mandó á Moisés.
texts.exo.39.27: Igualmente hicieron las túnicas de lino fino de obra de tejedor, para Aarón y para sus hijos;
texts.exo.39.28: Asimismo la mitra de lino fino, y los adornos de los chapeos (tiaras) de lino fino, y los pañetes de lino, de lino torcido;
texts.exo.39.29: También el cinto de lino torcido, y de jacinto, y púrpura, y carmesí, de obra de recamador; como Jehová lo mandó á Moisés.
texts.exo.39.30: Hicieron asimismo la plancha de la diadema santa de oro puro, y escribieron en ella de grabadura de sello, el rótulo, SANTIDAD A JEHOVA.
texts.exo.39.31: Y pusieron en ella un cordón de jacinto, para colocarla en alto sobre la mitra; como Jehová lo había mandado á Moisés.
texts.exo.39.32: Y fue acabada toda la obra del tabernáculo, del tabernáculo del testimonio: é hicieron los hijos de Israel como Jehová lo había mandado á Moisés: así lo hicieron.
texts.exo.39.33: Y trajeron el tabernáculo á Moisés, el tabernáculo y todos sus vasos; sus corchetes, sus tablas, sus barras, y sus columnas, y sus basas;
texts.exo.39.34: Y la cubierta de pieles rojas de carneros, y la cubierta de pieles de tejones, y el velo del pabellón;
texts.exo.39.35: El arca del testimonio, y sus varas, y la cubierta;
texts.exo.39.36: La mesa, todos sus vasos, y el pan de la proposición;
texts.exo.39.37: El candelero limpio, sus candilejas, las lámparas que debían mantenerse en orden, y todos sus vasos, y el aceite para la luminaria;
texts.exo.39.38: Y el altar de oro, y el aceite de la unción, y el perfume aromático, y el pabellón para la puerta del tabernáculo;
texts.exo.39.39: El altar de metal, con su enrejado de metal, sus varas, y todos sus vasos; y la fuente, y su basa;
texts.exo.39.40: Las cortinas del atrio, y sus columnas, y sus basas, y el pabellón para la puerta del atrio, y sus cuerdas, y sus estacas, y todos los vasos del servicio del tabernáculo, del tabernáculo del testimonio;
texts.exo.39.41: Las vestimentas del servicio para ministrar en el santuario, las sagradas vestiduras para Aarón el sacerdote, y las vestiduras de sus hijos, para ministrar en el sacerdocio.
texts.exo.39.42: En conformidad á todas las cosas que Jehová había mandado á Moisés, así hicieron los hijos de Israel toda la obra.
texts.exo.39.43: Y vió Moisés toda la obra, y he aquí que la habían hecho como Jehová había mandado; y bendíjolos.
texts.exo.40.1: Y JEHOVA habló á Moisés, diciendo:
texts.exo.40.2: En el primer día del mes primero harás levantar el tabernáculo, el tabernáculo del testimonio:
texts.exo.40.3: Y pondrás en él el arca del testimonio, y la cubrirás con el velo:
texts.exo.40.4: Y meterás la mesa, y la pondrás en orden: meterás también el candelero y encenderás sus lámparas:
texts.exo.40.5: Y pondrás el altar de oro para el perfume delante del arca del testimonio, y pondrás el pabellón delante de la puerta del tabernáculo.
texts.exo.40.6: Después pondrás el altar del holocausto delante de la puerta del tabernáculo, del tabernáculo del testimonio.
texts.exo.40.7: Luego pondrás la fuente entre el tabernáculo del testimonio y el altar; y pondrás agua en ella.
texts.exo.40.8: Finalmente pondrás el atrio en derredor, y el pabellón de la puerta del atrio.
texts.exo.40.9: Y tomarás el aceite de la unción y ungirás el tabernáculo, y todo lo que está en él; y le santificarás con todos sus vasos, y será santo.
texts.exo.40.10: Ungirás también el altar del holocausto y todos sus vasos: y santificarás el altar, y será un altar santísimo.
texts.exo.40.11: Asimismo ungirás la fuente y su basa, y la santificarás.
texts.exo.40.12: Y harás llegar á Aarón y á sus hijos á la puerta del tabernáculo del testimonio, y los lavarás con agua.
texts.exo.40.13: Y harás vestir á Aarón las vestiduras sagradas, y lo ungirás, y lo consagrarás, para que sea mi sacerdote.
texts.exo.40.14: Después harás llegar sus hijos, y les vestirás las túnicas:
texts.exo.40.15: Y los ungirás como ungiste á su padre, y serán mis sacerdotes: y será que su unción les servirá por sacerdocio perpetuo por sus generaciones.
texts.exo.40.16: Y Moisés hizo conforme á todo lo que Jehová le mandó; así lo hizo.
texts.exo.40.17: Y así en el día primero del primer mes, en el segundo año, el tabernáculo fué erigido.
texts.exo.40.18: Y Moisés hizo levantar el tabernáculo, y asentó sus basas, y colocó sus tablas, y puso sus barras, é hizo alzar sus columnas.
texts.exo.40.19: Y extendió la tienda sobre el tabernáculo, y puso la sobrecubierta encima del mismo; como Jehová había mandado á Moisés.
texts.exo.40.20: Y tomó y puso el testimonio dentro del arca, y colocó las varas en el arca, y encima la cubierta sobre el arca:
texts.exo.40.21: Y metió el arca en el tabernáculo, y puso el velo de la tienda, y cubrió el arca del testimonio; como Jehová había mandado á Moisés.
texts.exo.40.22: Y puso la mesa en el tabernáculo del testimonio, al lado septentrional del pabellón, fuera del velo:
texts.exo.40.23: Y sobre ella puso por orden los panes delante de Jehová, como Jehová había mandado á Moisés.
texts.exo.40.24: Y puso el candelero en el tabernáculo del testimonio, enfrente de la mesa, al lado meridional del pabellón.
texts.exo.40.25: Y encendió las lámparas delante de Jehová; como Jehová había mandado á Moisés.
texts.exo.40.26: Puso también el altar de oro en el tabernáculo del testimonio, delante del velo:
texts.exo.40.27: Y encendió sobre él el perfume aromático; como Jehová había mandado á Moisés.
texts.exo.40.28: Puso asimismo la cortina de la puerta del tabernáculo.
texts.exo.40.29: Y colocó el altar del holocausto á la puerta del tabernáculo, del tabernáculo del testimonio; y ofreció sobre él holocausto y presente; como Jehová había mandado á Moisés.
texts.exo.40.30: Y puso la fuente entre el tabernáculo del testimonio y el altar; y puso en ella agua para lavar.
texts.exo.40.31: Y Moisés y Aarón y sus hijos lavaban en ella sus manos y sus pies.
texts.exo.40.32: Cuando entraban en el tabernáculo del testimonio, y cuando se llegaban al altar, se lavaban; como Jehová había mandado á Moisés.
texts.exo.40.33: Finalmente erigió el atrio en derredor del tabernáculo y del altar, y puso la cortina de la puerta del atrio. Y así acabó Moisés la obra.
texts.exo.40.34: Entonces una nube cubrió el tabernáculo del testimonio, y la gloria de Jehová hinchió el tabernáculo.
texts.exo.40.35: Y no podía Moisés entrar en el tabernáculo del testimonio, porque la nube estaba sobre él, y la gloria de Jehová lo tenía lleno.
texts.exo.40.36: Y cuando la nube se alzaba del tabernáculo, los hijos de Israel se movían en todas sus jornadas:
texts.exo.40.37: Pero si la nube no se alzaba, no se partían hasta el día en que ella se alzaba.
texts.exo.40.38: Porque la nube de Jehová estaba de día sobre el tabernáculo, y el fuego estaba de noche en él, á vista de toda la casa de Israel, en todas sus jornadas.

texts.exo.1.1: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt (every man and his household came with Jacob):
texts.exo.1.4: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
texts.exo.1.5: And all the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls: and Joseph was in Egypt already.
texts.exo.1.6: And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.
texts.exo.1.7: And the children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.
texts.exo.1.8: Now there arose a new king over Egypt, who knew not Joseph.
texts.exo.1.9: And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we:
texts.exo.1.10: come, let us deal wisely with them, lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they also join themselves unto our enemies, and fight against us, and get them up out of the land.
texts.exo.1.11: Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh store-cities, Pithom and Raamses.
texts.exo.1.12: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and the more they spread abroad. And they were grieved because of the children of Israel.
texts.exo.1.13: And the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigor:
texts.exo.1.14: and they made their lives bitter with hard service, in mortar and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field, all their service, wherein they made them serve with rigor.
texts.exo.1.15: And the king of Egypt spake to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah:
texts.exo.1.16: and he said, When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them upon the birth-stool; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him; but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.
texts.exo.1.17: But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men-children alive.
texts.exo.1.18: And the king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said unto them, Why have ye done this thing, and have saved the men-children alive?
texts.exo.1.19: And the midwives said unto Pharaoh, Because the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women; for they are lively, and are delivered ere the midwife come unto them.
texts.exo.1.20: And God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty.
texts.exo.1.21: And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them households.
texts.exo.1.22: And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive.
texts.exo.2.1: And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.
texts.exo.2.2: And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.
texts.exo.2.3: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch; and she put the child therein, and laid it in the flags by the river's brink.
texts.exo.2.4: And his sister stood afar off, to know what would be done to him.
texts.exo.2.5: And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river-side; and she saw the ark among the flags, and sent her handmaid to fetch it.
texts.exo.2.6: And she opened it, and saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews' children.
texts.exo.2.7: Then said his sister to Pharaoh's daughter, Shall I go and call thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee?
texts.exo.2.8: And Pharaoh's daughter said to her, Go. And the maiden went and called the child's mother.
texts.exo.2.9: And Pharaoh's daughter said unto her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages. And the woman took the child, and nursed it.
texts.exo.2.10: And the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses, and said, Because I drew him out of the water.
texts.exo.2.11: And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown up, that he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: and he saw an Egyptian smiting a Hebrew, one of his brethren.
texts.exo.2.12: And he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he smote the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.
texts.exo.2.13: And he went out the second day, and, behold, two men of the Hebrews were striving together: and he said to him that did the wrong, Wherefore smitest thou thy fellow?
texts.exo.2.14: And he said, Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? Thinkest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? And Moses feared, and said, Surely the thing is known.
texts.exo.2.15: Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.
texts.exo.2.16: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.
texts.exo.2.17: And the shepherds came and drove them away; but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.
texts.exo.2.18: And when they came to Reuel their father, he said, How is it that ye are come so soon to-day?
texts.exo.2.19: And they said, An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and moreover he drew water for us, and watered the flock.
texts.exo.2.20: And he said unto his daughters, And where is he? Why is it that ye have left the man? Call him, that he may eat bread.
texts.exo.2.21: And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.
texts.exo.2.22: And she bare a son, and he called his name Gershom; for he said, I have been a sojourner in a foreign land.
texts.exo.2.23: And it came to pass in the course of those many days, that the king of Egypt died: and the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up unto God by reason of the bondage.
texts.exo.2.24: And God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
texts.exo.2.25: And God saw the children of Israel, and God took knowledge [of them].
texts.exo.3.1: Now Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian: and he led the flock to the back of the wilderness, and came to the mountain of God, unto Horeb.
texts.exo.3.2: And the angel of Jehovah appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
texts.exo.3.3: And Moses said, I will turn aside now, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt.
texts.exo.3.4: And when Jehovah saw that he turned aside to see, God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses. And he said, Here am I.
texts.exo.3.5: And he said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.
texts.exo.3.6: Moreover he said, I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. And Moses hid his face; for he was afraid to look upon God.
texts.exo.3.7: And Jehovah said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people that are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows;
texts.exo.3.8: and I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land unto a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey; unto the place of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
texts.exo.3.9: And now, behold, the cry of the children of Israel is come unto me: moreover I have seen the oppression wherewith the Egyptians oppress them.
texts.exo.3.10: Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt.
texts.exo.3.11: And Moses said unto God, Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt?
texts.exo.3.12: And he said, Certainly I will be with thee; and this shall be the token unto thee, that I have sent thee: when thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain.
texts.exo.3.13: And Moses said unto God, Behold, when I come unto the children of Israel, and shall say unto them, The God of your fathers hath sent me unto you; and they shall say to me, What is his name? What shall I say unto them?
texts.exo.3.14: And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.
texts.exo.3.15: And God said moreover unto Moses, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, Jehovah, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath sent me unto you: this is my name forever, and this is my memorial unto all generations.
texts.exo.3.16: Go, and gather the elders of Israel together, and say unto them, Jehovah, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, hath appeared unto me, saying, I have surely visited you, and [seen] that which is done to you in Egypt:
texts.exo.3.17: and I have said, I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt unto the land of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, unto a land flowing with milk and honey.
texts.exo.3.18: And they shall hearken to thy voice: and thou shalt come, thou and the elders of Israel, unto the king of Egypt, and ye shall say unto him, Jehovah, the God of the Hebrews, hath met with us: and now let us go, we pray thee, three days' journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to Jehovah our God.
texts.exo.3.19: And I know that the king of Egypt will not give you leave to go, no, not by a mighty hand.
texts.exo.3.20: And I will put forth my hand, and smite Egypt with all my wonders which I will do in the midst thereof: and after that he will let you go.
texts.exo.3.21: And I will give this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians: and it shall come to pass, that, when ye go, ye shall not go empty.
texts.exo.3.22: But every woman shall ask of her neighbor, and of her that sojourneth in her house, jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment: and ye shall put them upon your sons, and upon your daughters; and ye shall despoil the Egyptians.
texts.exo.4.1: And Moses answered and said, But, behold, they will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice; for they will say, Jehovah hath not appeared unto thee.
texts.exo.4.2: And Jehovah said unto him, What is that in thy hand? And he said, A rod.
texts.exo.4.3: And he said, Cast in on the ground. And he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from before it.
texts.exo.4.4: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Put forth thy hand, and take it by the tail: (and he put forth his hand, and laid hold of it, and it became a rod in his hand:)
texts.exo.4.5: That they may believe that Jehovah, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared unto thee.
texts.exo.4.6: And Jehovah said furthermore unto him, Put now thy hand into thy bosom. And he put his hand into his bosom: and when he took it out, behold, his hand was leprous, as [white as] snow.
texts.exo.4.7: And he said, Put thy hand into thy bosom again. (And he put his hand into his bosom again; and when he took it out of his bosom, behold, it was turned again as his [other] flesh.)
texts.exo.4.8: And it shall come to pass, if they will not believe thee, neither hearken to the voice of the first sign, that they will believe the voice of the latter sign.
texts.exo.4.9: And it shall come to pass, if they will not believe even these two signs, neither hearken unto thy voice, that thou shalt take of the water of the river, and pour it upon the dry land: and the water which thou takest out of the river shall become blood upon the dry land.
texts.exo.4.10: And Moses said unto Jehovah, Oh, Lord, I am not eloquent, neither heretofore, nor since thou hast spoken unto thy servant; for I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.
texts.exo.4.11: And Jehovah said unto him, Who hath made man's mouth? Or who maketh [a man] dumb, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Is it not I, Jehovah?
texts.exo.4.12: Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt speak.
texts.exo.4.13: And he said, Oh, Lord, send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send.
texts.exo.4.14: And the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Moses, and he said, Is there not Aaron thy brother the Levite? I know that he can speak well. And also, behold, he cometh forth to meet thee: and when he seeth thee, he will be glad in his heart.
texts.exo.4.15: And thou shalt speak unto him, and put the words in his mouth: and I will be with thy mouth, and with his mouth, and will teach you what ye shall do.
texts.exo.4.16: And he shall be thy spokesman unto the people; and it shall come to pass, that he shall be to thee a mouth, and thou shalt be to him as God.
texts.exo.4.17: And thou shalt take in thy hand this rod, wherewith thou shalt do the signs.
texts.exo.4.18: And Moses went and returned to Jethro his father-in-law, and said unto him, Let me go, I pray thee, and return unto my brethren that are in Egypt, and see whether they be yet alive. And Jethro said to Moses, Go in peace.
texts.exo.4.19: And Jehovah said unto Moses in Midian, Go, return into Egypt; for all the men are dead that sought thy life.
texts.exo.4.20: And Moses took his wife and his sons, and set them upon an ass, and he returned to the land of Egypt: and Moses took the rod of God in his hand.
texts.exo.4.21: And Jehovah said unto Moses, When thou goest back into Egypt, see that thou do before Pharaoh all the wonders which I have put in thy hand: but I will harden his heart and he will not let the people go.
texts.exo.4.22: And thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith Jehovah, Israel is my son, my first-born:
texts.exo.4.23: and I have said unto thee, Let my son go, that he may serve me; and thou hast refused to let him go: behold, I will slay thy son, thy first-born.
texts.exo.4.24: And it came to pass on the way at the lodging-place, that Jehovah met him, and sought to kill him.
texts.exo.4.25: Then Zipporah took a flint, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet; and she said, Surely a bridegroom of blood art thou to me.
texts.exo.4.26: So he let him alone. Then she said, A bridegroom of blood [art thou], because of the circumcision.
texts.exo.4.27: And Jehovah said to Aaron, Go into the wilderness to meet Moses. And he went, and met him in the mountain of God, and kissed him.
texts.exo.4.28: And Moses told Aaron all the words of Jehovah wherewith he had sent him, and all the signs wherewith he had charged him.
texts.exo.4.29: And Moses and Aaron went and gathered together all the elders of the children of Israel:
texts.exo.4.30: and Aaron spake all the words which Jehovah had spoken unto Moses, and did the signs in the sight of the people.
texts.exo.4.31: And the people believed: and when they heard that Jehovah had visited the children of Israel, and that he had seen their affliction, then they bowed their heads and worshipped.
texts.exo.5.1: And afterward Moses and Aaron came, and said unto Pharaoh, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness.
texts.exo.5.2: And Pharaoh said, Who is Jehovah, that I should hearken unto his voice to let Israel go? I know not Jehovah, and moreover I will not let Israel go.
texts.exo.5.3: And they said, The God of the Hebrews hath met with us: let us go, we pray thee, three days' journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice unto Jehovah our God, lest he fall upon us with pestilence, or with the sword.
texts.exo.5.4: And the king of Egypt said unto them, Wherefore do ye, Moses and Aaron, loose the people from their works? get you unto your burdens.
texts.exo.5.5: And Pharaoh said, Behold, the people of the land are now many, and ye make them rest from their burdens.
texts.exo.5.6: And the same day Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters of the people, and their officers, saying,
texts.exo.5.7: Ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick, as heretofore: let them go and gather straw for themselves.
texts.exo.5.8: And the number of the bricks, which they did make heretofore, ye shall lay upon them; ye shall not diminish aught thereof: for they are idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our God.
texts.exo.5.9: Let heavier work be laid upon the men, that they may labor therein; and let them not regard lying words.
texts.exo.5.10: And the taskmasters of the people went out, and their officers, and they spake to the people, saying, Thus saith Pharaoh, I will not give you straw.
texts.exo.5.11: Go yourselves, get you straw where ye can find it: for nought of your work shall be diminished.
texts.exo.5.12: So the people were scattered abroad throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
texts.exo.5.13: And the taskmasters were urgent saying, Fulfil your works, [your] daily tasks, as when there was straw.
texts.exo.5.14: And the officers of the children of Israel, whom Pharaoh's taskmasters had set over them, were beaten, and demanded, Wherefore have ye not fulfilled your task both yesterday and to-day, in making brick as heretofore?
texts.exo.5.15: Then the officers of the children of Israel came and cried unto Pharaoh, saying, Wherefore dealest thou thus with thy servants?
texts.exo.5.16: There is no straw given unto thy servants, and they say to us, Make brick: and, behold, thy servants are beaten; but the fault it in thine own people.
texts.exo.5.17: But he said, Ye are idle, ye are idle: therefore ye say, Let us go and sacrifice to Jehovah.
texts.exo.5.18: Go therefore now, and work; for there shall no straw be given you, yet shall ye deliver the number of bricks.
texts.exo.5.19: And the officers of the children of Israel did see that they were in evil case, when it was said, Ye shall not diminish aught from your bricks, [your] daily tasks.
texts.exo.5.20: And they met Moses and Aaron, who stood in the way, as they came forth from Pharaoh:
texts.exo.5.21: and they said unto them, Jehovah look upon you, and judge: because ye have made our savor to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to slay us.
texts.exo.5.22: And Moses returned unto Jehovah, and said, Lord, wherefore hast thou dealt ill with this people? why is it that thou hast sent me?
texts.exo.5.23: For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in thy name, he hath dealt ill with this people; neither hast thou delivered thy people at all.
texts.exo.6.1: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Now shalt thou see what I will do to Pharaoh: for by a strong hand shall he let them go, and by a strong hand shall he drive them out of his land.
texts.exo.6.2: And God spake unto Moses, and said unto him, I am Jehovah:
texts.exo.6.3: and I appeared unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, as God Almighty; but by my name Jehovah I was not known to them.
texts.exo.6.4: And I have also established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojournings, wherein they sojourned.
texts.exo.6.5: And moreover I have heard the groaning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians keep in bondage; and I have remembered my covenant.
texts.exo.6.6: Wherefore say unto the children of Israel, I am Jehovah, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will rid you out of their bondage, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm, and with great judgments:
texts.exo.6.7: and I will take you to me for a people, and I will be to you a God; and ye shall know that I am Jehovah your God, who bringeth you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians.
texts.exo.6.8: And I will bring you in unto the land which I sware to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will give it you for a heritage: I am Jehovah.
texts.exo.6.9: And Moses spake so unto the children of Israel: but they hearkened not unto Moses for anguish of spirit, and for cruel bondage.
texts.exo.6.10: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
texts.exo.6.11: Go in, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.
texts.exo.6.12: And Moses spake before Jehovah, saying, Behold, the children of Israel have not hearkened unto me; how then shall Pharaoh hear me, who am of uncircumcised lips?
texts.exo.6.13: And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, and gave them a charge unto the children of Israel, and unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.6.14: These are the heads of their fathers' houses. The sons of Reuben the first-born of Israel: Hanoch, and Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi; these are the families of Reuben.
texts.exo.6.15: And the sons of Simeon: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman; these are the families of Simeon.
texts.exo.6.16: And these are the names of the sons of Levi according to their generations: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari; and the years of the life of Levi were a hundred thirty and seven years.
texts.exo.6.17: The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, according to their families.
texts.exo.6.18: And the sons of Kohath: Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel; and the years of the life of Kohath were a hundred thirty and three years.
texts.exo.6.19: And the sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to their generations.
texts.exo.6.20: And Amram took him Jochebed his father's sister to wife; and she bare him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram were a hundred and thirty and seven years.
texts.exo.6.21: And the sons of Izhar: Korah, and Nepheg, and Zichri.
texts.exo.6.22: And the sons of Uzziel: Mishael, and Elzaphan, and Sithri.
texts.exo.6.23: And Aaron took him Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab, the sister of Nahshon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
texts.exo.6.24: And the sons of Korah: Assir, and Elkanah, and Abiasaph; these are the families of the Korahites.
texts.exo.6.25: And Eleazar Aaron's son took him one of the daughters of Putiel to wife; and she bare him Phinehas. These are the heads of the fathers' [houses] of the Levites according to their families.
texts.exo.6.26: These are that Aaron and Moses, to whom Jehovah said, Bring out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt according to their hosts.
texts.exo.6.27: These are they that spake to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring out the children of Israel from Egypt: these are that Moses and Aaron.
texts.exo.6.28: And it came to pass on the day when Jehovah spake unto Moses in the land of Egypt,
texts.exo.6.29: that Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying, I am Jehovah: speak thou unto Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I speak unto thee.
texts.exo.6.30: And Moses said before Jehovah, Behold, I am of uncircumcised lips, and how shall Pharaoh hearken unto me?
texts.exo.7.1: And Jehovah said unto Moses, See, I have made thee as God to Pharaoh; and Aaron thy brother shall be thy prophet.
texts.exo.7.2: Thou shalt speak all that I command thee; and Aaron thy brother shall speak unto Pharaoh, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.
texts.exo.7.3: And I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.7.4: But Pharaoh will not hearken unto you, and I will lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth my hosts, my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.
texts.exo.7.5: And the Egyptians shall know that I am Jehovah, when I stretch forth my hand upon Egypt, and bring out the children of Israel from among them.
texts.exo.7.6: And Moses and Aaron did so; as Jehovah commanded them, so did they.
texts.exo.7.7: And Moses was fourscore years old, and Aaron fourscore and three years old, when they spake unto Pharaoh.
texts.exo.7.8: And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,
texts.exo.7.9: When Pharaoh shall speak unto you, saying, Show a wonder for you; then thou shalt say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and cast it down before Pharaoh, that it become a serpent.
texts.exo.7.10: And Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharaoh, and they did so, as Jehovah had commanded: and Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.
texts.exo.7.11: Then Pharaoh also called for the wise men and the sorcerers: and they also, the magicians of Egypt, did in like manner with their enchantments.
texts.exo.7.12: For they cast down every man his rod, and they became serpents: but Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods.
texts.exo.7.13: And Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them; as Jehovah had spoken.
texts.exo.7.14: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Pharaoh's heart is stubborn, he refuseth to let the people go.
texts.exo.7.15: Get thee unto Pharaoh in the morning; lo, he goeth out unto the water; and thou shalt stand by the river's brink to meet him; and the rod which was turned to a serpent shalt thou take in thy hand.
texts.exo.7.16: And thou shalt say unto him, Jehovah, the God of the Hebrews, hath sent me unto thee, saying, Let my people go, that they may serve me in the wilderness: and, behold, hitherto thou hast not hearkened.
texts.exo.7.17: Thus saith Jehovah, In this thou shalt know that I am Jehovah: behold, I will smite with the rod that is in my hand upon the waters which are in the river, and they shall be turned to blood.
texts.exo.7.18: And the fish that are in the river shall die, and the river shall become foul; and the Egyptians shall loathe to drink water from the river.
texts.exo.7.19: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and stretch out thy hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, over their streams, and over their pools, and over all their ponds of water, that they may become blood; and there shall be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood and in vessels of stone.
texts.exo.7.20: And Moses and Aaron did so, as Jehovah commanded; and he lifted up the rod, and smote the waters that were in the river, in the sight of Pharaoh, and in the sight of his servants; and all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood.
texts.exo.7.21: And the fish that were in the river died; and the river became foul, and the Egyptians could not drink water from the river; and the blood was throughout all the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.7.22: And the magicians of Egypt did in like manner with their enchantments: and Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them; as Jehovah had spoken.
texts.exo.7.23: And Pharaoh turned and went into his house, neither did he lay even this to heart.
texts.exo.7.24: And all the Egyptians digged round about the river for water to drink; for they could not drink of the water of the river.
texts.exo.7.25: And seven days were fulfilled, after that Jehovah had smitten the river.
texts.exo.8.1: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh, and say unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, Let my people go, that they may serve me.
texts.exo.8.2: And if thou refuse to let them go, behold, I will smite all thy borders with frogs:
texts.exo.8.3: and the river shall swarm with frogs, which shall go up and come into thy house, and into thy bedchamber, and upon thy bed, and into the house of thy servants, and upon thy people, and into thine ovens, and into thy kneading-troughs:
texts.exo.8.4: and the frogs shall come up both upon thee, and upon thy people, and upon all thy servants.
texts.exo.8.5: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch forth thy hand with thy rod over the rivers, over the streams, and over the pools, and cause frogs to come up upon the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.8.6: And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt; and the frogs came up, and covered the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.8.7: And the magicians did in like manner with their enchantments, and brought up frogs upon the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.8.8: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron, and said, Entreat Jehovah, that he take away the frogs from me, and from my people; and I will let the people go, that they may sacrifice unto Jehovah.
texts.exo.8.9: And Moses said unto Pharaoh, Have thou this glory over me: against what time shall I entreat for thee, and for thy servants, and for thy people, that the frogs be destroyed from thee and thy houses, and remain in the river only?
texts.exo.8.10: And he said, Against to-morrow. And he said, Be it according to thy word; that thou mayest know that there is none like unto Jehovah our God.
texts.exo.8.11: And the frogs shall depart from thee, and from thy houses, and from thy servants, and from thy people; they shall remain in the river only.
texts.exo.8.12: And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh: and Moses cried unto Jehovah concerning the frogs which he had brought upon Pharaoh.
texts.exo.8.13: And Jehovah did according to the word of Moses; and the frogs died out of the houses, out of the courts, and out of the fields.
texts.exo.8.14: And they gathered them together in heaps; and the land stank.
texts.exo.8.15: But when Pharaoh saw that there was respite, he hardened his heart, and hearkened not unto them, as Jehovah had spoken.
texts.exo.8.16: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy rod, and smite the dust of the earth, that is may become lice throughout all the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.8.17: And they did so; and Aaron stretched out his hand with his rod, and smote the dust of the earth, and there were lice upon man, and upon beast; all the dust of the earth became lice throughout all the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.8.18: And the magicians did so with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but they could not: and there were lice upon man, and upon beast.
texts.exo.8.19: Then the magicians said unto Pharaoh, This is the finger of God: and Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them; as Jehovah had spoken.
texts.exo.8.20: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh; lo, he cometh forth to the water; and say unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, Let my people go, that they may serve me.
texts.exo.8.21: Else, if thou wilt not let my people go, behold, I will send swarms of flies upon thee, and upon they servants, and upon thy people, and into thy houses: and the houses of the Egyptians shall be full of swarms of flies, and also the ground whereon they are.
texts.exo.8.22: And I will set apart in that day the land of Goshen, in which my people dwell, that no swarms of flies shall be there; to the end thou mayest know that I am Jehovah in the midst of the earth.
texts.exo.8.23: And I will put a division between my people and thy people: by to-morrow shall this sign be.
texts.exo.8.24: And Jehovah did so; and there came grievous swarms of flies into the house of Pharaoh, and into his servants' houses: and in all the land of Egypt the land was corrupted by reason of the swarms of flies.
texts.exo.8.25: And Pharaoh called for Moses and for Aaron, and said, Go ye, sacrifice to your God in the land.
texts.exo.8.26: And Moses said, It is not meet so to do; for we shall sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians to Jehovah our God: lo, shall we sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, and will they not stone us?
texts.exo.8.27: We will go three days' journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice to Jehovah our God, as he shall command us.
texts.exo.8.28: And Pharaoh said, I will let you go, that ye may sacrifice to Jehovah your God in the wilderness; only ye shall not go very far away: entreat for me.
texts.exo.8.29: And Moses said, Behold, I go out from thee, and I will entreat Jehovah that the swarms of flies may depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people, to-morrow: only let not Pharaoh deal deceitfully any more in not letting the people go to sacrifice to Jehovah.
texts.exo.8.30: And Moses went out from Pharaoh, and entreated Jehovah.
texts.exo.8.31: And Jehovah did according to the word of Moses; and he removed the swarms of flies from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people; there remained not one.
texts.exo.8.32: And Pharaoh hardened his heart this time also, and he did not let the people go.
texts.exo.9.1: Then Jehovah said unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh, and tell him, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of the Hebrews, Let my people go, that they may serve me.
texts.exo.9.2: For if thou refuse to let them go, and wilt hold them still,
texts.exo.9.3: behold, the hand of Jehovah is upon thy cattle which are in the field, upon the horses, upon the asses, upon the camels, upon the herds, and upon the flocks: [there shall be] a very grievous murrain.
texts.exo.9.4: And Jehovah shall make a distinction between the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt; and there shall nothing die of all that belongeth to the children of Israel.
texts.exo.9.5: And Jehovah appointed a set time, saying, To-morrow Jehovah shall do this thing in the land.
texts.exo.9.6: And Jehovah did that thing on the morrow; and all the cattle of Egypt died; but of the cattle of the children of Israel died not one.
texts.exo.9.7: And Pharaoh sent, and, behold, there was not so much as one of the cattle of the Israelites dead. But the heart of Pharaoh was stubborn, and he did not let the people go.
texts.exo.9.8: And Jehovah said unto Moses and unto Aaron, Take to you handfuls of ashes of the furnace, and let Moses sprinkle it toward heaven in the sight of Pharaoh.
texts.exo.9.9: And it shall become small dust over all the land of Egypt, and shall be a boil breaking forth with blains upon man and upon beast, throughout all the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.9.10: And they took ashes of the furnace, and stood before Pharaoh; and Moses sprinkled it up toward heaven; and it became a boil breaking forth with blains upon man and upon beast.
texts.exo.9.11: And the magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils; for the boils were upon the magicians, and upon all the Egyptians.
texts.exo.9.12: And Jehovah hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he hearkened not unto them, as Jehovah had spoken unto Moses.
texts.exo.9.13: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh, and say unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of the Hebrews, Let my people go, that they may serve me.
texts.exo.9.14: For I will this time send all my plagues upon thy heart, and upon thy servants, and upon thy people; that thou mayest know that there is none like me in all the earth.
texts.exo.9.15: For now I had put forth my hand, and smitten thee and thy people with pestilence, and thou hadst been cut off from the earth:
texts.exo.9.16: but in very deed for this cause have I made thee to stand, to show thee my power, and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth.
texts.exo.9.17: As yet exaltest thou thyself against my people, that thou wilt not let them go?
texts.exo.9.18: Behold, to-morrow about this time I will cause it to rain a very grievous hail, such as hath not been in Egypt since the day it was founded even until now.
texts.exo.9.19: Now therefore send, hasten in thy cattle and all that thou hast in the field; [for] every man and beast that shall be found in the field, and shall not be brought home, the hail shall come down upon them, and they shall die.
texts.exo.9.20: He that feared the word of Jehovah among the servants of Pharaoh made his servants and his cattle flee into the houses.
texts.exo.9.21: And he that regarded not the word of Jehovah left his servants and his cattle in the field.
texts.exo.9.22: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Stretch forth thy hand toward heaven, that there may be hail in all the land of Egypt, upon man, and upon beast, and upon every herb of the field, throughout the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.9.23: And Moses stretched forth his rod toward heaven: and Jehovah sent thunder and hail, and fire ran down unto the earth; and Jehovah rained hail upon the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.9.24: So there was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous, such as had not been in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.
texts.exo.9.25: And the hail smote throughout all the land of Egypt all that was in the field, both man and beast; and the hail smote every herb of the field, and brake every tree of the field.
texts.exo.9.26: Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, was there no hail.
texts.exo.9.27: And Pharaoh sent, and called for Moses and Aaron, and said unto them, I have sinned this time: Jehovah is righteous, and I and my people are wicked.
texts.exo.9.28: Entreat Jehovah; for there hath been enough of [these] mighty thunderings and hail; and I will let you go, and ye shall stay no longer.
texts.exo.9.29: And Moses said unto him, As soon as I am gone out of the city, I will spread abroad my hands unto Jehovah; the thunders shall cease, neither shall there be any more hail; that thou mayest know that the earth is Jehovah's.
texts.exo.9.30: But as for thee and thy servants, I know that ye will not yet fear Jehovah God.
texts.exo.9.31: And the flax and the barley were smitten: for the barley was in the ear, and the flax was in bloom.
texts.exo.9.32: But the wheat and the spelt were not smitten: for they were not grown up.
texts.exo.9.33: And Moses went out of the city from Pharaoh, and spread abroad his hands unto Jehovah: and the thunders and hail ceased, and the rain was not poured upon the earth.
texts.exo.9.34: And when Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunders were ceased, he sinned yet more, and hardened his heart, he and his servants.
texts.exo.9.35: And the heart of Pharaoh was hardened, and he did not let the children of Israel go, as Jehovah had spoken by Moses.
texts.exo.10.1: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh: for I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his servants, that I may show these my signs in the midst of them,
texts.exo.10.2: and that thou mayest tell in the ears of thy son, and of thy son's son, what things I have wrought upon Egypt, and my signs which I have done among them; that ye may know that I am Jehovah.
texts.exo.10.3: And Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharaoh, and said unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of the Hebrews, How long wilt thou refuse to humble thyself before me? let my people go, that they may serve me.
texts.exo.10.4: Else, if thou refuse to let my people go, behold, to-morrow will I bring locusts into thy border:
texts.exo.10.5: and they shall cover the face of the earth, so that one shall not be able to see the earth: and they shall eat the residue of that which is escaped, which remaineth unto you from the hail, and shall eat every tree which groweth for you out of the field:
texts.exo.10.6: and thy houses shall be filled, and the houses of all thy servants, and the houses of all the Egyptians; as neither thy fathers nor thy fathers' fathers have seen, since the day that they were upon the earth unto this day. And he turned, and went out from Pharaoh.
texts.exo.10.7: And Pharaoh's servants said unto him, How long shall this man be a snare unto us? let the men go, that they may serve Jehovah their God: knowest thou not yet that Egypt is destroyed?
texts.exo.10.8: And Moses and Aaron were brought again unto Pharaoh: and he said unto them, Go, serve Jehovah your God; but who are they that shall go?
texts.exo.10.9: And Moses said, We will go with our young and with our old; with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds will we go; for we must hold a feast unto Jehovah.
texts.exo.10.10: And he said unto them, So be Jehovah with you, as I will let you go, and your little ones: look to it; for evil is before you.
texts.exo.10.11: Not so: go now ye that are men, and serve Jehovah; for that is what ye desire. And they were driven out from Pharaoh's presence.
texts.exo.10.12: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Stretch out thy hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come up upon the land of Egypt, and eat every herb of the land, even all that the hail hath left.
texts.exo.10.13: And Moses stretched forth his rod over the land of Egypt, and Jehovah brought an east wind upon the land all that day, and all the night; and when it was morning, the east wind brought the locusts.
texts.exo.10.14: And the locusts went up over all the land of Egypt, and rested in all the borders of Egypt; very grievous were they; before them there were no such locusts as they, neither after them shall be such.
texts.exo.10.15: For they covered the face of the whole earth, so that the land was darkened; and they did eat every herb of the land, and all the fruit of the trees which the hail had left: and there remained not any green thing, either tree or herb of the field, through all the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.10.16: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron in haste; and he said, I have sinned against Jehovah your God, and against you.
texts.exo.10.17: Now therefore forgive, I pray thee, my sin only this once, and entreat Jehovah your God, that he may take away from me this death only.
texts.exo.10.18: And he went out from Pharaoh, and entreated Jehovah.
texts.exo.10.19: And Jehovah turned an exceeding strong west wind, which took up the locusts, and drove them into the Red Sea; there remained not one locust in all the border of Egypt.
texts.exo.10.20: But Jehovah hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not let the children of Israel go.
texts.exo.10.21: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Stretch out thy hand toward heaven, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt.
texts.exo.10.22: And Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven; and there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days;
texts.exo.10.23: they saw not one another, neither rose any one from his place for three days: but all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.
texts.exo.10.24: And Pharaoh called unto Moses, and said, Go ye, serve Jehovah; only let your flocks and your herds be stayed: let your little ones also go with you.
texts.exo.10.25: And Moses said, Thou must also give into our hand sacrifices and burnt-offerings, that we may sacrifice unto Jehovah our God.
texts.exo.10.26: Our cattle also shall go with us; there shall not a hoof be left behind: for thereof must we take to serve Jehovah our God; and we know not with what we must serve Jehovah, until we come thither.
texts.exo.10.27: But Jehovah hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not let them go.
texts.exo.10.28: And Pharaoh said unto him, Get thee from me, take heed to thyself, see my face no more; for in the day thou seest my face thou shalt die.
texts.exo.10.29: And Moses said, Thou hast spoken well. I will see thy face again no more.
texts.exo.11.1: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Yet one plague more will I bring upon Pharaoh, and upon Egypt; afterwards he will let you go hence: when he shall let you go, he shall surely thrust you out hence altogether.
texts.exo.11.2: Speak now in the ears of the people, and let them ask every man of his neighbor, and every woman of her neighbor, jewels of silver, and jewels of gold.
texts.exo.11.3: And Jehovah gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians. Moreover the man Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh's servants, and in the sight of the people.
texts.exo.11.4: And Moses said, Thus saith Jehovah, About midnight will I go out into the midst of Egypt:
texts.exo.11.5: and all the first-born in the land of Egypt shall die, from the first-born of Pharaoh that sitteth upon his throne, even unto the first-born of the maid-servant that is behind the mill; and all the first-born of cattle.
texts.exo.11.6: And there shall be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as there hath not been, nor shall be any more.
texts.exo.11.7: But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that Jehovah doth make a distinction between the Egyptians and Israel.
texts.exo.11.8: And all these thy servants shall come down unto me, and bow down themselves unto me, saying, Get thee out, and all the people that follow thee: and after that I will go out. And he went out from Pharaoh in hot anger.
texts.exo.11.9: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Pharaoh will not hearken unto you; that my wonders may be multiplied in the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.11.10: And Moses and Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh: and Jehovah hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not let the children of Israel go out of his land.
texts.exo.12.1: And Jehovah spake unto Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
texts.exo.12.2: This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.
texts.exo.12.3: Speak ye unto all the congregation of Israel, saying, In the tenth [day] of this month they shall take to them every man a lamb, according to their fathers' houses, a lamb for a household:
texts.exo.12.4: and if the household be too little for a lamb, then shall he and his neighbor next unto his house take one according to the number of the souls; according to every man's eating ye shall make your count for the lamb.
texts.exo.12.5: Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male a year old: ye shall take it from the sheep, or from the goats:
texts.exo.12.6: and ye shall keep it until the fourteenth day of the same month; and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it at even.
texts.exo.12.7: And they shall take of the blood, and put it on the two side-posts and on the lintel, upon the houses wherein they shall eat it.
texts.exo.12.8: And they shall eat the flesh in that night, roast with fire, and unleavened bread; with bitter herbs they shall eat it.
texts.exo.12.9: Eat not of it raw, nor boiled at all with water, but roast with fire; its head with its legs and with the inwards thereof.
texts.exo.12.10: And ye shall let nothing of it remain until the morning; but that which remaineth of it until the morning ye shall burn with fire.
texts.exo.12.11: And thus shall ye eat it: with your loins girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and ye shall eat it in haste: it is Jehovah's passover.
texts.exo.12.12: For I will go through the land of Egypt in that night, and will smite all the first-born in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments: I am Jehovah.
texts.exo.12.13: And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and there shall no plague be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.12.14: And this day shall be unto you for a memorial, and ye shall keep it a feast to Jehovah: throughout your generations ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.
texts.exo.12.15: Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread; even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses: for whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.
texts.exo.12.16: And in the first day there shall be to you a holy convocation, and in the seventh day a holy convocation; no manner of work shall be done in them, save that which every man must eat, that only may be done by you.
texts.exo.12.17: And ye shall observe the [feast of] unleavened bread; for in this selfsame day have I brought your hosts out of the land of Egypt: therefore shall ye observe this day throughout your generations by an ordinance for ever.
texts.exo.12.18: In the first [month], on the fourteenth day of the month at even, ye shall eat unleavened bread, until the one and twentieth day of the month at even.
texts.exo.12.19: Seven days shall there be no leaven found in your houses: for whosoever eateth that which is leavened, that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether he be a sojourner, or one that is born in the land.
texts.exo.12.20: Ye shall eat nothing leavened; in all your habitations shall ye eat unleavened bread.
texts.exo.12.21: Then Moses called for all the elders of Israel, and said unto them, Draw out, and take you lambs according to your families, and kill the passover.
texts.exo.12.22: And ye shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and strike the lintel and the two side-posts with the blood that is in the basin; and none of you shall go out of the door of his house until the morning.
texts.exo.12.23: For Jehovah will pass through to smite the Egyptians; and when he seeth the blood upon the lintel, and on the two side-posts, Jehovah will pass over the door, and will not suffer the destroyer to come in unto your houses to smite you.
texts.exo.12.24: And ye shall observe this thing for an ordinance to thee and to thy sons for ever.
texts.exo.12.25: And it shall come to pass, when ye are come to the land which Jehovah will give you, according as he hath promised, that ye shall keep this service.
texts.exo.12.26: And it shall come to pass, when your children shall say unto you, What mean ye by this service?
texts.exo.12.27: that ye shall say, It is the sacrifice of Jehovah's passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he smote the Egyptians, and delivered our houses. And the people bowed the head and worshipped.
texts.exo.12.28: And the children of Israel went and did so; as Jehovah had commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they.
texts.exo.12.29: And it came to pass at midnight, that Jehovah smote all the first-born in the land of Egypt, from the first-born of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the first-born of the captive that was in the dungeon; and all the first-born of cattle.
texts.exo.12.30: And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt, for there was not a house where there was not one dead.
texts.exo.12.31: And he called for Moses and Aaron by night, and said, Rise up, get you forth from among my people, both ye and the children of Israel; and go, serve Jehovah, as ye have said.
texts.exo.12.32: Take both your flocks and your herds, as ye have said, and be gone; and bless me also.
texts.exo.12.33: And the Egyptians were urgent upon the people, to send them out of the land in haste; for they said, We are all dead men.
texts.exo.12.34: And the people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneading-troughs being bound up in their clothes upon their shoulders.
texts.exo.12.35: And the children of Israel did according to the word of Moses; and they asked of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment.
texts.exo.12.36: And Jehovah gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they let them have what they asked. And they despoiled the Egyptians.
texts.exo.12.37: And the children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot that were men, besides children.
texts.exo.12.38: And a mixed multitude went up also with them; and flocks, and herds, even very much cattle.
texts.exo.12.39: And they baked unleavened cakes of the dough which they brought forth out of Egypt; for it was not leavened, because they were thrust out of Egypt, and could not tarry, neither had they prepared for themselves any victuals.
texts.exo.12.40: Now the time that the children of Israel dwelt in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years.
texts.exo.12.41: And it came to pass at the end of four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day it came to pass, that all the hosts of Jehovah went out from the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.12.42: It is a night to be much observed unto Jehovah for bringing them out from the land of Egypt: this is that night of Jehovah, to be much observed of all the children of Israel throughout their generations.
texts.exo.12.43: And Jehovah said unto Moses and Aaron, This is the ordinance of the passover: there shall no foreigner eat thereof;
texts.exo.12.44: but every man's servant that is bought for money, when thou hast circumcised him, then shall he eat thereof.
texts.exo.12.45: A sojourner and a hired servant shall not eat thereof.
texts.exo.12.46: In one house shall it be eaten; thou shalt not carry forth aught of the flesh abroad out of the house; neither shall ye break a bone thereof.
texts.exo.12.47: All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.
texts.exo.12.48: And when a stranger shall sojourn with thee, and will keep the passover to Jehovah, let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near and keep it; and he shall be as one that is born in the land: but no uncircumcised person shall eat thereof.
texts.exo.12.49: One law shall be to him that is home-born, and unto the stranger that sojourneth among you.
texts.exo.12.50: Thus did all the children of Israel; as Jehovah commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they.
texts.exo.12.51: And it came to pass the selfsame day, that Jehovah did bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their hosts.
texts.exo.13.1: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
texts.exo.13.2: Sanctify unto me all the first-born, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of beast: it is mine.
texts.exo.13.3: And Moses said unto the people, Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand Jehovah brought you out from this place: there shall no leavened bread be eaten.
texts.exo.13.4: This day ye go forth in the month Abib.
texts.exo.13.5: And it shall be, when Jehovah shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, which he sware unto thy fathers to give thee, a land flowing with milk and honey, that thou shalt keep this service in this month.
texts.exo.13.6: Seven days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, and in the seventh day shall be a feast to Jehovah.
texts.exo.13.7: Unleavened bread shall be eaten throughout the seven days; and there shall no leavened bread be seen with thee, neither shall there be leaven seen with thee, in all thy borders.
texts.exo.13.8: And thou shalt tell thy son in that day, saying, It is because of that which Jehovah did for me when I came forth out of Egypt.
texts.exo.13.9: And it shall be for a sign unto thee upon thy hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes, that the law of Jehovah may be in thy mouth: for with a strong hand hath Jehovah brought thee out of Egypt.
texts.exo.13.10: Thou shalt therefore keep this ordinance in its season from year to year.
texts.exo.13.11: And it shall be, when Jehovah shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanite, as he sware unto thee and to thy fathers, and shall give it thee,
texts.exo.13.12: that thou shalt set apart unto Jehovah all that openeth the womb, and every firstling which thou hast that cometh of a beast; the males shall be Jehovah's.
texts.exo.13.13: And every firstling of an ass thou shalt redeem with a lamb; and if thou wilt not redeem it, then thou shalt break its neck: and all the first-born of man among thy sons shalt thou redeem.
texts.exo.13.14: And it shall be, when thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What is this? that thou shalt say unto him, By strength of hand Jehovah brought us out from Egypt, from the house of bondage:
texts.exo.13.15: and it came to pass, when Pharaoh would hardly let us go, that Jehovah slew all the first-born in the land of Egypt, both the first-born of man, and the first-born of beast: therefore I sacrifice to Jehovah all that openeth the womb, being males; but all the first-born of my sons I redeem.
texts.exo.13.16: And it shall be for a sign upon thy hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes: for by strength of hand Jehovah brought us forth out of Egypt.
texts.exo.13.17: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God led them not by the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt:
texts.exo.13.18: but God led the people about, by the way of the wilderness by the Red Sea: and the children of Israel went up armed out of the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.13.19: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.
texts.exo.13.20: And they took their journey from Succoth, and encamped in Etham, in the edge of the wilderness.
texts.exo.13.21: And Jehovah went before them by day in a pillar of cloud, to lead them the way, and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light, that they might go by day and by night:
texts.exo.13.22: the pillar of cloud by day, and the pillar of fire by night, departed not from before the people.
texts.exo.14.1: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
texts.exo.14.2: Speak unto the children of Israel, that they turn back and encamp before Pihahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal-zephon: over against it shall ye encamp by the sea.
texts.exo.14.3: And Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel, They are entangled in the land, the wilderness hath shut them in.
texts.exo.14.4: And I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and he shall follow after them; and I will get me honor upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host: and the Egyptians shall know that I am Jehovah. And they did so.
texts.exo.14.5: And it was told the king of Egypt that the people were fled: and the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was changed towards the people, and they said, What is this we have done, that we have let Israel go from serving us?
texts.exo.14.6: And he made ready his chariot, and took his people with him:
texts.exo.14.7: and he took six hundred chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Egypt, and captains over all of them.
texts.exo.14.8: And Jehovah hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued after the children of Israel: for the children of Israel went out with a high hand.
texts.exo.14.9: And the Egyptians pursued after them, all the horses [and] chariots of Pharaoh, and his horsemen, and his army, and overtook them encamping by the sea, beside Pihahiroth, before Baal-zephon.
texts.exo.14.10: And when Pharaoh drew nigh, the children of Israel lifted up their eyes, and, behold, the Egyptians were marching after them; and they were sore afraid: and the children of Israel cried out unto Jehovah.
texts.exo.14.11: And they said unto Moses, Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness? wherefore hast thou dealt thus with us, to bring us forth out of Egypt?
texts.exo.14.12: Is not this the word that we spake unto thee in Egypt, saying, Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians? For it were better for us to serve the Egyptians, than that we should die in the wilderness.
texts.exo.14.13: And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of Jehovah, which he will work for you to-day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to-day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.
texts.exo.14.14: Jehovah will fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.
texts.exo.14.15: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Wherefore criest thou unto me? speak unto the children of Israel, that they go forward.
texts.exo.14.16: And lift thou up thy rod, and stretch out thy hand over the sea, and divide it: and the children of Israel shall go into the midst of the sea on dry ground.
texts.exo.14.17: And I, behold, I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians, and they shall go in after them: and I will get me honor upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host, upon his chariots, and upon his horsemen.
texts.exo.14.18: And the Egyptians shall know that I am Jehovah, when I have gotten me honor upon Pharaoh, upon his chariots, and upon his horsemen.
texts.exo.14.19: And the angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, removed and went behind them; and the pillar of cloud removed from before them, and stood behind them:
texts.exo.14.20: and it came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel; and there was the cloud and the darkness, yet gave it light by night: and the one came not near the other all the night.
texts.exo.14.21: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and Jehovah caused the sea to go [back] by a strong east wind all the night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.
texts.exo.14.22: And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.
texts.exo.14.23: And the Egyptians pursued, and went in after them into the midst of the sea, all Pharaoh's horses, his chariots, and his horsemen.
texts.exo.14.24: And it came to pass in the morning watch, that Jehovah looked forth upon the host of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and of cloud, and discomfited the host of the Egyptians.
texts.exo.14.25: And he took off their chariot wheels, and they drove them heavily; so that the Egyptians said, Let us flee from the face of Israel; for Jehovah fighteth for them against the Egyptians.
texts.exo.14.26: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Stretch out thy hand over the sea, that the waters may come again upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots, and upon their horsemen.
texts.exo.14.27: And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to its strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and Jehovah overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.
texts.exo.14.28: And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, even all the host of Pharaoh that went in after them into the sea; there remained not so much as one of them.
texts.exo.14.29: But the children of Israel walked upon dry land in the midst of the sea; and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.
texts.exo.14.30: Thus Jehovah saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians; and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea-shore.
texts.exo.14.31: And Israel saw the great work which Jehovah did upon the Egyptians, and the people feared Jehovah: and they believed in Jehovah, and in his servant Moses.
texts.exo.15.1: Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto Jehovah, and spake, saying, I will sing unto Jehovah, for he hath triumphed gloriously: The horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.
texts.exo.15.2: Jehovah is my strength and song, And he is become my salvation: This is my God, and I will praise him; My father's God, and I will exalt him.
texts.exo.15.3: Jehovah is a man of war: Jehovah is his name.
texts.exo.15.4: Pharaoh's chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea; And his chosen captains are sunk in the Red Sea.
texts.exo.15.5: The deeps cover them: They went down into the depths like a stone.
texts.exo.15.6: Thy right hand, O Jehovah, is glorious in power, Thy right hand, O Jehovah, dasheth in pieces the enemy.
texts.exo.15.7: And in the greatness of thine excellency thou overthrowest them that rise up against thee: Thou sendest forth thy wrath, it consumeth them as stubble.
texts.exo.15.8: And with the blast of thy nostrils the waters were piled up, The floods stood upright as a heap; The deeps were congealed in the heart of the sea.
texts.exo.15.9: The enemy said, I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoil; My desire shall be satisfied upon them; I will draw my sword, my hand shall destroy them.
texts.exo.15.10: Thou didst blow with thy wind, the sea covered them: They sank as lead in the mighty waters.
texts.exo.15.11: Who is like unto thee, O Jehovah, among the gods? Who is like thee, glorious in holiness, Fearful in praises, doing wonders?
texts.exo.15.12: Thou stretchedst out thy right hand, The earth swallowed them.
texts.exo.15.13: Thou in thy lovingkindness hast led the people that thou hast redeemed: Thou hast guided them in thy strength to thy holy habitation.
texts.exo.15.14: The peoples have heard, they tremble: Pangs have taken hold on the inhabitants of Philistia.
texts.exo.15.15: Then were the chiefs of Edom dismayed; The mighty men of Moab, trembling taketh hold upon them: All the inhabitants of Canaan are melted away.
texts.exo.15.16: Terror and dread falleth upon them; By the greatness of thine arm they are as still as a stone; Till thy people pass over, O Jehovah, Till the people pass over that thou hast purchased.
texts.exo.15.17: Thou wilt bring them in, and plant them in the mountain of thine inheritance, The place, O Jehovah, which thou hast made for thee to dwell in, The sanctuary, O Lord, which thy hands have established.
texts.exo.15.18: Jehovah shall reign for ever and ever.
texts.exo.15.19: For the horses of Pharaoh went in with his chariots and with his horsemen into the sea, and Jehovah brought back the waters of the sea upon them; but the children of Israel walked on dry land in the midst of the sea.
texts.exo.15.20: And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances.
texts.exo.15.21: And Miriam answered them, Sing ye to Jehovah, for he hath triumphed gloriously; The horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.
texts.exo.15.22: And Moses led Israel onward from the Red Sea, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water.
texts.exo.15.23: And when they came to Marah, they could not drink of the waters of Marah, for they were bitter: therefore the name of it was called Marah.
texts.exo.15.24: And the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink?
texts.exo.15.25: An he cried unto Jehovah; And Jehovah showed him a tree, and he cast it into the waters, and the waters were made sweet. There he made for them a statute and an ordinance, and there he proved them;
texts.exo.15.26: and he said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of Jehovah thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his eyes, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of the diseases upon thee, which I have put upon the Egyptians: for I am Jehovah that healeth thee.
texts.exo.15.27: And they came to Elim, where were twelve springs of water, and threescore and ten palm-trees: and they encamped there by the waters.
texts.exo.16.1: And they took their journey from Elim, and all the congregation of the children of Israel came unto the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their departing out of the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.16.2: And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron in the wilderness:
texts.exo.16.3: and the children of Israel said unto them, Would that we had died by the hand of Jehovah in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh-pots, when we did eat bread to the full; for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.
