texts.exo.33.18: And he said, I beseech thee, show me thy glory.
texts.exo.33.19: And he said, I will make all my goodness pass before thee, and I will proclaim the name of the LORD before thee; and will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy.
texts.exo.33.20: And he said, Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live.
texts.exo.33.21: And the LORD said, Behold, there is a place by me, and thou shalt stand upon a rock:
texts.exo.33.22: And it shall come to pass, while my glory passeth by, that I will put thee in a cleft of the rock: and will cover thee with my hand while I pass by:
texts.exo.33.23: And I will take away my hand, and thou shalt see my back parts: but my face shall not be seen.
texts.exo.34.1: And the LORD said to Moses, Hew thee two tables of stone like the first; and I will write upon these tables the words that were in the first tables which thou didst break.
texts.exo.34.2: And be ready in the morning, and come up in the morning to mount Sinai, and present thyself there to me on the top of the mount.
texts.exo.34.3: And no man shall come up with thee, neither let any man be seen throughout all the mount: neither let the flocks nor herds feed before that mount.
texts.exo.34.4: And he hewed two tables of stone, like the first; and Moses rose up early in the morning, and went up to mount Sinai, as the LORD had commanded him, and took in his hand the two tables of stone.
texts.exo.34.5: And the LORD descended in the cloud, and stood with him there, and proclaimed the name of the LORD.
texts.exo.34.6: And the LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed, The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, long-suffering, and abundant in goodness and truth.
texts.exo.34.7: Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children's children, to the third and to the fourth generation.
texts.exo.34.8: And Moses made haste, and bowed his head towards the earth, and worshiped.
texts.exo.34.9: And he said, If now I have found grace in thy sight, O Lord, let my Lord, I pray thee, go among us (for it is a stiff-necked people) and pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us for thy inheritance.
texts.exo.34.10: And he said, Behold, I make a covenant: before all thy people I will do wonders, such as have not been done in all the earth, nor in any nation: and all the people among which thou art, shall see the work of the LORD: for it is a terrible thing that I will do with thee.
texts.exo.34.11: Observe thou that which I command thee this day: Behold, I drive out before thee the Amorite, and the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
texts.exo.34.12: Take heed to thyself, lest thou make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land whither thou goest, lest it be for a snare in the midst of thee:
texts.exo.34.13: But ye shall destroy their altars, break their images, and cut down their groves.
texts.exo.34.14: For thou shalt worship no other god: for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God:
texts.exo.34.15: Lest thou make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, and they go astray after their gods, and do sacrifice to their gods, and one call thee, and thou eat of his sacrifice;
texts.exo.34.16: And thou take of their daughters to thy sons, and their daughters go astray after their gods, and make thy sons go astray after their gods.
texts.exo.34.17: Thou shalt make thee no molten gods.
texts.exo.34.18: The feast of unleavened bread shalt thou keep. Seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread, as I commanded thee, in the time of the month Abib: for in the month Abib thou camest out of from Egypt.
texts.exo.34.19: Every first-born is mine: and every firstling among thy cattle, whether ox or sheep, that is male.
texts.exo.34.20: But the firstling of an ass thou shalt redeem with a lamb: and if thou shalt not redeem him, then shalt thou break his neck. All the first-born of thy sons thou shalt redeem. And none shall appear before me empty.
texts.exo.34.21: Six days thou shalt work, but on the seventh day thou shalt rest: in time of plowing and in harvest thou shalt rest.
texts.exo.34.22: And thou shalt observe the feast of weeks, of the first-fruits of wheat-harvest, and the feast of in-gathering at the year's end.
texts.exo.34.23: Thrice in the year shall all your male children appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel.
texts.exo.34.24: For I will drive out the nations before thee, and enlarge thy borders: neither shall any man desire thy land, when thou shalt go up to appear before the LORD thy God, thrice in the year.
texts.exo.34.25: Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leaven, neither shall the sacrifice of the feast of the passover be left until the morning.
texts.exo.34.26: The first of the first-fruits of thy land thou shalt bring to the house of the LORD thy God. Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk.
texts.exo.34.27: And the LORD said to Moses, Write thou these words: for after the tenor of these words I have made a covenant with thee, and with Israel.
texts.exo.34.28: And he was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights; he neither ate bread nor drank water: and he wrote upon the tables the words of the covenant, the ten commandments.
texts.exo.34.29: And it came to pass when Moses came down from mount Sinai (with the two tables of testimony in Moses's hand, when he came down from the mount) that Moses knew not that the skin of his face shone, while he talked with him.
texts.exo.34.30: And when Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone, and they were afraid to come nigh him.
texts.exo.34.31: And Moses called to them; and Aaron and all the rulers of the congregation returned to him; and Moses talked with them.
texts.exo.34.32: And afterward all the children of Israel came nigh: and he gave them in commandment all that the LORD had spoken with him in mount Sinai.
texts.exo.34.33: And till Moses had done speaking with them, he put a vail on his face.
texts.exo.34.34: But when Moses went in before the LORD to speak with him, he took the vail off, until he came out. And he came out and spoke to the children of Israel that which he was commanded.
texts.exo.34.35: And the children of Israel saw the face of Moses, that the skin of Moses's face shone: and Moses put the vail upon his face again, until he went in to speak with him.
texts.exo.35.1: And Moses assembled all the congregation of the children of Israel, and said to them, These are the words which the LORD hath commanded, that ye should do them.
texts.exo.35.2: Six days shall work be done; but on the seventh day there shall be to you a holy day, a sabbath of rest to the LORD: whoever doth work therein shall be put to death.
texts.exo.35.3: Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath-day.
texts.exo.35.4: And Moses spoke to all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying, This is the thing which the LORD commanded, saying,
texts.exo.35.5: Take ye from among you an offering to the LORD: whoever is of a willing heart, let him bring it, an offering of the LORD; gold, and silver, and brass,
texts.exo.35.6: And blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats' hair,
texts.exo.35.7: And rams' skins dyed red, and badgers' skins, and shittim wood,
texts.exo.35.8: And oil for the light, and spices for anointing oil, and for the sweet incense,
texts.exo.35.9: And onyx stones, and stones to be set for the ephod, and for the breast-plate.
texts.exo.35.10: And every wise-hearted among you shall come, and make all that the LORD hath commanded;
texts.exo.35.11: The tabernacle, its tent, and its covering, its buttons, and its boards, its bars, its pillars, and its sockets,
texts.exo.35.12: The ark, and its staffs, with the mercy-seat, and the vail of the covering,
texts.exo.35.13: The table, and its staffs, and all its vessels, and the show-bread,
texts.exo.35.14: The candlestick also for the light, and its furniture, and its lamps, with the oil for the light,
texts.exo.35.15: And the incense-altar, and its staffs, and the anointing oil, and the sweet incense, and the hanging for the door at the entrance of the tabernacle,
texts.exo.35.16: The altar of burnt-offering, with its brazen grate, its staffs, and all its vessels, the laver and its foot,
texts.exo.35.17: The hangings of the court, its pillars, and their sockets, and the hanging for the door of the court,
texts.exo.35.18: The pins of the tabernacle, and the pins of the court, and their cords,
texts.exo.35.19: The clothes of service, to do service in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest's office.
texts.exo.35.20: And all the congregation of the children of Israel departed from the presence of Moses.
texts.exo.35.21: And they came, every one whose heart excited him, and every one whom his spirit made willing, and they brought the LORD'S offering to the work of the tabernacle of the congregation, and for all his service, and for the holy garments.
texts.exo.35.22: And they came, both men and women, as many as were willing-hearted, and brought bracelets, and ear-rings, and rings, and tablets, all jewels of gold; and every man that offered, offered an offering of gold to the LORD.
texts.exo.35.23: And every man, with whom was found blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats' hair, and red skins of rams, and badgers' skins, brought them.
texts.exo.35.24: Every one that offered an offering of silver and brass brought the LORD'S offering: and every man with whom was found shittim wood for any work of the service, brought it.
texts.exo.35.25: And all the women that were wise-hearted spun with their hands, and brought that which they had spun, both of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, and of fine linen.
texts.exo.35.26: And all the women whose heart moved them in wisdom spun goats' hair.
texts.exo.35.27: And the rulers brought onyx stones, and stones to be set, for the ephod, and for the breast-plate;
texts.exo.35.28: And spice, and oil for the light, and for the anointing oil, and for the sweet incense.
texts.exo.35.29: The children of Israel brought a willing offering to the LORD, every man and woman, whose heart made them willing to bring for all manner of work, which the LORD had commanded to be made by the hand of Moses.
texts.exo.35.30: And Moses said to the children of Israel, See, the LORD hath called by name Bezaleel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah;
texts.exo.35.31: And he hath filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship;
texts.exo.35.32: And to devise curious works, to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass,
texts.exo.35.33: And in the cutting of stones, to set them, and in carving of wood, to make any manner of curious work.
texts.exo.35.34: And he hath put in his heart that he may teach, both he and Aholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.
texts.exo.35.35: Them hath he filled with wisdom of heart, to work all manner of work, of the engraver, and of the skillful workmen, and of the embroiderer, in blue, and in purple, in scarlet, and in fine linen, and of the weaver, even of them that do any work, and of those that devise curious work.
texts.exo.36.1: Then wrought Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise-hearted man, in whom the LORD put wisdom and understanding, to know how to work all manner of work for the service of the sanctuary, according to all that the LORD had commanded.
texts.exo.36.2: And Moses called Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise-hearted man, in whose heart the LORD had put wisdom, even every one whose heart excited him to come to the work to do it:
texts.exo.36.3: And they received from Moses all the offering which the children of Israel had brought for the work of the service of the sanctuary, to make it. And they brought yet to him free-offerings every morning.
texts.exo.36.4: And all the wise men, that wrought all the work of the sanctuary, came every man from his work which they made.
texts.exo.36.5: And they spoke to Moses, saying, The people bring much more than enough for the service of the work, which the LORD commanded to make.
texts.exo.36.6: And Moses gave commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp, saying, Let neither man nor woman make any more work for the offering of the sanctuary. So the people were restrained from bringing.
texts.exo.36.7: For the stuff they had was sufficient for all the work to make it, and too much.
texts.exo.36.8: And every wise-hearted man among them that wrought the work of the tabernacle made ten curtains of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet: he made them with cherubim of curious work.
texts.exo.36.9: The length of one curtain was twenty and eight cubits, and the breadth of one curtain four cubits: the curtains were all of one size.
texts.exo.36.10: And he coupled the five curtains one to another: and the other five curtains he coupled one to another.
texts.exo.36.11: And he made loops of blue on the edge of one curtain from the selvedge in the coupling: likewise he made in the extremity of another curtain, in the coupling of the second.
texts.exo.36.12: Fifty loops he made in one curtain, and fifty loops he made in the edge of the curtain which was in the coupling of the second: the loops held one curtain to another.
texts.exo.36.13: And he made fifty buttons of gold, and coupled the curtains one to another with the buttons. So it became one tabernacle.
texts.exo.36.14: And he made curtains of goats' hair for the tent over the tabernacle: eleven curtains he made them.
texts.exo.36.15: The length of one curtain was thirty cubits, and four cubits was the breadth of one curtain: the eleven curtains were of one size.
texts.exo.36.16: And he coupled five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves.
texts.exo.36.17: And he made fifty loops upon the outermost edge of the curtain in the coupling, and fifty loops made he upon the edge of the curtain which coupleth the second.
texts.exo.36.18: And he made fifty buttons of brass to couple the tent together, that it might be one.
texts.exo.36.19: And he made a covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and a covering of badgers' skins above that.
texts.exo.36.20: And he made boards for the tabernacle of shittim wood, standing up.
texts.exo.36.21: The length of a board was ten cubits, and the breadth of a board one cubit and a half.
texts.exo.36.22: One board had two tenons, equally distant one from another; thus did he make for all the boards of the tabernacle.
texts.exo.36.23: And he made boards for the tabernacle; twenty boards for the south side southward:
texts.exo.36.24: And forty sockets of silver he made under the twenty boards; two sockets under one board for its two tenons, and two sockets under another board for its two tenons.
texts.exo.36.25: And for the other side of the tabernacle which is towards the north corner, he made twenty boards.
texts.exo.36.26: And their forty sockets of silver; two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.
texts.exo.36.27: And for the sides of the tabernacle westward he made six boards.
texts.exo.36.28: And two boards he made for the corners of the tabernacle in the two sides.
texts.exo.36.29: And they were coupled beneath, and coupled together at the head thereof, to one ring: thus he did to both of them in both the corners.
texts.exo.36.30: And there were eight boards; and their sockets were sixteen sockets of silver, under every board two sockets.
texts.exo.36.31: And he made bars of shittim wood; five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
texts.exo.36.32: And five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the tabernacle for the sides westward.
texts.exo.36.33: And he made the middle bar to shoot through the boards from the one end to the other.
texts.exo.36.34: And he overlaid the boards with gold, and made their rings of gold to be places for the bars, and overlaid the bars with gold.
texts.exo.36.35: And he made a vail of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen: with cherubim he made it of curious work.
texts.exo.36.36: And he made to it four pillars of shittim wood, and overlaid them with gold: their hooks were of gold; and he cast for them four sockets of silver.
texts.exo.36.37: And he made a hanging for the tabernacle-door of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, of needle-work;
texts.exo.36.38: And the five pillars of it, with their hooks: and he overlaid their capitals and their fillets with gold: but their five sockets were of brass.
texts.exo.37.1: And Bezaleel made the ark of shittim wood: two cubits and a half was the length of it, and a cubit and a half the breadth of it, and a cubit and a half the hight of it:
texts.exo.37.2: And he overlaid it with pure gold within and without, and made a crown of gold to it round about.
texts.exo.37.3: And he cast for it four rings of gold, to be set by the four corners of it; even two rings upon the one side of it, and two rings upon the other side of it.
texts.exo.37.4: And he made staffs of shittim wood, and overlaid them with gold.
texts.exo.37.5: And he put the staffs into the rings by the sides of the ark, to bear the ark.
texts.exo.37.6: And he made the mercy-seat of pure gold: two cubits and a half was the length of it, and one cubit and a half the breadth of it.
texts.exo.37.7: And he made two cherubim of gold, beaten out of one piece he made them, on the two ends of the mercy-seat;
texts.exo.37.8: One cherub on the end on this side, and another cherub on the other end on that side: out of the mercy-seat made he the cherubim on the two ends of it.
texts.exo.37.9: And the cherubim spread out their wings on high, and covered with their wings over the mercy-seat, with their faces one to another; even towards the mercy-seat were the faces of the cherubim.
texts.exo.37.10: And he made the table of shittim wood: two cubits was its length, and a cubit its breadth, and a cubit and a half its hight:
texts.exo.37.11: And he overlaid it with pure gold, and made to it a crown of gold round about.
texts.exo.37.12: Also he made to it a border of a hand-breadth round about; and made a crown of gold for its border round about.
texts.exo.37.13: And he cast for it four rings of gold, and put the rings upon the four corners that were in its four feet.
texts.exo.37.14: Over against the border were the rings, the places for the staffs, to bear the table.
texts.exo.37.15: And he made the staffs of shittim wood, and overlaid them with gold, to bear the table.
texts.exo.37.16: And he made the vessels which were upon the table, its dishes, and its spoons, and its bowls, and its covers to cover with, of pure gold.
texts.exo.37.17: And he made the candlestick of pure gold; of beaten work he made the candlestick; its shaft, and its branch, its bowls, its knobs, and its flowers were of the same:
texts.exo.37.18: And six branches proceeding from its sides; three branches of the candlestick from the one side of it, and three branches of the candlestick from the other side of it.
texts.exo.37.19: Three bowls made after the fashion of almonds in one branch, a knob and a flower; and three bowls made like almonds in another branch, a knob and a flower: so throughout the six branches proceeding from the candlestick.
texts.exo.37.20: And in the candlestick were four bowls made like almonds, its knobs, and its flowers:
texts.exo.37.21: And a knob under two branches of the same, and a knob under two branches of the same, and a knob under two branches of the same, according to the six branches proceeding from it.
texts.exo.37.22: Their knobs and their branches were of the same: all of it was one beaten work of pure gold.
texts.exo.37.23: And he made its seven lamps, and its snuffers, and its snuff-dishes, of pure gold.
texts.exo.37.24: Of a talent of pure gold he made it, and all its vessels.
texts.exo.37.25: And he made the incense-altar of shittim wood: the length of it was a cubit, and the breadth of it a cubit; it was foursquare; and two cubits was the hight of it; the horns of it were of the same.
texts.exo.37.26: And he overlaid it with pure gold, both the top of it, and its sides round about, and its horns: also he made to it a crown of gold round about.
texts.exo.37.27: And he made two rings of gold for it under its crown, by the two corners of it, upon its two sides, to be places for the staffs to bear it with.
texts.exo.37.28: And he made the staffs of shittim wood, and overlaid them with gold.
texts.exo.37.29: And he made the holy anointing oil, and the pure incense of sweet spices, according to the work of the apothecary.
texts.exo.38.1: And he made the altar of burnt-offering of shittim wood: five cubits was the length of it, and five cubits the breadth of it; it was foursquare; and its hight was three cubits.
texts.exo.38.2: And he made its horns on the four corners of it; its horns were of the same: and he overlaid it with brass.
texts.exo.38.3: And he made all the vessels of the altar, the pots, and the shovels, and the basins, and the flesh-hooks, and the fire-pans: all the vessels of it he made of brass.
texts.exo.38.4: And he made for the altar a brazen grate of net-work under the compass of it beneath to the midst of it.
texts.exo.38.5: And he cast four rings for the four ends of the grate of brass, to be places for the staffs.
texts.exo.38.6: And he made the staffs of shittim wood, and overlaid them with brass.
texts.exo.38.7: And he put the staffs into the rings on the sides of the altar, to bear it with; he made the altar hollow with boards.
texts.exo.38.8: And he made the laver of brass, and the foot of it of brass, of the looking-glasses of the women assembling, who assembled at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.
texts.exo.38.9: And he made the court: on the south side southward the hangings of the court were of fine twined linen, a hundred cubits:
texts.exo.38.10: Their pillars were twenty, and their brazen sockets twenty; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, were of silver.
texts.exo.38.11: And for the north side, the hangings were a hundred cubits, their pillars were twenty, and their sockets of brass twenty: the hooks of the pillars, and their filets, of silver.
texts.exo.38.12: And for the west side were hangings of fifty cubits, their pillars ten, and their sockets ten; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver.
texts.exo.38.13: And for the east side eastward fifty cubits.
texts.exo.38.14: The hangings of the one side of the gate were fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.
texts.exo.38.15: And for the other side of the court-gate, on this hand and that hand, were hangings of fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.
texts.exo.38.16: All the hangings of the court round about were of fine twined linen.
texts.exo.38.17: And the sockets for the pillars were of brass; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver; and the overlaying of their capitals of silver; and all the pillars of the court were filleted with silver.
texts.exo.38.18: And the hanging for the gate of the court was needle-work, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen: and twenty cubits was the length, and the hight in the breadth was five cubits, answerable to the hangings of the court.
texts.exo.38.19: And their pillars were four, and their sockets of brass four; their hooks of silver, and the overlaying of their capitals and their fillets of silver.
texts.exo.38.20: And all the pins of the tabernacle, and of the court round about, were of brass.
texts.exo.38.21: This is the sum of the tabernacle, even of the tabernacle of testimony, as it was counted, according to the commandment of Moses, for the service of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar, son to Aaron the priest.
texts.exo.38.22: And Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made all that the LORD commanded Moses.
texts.exo.38.23: And with him was Aholiab, son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver, and a skillful workman, and an embroiderer in blue, and in purple, and in scarlet, and fine linen.
texts.exo.38.24: All the gold that was occupied for the work in all the work of the holy place, even the gold of the offering, was twenty and nine talents, and seven hundred and thirty shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary.
texts.exo.38.25: And the silver of them that were numbered of the congregation was a hundred talents, and a thousand seven hundred and seventy five shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary:
texts.exo.38.26: A bekah for every man, that is, half a shekel, after the shekel of the sanctuary, for every one that went to be numbered, from twenty years old and upward, for six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty men.
texts.exo.38.27: And of the hundred talents of silver were cast the sockets of the sanctuary, and the sockets of the vail; a hundred sockets of the hundred talents, a talent for a socket.
texts.exo.38.28: And of the thousand seven hundred seventy and five shekels he made hooks for the pillars, and overlaid their capitals, and filleted them.
texts.exo.38.29: And the brass of the offering was seventy talents, and two thousand and four hundred shekels.
texts.exo.38.30: And with this he made the sockets to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and the brazen altar, and the brazen grate for it, and all the vessels of the altar,
texts.exo.38.31: And the sockets of the court round about, and the sockets of the court gate, and all the pins of the tabernacle, and all the pins of the court round about.
texts.exo.39.1: And of the blue, and purple, and scarlet, they made clothes of service, to do service in the holy place, and made the holy garments for Aaron; as the LORD commanded Moses.
texts.exo.39.2: And he made the ephod of gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen.
texts.exo.39.3: And they beat the gold into thin plates, and cut it into wires, to work it in the blue, and in the purple, and in the scarlet, and in the fine linen, with curious work.
texts.exo.39.4: They made shoulder-pieces for it, to couple it together: by the two edges was it coupled together.
texts.exo.39.5: And the curious girdle of his ephod, that was upon it, was of the same, according to the work thereof; of gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen; as the LORD commanded Moses.
texts.exo.39.6: And they wrought onyx stones inclosed in ouches of gold, graven as signets are graven, with the names of the children of Israel.
texts.exo.39.7: And he put them on the shoulders of the ephod, that they should be stones for a memorial to the children of Israel; as the LORD commanded Moses.
texts.exo.39.8: And he made the breast-plate of curious work, like the work of the ephod; of gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen.
texts.exo.39.9: It was foursquare; they made the breast-plate double: a span was the length of it, and a span the breadth of it, being doubled.
texts.exo.39.10: And they set in it four rows of stones: the first row was a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle: this was the first row.
texts.exo.39.11: And the second row, an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond.
texts.exo.39.12: And the third row, a ligure, an agate, and an amethyst.
texts.exo.39.13: And the fourth row, a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper: they were inclosed in ouches of gold in their inclosings.
texts.exo.39.14: And the stones were according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names, like the engravings of a signet, every one with his name, according to the twelve tribes.
texts.exo.39.15: And they made upon the breast-plate chains at the ends, of wreathed work of pure gold.
texts.exo.39.16: And they made two ouches of gold, and two gold rings, and put the two rings in the two ends of the breast-plate.
texts.exo.39.17: And they put the two wreathed chains of gold in the two rings on the ends of the breast-plate.
texts.exo.39.18: And the two ends of the two wreathed chains they fastened in the two ouches, and put them on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod, before it.
texts.exo.39.19: And they made two rings of gold, and put them on the two ends of the breast-plate, upon the border of it, which was on the side of the ephod inward.
texts.exo.39.20: And they made two other golden rings, and put them on the two sides of the ephod underneath, towards the forepart of it, over against the other coupling thereof, above the curious girdle of the ephod:
texts.exo.39.21: And they bound the breast-plate by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, that it might be above the curious girdle of the ephod, and that the breast-plate might not be loosed from the ephod; as the LORD commanded Moses.
texts.exo.39.22: And he made the robe of the ephod of woven work, all of blue.
texts.exo.39.23: And there was a hole in the midst of the robe, as the hole of an habergeon, with a band around the hole, that it should not rend.
texts.exo.39.24: And they made upon the hems of the robe pomegranates of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and twined linen.
texts.exo.39.25: And they made bells of pure gold, and put the bells between the pomegranates upon the hem of the robe, around between the pomegranates;
texts.exo.39.26: A bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, around the hem of the robe to minister in; as the LORD commanded Moses.
texts.exo.39.27: And they made coats of fine linen, of woven work, for Aaron and for his sons,
texts.exo.39.28: And a miter of fine linen, and goodly bonnets of fine linen, and linen breeches of fine twined linen,
texts.exo.39.29: And a girdle of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, of needle-work; as the LORD commanded Moses.
texts.exo.39.30: And they made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, and wrote upon it a writing, like to the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD.
texts.exo.39.31: And they tied to it a lace of blue, to fasten it on high upon the miter; as the LORD commanded Moses.
texts.exo.39.32: Thus was all the work of the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation finished: and the children of Israel did according to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so did they.
texts.exo.39.33: And they brought the tabernacle to Moses, the tent, and all its furniture, its buttons, its boards, its bars, and its pillars, and its sockets,
texts.exo.39.34: And the covering of rams' skins dyed red, and the covering of badgers' skins, and the vail of the covering,
texts.exo.39.35: The ark of the testimony, and its staffs, and the mercy-seat,
texts.exo.39.36: The table, and all its vessels, and the show-bread,
texts.exo.39.37: The pure candlestick, with its lamps, even with the lamps to be set in order, and all its vessels, and the oil for light,
texts.exo.39.38: And the golden altar, and the anointing oil, and the sweet incense, and the hanging for the tabernacle-door,
texts.exo.39.39: The brazen altar, and its grate of brass, its staffs, and all its vessels, the laver and its foot,
texts.exo.39.40: The hangings of the court, its pillars, and its sockets, and the hanging for the court-gate, its cords, and its pins, and all the vessels of the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of the congregation,
texts.exo.39.41: The clothes of service to do service in the holy place, and the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and his sons' garments, to minister in the priest's office.
texts.exo.39.42: According to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so the children of Israel made all the work.
texts.exo.39.43: And Moses looked upon all the work, and behold, they had done it as the LORD had commanded, even so had they done it: and Moses blessed them.
texts.exo.40.1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.exo.40.2: On the first day of the first month shalt thou set up the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation.
texts.exo.40.3: And thou shalt put in it the ark of the testimony, and cover the ark with the vail.
texts.exo.40.4: And thou shalt bring in the table, and set in order the things that are to be set in order upon it; and thou shalt bring in the candlestick, and light its lamps.
texts.exo.40.5: And thou shalt set the altar of gold for the incense before the ark of the testimony, and put the hanging of the door to the tabernacle.
texts.exo.40.6: And thou shalt set the altar of the, burnt-offering before the door of the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation.
texts.exo.40.7: And thou shalt set the laver between the tent of the congregation and the altar, and shalt put water in it.
texts.exo.40.8: And thou shalt set up the court round about, and hang up the hanging at the court-gate.
texts.exo.40.9: And thou shalt take the anointing oil, and anoint the tabernacle, and all that is in it, and shalt hallow it, and all its vessels: and it shall be holy.
texts.exo.40.10: And thou shalt anoint the altar of the burnt-offering and all its vessels, and sanctify the altar: and it shall be an altar most holy.
texts.exo.40.11: And thou shalt anoint the laver and its foot, and sanctify it.
texts.exo.40.12: And thou shalt bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and wash them with water.
texts.exo.40.13: And thou shalt put upon Aaron the holy garments, and anoint him, and sanctify him; that he may minister to me in the priest's office.
texts.exo.40.14: And thou shalt bring his sons, and clothe them with coats:
texts.exo.40.15: And thou shalt anoint them, as thou didst anoint their father, that they may minister to me in the priest's office: for their anointing shall surely be an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.
texts.exo.40.16: Thus did Moses; according to all that the LORD commanded him, so did he.
texts.exo.40.17: And it came to pass in the first month, in the second year, on the first day of the month, that the tabernacle was reared up.
texts.exo.40.18: And Moses reared up the tabernacle, and fastened its sockets, and set up its boards, and put in its bars, and reared up its pillars.
texts.exo.40.19: And he spread abroad the tent over the tabernacle, and put the covering of the tent above upon it; as the LORD commanded Moses.
texts.exo.40.20: And he took and put the testimony into the ark, and set the staffs on the ark, and put the mercy-seat above upon the ark:
texts.exo.40.21: And he brought the ark into the tabernacle, and set up the vail of the covering, and covered the ark of the testimony; as the LORD commanded Moses.
texts.exo.40.22: And he put the table in the tent of the congregation, upon the side of the tabernacle northward, without the vail.
texts.exo.40.23: And he set the bread in order upon it before the LORD; as the LORD had commanded Moses.
texts.exo.40.24: And he put the candlestick in the tent of the congregation, over against the table, on the side of the tabernacle southward.
texts.exo.40.25: And he lighted the lamps before the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.
texts.exo.40.26: And he put the golden altar in the tent of the congregation, before the vail:
texts.exo.40.27: And he burnt sweet incense on it; as the LORD commanded Moses.
texts.exo.40.28: And he set up the hanging at the door of the tabernacle.
texts.exo.40.29: And he put the altar of burnt-offering by the door of the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation, and offered upon it the burnt-offering, and the meat-offering; as the LORD commanded Moses.
texts.exo.40.30: And he set the laver between the tent of the congregation and the altar, and put water there, to wash with.
texts.exo.40.31: And Moses, and Aaron, and his sons, washed their hands and their feet thereat:
texts.exo.40.32: When they went into the tent of the congregation, and when they came near to the altar, they washed; as the LORD commanded Moses.
texts.exo.40.33: And he reared up the court round about the tabernacle and the altar, and set up the hanging of the court-gate: so Moses finished the work.
texts.exo.40.34: Then a cloud covered the tent of the congregation, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
texts.exo.40.35: And Moses was not able to enter into the tent of the congregation, because the cloud abode upon it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
texts.exo.40.36: And when the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel went onward in all their journeys:
texts.exo.40.37: But if the cloud was not taken up, then they journeyed not till the day that it was taken up.
texts.exo.40.38: For the cloud of the LORD was upon the tabernacle by day, and fire was on it by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.

texts.exo.1.1: And these are the names of the sons of Israel who had come into Egypt; with Jacob had they come, each with his household:
texts.exo.1.4: Dan and Naphtali; Gad and Asher.
texts.exo.1.5: And all the souls that had come out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls; and Joseph was in Egypt.
texts.exo.1.6: And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.
texts.exo.1.7: And the children of Israel were fruitful, and swarmed and multiplied, and became exceeding strong; and the land was full of them.
texts.exo.1.8: And there arose a new king over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.
texts.exo.1.9: And he said to his people, Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more numerous and stronger than we.
texts.exo.1.10: Come on, let us deal wisely with them, lest they multiply, and it come to pass that, if war occur, they take side with our enemies and fight against us, and go up out of the land.
texts.exo.1.11: And they set over them service-masters to oppress them with their burdens. And they built store-cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Rameses.
texts.exo.1.12: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and spread; and they were distressed because of the children of Israel.
texts.exo.1.13: And the Egyptians made the children of Israel serve with harshness;
texts.exo.1.14: and they embittered their life with hard labour in clay and bricks, and in all manner of labour in the field: all their labour with which they made them serve was with harshness.
texts.exo.1.15: And the king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives -- of whom the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other was Puah --
texts.exo.1.16: and he said, When ye help the Hebrew women in bearing, and see [them] on the stool, if it be a son, then ye shall kill him, but if a daughter, then she shall live.
texts.exo.1.17: But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt had said to them, but saved the male children alive.
texts.exo.1.18: And the king of Egypt called the midwives and said to them, Why have ye done this, and saved the male children alive?
texts.exo.1.19: And the midwives said to Pharaoh, Because the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian; for they are strong, and they have borne before the midwife comes to them.
texts.exo.1.20: And God dealt well with the midwives; and the people multiplied and became very strong.
texts.exo.1.21: And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them houses.
texts.exo.1.22: Then Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, but every daughter ye shall save alive.
texts.exo.2.1: And a man of the house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi.
texts.exo.2.2: And the woman conceived, and bore a son. And she saw him that he was fair, and hid him three months.
texts.exo.2.3: And when she could no longer hide him, she took for him an ark of reeds, and plastered it with resin and with pitch, and put the child in it, and laid [it] in the sedge on the bank of the river.
texts.exo.2.4: And his sister stood afar off to see what would happen to him.
texts.exo.2.5: And the daughter of Pharaoh went down to bathe in the river; and her maids went along by the river's side. And she saw the ark in the midst of the sedge, and sent her handmaid and fetched it.
texts.exo.2.6: And she opened [it], and saw the child, and behold, the boy wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is [one] of the Hebrews' children.
texts.exo.2.7: And his sister said to Pharaoh's daughter, Shall I go and call thee a wet-nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee?
texts.exo.2.8: And Pharaoh's daughter said to her, Go. And the damsel went and called the child's mother.
texts.exo.2.9: And Pharaoh's daughter said to her, Take this child away and nurse it for me, and I will give [thee] thy wages. And the woman took the child and nursed it.
texts.exo.2.10: And when the child was grown, she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses, and said, Because I drew him out of the water.
texts.exo.2.11: And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown, that he went out to his brethren and looked on their burdens; and he saw an Egyptian smiting a Hebrew, one of his brethren.
texts.exo.2.12: And he turned this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he smote the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.
texts.exo.2.13: And he went out on the second day, and behold, two Hebrew men were quarrelling; and he said to him that was in the wrong, Why art thou smiting thy neighbour?
texts.exo.2.14: And he said, Who made thee ruler and judge over us? dost thou intend to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? Then Moses feared, and said, Surely the matter is known.
texts.exo.2.15: And Pharaoh heard of this matter, and sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from before Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian. And he sat by the well.
texts.exo.2.16: And the priest of Midian had seven daughters; and they came and drew [water], and filled the troughs, to water their father's flock.
texts.exo.2.17: And the shepherds came and drove them away; but Moses rose and helped them, and watered their flock.
texts.exo.2.18: And when they came to Reuel their father, he said, Why are ye come so soon to-day?
texts.exo.2.19: And they said, An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also drew [water] abundantly for us, and watered the flock.
texts.exo.2.20: And he said to his daughters, And where is he? why then have ye left the man behind? Call him, that he may eat bread.
texts.exo.2.21: And Moses consented to remain with the man; and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.
texts.exo.2.22: And she bore a son, and he called his name Gershom; for he said, I have been a sojourner in a foreign land.
texts.exo.2.23: And it came to pass during those many days, that the king of Egypt died. And the children of Israel sighed because of the bondage, and cried; and their cry came up to God because of the bondage;
texts.exo.2.24: and God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob;
texts.exo.2.25: and God looked upon the children of Israel, and God acknowledged [them].
texts.exo.3.1: And Moses tended the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian. And he led the flock behind the wilderness, and came to the mountain of God -- to Horeb.
texts.exo.3.2: And the Angel of Jehovah appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a thorn-bush: and he looked, and behold, the thorn-bush burned with fire, and the thorn-bush was not being consumed.
texts.exo.3.3: And Moses said, Let me now turn aside and see this great sight, why the thorn-bush is not burnt.
texts.exo.3.4: And Jehovah saw that he turned aside to see, and God called to him out of the midst of the thorn-bush and said, Moses, Moses! And he said, Here am I.
texts.exo.3.5: And he said, Draw not nigh hither: loose thy sandals from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.
texts.exo.3.6: And he said, I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. And Moses hid his face; for he was afraid to look at God.
texts.exo.3.7: And Jehovah said, I have seen assuredly the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and their cry have I heard on account of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows.
texts.exo.3.8: And I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land unto a good and spacious land, unto a land flowing with milk and honey, unto the place of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
texts.exo.3.9: And now behold, the cry of the children of Israel is come unto me; and I have also seen the oppression with which the Egyptians oppress them.
texts.exo.3.10: And now come, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt.
texts.exo.3.11: And Moses said to God, Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt?
texts.exo.3.12: And he said, For I will be with thee; and this shall be the sign to thee that I have sent thee: when thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain.
texts.exo.3.13: And Moses said to God, Behold, [when] I come unto the children of Israel, and shall say unto them, The God of your fathers hath sent me unto you; and they shall say, What is his name? what shall I say unto them?
texts.exo.3.14: And God said to Moses, I AM THAT I AM. And he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel: I AM hath sent me unto you.
texts.exo.3.15: And God said moreover to Moses, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel: Jehovah, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath sent me unto you. This is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations.
texts.exo.3.16: Go and gather the elders of Israel together, and say unto them, Jehovah the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, hath appeared to me, saying, I have indeed visited you, and [seen] that which is done unto you in Egypt;
texts.exo.3.17: and I have said, I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt, unto the land of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, unto a land flowing with milk and honey.
texts.exo.3.18: And they shall hearken to thy voice. And thou shalt come, thou and the elders of Israel, unto the king of Egypt, and ye shall say unto him, Jehovah, the God of the Hebrews, hath met with us; and now, let us go, we pray thee, three days' journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to Jehovah our God.
texts.exo.3.19: But I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go, no, not by a powerful hand.
texts.exo.3.20: And I will stretch out my hand and smite Egypt with all my wonders which I will do in the midst thereof; and after that he will let you go.
texts.exo.3.21: And I will give this people favour in the eyes of the Egyptians, and it shall come to pass, when ye go out, that ye shall not go out empty;
texts.exo.3.22: but every woman shall ask of her neighbour, and of her that is the inmate of her house, utensils of silver, and utensils of gold, and clothing; and ye shall put [them] on your sons and on your daughters, and shall spoil the Egyptians.
texts.exo.4.1: And Moses answered and said, But behold, they will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice; for they will say, Jehovah has not appeared to thee.
texts.exo.4.2: And Jehovah said to him, What is that in thy hand? And he said, A staff.
texts.exo.4.3: And he said, Cast it on the ground. And he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from before it.
texts.exo.4.4: And Jehovah said to Moses, Stretch out thy hand and take it by the tail -- and he stretched out his hand and caught it, and it became a staff in his hand --
texts.exo.4.5: that they may believe that Jehovah, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared unto thee.
texts.exo.4.6: And Jehovah said moreover to him, Put now thy hand into thy bosom. And he put his hand into his bosom, and took it out, and behold, his hand was leprous, as snow.
texts.exo.4.7: And he said, Put thy hand into thy bosom again. And he put his hand into his bosom again, and took it out of his bosom, and behold, it was turned again as his flesh.
texts.exo.4.8: And it shall come to pass, if they will not believe thee, neither hearken to the voice of the first sign, that they will believe the voice of the other sign.
texts.exo.4.9: And it shall come to pass, if they will not believe also those two signs, neither hearken unto thy voice, that thou shalt take of the water of the river, and pour [it] on the dry [land]; and the water that thou takest out of the river shall become blood upon the dry [land].
texts.exo.4.10: And Moses said to Jehovah, Ah Lord! I am not eloquent, neither heretofore nor since thou hast spoken to thy servant, for I am slow of speech and of a slow tongue.
texts.exo.4.11: And Jehovah said to him, Who gave man a mouth? or who maketh dumb, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? [have] not I, Jehovah?
texts.exo.4.12: And now go, and I will be with thy mouth, and will teach thee what thou shalt say.
texts.exo.4.13: And he said, Ah Lord! send, I pray thee, by the hand [of him whom] thou wilt send.
texts.exo.4.14: Then the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Moses, and he said, Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he can speak well. And also behold, he goeth out to meet thee; and when he seeth thee he will be glad in his heart.
texts.exo.4.15: And thou shalt speak unto him, and put the words in his mouth; and I will be with thy mouth, and with his mouth, and will teach you what ye shall do.
texts.exo.4.16: And he shall speak for thee unto the people; and it shall come to pass that he shall be to thee for a mouth, and thou shalt be to him for God.
texts.exo.4.17: And thou shalt take this staff in thy hand, with which thou shalt do the signs.
texts.exo.4.18: And Moses went and returned to Jethro his father-in-law, and said to him, Let me go, I pray thee, and return to my brethren who are in Egypt, that I may see whether they are yet alive. And Jethro said to Moses, Go in peace.
texts.exo.4.19: And Jehovah said to Moses in Midian, Go, return to Egypt; for all the men are dead who sought thy life.
texts.exo.4.20: And Moses took his wife and his sons, and set them riding upon an ass, and he returned to the land of Egypt. And Moses took the staff of God in his hand.
texts.exo.4.21: And Jehovah said to Moses, When thou goest to return to Egypt, see that thou do all the wonders before Pharaoh that I have put in thy hand. And I will harden his heart, that he shall not let the people go.
texts.exo.4.22: And thou shalt say to Pharaoh, Thus saith Jehovah: Israel is my son, my firstborn.
texts.exo.4.23: And I say to thee, Let my son go, that he may serve me. And if thou refuse to let him go, behold, I will kill thy son, thy firstborn.
texts.exo.4.24: And it came to pass on the way, in the inn, that Jehovah came upon him, and sought to slay him.
texts.exo.4.25: Then Zipporah took a stone and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet, and said, A bloody husband indeed art thou to me!
texts.exo.4.26: And he let him go. Then she said, A bloody husband -- because of the circumcision.
texts.exo.4.27: And Jehovah said to Aaron, Go into the wilderness to meet Moses. And he went, and met him on the mountain of God, and kissed him.
texts.exo.4.28: And Moses told Aaron all the words of Jehovah who had sent him, and all the signs that he had commanded him.
texts.exo.4.29: And Moses and Aaron went and gathered all the elders of the children of Israel;
texts.exo.4.30: and Aaron spoke all the words that Jehovah had spoken to Moses, and did the signs before the eyes of the people.
texts.exo.4.31: And the people believed. And when they heard that Jehovah had visited the children of Israel, and that he had seen their affliction, then they bowed their heads and worshipped.
texts.exo.5.1: And afterwards Moses and Aaron went in, and said to Pharaoh, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, Let my people go that they may celebrate a feast to me in the wilderness.
texts.exo.5.2: And Pharaoh said, Who is Jehovah, to whose voice I am to hearken to let Israel go? I do not know Jehovah, neither will I let Israel go.
texts.exo.5.3: And they said, The God of the Hebrews has met with us: let us go, we pray thee, three days' journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice to Jehovah our God; lest he fall upon us with pestilence or with sword.
texts.exo.5.4: And the king of Egypt said to them, Why do ye, Moses and Aaron, wish to have the people go off from their works? Away, to your burdens!
texts.exo.5.5: And Pharaoh said, Behold the people of the land are now many, and ye wish to make them rest from their burdens.
texts.exo.5.6: And Pharaoh commanded the same day the taskmasters of the people, and their officers, saying,
texts.exo.5.7: Ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick, as heretofore: let them go and gather straw for themselves.
texts.exo.5.8: And the number of the bricks they have made heretofore shall ye lay upon them: ye shall not diminish any of it, for they are idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us go [and] sacrifice to our God.
texts.exo.5.9: Let them put heavier labour on the men, that they may be taken up with it, and not regard vain words.
texts.exo.5.10: And the taskmasters of the people and their officers went out and spoke to the people, saying, Thus says Pharaoh: I will not give you straw:
texts.exo.5.11: go ye, get yourselves straw where ye may find it; but none of your work shall be diminished.
texts.exo.5.12: And the people were scattered abroad throughout the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
texts.exo.5.13: And the taskmasters urged [them], saying, Fulfil your labours, the daily work, as when there was straw.
texts.exo.5.14: And the officers of the children of Israel, whom Pharaoh's taskmasters had set over them, were beaten, [and] it was said, Why have ye not fulfilled your task in making brick, both yesterday and to-day, as heretofore?
texts.exo.5.15: Then the officers of the children of Israel came and cried to Pharaoh, saying, Why dost thou deal thus with thy bondmen?
texts.exo.5.16: There is no straw given to thy bondmen, and they say to us, Make brick; and behold, thy bondmen are beaten, but it is the fault of thy people.
texts.exo.5.17: And he said, Ye are idle, idle! therefore ye say, Let us go and sacrifice to Jehovah.
texts.exo.5.18: And now go -- work! and straw shall not be given you, and ye shall deliver the measure of bricks.
texts.exo.5.19: And the officers of the children of Israel saw [that] it stood ill with them, because it was said, Ye shall not diminish anything from your bricks, the daily work.
texts.exo.5.20: And they met Moses and Aaron, who stood there to meet them, as they came out from Pharaoh.
texts.exo.5.21: And they said to them, Jehovah look upon you and judge, that ye have made our odour to stink in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his bondmen, putting a sword into their hand to kill us!
texts.exo.5.22: And Moses returned to Jehovah, and said, Lord, why hast thou done evil to this people? why now hast thou sent me?
texts.exo.5.23: For ever since I came to Pharaoh to speak in thy name, he hath done evil to this people; neither hast thou delivered thy people at all!
texts.exo.6.1: And Jehovah said to Moses, Now shalt thou see what I will do to Pharaoh; for by a strong hand shall he let them go, and by a strong hand shall he drive them out of his land.
texts.exo.6.2: And God spoke to Moses, and said to him, I am Jehovah.
texts.exo.6.3: And I appeared unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, as the Almighty ùGod; but by my name Jehovah I was not made known to them.
texts.exo.6.4: And I established also my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their pilgrimage, in which they were sojourners.
texts.exo.6.5: And I have heard also the groaning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians have forced to serve, and I have remembered my covenant.
texts.exo.6.6: Therefore say unto the children of Israel, I am Jehovah, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will deliver you from their service, and I will redeem you with a stretched-out arm, and with great judgments.
texts.exo.6.7: And I will take you to me for a people, and will be your God; and ye shall know that I, Jehovah your God, am he who bringeth you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians.
texts.exo.6.8: And I will bring you into the land concerning which I swore to give it unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob; and I will give it you for a possession: I am Jehovah.
texts.exo.6.9: And Moses spoke thus to the children of Israel; but they did not listen to Moses from anguish of spirit, and from hard service.
texts.exo.6.10: And Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.exo.6.11: Go in, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.
texts.exo.6.12: And Moses spoke before Jehovah, saying, Lo, the children of Israel do not hearken to me: how then should Pharaoh hearken to me, to me of uncircumcised lips?
texts.exo.6.13: And Jehovah spoke to Moses and to Aaron, and gave them a commandment to the children of Israel, and to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.6.14: These are the heads of their fathers' houses: the sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: Enoch and Phallu, Hezron and Carmi: these are the families of Reuben.
texts.exo.6.15: -- And the sons of Simeon: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Saul the son of a Canaanitish woman: these are the families of Simeon.
texts.exo.6.16: And these are the names of the sons of Levi, according to their generations: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari. And the years of the life of Levi were a hundred and thirty-seven years.
texts.exo.6.17: The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, according to their families.
texts.exo.6.18: And the sons of Kohath: Amram, and Jizhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel. And the years of the life of Kohath were a hundred and thirty-three years.
texts.exo.6.19: And the sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi: these are the families of Levi according to their generations.
texts.exo.6.20: And Amram took Jochebed his aunt as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses. And the years of the life of Amram were a hundred and thirty-seven years.
texts.exo.6.21: And the sons of Jizhar: Korah, and Nepheg, and Zicri.
texts.exo.6.22: And the sons of Uzziel: Mishael, and Elzaphan, and Sithri.
texts.exo.6.23: And Aaron took Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Nahshon, as wife; and she bore him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
texts.exo.6.24: And the sons of Korah: Assir, and Elkanah, and Abiasaph: these are the families of the Korahites.
texts.exo.6.25: And Eleazar Aaron's son took [one] of the daughters of Putiel as wife; and she bore him Phinehas: these are the heads of the fathers of the Levites according to their families.
texts.exo.6.26: This is that Aaron and Moses, to whom Jehovah said, Bring out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt according to their hosts.
texts.exo.6.27: These are they who spoke to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring out the children of Israel from Egypt: this is that Moses and Aaron.
texts.exo.6.28: And it came to pass on the day when Jehovah spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
texts.exo.6.29: that Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying, I am Jehovah: speak thou unto Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I say unto thee.
texts.exo.6.30: And Moses said before Jehovah, Behold, I am of uncircumcised lips, and how will Pharaoh hearken unto me?
texts.exo.7.1: And Jehovah said to Moses, See, I have made thee God to Pharaoh; and Aaron thy brother shall be thy prophet.
texts.exo.7.2: Thou shalt speak all that I command thee; and Aaron thy brother shall speak unto Pharaoh, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.
texts.exo.7.3: And I will render Pharaoh's heart obdurate, and multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.7.4: And Pharaoh will not hearken unto you; and I will lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth my hosts, my people, the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.
texts.exo.7.5: And the Egyptians shall know that I am Jehovah, when I stretch forth my hand on Egypt, and bring out the children of Israel from among them.
texts.exo.7.6: And Moses and Aaron did as Jehovah had commanded them: so did they.
texts.exo.7.7: And Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron was eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.
texts.exo.7.8: And Jehovah spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
texts.exo.7.9: When Pharaoh shall speak to you, saying, Do a miracle for yourselves, -- then thou shalt say unto Aaron, Take thy staff and cast [it] before Pharaoh -- it will become a serpent.
texts.exo.7.10: And Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh, and did so, as Jehovah had commanded; and Aaron cast down his staff before Pharaoh, and before his bondmen, and it became a serpent.
texts.exo.7.11: And Pharaoh also called the sages and the sorcerers; and they too, the scribes of Egypt, did so with their enchantments:
texts.exo.7.12: they cast down every man his staff, and they became serpents; but Aaron's staff swallowed up their staves.
texts.exo.7.13: And Pharaoh's heart was stubborn, and he hearkened not to them, as Jehovah had said.
texts.exo.7.14: And Jehovah said to Moses, Pharaoh's heart is hardened: he refuseth to let the people go.
texts.exo.7.15: Go unto Pharaoh in the morning -- behold, he will go out unto the water -- and take thy stand by the bank of the river in front of him; and take in thy hand the staff that was turned into a serpent.
texts.exo.7.16: And say unto him, Jehovah the God of the Hebrews has sent me to thee, saying, Let my people go, that they may serve me in the wilderness; but behold, hitherto thou hast not hearkened.
texts.exo.7.17: Thus saith Jehovah: In this shalt thou know that I am Jehovah -- behold, I will smite with the staff that is in my hand upon the water which is in the river, and it shall be turned into blood.
texts.exo.7.18: And the fish that is in the river shall die; and the river shall stink; and the Egyptians shall loathe to drink the water out of the river.
texts.exo.7.19: And Jehovah said to Moses, Say unto Aaron, Take thy staff, and stretch out thy hand upon the waters of the Egyptians -- upon their streams, upon their rivers, and upon their ponds, and upon all their reservoirs of water, that they may become blood; and there shall be blood throughout the land of Egypt, both in [vessels of] wood and in [vessels of] stone.
texts.exo.7.20: And Moses and Aaron did so, as Jehovah had commanded; and he lifted up the staff, and smote the waters that were in the river before the eyes of Pharaoh, and before the eyes of his bondmen; and all the waters that were in the river were turned into blood.
texts.exo.7.21: And the fish that was in the river died; and the river stank, and the Egyptians could not drink the water of the river; and the blood was throughout the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.7.22: And the scribes of Egypt did so with their sorceries; and Pharaoh's heart was stubborn, neither did he hearken to them, as Jehovah had said.
texts.exo.7.23: And Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and took not this to heart either.
texts.exo.7.24: And all the Egyptians dug round about the river for water to drink; for they could not drink of the water of the river.
texts.exo.7.25: And seven days were fulfilled, after Jehovah had smitten the river.
texts.exo.8.1: And Jehovah said to Moses, Go unto Pharaoh, and say unto him, Thus saith Jehovah: Let my people go, that they may serve me.
texts.exo.8.2: And if thou refuse to let [them] go, behold, I will smite all thy borders with frogs.
texts.exo.8.3: And the river shall swarm with frogs, and they shall go up and come into thy house, and into thy bedroom, and upon thy bed, and into the house of thy bondmen, and upon thy people, and into thine ovens, and into thy kneading-troughs.
texts.exo.8.4: And the frogs shall come up both upon thee and upon thy people, and upon all thy bondmen.
texts.exo.8.5: And Jehovah said to Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy hand with thy staff over the streams, over the rivers, and over the ponds, and cause frogs to come up on the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.8.6: And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt; and the frogs came up, and covered the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.8.7: And the scribes did so with their sorceries, and brought up frogs on the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.8.8: And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron, and said, Intreat Jehovah, that he may take away the frogs from me and from my people; and I will let the people go, that they may sacrifice to Jehovah.
texts.exo.8.9: And Moses said to Pharaoh, Glory over me, for what time shall I intreat for thee, and for thy bondmen, and for thy people, to cut off the frogs from thee and from thy houses; [so that] they shall remain in the river only?
texts.exo.8.10: And he said, For to-morrow. And he said, Be it according to thy word; that thou mayest know that there is none like Jehovah our God.
texts.exo.8.11: And the frogs shall depart from thee, and from thy houses, and from thy bondmen, and from thy people: they shall remain in the river only.
texts.exo.8.12: And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh; and Moses cried to Jehovah because of the frogs that he had brought against Pharaoh.
texts.exo.8.13: And Jehovah did according to the word of Moses; and the frogs died out of the houses, out of the courts, and out of the fields.
texts.exo.8.14: And they gathered them in heaps; and the land stank.
texts.exo.8.15: And Pharaoh saw that there was respite; and he hardened his heart, and hearkened not to them, as Jehovah had said.
texts.exo.8.16: And Jehovah said to Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy staff, and smite the dust of the earth, and it shall become gnats throughout the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.8.17: And they did so; and Aaron stretched out his hand with his staff, and smote the dust of the earth, and there arose gnats on man and on beast: all the dust of the land became gnats throughout the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.8.18: And the scribes did so with their sorceries, to bring forth gnats; but they could not. And the gnats were on man and on beast.
texts.exo.8.19: Then the scribes said to Pharaoh, This is the finger of God! But Pharaoh's heart was stubborn, and he hearkened not to them, as Jehovah had said.
texts.exo.8.20: And Jehovah said to Moses, Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh -- behold, he will go out to the water -- and say to him, Thus saith Jehovah, Let my people go, that they may serve me.
texts.exo.8.21: For, if thou do not let my people go, behold, I will send dog-flies upon thee, and upon thy bondmen, and upon thy people, and into thy houses; and the houses of the Egyptians shall be full of dog-flies, and also the ground on which they are.
texts.exo.8.22: And I will distinguish in that day the land of Goshen, in which my people dwell, that no dog-flies shall be there; that thou mayest know that I Jehovah am in the midst of the land.
texts.exo.8.23: And I will put a separation between my people and thy people; to-morrow shall this sign be.
texts.exo.8.24: And Jehovah did so; and there came dog-flies in a multitude into the house of Pharaoh, and [into] the houses of his bondmen; and throughout the land of Egypt, the land was corrupted by the dog-flies.
texts.exo.8.25: And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron, and said, Go, sacrifice to your God in the land.
texts.exo.8.26: And Moses said, It is not proper to do so; for we should sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians to Jehovah our God: lo, if we sacrificed the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, would they not stone us?
texts.exo.8.27: We will go three days' journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice to Jehovah our God, as he shall command us.
texts.exo.8.28: And Pharaoh said, I will let you go, that you may sacrifice to Jehovah your God in the wilderness; only, go not very far away: intreat for me!
texts.exo.8.29: And Moses said, Behold, I go out from thee, and will intreat Jehovah; and the dog-flies will depart from Pharaoh, from his bondmen, and from his people, to-morrow; only let not Pharaoh deal deceitfully any more in not letting the people go to sacrifice to Jehovah.
texts.exo.8.30: And Moses went out from Pharaoh, and intreated Jehovah.
texts.exo.8.31: And Jehovah did according to the word of Moses; and he removed the dog-flies from Pharaoh, from his bondmen, and from his people; there remained not one.
texts.exo.8.32: And Pharaoh hardened his heart this time also, and would not let the people go.
texts.exo.9.1: And Jehovah said to Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh, and tell him, Thus saith Jehovah the God of the Hebrews: Let my people go, that they may serve me.
texts.exo.9.2: For if thou refuse to let them go, and shalt retain them still,
texts.exo.9.3: behold, the hand of Jehovah shall be on thy cattle which is in the field, on the horses, on the asses, on the camels, on the oxen and on the sheep, with a very grievous plague.
texts.exo.9.4: And Jehovah will distinguish between the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt; and there shall nothing die of all that the children of Israel have.
texts.exo.9.5: And Jehovah appointed a set time, saying, To-morrow will Jehovah do this thing in the land.
texts.exo.9.6: And Jehovah did this thing on the following day, and all the cattle of Egypt died; but of the cattle of the children of Israel died not one.
texts.exo.9.7: And Pharaoh sent, and behold, there was not one of the cattle of the Israelites dead. But the heart of Pharaoh was hardened, and he did not let the people go.
texts.exo.9.8: And Jehovah said to Moses and to Aaron, Take to yourselves handfuls of ashes of the furnace, and let Moses scatter it toward the heavens before the eyes of Pharaoh.
texts.exo.9.9: And it shall become fine dust over all the land of Egypt, and shall become boils on man and on cattle, breaking out [with] blisters, throughout the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.9.10: And they took ashes of the furnace, and stood before Pharaoh; and Moses sprinkled it toward the heavens; and it became boils [with] blisters breaking out on man and on cattle.
texts.exo.9.11: And the scribes could not stand before Moses because of the boils; for the boils were on the scribes, and on all the Egyptians.
texts.exo.9.12: And Jehovah made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, and he did not hearken to them, as Jehovah had told Moses.
texts.exo.9.13: And Jehovah said to Moses, Rise up early in the morning, and set thyself before Pharaoh, and say to him, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of the Hebrews: Let my people go, that they may serve me.
texts.exo.9.14: For I will at this time send all my plagues to thy heart, and on thy bondmen, and on thy people; that thou mayest know that there is none like me in all the earth.
texts.exo.9.15: For now shall I put forth my hand, and I will smite thee and thy people with pestilence; and thou shalt be cut off from the earth.
texts.exo.9.16: And for this very cause have I raised thee up, to shew thee my power; and that my name may be declared in all the earth.
texts.exo.9.17: Dost thou still exalt thyself against my people, that thou wilt not let them go?
texts.exo.9.18: Behold, to-morrow about this time I will cause it to rain a very grievous hail, such as hath not been in Egypt since its foundation until now.
texts.exo.9.19: And now send, [and] secure thy cattle, and all that thou hast in the field: all the men and the cattle that are found in the field, and are not brought home -- on them the hail shall come down, and they shall die.
texts.exo.9.20: He that feared the word of Jehovah among the bondmen of Pharaoh made his bondmen and his cattle flee into the houses.
texts.exo.9.21: But he that did not regard the word of Jehovah left his bondmen and his cattle in the field.
texts.exo.9.22: And Jehovah said to Moses, Stretch out thy hand toward the heavens, that there may be hail throughout the land of Egypt, upon men, and upon cattle, and upon every herb of the field in the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.9.23: And Moses stretched out his staff toward the heavens, and Jehovah gave thunder and hail; and the fire ran along the ground; and Jehovah rained hail on the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.9.24: And there was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous, such as there had been none like it in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.
texts.exo.9.25: And the hail smote throughout the land of Egypt all that was in the field, both men and cattle; and the hail smote every herb of the field, and broke every tree of the field.
texts.exo.9.26: Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, was there no hail.
texts.exo.9.27: And Pharaoh sent, and called Moses and Aaron, and said to them, I have sinned this time: Jehovah is the righteous [one], but I and my people are the wicked [ones].
texts.exo.9.28: Intreat Jehovah that it may be enough, that there be no more thunder of God and hail; and I will let you go, and ye shall stay no longer!
texts.exo.9.29: And Moses said to him, When I go out of the city, I will spread out my hands to Jehovah: the thunder will cease, and there will be no more hail; that thou mayest know that the earth is Jehovah's.
texts.exo.9.30: But as to thee and thy bondmen, I know that ye do not yet fear Jehovah Elohim.
texts.exo.9.31: And the flax and the barley were smitten; for the barley was in the ear, and the flax was bolled.
texts.exo.9.32: But the wheat and the spelt were not smitten; for they were not come out into ear.
texts.exo.9.33: And Moses went out of the city from Pharaoh, and spread out his hands to Jehovah; and the thunders and hail ceased, and the rain was not [any more] poured on the earth.
texts.exo.9.34: And Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunders had ceased, and he sinned yet more, and hardened his heart, he, and his bondmen.
texts.exo.9.35: And the heart of Pharaoh was stubborn, neither would he let the children of Israel go, as Jehovah had spoken by Moses.
texts.exo.10.1: And Jehovah said to Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh; for I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his bondmen, that I might do these my signs in their midst,
texts.exo.10.2: and that thou mightest tell in the ears of thy son and thy son's son what I have wrought in Egypt, and my signs which I have done among them; and ye shall know that I am Jehovah.
texts.exo.10.3: And Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh, and said to him, Thus saith Jehovah the God of the Hebrews: How long dost thou refuse to humble thyself before me? let my people go, that they may serve me.
texts.exo.10.4: For, if thou refuse to let my people go, behold, I will to-morrow bring locusts into thy borders;
texts.exo.10.5: and they shall cover the face of the land, so that ye will not be able to see the land; and they shall eat the residue of that which is escaped, which ye have remaining from the hail, and shall eat every tree which ye have growing in the field;
texts.exo.10.6: and they shall fill thy houses, and the houses of all thy bondmen, and the houses of all the Egyptians; which neither thy fathers nor thy fathers' fathers have seen, since the day that they were upon the earth unto this day. And he turned and went out from Pharaoh.
texts.exo.10.7: And Pharaoh's bondmen said to him, How long shall this man be a snare to us? let the men go, that they may serve Jehovah their God: dost thou not yet know that Egypt is ruined?
texts.exo.10.8: And Moses and Aaron were brought again to Pharaoh. And he said to them, Go, serve Jehovah your God. Who are they that shall go?
texts.exo.10.9: And Moses said, We will go with our young and with our old, with our sons and with our daughters; with our flocks and with our herds will we go; for we have a feast of Jehovah.
texts.exo.10.10: And he said to them, Let Jehovah be so with you, as I let you go, and your little ones: see that evil is before you!
texts.exo.10.11: Not so: go now, ye [that are] men, and serve Jehovah! for it is that ye have desired. And they were driven out from Pharaoh's presence.
texts.exo.10.12: And Jehovah said to Moses, Stretch out thy hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come up over the land of Egypt, and eat every herb of the land -- all that the hail hath left.
texts.exo.10.13: And Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and Jehovah brought an east wind on the land all that day and all that night. When it was morning, the east wind brought the locusts.
texts.exo.10.14: And the locusts went up over all the land of Egypt, and rested in all the borders of Egypt, very grievous; before them there were no such locusts as they, neither after them will be such.
texts.exo.10.15: And they covered the face of the whole land, so that the land was darkened; and they ate every herb of the land, and all the fruit of the trees that the hail had left; and there remained not any green thing on the trees, and in the herbs of the field, throughout the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.10.16: And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron in haste; and he said, I have sinned against Jehovah your God, and against you.
texts.exo.10.17: And now, forgive, I pray you, my sin only this time, and intreat Jehovah your God that he may take away from me this death only!
texts.exo.10.18: And he went out from Pharaoh, and intreated Jehovah.
texts.exo.10.19: And Jehovah turned a very powerful west wind, which took away the locusts, and drove them into the Red Sea: there remained not one locust in all the borders of Egypt.
texts.exo.10.20: And Jehovah made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, and he did not let the children of Israel go.
texts.exo.10.21: And Jehovah said to Moses, Stretch out thy hand toward the heavens, that there may be darkness in the land of Egypt -- so that one may feel darkness.
texts.exo.10.22: And Moses stretched out his hand toward the heavens; and there was a thick darkness throughout the land of Egypt three days:
texts.exo.10.23: they saw not one another, neither rose any from his place, for three days. But all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.
texts.exo.10.24: And Pharaoh called Moses and said, Go, serve Jehovah; only, let your flocks and your herds remain; let your little ones also go with you.
texts.exo.10.25: And Moses said, Thou must give also sacrifices and burnt-offerings into our hands, that we may sacrifice to Jehovah our God.
texts.exo.10.26: Our cattle also must go with us: there shall not a hoof be left behind; for we must take thereof to serve Jehovah our God; and we do not know with what we must serve Jehovah, until we come there.
texts.exo.10.27: But Jehovah made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, and he would not let them go.
texts.exo.10.28: And Pharaoh said to him, Get thee from me, take heed to thyself, see my face no more; for in the day thou seest my face thou shalt die.
texts.exo.10.29: And Moses said, Thou hast spoken rightly: I will see thy face again no more!
texts.exo.11.1: And Jehovah said to Moses, Yet one plague will I bring upon Pharaoh, and upon Egypt; afterwards he will let you go hence: when he shall let [you] go altogether, he shall utterly drive you out hence.
