texts.exo.11.2: Speak now in the ears of the people, that they ask every man of his neighbour, and every woman of her neighbour, utensils of silver and utensils of gold.
texts.exo.11.3: And Jehovah gave the people favour in the eyes of the Egyptians. Moreover the man Moses was very great in the land of Egypt -- in the eyes of Pharaoh's bondmen, and in the eyes of the people.
texts.exo.11.4: And Moses said, Thus saith Jehovah: About midnight I will go out into the midst of Egypt.
texts.exo.11.5: And all the firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sitteth on his throne, even unto the firstborn of the bondwoman that is behind the mill; and all the firstborn of cattle.
texts.exo.11.6: And there shall be a great cry throughout the land of Egypt, such as there hath been none like it, nor shall be like it any more.
texts.exo.11.7: But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast; that ye may know that Jehovah distinguisheth between the Egyptians and Israel.
texts.exo.11.8: And all these thy bondmen shall come down unto me, and bow down to me, saying, Go out, thou, and all the people that follow thee; and after that I will go out. And he went out from Pharaoh in a glowing anger.
texts.exo.11.9: And Jehovah had said to Moses, Pharaoh shall not hearken to you; that my wonders may be multiplied in the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.11.10: And Moses and Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh; but Jehovah made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, and he did not let the children of Israel go out of his land.
texts.exo.12.1: And Jehovah spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
texts.exo.12.2: This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.
texts.exo.12.3: Speak unto all the assembly of Israel, saying, On the tenth of this month let them take themselves each a lamb, for a father's house, a lamb for a house.
texts.exo.12.4: And if the household be too small for a lamb, let him and his neighbour next unto his house take [it] according to the number of the souls; each according to [the measure] of his eating shall ye count for the lamb.
texts.exo.12.5: Your lamb shall be without blemish, a yearling male; ye shall take [it] from the sheep, or from the goats.
texts.exo.12.6: And ye shall keep it until the fourteenth day of this month; and the whole congregation of the assembly of Israel shall kill it between the two evenings.
texts.exo.12.7: And they shall take of the blood, and put [it] on the two door-posts and on the lintel of the houses in which they eat it.
texts.exo.12.8: And they shall eat the flesh in that night, roast with fire, and unleavened bread; with bitter [herbs] shall they eat it.
texts.exo.12.9: Ye shall eat none of it raw, nor boiled at all with water, but roast with fire; its head with its legs and with its in-wards.
texts.exo.12.10: And ye shall let none of it remain until the morning; and what remaineth of it until the morning ye shall burn with fire.
texts.exo.12.11: And thus shall ye eat it: your loins shall be girded, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and ye shall eat it in haste; it is Jehovah's passover.
texts.exo.12.12: And I will go through the land of Egypt in that night, and smite all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I am Jehovah.
texts.exo.12.13: And the blood shall be for you as a sign on the houses in which ye are; and when I see the blood, I will pass over you; and the plague shall not be among you for destruction, when I smite the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.12.14: And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall celebrate it [as] a feast to Jehovah; throughout your generations [as] an ordinance for ever shall ye celebrate it.
texts.exo.12.15: Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread: on the very first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses; for whoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day -- that soul shall be cut off from Israel.
texts.exo.12.16: And on the first day ye shall have a holy convocation, and on the seventh day a holy convocation: no manner of work shall be done on them, save what is eaten by every person -- that only shall be done by you.
texts.exo.12.17: And ye shall keep the [feast of] unleavened [bread]; for in this same day have I brought your hosts out of the land of Egypt; and ye shall keep this day in your generations [as] an ordinance for ever.
texts.exo.12.18: In the first [month], on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, ye shall eat unleavened bread until the one and twentieth day of the month in the evening.
texts.exo.12.19: Seven days shall there be no leaven found in your houses; for whoever eateth what is leavened -- that soul shall be cut off from the assembly of Israel, whether he be a sojourner, or born in the land.
texts.exo.12.20: Ye shall eat nothing leavened: in all your dwellings shall ye eat unleavened bread.
texts.exo.12.21: And Moses called all the elders of Israel, and said to them, Seize and take yourselves lambs for your families, and kill the passover.
texts.exo.12.22: And take a bunch of hyssop, and dip [it] in the blood that is in the bason, and smear the lintel and the two door-posts with the blood that is in the bason; and none of you shall go out of the door of his house until the morning.
texts.exo.12.23: And Jehovah will pass through to smite the Egyptians; and when he sees the blood on the lintel, and on the two door-posts, Jehovah will pass over the door, and will not suffer the destroyer to come into your houses to smite [you].
texts.exo.12.24: And ye shall observe this as an ordinance for thee and for thy sons for ever.
texts.exo.12.25: And it shall come to pass, when ye are come into the land that Jehovah will give you, as he has promised, that ye shall keep this service.
texts.exo.12.26: And it shall come to pass, when your children shall say to you, What mean ye by this service?
texts.exo.12.27: that ye shall say, It is a sacrifice of passover to Jehovah, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt when he smote the Egyptians and delivered our houses. And the people bowed their heads and worshipped.
texts.exo.12.28: And the children of Israel went away, and did as Jehovah had commanded Moses and Aaron; so did they.
texts.exo.12.29: And it came to pass that at midnight Jehovah smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne to the firstborn of the captive that was in the dungeon, and all the firstborn of cattle.
texts.exo.12.30: And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his bondmen, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house in which there was not one dead.
texts.exo.12.31: And he called Moses and Aaron in the night, and said, Rise up, go away from among my people, both ye and the children of Israel; and go, serve Jehovah, as ye have said.
texts.exo.12.32: Also take your flocks and your herds, as ye have said, and go; and bless me also.
texts.exo.12.33: And the Egyptians urged the people, to send them out of the land in haste; for they said, We are all dead [men]!
texts.exo.12.34: And the people took their dough before it was leavened; their kneading-troughs bound up in their clothes upon their shoulders.
texts.exo.12.35: And the children of Israel had done according to the word of Moses, and they had asked of the Egyptians utensils of silver, and utensils of gold, and clothing.
texts.exo.12.36: And Jehovah had given the people favour in the eyes of the Egyptians, and they gave to them; and they spoiled the Egyptians.
texts.exo.12.37: And the children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot [that were] men, besides children.
texts.exo.12.38: And a mixed multitude went up also with them; and flocks and herds -- very much cattle.
texts.exo.12.39: And they baked the dough that they brought forth out of Egypt into unleavened cakes, for it was not leavened; for they were driven out of Egypt, and could not wait; neither had they prepared for themselves any food.
texts.exo.12.40: And the residence of the children of Israel that they resided in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years.
texts.exo.12.41: And it came to pass at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, on that same day it came to pass that all the hosts of Jehovah went out from the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.12.42: It is a night of observance to Jehovah, because of their being brought out from the land of Egypt: that same night is an observance to Jehovah for all the children of Israel in their generations.
texts.exo.12.43: And Jehovah said to Moses and Aaron, This is the ordinance of the passover: No stranger shall eat of it;
texts.exo.12.44: but every man's bondman that is bought for money -- let him be circumcised: then shall he eat it.
texts.exo.12.45: A settler and a hired servant shall not eat it.
texts.exo.12.46: In one house shall it be eaten; thou shalt not carry forth any of the flesh abroad out of the house; neither shall ye break a bone thereof.
texts.exo.12.47: All the assembly of Israel shall hold it.
texts.exo.12.48: And when a sojourner sojourneth with thee, and would hold the passover to Jehovah, let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near and hold it; and he shall be as one that is born in the land; but no uncircumcised person shall eat thereof.
texts.exo.12.49: One law shall be for him that is home-born and for the sojourner that sojourneth among you.
texts.exo.12.50: And all the children of Israel did as Jehovah had commanded Moses and Aaron; so did they.
texts.exo.12.51: And it came to pass on that same day, [that] Jehovah brought the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt according to their hosts.
texts.exo.13.1: And Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.exo.13.2: Hallow unto me every firstborn, whatever breaketh open the womb among the children of Israel, of man and of cattle: it is mine.
texts.exo.13.3: And Moses said to the people, Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for with a powerful hand hath Jehovah brought you out from this; and nothing leavened shall be eaten.
texts.exo.13.4: Ye come out to-day, in the month Abib.
texts.exo.13.5: And it shall be when Jehovah hath brought thee into the land of the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Amorite and the Hivite and the Jebusite, which he swore to thy fathers to give thee, a land flowing with milk and honey, that thou shalt keep this service in this month.
texts.exo.13.6: Seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread; and in the seventh day is a feast to Jehovah.
texts.exo.13.7: Unleavened bread shall be eaten the seven days; and leavened bread shall not be seen with thee, neither shall there be leaven seen with thee in all thy borders.
texts.exo.13.8: And thou shalt inform thy son in that day, saying, It is because of what Jehovah did to me when I came out of Egypt.
texts.exo.13.9: And it shall be for a sign to thee on thy hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes, that the law of Jehovah may be in thy mouth; for with a powerful hand hath Jehovah brought thee out of Egypt.
texts.exo.13.10: And thou shalt keep this ordinance at its set time from year to year.
texts.exo.13.11: And it shall be when Jehovah hath brought thee into the land of the Canaanites, as he hath sworn to thee and to thy fathers, and hath given it thee,
texts.exo.13.12: that thou shalt offer unto Jehovah all that breaketh open the womb, and every firstling that cometh of cattle which is thine: the males [shall be] Jehovah's.
texts.exo.13.13: And every firstling of an ass shalt thou ransom with a lamb; and if thou do not ransom it, thou shalt break its neck; and every firstborn of a man among thy sons shalt thou ransom.
texts.exo.13.14: And it shall be when thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What is this? that thou shalt say to him, With a powerful hand Jehovah brought us out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
texts.exo.13.15: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, that Jehovah slew all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both the firstborn of men and the firstborn of cattle: therefore I sacrifice to Jehovah all that breaketh open the womb -- being males; and every firstborn of my children I ransom.
texts.exo.13.16: And it shall be for a sign on thy hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes, for with a powerful hand Jehovah brought us forth out of Egypt.
texts.exo.13.17: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh let the people go, that God did not lead them the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, That the people may not repent when they see conflict, and return to Egypt.
texts.exo.13.18: And God led the people about, the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea; and the children of Israel went arrayed out of the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.13.19: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him; for he had made the children of Israel swear an oath, saying, God will be sure to visit you; then ye shall carry my bones with you hence.
texts.exo.13.20: And they took their journey from Succoth, and encamped in Etham, at the end of the wilderness.
texts.exo.13.21: And Jehovah went before their face by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them [in] the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; so that they could go day and night.
texts.exo.13.22: The pillar of the cloud did not remove [from] before the people by day, nor the pillar of fire by night.
texts.exo.14.1: And Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.exo.14.2: Speak unto the children of Israel, that they turn and encamp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea: before Baal-Zephon, opposite to it, shall ye encamp by the sea.
texts.exo.14.3: And Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel, They are entangled in the land, the wilderness has hemmed them in.
texts.exo.14.4: And I will harden Pharaoh's heart, that he may pursue after them; and I will glorify myself in Pharaoh, and in all his host; and the Egyptians shall know that I am Jehovah. And they did so.
texts.exo.14.5: And it was told the king of Egypt that the people had fled; and the heart of Pharaoh and of his bondmen was turned against the people, and they said, Why have we done this, that we have let Israel go from our service?
texts.exo.14.6: And he yoked his chariot, and took his people with him.
texts.exo.14.7: And he took six hundred chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Egypt, and captains over every one of them.
texts.exo.14.8: And Jehovah hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued after the children of Israel; and the children of Israel had gone out with a high hand.
texts.exo.14.9: And the Egyptians pursued after them, -- all the horses and chariots of Pharaoh, and his horsemen, and his army, and overtook them where they had encamped by the sea, beside Pi-hahiroth, opposite to Baal-Zephon.
texts.exo.14.10: And Pharaoh approached; and the children of Israel lifted up their eyes, and behold, the Egyptians marched after them; and the children of Israel were much afraid, and cried out to Jehovah.
texts.exo.14.11: And they said to Moses, Is it because there were no graves in Egypt, thou hast taken us away to die in the wilderness? why hast thou done this to us, that thou hast led us out of Egypt?
texts.exo.14.12: Is not this what we told thee in Egypt, when we said, Let us alone, and we will serve the Egyptians? For [it had been] better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.
texts.exo.14.13: And Moses said to the people, Fear not: stand still, and see the salvation of Jehovah, which he will work for you to-day; for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to-day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.
texts.exo.14.14: Jehovah will fight for you, and ye shall be still.
texts.exo.14.15: And Jehovah said to Moses, Why dost thou cry unto me? Speak unto the children of Israel, that they go forward.
texts.exo.14.16: And thou, lift thy staff, and stretch out thy hand over the sea, and divide it; and the children of Israel shall go on dry [ground] through the midst of the sea.
texts.exo.14.17: And I, behold, I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians, and they shall pursue after them; and I will glorify myself in Pharaoh and in all his host, in his chariots and in his horsemen.
texts.exo.14.18: And the Egyptians shall know that I am Jehovah, when I have glorified myself in Pharaoh, in his chariots and in his horsemen.
texts.exo.14.19: And the Angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, removed and went behind them; and the pillar of the cloud went from before them, and stood behind them.
texts.exo.14.20: And it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel; and was a cloud and darkness, and lit up the night; and the one did not come near the other all the night.
texts.exo.14.21: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and Jehovah made the sea go [back] by a strong east wind all the night, and made the sea dry [land], and the waters were divided.
texts.exo.14.22: And the children of Israel went through the midst of the sea on the dry [ground]; and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.
texts.exo.14.23: And the Egyptians pursued and came after them -- all Pharaoh's horses, his chariots and his horsemen, into the midst of the sea.
texts.exo.14.24: And it came to pass in the morning watch, that Jehovah looked upon the camp of the Egyptians, in the pillar of fire and of the cloud, and embarrassed the camp of the Egyptians.
texts.exo.14.25: And he took off their chariot wheels, and caused them to drive with difficulty; and the Egyptians said, Let us flee before Israel, for Jehovah is fighting for them against the Egyptians!
texts.exo.14.26: And Jehovah said to Moses, Stretch out thy hand over the sea, that the waters may return upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots and upon their horsemen.
texts.exo.14.27: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to its strength toward the morning; and the Egyptians fled against it; and Jehovah overturned the Egyptians into the midst of the sea.
texts.exo.14.28: And the waters returned, and covered the chariots and the horsemen of all the host of Pharaoh that had come into the sea after them; there remained not even one of them.
texts.exo.14.29: And the children of Israel walked on dry [ground] through the midst of the sea; and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.
texts.exo.14.30: Thus Jehovah saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians; and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the sea-shore.
texts.exo.14.31: And Israel saw the great power [with] which Jehovah had wrought against the Egyptians; and the people feared Jehovah, and believed in Jehovah, and in Moses his bondman.
texts.exo.15.1: Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song to Jehovah, and spoke, saying, I will sing unto Jehovah, for he is highly exalted: The horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.
texts.exo.15.2: My strength and song is Jah, and he is become my salvation: This is my ùGod, and I will glorify him; My father's God, and I will extol him.
texts.exo.15.3: Jehovah is a man of war; Jehovah, his name.
texts.exo.15.4: Pharaoh's chariots and his army hath he cast into the sea; His chosen captains also are drowned in the Red Sea.
texts.exo.15.5: The depths covered them; they sank to the bottom as a stone.
texts.exo.15.6: Thy right hand, Jehovah, is become glorious in power: Thy right hand, Jehovah, hath dashed in pieces the enemy.
texts.exo.15.7: And by the greatness of thine excellency thou hast overthrown thine adversaries: Thou sentest forth thy burning wrath, it consumed them as stubble.
texts.exo.15.8: And by the breath of thy nostrils the waters were heaped up; The streams stood as a mound; The depths were congealed in the heart of the sea.
texts.exo.15.9: The enemy said, I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoil; my soul shall be sated upon them; I will unsheath my sword, my hand shall dispossess them.
texts.exo.15.10: Thou didst blow with thy breath, the sea covered them; They sank as lead in the mighty waters.
texts.exo.15.11: Who is like unto thee, Jehovah, among the gods? Who is like unto thee, glorifying thyself in holiness, Fearful [in] praises, doing wonders?
texts.exo.15.12: Thou stretchedst out thy right hand, the earth swallowed them.
texts.exo.15.13: Thou by thy mercy hast led forth the people that thou hast redeemed; Thou hast guided them by thy strength unto the abode of thy holiness.
texts.exo.15.14: The peoples heard it, they were afraid: A thrill seized the inhabitants of Philistia.
texts.exo.15.15: Then the princes of Edom were amazed; The mighty men of Moab, trembling hath seized them; All the inhabitants of Canaan melted away.
texts.exo.15.16: Fear and dread fall upon them; By the greatness of thine arm they are still as a stone; Till thy people pass over, Jehovah, Till the people pass over that thou hast purchased.
texts.exo.15.17: Thou shalt bring them in, and plant them in the mountain of thine inheritance, The place that thou, Jehovah, hast made thy dwelling, The Sanctuary, Lord, that thy hands have prepared.
texts.exo.15.18: Jehovah shall reign for ever and ever!
texts.exo.15.19: For the horse of Pharaoh, with his chariots and with his horsemen, came into the sea, and Jehovah brought again the waters of the sea upon them; and the children of Israel went on dry [ground] through the midst of the sea.
texts.exo.15.20: And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took the tambour in her hand, and all the women went out after her with tambours and with dances.
texts.exo.15.21: And Miriam answered them, Sing to Jehovah, for he is highly exalted: The horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.
texts.exo.15.22: And Moses brought Israel from the Red Sea, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water.
texts.exo.15.23: And they came to Marah, and could not drink the waters of Marah, for they were bitter; therefore the name of it was called Marah.
texts.exo.15.24: And the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink?
texts.exo.15.25: And he cried to Jehovah; and Jehovah shewed him wood, and he cast it into the waters, and the waters became sweet. There he made for them a statute and an ordinance; and there he tested them.
texts.exo.15.26: And he said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of Jehovah thy God, and do what is right in his eyes, and incline thine ears to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of the complaints upon thee that I have put upon the Egyptians; for I am Jehovah who healeth thee.
texts.exo.15.27: And they came to Elim; and twelve springs of water were there, and seventy palm trees; and they encamped there by the waters.
texts.exo.16.1: And they journeyed from Elim, and the whole assembly of the children of Israel came into the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their departure out of the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.16.2: And the whole assembly of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron in the wilderness.
texts.exo.16.3: And the children of Israel said to them, Would that we had died by the hand of Jehovah in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh-pots, when we ate bread to the full; for ye have brought us out into this wilderness, to kill this whole congregation with hunger!
texts.exo.16.4: Then said Jehovah to Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather the daily need on its day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or not.
texts.exo.16.5: And it shall come to pass on the sixth day, that they shall prepare what they have brought in; and it shall be twice as much as they shall gather daily.
texts.exo.16.6: And Moses and Aaron said to all the children of Israel, In the evening, then shall ye know that Jehovah has brought you out from the land of Egypt;
texts.exo.16.7: and in the morning, then shall ye see the glory of Jehovah; for he has heard your murmurings against Jehovah; -- and what are we, that ye murmur against us?
texts.exo.16.8: And Moses said, When Jehovah gives you in the evening flesh to eat, and in the morning bread to the full; for Jehovah hears your murmurings which ye murmur against him ... and what [are] we? your murmurings are not against us, but against Jehovah.
texts.exo.16.9: And Moses spoke to Aaron, Say to all the assembly of the children of Israel, Come near into the presence of Jehovah; for he has heard your murmurings.
texts.exo.16.10: And it came to pass, when Aaron spoke to the whole assembly of the children of Israel, that they turned toward the wilderness, and behold, the glory of Jehovah appeared in the cloud.
texts.exo.16.11: And Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.exo.16.12: I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel: speak to them, saying, Between the two evenings ye shall eat flesh, and in the morning ye shall be filled with bread; and ye shall know that I am Jehovah your God.
texts.exo.16.13: And it came to pass in the evening, that quails came up, and covered the camp; and in the morning the dew lay round the camp.
texts.exo.16.14: And when the dew that lay [round it] was gone up, behold, on the face of the wilderness there was [something] fine, granular, fine as hoar-frost, on the ground.
texts.exo.16.15: And the children of Israel saw [it], and said one to another, What is it? for they did not know what it was. And Moses said to them, This is the bread which Jehovah has given you to eat.
texts.exo.16.16: This is the thing which Jehovah has commanded: Gather of it every man according to what he can eat, an omer a poll, [according to] the number of your persons: ye shall take every man for those that are in his tent.
texts.exo.16.17: And the children of Israel did so, and gathered, some much, some little.
texts.exo.16.18: And they measured with the omer: then he that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little wanted nothing: they had gathered every man according to the measure of his eating.
texts.exo.16.19: And Moses said to them, Let no man leave [any] of it until the morning.
texts.exo.16.20: But they did not hearken to Moses; and some men left of it until the morning; then worms bred in it and it stank. And Moses was wroth with them.
texts.exo.16.21: And they gathered it every morning, every man as much as he could eat; and when the sun became hot, it melted.
texts.exo.16.22: And it came to pass on the sixth day, that they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for one; and all the princes of the assembly came and told Moses.
texts.exo.16.23: And he said to them, This is what Jehovah has said: To-morrow is the rest, the holy sabbath, of Jehovah: bake what ye will bake, and cook what ye will cook; and lay up for yourselves all that remains over, to be kept for the morning.
texts.exo.16.24: And they laid it up for the morning, as Moses had commanded; and it did not stink, neither was there any worm in it.
texts.exo.16.25: And Moses said, Eat it to-day; for to-day is sabbath to Jehovah: to-day ye shall not find it in the field.
texts.exo.16.26: Six days shall ye gather it; but on the seventh day is sabbath: on it there shall be none.
texts.exo.16.27: And it came to pass on the seventh day that there went out [some] from the people to gather [it], and they found none.
texts.exo.16.28: And Jehovah said to Moses, How long do ye refuse to keep my commandments and my laws?
texts.exo.16.29: See, for Jehovah hath given you the sabbath; therefore he giveth you on the sixth day the bread for two days. Abide every man in his place: let no man go from his place on the seventh day.
texts.exo.16.30: And the people rested on the seventh day.
texts.exo.16.31: And the house of Israel called its name Manna; and it was like coriander-seed, white; and the taste of it was like cake with honey.
texts.exo.16.32: And Moses said, This is the thing which Jehovah has commanded: Fill an omer of it to be kept for your generations; that they may see the bread that I gave you to eat in the wilderness, when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.16.33: And Moses said to Aaron, Take a pot, and put in it an omer full of manna, and deposit it before Jehovah, to be kept for your generations.
texts.exo.16.34: As Jehovah had commanded Moses, so Aaron deposited it before the Testimony, to be kept.
texts.exo.16.35: And the children of Israel ate the manna forty years, until they came into an inhabited land: they ate the manna until they came to the borders of the land of Canaan.
texts.exo.16.36: Now an omer is the tenth [part] of an ephah.
texts.exo.17.1: And all the assembly of the children of Israel journeyed from the wilderness of Sin, according to their journeys, at the command of Jehovah; and they encamped in Rephidim; and there was no water for the people to drink.
texts.exo.17.2: And the people contended with Moses, and said, Give us water, that we may drink! And Moses said to them, Why do ye dispute with me? Why do ye tempt Jehovah?
texts.exo.17.3: And the people thirsted there for water; and the people murmured against Moses, and said, Why is it that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst?
texts.exo.17.4: And Moses cried to Jehovah, saying, What shall I do with this people? Yet a little, and they will stone me!
texts.exo.17.5: And Jehovah said to Moses, Go on before the people, and take with thee of the elders of Israel, and thy staff with which thou didst smite the river, take in thy hand, and go.
texts.exo.17.6: Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock on Horeb; and thou shalt strike the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink. And Moses did so before the eyes of the elders of Israel.
texts.exo.17.7: And he called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the contention of the children of Israel, and because they had tempted Jehovah, saying, Is Jehovah among us, or not?
texts.exo.17.8: And Amalek came and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
texts.exo.17.9: And Moses said to Joshua, Choose us men, and go out, fight with Amalek; to-morrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand.
texts.exo.17.10: And Joshua did as Moses had said to him, to fight with Amalek; and Moses, Aaron and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
texts.exo.17.11: And it came to pass when Moses raised his hand, that Israel prevailed; and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.
texts.exo.17.12: And Moses' hands were heavy; then they took a stone, and put [it] under him, and he sat on it; and Aaron and Hur supported his hands, one on this side, and one on that side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.
texts.exo.17.13: And Joshua broke the power of Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
texts.exo.17.14: And Jehovah said to Moses, Write this [for] a memorial in the book, and rehearse [it] in the ears of Joshua, that I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens.
texts.exo.17.15: And Moses built an altar, and called the name of it Jehovah-nissi.
texts.exo.17.16: And he said, For the hand is on the throne of Jah; Jehovah will have war with Amalek from generation to generation!
texts.exo.18.1: And Jethro the priest of Midian, Moses' father-in-law, heard of all that God had done to Moses, and to Israel his people; that Jehovah had brought Israel out of Egypt.
texts.exo.18.2: And Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, took Zipporah, Moses' wife, after he had sent her back,
texts.exo.18.3: and her two sons, of whom the name of the one was Gershom -- for he said, I have been a sojourner in a foreign land,
texts.exo.18.4: -- and the name of the other, Eliezer -- For the God of my father has been my help, and has delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.
texts.exo.18.5: And Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came to Moses with his sons and his wife into the wilderness, where he encamped at the mountain of God.
texts.exo.18.6: And he sent word to Moses: I, thy father-in-law Jethro, am come to thee, and thy wife, and her two sons with her.
texts.exo.18.7: And Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, and did obeisance, and kissed him; and they asked each other [after] their welfare, and went into the tent.
texts.exo.18.8: And Moses told his father-in-law all that Jehovah had done to Pharaoh and to the Egyptians for Israel's sake; all the trouble that had befallen them on the way, and [how] Jehovah had delivered them.
texts.exo.18.9: And Jethro rejoiced for all the goodness that Jehovah had done to Israel; that he had delivered them out of the hand of the Egyptians.
texts.exo.18.10: And Jethro said, Blessed be Jehovah, who has delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh; who has delivered the people from under the hand of the Egyptians.
texts.exo.18.11: Now I know that Jehovah is greater than all gods; for in the thing in which they acted haughtily [he was] above them.
texts.exo.18.12: And Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, took a burnt-offering and sacrifices for God; and Aaron came, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with Moses' father-in-law in the presence of God.
texts.exo.18.13: And it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses sat to judge the people; and the people stood by Moses from the morning to the evening.
texts.exo.18.14: And Moses' father-in-law saw all that he did with the people, and said, What is this thing which thou art doing with the people? why dost thou sit alone, and all the people are standing by thee from morning to evening?
texts.exo.18.15: And Moses said to his father-in-law, Because the people come to me to enquire of God.
texts.exo.18.16: When they have a matter, they come to me, and I judge between one and another; and I make known [to them] the statutes of God, and his laws.
texts.exo.18.17: And Moses' father-in-law said to him, The thing that thou art doing is not good.
texts.exo.18.18: Thou wilt be quite exhausted, both thou and this people that is with thee; for the thing is too heavy for thee: thou canst not perform it alone.
texts.exo.18.19: Hearken now to my voice: I will give thee counsel, and God shall be with thee. Be thou for the people with God, and bring the matters before God;
texts.exo.18.20: and teach them the statutes and the laws, and make known to them the way in which they must walk, and the work that they must do.
texts.exo.18.21: But do thou provide among all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness; and place [them] over them, chiefs of thousands, chiefs of hundreds, chiefs of fifties, and chiefs of tens,
texts.exo.18.22: that they may judge the people at all times; and it shall be [that] they shall bring to thee every great matter, and that they shall judge every small matter, and they shall lighten [the task] on thee, and they shall bear [it] with thee.
texts.exo.18.23: If thou do this thing, and God command thee [so], thou wilt be able to endure, and all this people shall also go to their place in peace.
texts.exo.18.24: And Moses hearkened to the voice of his father-in-law, and did all that he had said.
texts.exo.18.25: And Moses chose able men out of all Israel, and made them heads over the people, chiefs of thousands, chiefs of hundreds, chiefs of fifties, and chiefs of tens.
texts.exo.18.26: And they judged the people at all times: the hard matters they brought to Moses, but every small matter they judged.
texts.exo.18.27: And Moses sent away his father-in-law, and he departed into his land.
texts.exo.19.1: In the third month after the departure of the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt, the same day came they [into] the wilderness of Sinai:
texts.exo.19.2: they departed from Rephidim, and came [into] the wilderness of Sinai, and encamped in the wilderness; and Israel encamped there before the mountain.
texts.exo.19.3: And Moses went up to God, and Jehovah called to him out of the mountain, saying, Thus shalt thou say to the house of Jacob, and tell the children of Israel:
texts.exo.19.4: Ye have seen what I have done to the Egyptians, and [how] I have borne you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself.
texts.exo.19.5: And now, if ye will hearken to my voice indeed and keep my covenant, then shall ye be my own possession out of all the peoples -- for all the earth is mine --
texts.exo.19.6: and ye shall be to me a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak to the children of Israel.
texts.exo.19.7: And Moses came and called the elders of the people, and laid before the mall these words which Jehovah had commanded him.
texts.exo.19.8: And all the people answered together, and said, All that Jehovah has spoken will we do! And Moses brought the words of the people back to Jehovah.
texts.exo.19.9: And Jehovah said to Moses, Lo, I will come to thee in the cloud's thick darkness, that the people may hear when I speak with thee, and believe thee also for ever. And Moses told the words of the people to Jehovah.
texts.exo.19.10: And Jehovah said to Moses, Go to the people, and hallow them to-day and to-morrow, and let them wash their clothes;
texts.exo.19.11: and let them be ready for the third day; for on the third day Jehovah will come down before the eyes of all the people on mount Sinai.
texts.exo.19.12: And set bounds round about the people, saying, Take heed to yourselves, [not] to go up unto the mountain nor touch the border of it: whatever toucheth the mountain shall certainly be put to death:
texts.exo.19.13: not a hand shall touch it, but it shall certainly be stoned, or shot through; whether it be a beast or a man, it shall not live. When the long drawn note of the trumpet soundeth, they shall come up to the mountain.
texts.exo.19.14: And Moses came down from the mountain to the people, and hallowed the people; and they washed their clothes.
texts.exo.19.15: And he said to the people, Be ready for the third day; do not come near [your] wives.
texts.exo.19.16: And it came to pass on the third day, when it was morning, that there were thunders and lightnings and a heavy cloud on the mountain, and the sound of the trumpet exceeding loud; and the whole people that was in the camp trembled.
texts.exo.19.17: And Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet with God; and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
texts.exo.19.18: And the whole of mount Sinai smoked, because Jehovah descended on it in fire; and its smoke ascended as the smoke of a furnace; and the whole mountain shook greatly.
texts.exo.19.19: And the sound of the trumpet increased and became exceeding loud; Moses spoke, and God answered him by a voice.
texts.exo.19.20: And Jehovah came down on mount Sinai, on the top of the mountain; and Jehovah called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
texts.exo.19.21: And Jehovah said to Moses, Go down, testify to the people that they break not through to Jehovah to gaze, and many of them perish.
texts.exo.19.22: And the priests also, who come near to Jehovah, shall hallow themselves, lest Jehovah break forth on them.
texts.exo.19.23: And Moses said to Jehovah, The people cannot come up to mount Sinai; for thou hast testified to us, saying, Set bounds about the mountain, and hallow it.
texts.exo.19.24: And Jehovah said to him, Go, descend, and thou shalt come up, thou, and Aaron with thee; but the priests and the people shall not break through to go up to Jehovah, lest he break forth on them.
texts.exo.19.25: So Moses went down to the people, and told them.
texts.exo.20.1: And God spoke all these words, saying,
texts.exo.20.2: I am Jehovah thy God, who have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
texts.exo.20.3: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
texts.exo.20.4: Thou shalt not make thyself any graven image, or any form of what is in the heavens above, or what is in the earth beneath, or what is in the waters under the earth:
texts.exo.20.5: thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them; for I, Jehovah thy God, am a jealous ùGod, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the sons to the third and to the fourth [generation] of them that hate me,
texts.exo.20.6: and shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me and keep my commandments.
texts.exo.20.7: Thou shalt not idly utter the name of Jehovah thy God; for Jehovah will not hold him guiltless that idly uttereth his name.
texts.exo.20.8: Remember the sabbath day to hallow it.
texts.exo.20.9: Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work;
texts.exo.20.10: but the seventh day is the sabbath of Jehovah thy God: thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy bondman, nor thy handmaid, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates.
texts.exo.20.11: For in six days Jehovah made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested on the seventh day; therefore Jehovah blessed the sabbath day, and hallowed it.
texts.exo.20.12: Honour thy father and thy mother, that thy days may be prolonged in the land that Jehovah thy God giveth thee.
texts.exo.20.16: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.
texts.exo.20.17: Thou shalt not desire thy neighbour's house, thou shalt not desire thy neighbour's wife, nor his bondman, nor his handmaid, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor anything that is thy neighbour's.
texts.exo.20.18: And all the people saw the thunderings, and the flames, and the sound of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking; and when the people saw [it], they trembled, and stood afar off,
texts.exo.20.19: and said to Moses, Speak thou with us, and we will hear; but let not God speak with us, lest we die.
texts.exo.20.20: And Moses said to the people, Fear not; for God is come to prove you, and that his fear may be before you, that ye sin not.
texts.exo.20.21: And the people stood afar off, and Moses drew near to the obscurity where God was.
texts.exo.20.22: And Jehovah said to Moses, Thus shalt thou say to the children of Israel: Ye have seen that I have spoken with you from the heavens.
texts.exo.20.23: Ye shall not make beside me gods of silver, and ye shall not make to you gods of gold.
texts.exo.20.24: An altar of earth shalt thou make unto me, and shalt sacrifice on it thy burnt-offerings, and thy peace-offerings, thy sheep and thine oxen: in all places where I shall make my name to be remembered, I will come unto thee, and bless thee.
texts.exo.20.25: And if thou make me an altar of stone, thou shalt not build it of hewn stone; for if thou lift up thy sharp tool upon it, thou hast profaned it.
texts.exo.20.26: Neither shalt thou go up by steps unto mine altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon.
texts.exo.21.1: And these are the judgments which thou shalt set before them.
texts.exo.21.2: If thou buy a Hebrew bondman, six years shall he serve; and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.
texts.exo.21.3: If he came in alone, he shall go out alone: if he had a wife, then his wife shall go out with him.
texts.exo.21.4: If his master have given him a wife, and she have borne him sons or daughters, the wife and her children shall be her master's, and he shall go out alone.
texts.exo.21.5: But if the bondman shall say distinctly, I love my master, my wife, and my children, I will not go free;
texts.exo.21.6: then his master shall bring him before the judges, and shall bring him to the door, or to the door-post; and his master shall bore his ear through with an awl; and he shall be his bondman for ever.
texts.exo.21.7: And if a man shall sell his daughter as a handmaid, she shall not go out as the bondmen go out.
texts.exo.21.8: If she is unacceptable in the eyes of her master, who had taken her for himself, then shall he let her be ransomed: to sell her unto a foreign people he hath no power, after having dealt unfaithfully with her.
texts.exo.21.9: And if he have appointed her unto his son, he shall deal with her after the law of daughters.
texts.exo.21.10: If he take himself another, her food, her clothing, and her conjugal rights he shall not diminish.
texts.exo.21.11: And if he do not these three things unto her, then shall she go out free without money.
texts.exo.21.12: He that striketh a man, so that he die, shall certainly be put to death.
texts.exo.21.13: But if he have not lain in wait, and God have delivered [him] into his hand, I will appoint thee a place to which he shall flee.
texts.exo.21.14: But if a man act wantonly toward his neighbour, and slay him with guile, thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die.
texts.exo.21.15: And he that striketh his father, or his mother, shall certainly be put to death.
texts.exo.21.16: And he that stealeth a man, and selleth him, or if he be found in his hand, he shall certainly be put to death.
texts.exo.21.17: And he that curseth his father, or his mother, shall certainly be put to death.
texts.exo.21.18: And if men dispute, and one strike the other with a stone, or with the fist, and he die not, but take to [his] bed,
texts.exo.21.19: -- if he rise, and walk abroad upon his staff, then shall he that struck [him] be guiltless; only he shall pay [for] the loss of his time, and shall cause [him] to be thoroughly healed.
texts.exo.21.20: And if a man strike his bondman or his handmaid with a staff, and he die under his hand, he shall certainly be avenged.
texts.exo.21.21: Only, if he continue [to live] a day or two days, he shall not be avenged; for he is his money.
texts.exo.21.22: And if men strive together, and strike a woman with child, so that she be delivered, and no mischief happen, he shall in any case be fined, according as the woman's husband shall impose on him, and shall give it as the judges estimate.
texts.exo.21.23: But if mischief happen, then thou shalt give life for life,
texts.exo.21.24: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
texts.exo.21.25: branding for branding, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.
texts.exo.21.26: And if a man strike the eye of his bondman or the eye of his handmaid, and it be marred, he shall let him go for his eye.
texts.exo.21.27: And if he knock out his bondman's tooth or his handmaid's tooth, he shall let him go free for his tooth.
texts.exo.21.28: And if an ox gore a man or a woman, so that they die, then the ox shall certainly be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the ox shall be guiltless.
texts.exo.21.29: But if the ox have gored heretofore, and it have been testified to its owner, and he have not kept it in, and it kill a man or a woman, -- the ox shall be stoned, and its owner also shall be put to death.
texts.exo.21.30: If there be imposed on him a satisfaction, then he shall give the ransom of his life, according to what is imposed on him.
texts.exo.21.31: Whether it gore a son or gore a daughter, according to this judgment shall it be done to him.
texts.exo.21.32: If the ox gore a bondman or a handmaid, he shall give to their master thirty shekels of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.
texts.exo.21.33: -- And if a man open a pit, or if a man dig a pit, and do not cover it, and an ox or an ass fall into it,
texts.exo.21.34: the owner of the pit shall make it good, shall give money to the owner of them; and the dead [ox] shall be his.
texts.exo.21.35: -- And if one man's ox gore his neighbour's ox, and it die, then they shall sell the live ox, and divide the money thereof, and divide the dead also.
texts.exo.21.36: Or if it be known that the ox have gored heretofore, and its owner have not kept him in, he shall in any case restore ox for ox; and the dead shall be his.
texts.exo.22.1: If a man steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it, he shall restore five oxen for the ox, and four sheep for the sheep.
texts.exo.22.2: If the thief be encountered breaking in, and be smitten so that he die, there shall be no blood-guiltiness for him.
texts.exo.22.3: If the sun be risen on him, there shall be blood-guiltiness for him; he should have made full restitution: if he had nothing, he would have been sold for his theft.
texts.exo.22.4: If the stolen thing be actually found alive in his hand, whether it be ox, or ass, or sheep, he shall restore double.
texts.exo.22.5: If a man shall cause a field or vineyard to be eaten, and put in his cattle, and pasture in another man's field, of the best of his own field, and of the best of his own vineyard shall he make [it] good.
texts.exo.22.6: -- If fire break out, and seize the thorns, and the stacks of corn, or the standing corn, or the field be consumed, he that kindled the fire shall fully make it good.
texts.exo.22.7: -- If a man deliver unto his neighbour money or stuff to keep, and it be stolen out of the man's house; if the thief be found, let him restore double;
texts.exo.22.8: if the thief be not found, the master of the house shall be brought before the judges, [to see] if he has not put his hand unto his neighbour's goods.
texts.exo.22.9: As to all manner of fraud, -- as to ox, as to ass, as to sheep, as to clothing, as to everything lost, of which [a man] saith, It is this -- the cause of both parties shall come before the judges: he whom the judges shall condemn shall restore double to his neighbour.
texts.exo.22.10: If a man deliver unto his neighbour an ass, or an ox, or a sheep, or any cattle, to keep, and it die, or be hurt, or driven away, and no man see [it],
texts.exo.22.11: an oath of Jehovah shall be between them both, that he hath not put his hand unto his neighbour's goods; and the owner of it shall accept it, and he shall not make [it] good.
texts.exo.22.12: But if it have been stolen from him, he shall make [it] good unto its owner.
texts.exo.22.13: If it have been torn in pieces, let him bring it [as] witness: he shall not make good what was torn.
texts.exo.22.14: -- And if a man borrow anything of his neighbour, and it be hurt, or die, its owner not being with it, he shall fully make it good;
texts.exo.22.15: if the owner thereof be with it, he shall not make [it] good; if it be a hired [thing], it came for its hire.
texts.exo.22.16: And if a man seduce a virgin that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall certainly endow her, to be his wife.
texts.exo.22.17: If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall weigh money according to the dowry of virgins.
texts.exo.22.18: -- Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.
texts.exo.22.19: -- Every one that lieth with a beast shall certainly be put to death.
texts.exo.22.20: -- He that sacrificeth to [any] god, save to Jehovah only, shall be devoted to destruction.
texts.exo.22.21: Thou shalt neither vex a stranger, nor oppress him; for ye have been strangers in the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.22.22: Ye shall not afflict any widow or fatherless child.
texts.exo.22.23: If thou afflict him in any way, if he cry at all unto me, I will certainly hear his cry;
texts.exo.22.24: and my anger shall burn, and I will slay you with the sword; and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.
texts.exo.22.25: -- If thou lend money to my people, the poor with thee, thou shalt not be to him as a usurer: ye shall charge him no interest.
texts.exo.22.26: -- If thou at all take thy neighbour's garment in pledge, thou shalt return it to him before the sun goes down;
texts.exo.22.27: for that is his only covering, his garment for his skin: on what shall he lie down? And it shall come to pass, when he crieth unto me, that I will hear; for I am gracious.
texts.exo.22.28: Thou shalt not revile the judges, nor curse a prince amongst thy people.
texts.exo.22.29: -- Thou shalt not delay the fulness of thy [threshing-floor] and the outflow of thy [winepress]. The firstborn of thy sons shalt thou give unto me.
texts.exo.22.30: Likewise shalt thou do with thy calf, with thy sheep: seven days shall it be with its dam; on the eighth day thou shalt give it me.
texts.exo.22.31: -- And ye shall be holy men unto me; and ye shall not eat flesh torn in the field: ye shall cast it to the dog.
texts.exo.23.1: Thou shalt not accept a false report; extend not thy hand to the wicked, to be an unrighteous witness.
texts.exo.23.2: Thou shalt not follow the multitude for evil; neither shalt thou answer in a cause, to go after the multitude to pervert [judgment].
texts.exo.23.3: Neither shalt thou favour a poor man in his cause.
texts.exo.23.4: -- If thou meet thine enemy's ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt certainly bring it back to him.
texts.exo.23.5: If thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under its burden, beware of leaving [it] to him: thou shalt certainly loosen [it] with him.
texts.exo.23.6: Thou shalt not pervert the judgment of thy poor in his cause.
texts.exo.23.7: Thou shalt keep far from the cause of falsehood; and the innocent and righteous slay not; for I will not justify the wicked.
texts.exo.23.8: And thou shalt take no bribe; for the bribe blindeth those whose eyes are open, and perverteth the words of the righteous.
texts.exo.23.9: And the stranger thou shalt not oppress; for ye know the spirit of the stranger, for ye have been strangers in the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.23.10: And six years thou shalt sow thy land, and gather in its produce;
texts.exo.23.11: but in the seventh thou shalt let it rest and lie [fallow], that the poor of thy people may eat [of it]; and what they leave, the beasts of the field shall eat. In like manner thou shalt deal with thy vineyard, and with thine olive-tree.
texts.exo.23.12: -- Six days thou shalt do thy work, but on the seventh day thou shalt rest; that thine ox and thine ass may rest, and the son of thy handmaid, and the stranger may be refreshed.
texts.exo.23.13: And ye shall be on your guard as to everything that I have said unto you; and shall make no mention of the name of other gods -- it shall not be heard in thy mouth.
texts.exo.23.14: Thrice in the year thou shalt celebrate a feast to me.
texts.exo.23.15: Thou shalt keep the feast of unleavened bread, (thou shalt eat unleavened bread seven days, as I have commanded thee, in the time appointed of the month Abib; for in it thou camest out from Egypt; and none shall appear in my presence empty;)
texts.exo.23.16: and the feast of harvest, the first-fruits of thy labours which thou hast sown in the field, and the feast of in-gathering, at the end of the year, when thou gatherest in thy labours out of the field.
texts.exo.23.17: Three times in the year all thy males shall appear in the presence of the Lord Jehovah.
texts.exo.23.18: Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread; neither shall the fat of my feast remain all night until the morning.
texts.exo.23.19: The first of the first-fruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of Jehovah thy God. Thou shalt not boil a kid in its mother's milk.
texts.exo.23.20: Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee to the place that I have prepared.
texts.exo.23.21: Be careful in his presence, and hearken unto his voice: do not provoke him, for he will not forgive your transgressions; for my name is in him.
texts.exo.23.22: But if thou shalt diligently hearken unto his voice, and do all that I shall say, then I will be an enemy to thine enemies, and an adversary to thine adversaries.
texts.exo.23.23: For mine Angel shall go before thee, and bring thee in unto the Amorites and the Hittites and the Perizzites and the Canaanites, the Hivites and the Jebusites; and I will cut them off.
texts.exo.23.24: Thou shalt not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor do after their deeds; but thou shalt utterly destroy them, and utterly shatter their statues.
texts.exo.23.25: And ye shall serve Jehovah your God; and he shall bless thy bread and thy water; and I will take sickness away from thy midst.
texts.exo.23.26: There shall nothing cast their young, nor be barren, in thy land; the number of thy days will I fulfil.
texts.exo.23.27: I will send my fear before thee, and confound every people to which thou comest, and will make all thine enemies turn their back to thee.
texts.exo.23.28: And I will send hornets before thee, which shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee.
texts.exo.23.29: I will not drive them out from before thee in one year: lest the land become desolate, and the beast of the field multiply against thee.
texts.exo.23.30: By little and little I will drive them out from before thee, until thou art fruitful, and possess the land.
texts.exo.23.31: And I will set thy bounds from the Red Sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness unto the river; for I will give the inhabitants of the land into your hand, that thou mayest dispossess them from before thee.
texts.exo.23.32: Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods.
texts.exo.23.33: They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me; for if thou serve their gods, it is sure to be a snare unto thee.
texts.exo.24.1: And he said to Moses, Go up to Jehovah, thou and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel; and worship afar off.
texts.exo.24.2: And let Moses alone come near Jehovah; but they shall not come near; neither shall the people go up with him.
texts.exo.24.3: And Moses came and told the people all the words of Jehovah, and all the judgments; and all the people answered with one voice, and said, All the words that Jehovah has said will we do!
texts.exo.24.4: And Moses wrote all the words of Jehovah, and rose up early in the morning, and built an altar under the mountain, and twelve pillars, according to the twelve tribes of Israel.
texts.exo.24.5: And he sent the youths of the children of Israel, and they offered up burnt-offerings, and sacrificed sacrifices of peace-offering of bullocks to Jehovah.
texts.exo.24.6: And Moses took half the blood, and put [it] in basons; and half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar.
texts.exo.24.7: And he took the book of the covenant, and read [it] in the ears of the people; and they said, All that Jehovah has said will we do, and obey!
texts.exo.24.8: And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled [it] on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant that Jehovah has made with you concerning all these words.
texts.exo.24.9: And Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel went up;
texts.exo.24.10: and they saw the God of Israel; and there was under his feet as it were work of transparent sapphire, and as it were the form of heaven for clearness.
texts.exo.24.11: And on the nobles of the children of Israel he laid not his hand: they saw God, and ate and drank.
texts.exo.24.12: And Jehovah said to Moses, Come up to me into the mountain, and be there; and I will give thee the tables of stone, and the law, and the commandment that I have written, for their instruction.
texts.exo.24.13: And Moses rose up, and Joshua his attendant; and Moses went up to the mountain of God.
texts.exo.24.14: And he said to the elders, Wait here for us, until we return to you; and behold, Aaron and Hur are with you: if any man have any matter, let him come before them.
texts.exo.24.15: And Moses went up to the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
texts.exo.24.16: And the glory of Jehovah abode on mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days; and on the seventh day he called to Moses out of the midst of the cloud.
texts.exo.24.17: And the appearance of the glory of Jehovah was like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain, before the eyes of the children of Israel.
texts.exo.24.18: And Moses went into the midst of the cloud, and ascended the mountain. And Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
texts.exo.25.1: And Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.exo.25.2: Speak unto the children of Israel, that they bring me a heave-offering: of every one whose heart prompteth him, ye shall take my heave-offering.
texts.exo.25.3: And this is the heave-offering that ye shall take of them: gold, and silver, and copper,
texts.exo.25.4: and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and byssus, and goats' [hair],
texts.exo.25.5: and rams' skins dyed red, and badgers' skins; and acacia-wood;
texts.exo.25.6: oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil, and for the incense of fragrant drugs;
texts.exo.25.7: onyx stones, and stones to be set in the ephod, and in the breastplate.
texts.exo.25.8: And they shall make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them.
texts.exo.25.9: According to all that I shall shew thee, the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all the utensils thereof, even so shall ye make [it].
texts.exo.25.10: And they shall make an ark of acacia-wood; two cubits and a half the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof.
texts.exo.25.11: And thou shalt overlay it with pure gold: inside and outside shalt thou overlay it; and shalt make upon it a border of gold round about.
texts.exo.25.12: And cast four rings of gold for it, and put [them] at the four corners thereof, that two rings may be upon the one side thereof and two rings upon the other side thereof.
texts.exo.25.13: And make staves of acacia-wood and overlay them with gold.
texts.exo.25.14: And put the staves into the rings upon the sides of the ark, that the ark may be borne with them.
texts.exo.25.15: The staves shall be in the rings of the ark: they shall not come out from it.
texts.exo.25.16: And thou shalt put into the ark the testimony that I shall give thee.
texts.exo.25.17: And thou shalt make a mercy-seat of pure gold: two cubits and a half the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof.
texts.exo.25.18: And thou shalt make two cherubim of gold; [of] beaten work shalt thou make them, at the two ends of the mercy-seat.
texts.exo.25.19: And make one cherub at the end of the one side, and one cherub at the end of the other side; out of the mercy-seat shall ye make the cherubim at the two ends thereof.
texts.exo.25.20: And the cherubim shall stretch out [their] wings over it, covering over with their wings the mercy-seat, and their faces opposite to one another: toward the mercy-seat shall the faces of the cherubim be [turned].
texts.exo.25.21: And thou shalt put the mercy-seat above on the ark, and shalt put in the ark the testimony that I shall give thee.
texts.exo.25.22: And there will I meet with thee, and will speak with thee from above the mercy-seat, from between the two cherubim which are upon the ark of the testimony, everything that I will give thee in commandment unto the children of Israel.
texts.exo.25.23: And thou shalt make a table of acacia-wood, two cubits the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof.
texts.exo.25.24: And thou shalt overlay it with pure gold, and make upon it a border of gold round about.
texts.exo.25.25: And thou shalt make for it a margin of a handbreadth round about, and shalt make a border of gold for the margin thereof round about.
texts.exo.25.26: And thou shalt make for it four rings of gold, and put the rings at the four corners that are on the four feet thereof.
texts.exo.25.27: Close to the margin shall the rings be, as receptacles of the staves to carry the table.
texts.exo.25.28: And thou shalt make the staves of acacia-wood, and overlay them with gold; and the table shall be carried upon them.
texts.exo.25.29: And thou shalt make the dishes thereof, and cups thereof, and goblets thereof, and bowls thereof, with which to pour out: of pure gold shalt thou make them.
texts.exo.25.30: And thou shalt set upon the table shewbread before me continually.
texts.exo.25.31: And thou shalt make a lamp-stand of pure gold; [of] beaten work shall the lamp-stand be made: its base and its shaft, its cups, its knobs, and its flowers shall be of the same.
texts.exo.25.32: And six branches shall come out of the sides thereof -- three branches of the lamp-stand out of one side thereof, and three branches of the lamp-stand out of the other side thereof;
texts.exo.25.33: three cups shaped like almonds in the one branch, a knob and a flower: and three cups shaped like almonds in the other branch, a knob and a flower: so in the six branches that come out of the lamp-stand.
texts.exo.25.34: And in the lamp-stand four cups shaped like almonds, its knobs and its flowers;
texts.exo.25.35: and a knob under two branches of it, and [again] a knob under two branches of it, and [again] a knob under two branches of it, for the six branches that proceed out of the lamp-stand.
texts.exo.25.36: Their knobs and their branches shall be of itself -- all of one beaten work of pure gold.
texts.exo.25.37: And thou shalt make the seven lamps thereof, and they shall light the lamps thereof, that they may shine out before it;
texts.exo.25.38: and the snuffers thereof, and the snuff-trays thereof, of pure gold.
texts.exo.25.39: Of a talent of pure gold shall they make it, with all these utensils.
texts.exo.25.40: And see that thou make [them] according to their pattern, which hath been shewn to thee in the mountain.
texts.exo.26.1: And thou shalt make the tabernacle [with] ten curtains of twined byssus, and blue, and purple, and scarlet: with cherubim of artistic work shalt thou make them.
texts.exo.26.2: The length of one curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits, and the breadth of one curtain four cubits -- one measure for all the curtains.
texts.exo.26.3: Five of the curtains shall be coupled one to another, and [the other] five curtains coupled one to another.
texts.exo.26.4: And thou shalt make loops of blue on the edge of the one curtain at the end of the coupling; and likewise shalt thou make [them] in the edge of the outermost curtain in the other coupling.
texts.exo.26.5: Fifty loops shalt thou make in the one curtain, and fifty loops shalt thou make at the end of the curtain in the other coupling: the loops shall be opposite to one another.
texts.exo.26.6: And thou shalt make fifty clasps of gold, and couple the curtains together with the clasps, that the tabernacle may be one [whole].
texts.exo.26.7: And thou shalt make curtains of goats' [hair] for a tent over the tabernacle: eleven curtains shalt thou make them.
texts.exo.26.8: The length of one curtain shall be thirty cubits, and the breadth of one curtain four cubits -- one measure for the eleven curtains.
texts.exo.26.9: And thou shalt couple five of the curtains by themselves, and six of the curtains by themselves, and shalt double the sixth curtain in the front of the tent.
texts.exo.26.10: And thou shalt make fifty loops on the edge of the outermost curtain of the coupling, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain in the other coupling.
texts.exo.26.11: And thou shalt make fifty clasps of copper, and put the clasps into the loops, and couple the tent, that it may be one [whole].
texts.exo.26.12: And that which remaineth hanging over of the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that remaineth, shall hang over the rear of the tabernacle.
texts.exo.26.13: And the cubit on the one side, and the cubit on the other side of that which remaineth in the length of the curtains of the tent, shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle on this side and on that side, to cover it.
texts.exo.26.14: And thou shalt make a covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and a covering of badgers' skins over [that].
texts.exo.26.15: And the boards for the tabernacle thou shalt make of acacia-wood, standing up;
texts.exo.26.16: ten cubits the length of the board, and a cubit and a half the breadth of one board.
texts.exo.26.17: One board shall have two tenons, connected one with the other: thus shalt thou make for all the boards of the tabernacle.
texts.exo.26.18: And thou shalt make the boards for the tabernacle, twenty boards on the south side southward.
texts.exo.26.19: And thou shalt make forty bases of silver under the twenty boards; two bases under one board for its two tenons, and two bases under another board for its two tenons.
texts.exo.26.20: And for the other side of the tabernacle on the north side there shall be twenty boards.
texts.exo.26.21: And their forty bases of silver; two bases under one board, and two bases under another board.
texts.exo.26.22: And for the rear of the tabernacle westward thou shalt make six boards.
texts.exo.26.23: And two boards shalt thou make for the corners of the tabernacle at the rear;
texts.exo.26.24: and they shall be joined beneath, and together shall be united at the top thereof to one ring: thus shall it be for them both; they shall be for the two corners.
texts.exo.26.25: And there shall be eight boards, and their bases, of silver, sixteen bases; two bases under one board, and two bases under another board.
texts.exo.26.26: And thou shalt make bars of acacia-wood; five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
texts.exo.26.27: and five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the side of the tabernacle at the rear westward;
texts.exo.26.28: and the middle bar in the midst of the boards reaching from one end to the other.
texts.exo.26.29: And thou shalt overlay the boards with gold, and make [of] gold their rings, the receptacles of the bars, and shalt overlay the bars with gold.
texts.exo.26.30: And thou shalt set up the tabernacle according to its fashion, as hath been shewn thee on the mountain.
texts.exo.26.31: And thou shalt make a veil of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and twined byssus; of artistic work shall it be made, with cherubim.
texts.exo.26.32: And thou shalt attach it to four pillars of acacia-wood overlaid with gold, their hooks of gold; they shall be on four bases of silver.
texts.exo.26.33: And thou shalt bring the veil under the clasps, and bring in thither, inside the veil, the ark of the testimony; and the curtain shall make a division to you between the holy [place] and the holiest of all.
texts.exo.26.34: And thou shalt put the mercy-seat on the ark of the testimony in the holiest of all.
texts.exo.26.35: And thou shalt set the table outside the veil, and the lamp-stand opposite to the table on the side of the tabernacle southward; and thou shalt put the table on the north side.
texts.exo.26.36: And thou shalt make for the entrance of the tent a curtain of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and twined byssus, of embroidery.
texts.exo.26.37: And thou shalt make for the curtain five pillars of acacia[-wood], and overlay them with gold; their hooks shall be of gold; and thou shalt cast five bases of copper for them.
texts.exo.27.1: And thou shalt make the altar of acacia-wood, five cubits the length, and five cubits the breadth; the altar shall be square; and the height thereof three cubits.
texts.exo.27.2: And thou shalt make its horns at the four corners thereof; its horns shall be of itself; and thou shalt overlay it with copper.
texts.exo.27.3: And thou shalt make its pots to cleanse it of the fat, its shovels, and its bowls, and its forks, and its firepans; for all the utensils thereof thou shalt employ copper.
texts.exo.27.4: And thou shalt make for it a grating of network of copper; and on the net shalt thou make four copper rings at its four corners;
texts.exo.27.5: and thou shalt put it under the ledge of the altar beneath, and the net shall be to the very middle of the altar.
texts.exo.27.6: And thou shalt make staves for the altar, staves of acacia-wood, and overlay them with copper.
texts.exo.27.7: And its staves shall be put into the rings, that the staves may be on both sides of the altar, when it is carried.
texts.exo.27.8: Hollow with boards shalt thou make it: as it hath been shewn thee on the mountain, so shall they make [it].
texts.exo.27.9: And thou shalt make the court of the tabernacle. On the south side, southward, hangings for the court of twined byssus; a hundred cubits the length for the one side,
texts.exo.27.10: and the twenty pillars thereof, and their twenty bases of copper, the hooks of the pillars and their connecting-rods of silver.
texts.exo.27.11: And likewise on the north side in length, hangings a hundred [cubits] long, and its twenty pillars, and their twenty bases of copper; the hooks of the pillars and their connecting-rods of silver.
texts.exo.27.12: -- And the breadth of the court on the west side, hangings of fifty cubits; their pillars ten, and their bases ten.
texts.exo.27.13: -- And the breadth of the court on the east side, eastward, fifty cubits;
texts.exo.27.14: the hangings on the one wing, of fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their bases three.
texts.exo.27.15: And on the other wing hangings of fifteen [cubits]; their pillars three, and their bases three.
texts.exo.27.16: -- And for the gate of the court a curtain of twenty cubits, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and twined byssus, embroidered with needlework; their pillars four, and their bases four.
texts.exo.27.17: All the pillars of the court round about shall be fastened together with [rods of] silver; their hooks of silver, and their bases of copper.
texts.exo.27.18: The length of the court shall be a hundred cubits, and the breadth fifty everywhere, and the height five cubits of twined byssus; and their bases of copper.
texts.exo.27.19: All the utensils of the tabernacle for the service thereof and all the pegs thereof, and all the pegs of the court shall be of copper.
texts.exo.27.20: And thou shalt command the children of Israel, that they bring thee olive oil, pure, beaten, for the light, to light the lamp continually.
texts.exo.27.21: In the tent of meeting outside the veil, which is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall dress them from evening to morning before Jehovah: [it is] an everlasting statute, for their generations, on the part of the children of Israel.
texts.exo.28.1: And thou shalt take thee Aaron thy brother, and his sons with him, from among the children of Israel, that he may serve me as priest -- Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's sons.
texts.exo.28.2: And thou shalt make holy garments for Aaron thy brother, for glory and for ornament.
texts.exo.28.3: And thou shalt speak with all [that are] wise-hearted, whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom, that they may make Aaron's garments to hallow him, that he may serve me as priest.
texts.exo.28.4: And these are the garments which they shall make: a breastplate, and an ephod, and a cloak, and a checkered vest, a turban, and a girdle; and they shall make holy garments for Aaron thy brother, and his sons, that he may serve me as priest.
texts.exo.28.5: And they shall take gold, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and twined byssus,
texts.exo.28.6: and shall make the ephod of gold, blue, and purple, scarlet and twined byssus, of artistic work.
texts.exo.28.7: It shall have two shoulder-pieces joined at the two ends thereof, where it is joined together.
texts.exo.28.8: And the girdle of the ephod, which is upon it, shall be of the same, according to its work of gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet and twined byssus.
texts.exo.28.9: And thou shalt take two onyx stones, and engrave on them the names of the children of Israel:
texts.exo.28.10: six of their names on the one stone, and the six names of the rest on the other stone, according to their birth.
texts.exo.28.11: According to the work of an engraver in stone, as the engravings of a seal, shalt thou engrave the two stones with the names of the sons of Israel; surrounded by enclosures of gold shalt thou make them.
texts.exo.28.12: And thou shalt put the two stones upon the shoulder-pieces of the ephod [as] stones of memorial for the children of Israel; and Aaron shall bear their names before Jehovah upon his two shoulders for a memorial.
texts.exo.28.13: And thou shalt make enclosures of gold;
texts.exo.28.14: and two chains of pure gold; of laced work shalt thou make them, of wreathen work, and fasten the wreathen chains to the enclosures.
texts.exo.28.15: And thou shalt make the breastplate of judgment of artistic work, like the work of the ephod thou shalt make it; of gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and twined byssus shalt thou make it.
texts.exo.28.16: Square shall it be, doubled; a span the length thereof, and a span the breadth thereof.
texts.exo.28.17: And thou shalt set in it settings of stones -- four rows of stones: [one] row, a sardoin, a topaz, and an emerald -- the first row;
texts.exo.28.18: and the second row, a carbuncle, a sapphire, and a diamond;
texts.exo.28.19: and the third row, an opal, an agate, and an amethyst;
texts.exo.28.20: and the fourth row, a chrysolite, and an onyx, and a jasper; enclosed in gold shall they be in their settings.
texts.exo.28.21: And the stones shall be according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names, engraved as a seal: every one according to his name shall they be for the twelve tribes.
texts.exo.28.22: And thou shalt make on the breastplate chains of laced work, of wreathen work, of pure gold.
texts.exo.28.23: And thou shalt make on the breastplate two rings of gold, and shalt put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate.
texts.exo.28.24: And thou shalt put the two wreathen [cords] of gold in the two rings on the ends of the breastplate;
texts.exo.28.25: and the two ends of the two wreathen [cords] thou shalt fasten to the two enclosures, and shalt put [them] on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod, on the front thereof.
texts.exo.28.26: And thou shalt make two rings of gold, and shalt put them on the two ends of the breastplate, on the border thereof, which faceth the ephod inwards.
texts.exo.28.27: And two rings of gold shalt thou make, and shalt put them upon the two shoulder-pieces of the ephod underneath, to the front thereof just by the coupling thereof, above the girdle of the ephod.
texts.exo.28.28: And they shall bind the breastplate with its rings to the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, that it may be above the girdle of the ephod, and that the breastplate be not loosed from the ephod.
texts.exo.28.29: And Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastplate of judgment on his heart, when he goes in to the sanctuary, for a memorial before Jehovah continually.
texts.exo.28.30: And thou shalt put into the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim, that they may be upon Aaron's heart when he goeth in before Jehovah; and Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart before Jehovah continually.
texts.exo.28.31: And thou shalt make the cloak of the ephod all of blue.
texts.exo.28.32: And its opening for the head shall be in the midst thereof; there shall be a binding of woven work at its opening round about; as the opening of a coat of mail, it shall be in it -- it shall not rend.
texts.exo.28.33: And on the skirts thereof thou shalt make pomegranates of blue, and purple, and scarlet, round about the skirts thereof; and bells of gold between them round about:
texts.exo.28.34: a golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate, in the skirts of the cloak round about.
texts.exo.28.35: And it shall be on Aaron for service; that his sound may be heard when he goeth into the sanctuary before Jehovah, and when he cometh out, that he may not die.
texts.exo.28.36: And thou shalt make a thin plate of pure gold, and engrave on it, as the engravings of a seal, Holiness to Jehovah!
