texts.exo.5.6: And Pharaoh commandeth, on that day, the exactors among the people and its authorities, saying,
texts.exo.5.7: `Ye do not add to give straw to the people for the making of the bricks, as heretofore -- they go and have gathered straw for themselves;
texts.exo.5.8: and the proper quantity of the bricks which they are making heretofore ye do put on them, ye do not diminish from it, for they are remiss, therefore they are crying, saying, Let us go, let us sacrifice to our God;
texts.exo.5.9: let the service be heavy on the men, and let them work at it, and not be dazzled by lying words.'
texts.exo.5.10: And the exactors of the people, and its authorities, go out, and speak unto the people, saying, `Thus said Pharaoh, I do not give you straw,
texts.exo.5.11: ye -- go ye, take for yourselves straw where ye find [it], for there is nothing of your service diminished.'
texts.exo.5.12: And the people is scattered over all the land of Egypt, to gather stubble for straw,
texts.exo.5.13: and the exactors are making haste, saying, `Complete your works, the matter of a day in its day, as when there is straw.'
texts.exo.5.14: And the authorities of the sons of Israel, whom the exactors of Pharaoh have placed over them, are beaten, saying, `Wherefore have ye not completed your portion in making brick as heretofore, both yesterday and to-day?'
texts.exo.5.15: And the authorities of the sons of Israel come in and cry unto Pharaoh, saying, `Why dost thou thus to thy servants?
texts.exo.5.16: Straw is not given to thy servants, and they are saying to us, Make bricks, and lo, thy servants are smitten -- and thy people hath sinned.'
texts.exo.5.17: And he saith, `Remiss -- ye are remiss, therefore ye are saying, Let us go, let us sacrifice to Jehovah;
texts.exo.5.18: and now, go, serve; and straw is not given to you, and the measure of bricks ye do give.'
texts.exo.5.19: And the authorities of the sons of Israel see them in affliction, saying, `Ye do not diminish from your bricks; the matter of a day in its day.'
texts.exo.5.20: And they meet Moses and Aaron standing to meet them, in their coming out from Pharaoh,
texts.exo.5.21: and say unto them, `Jehovah look upon you, and judge, because ye have caused our fragrance to stink in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants -- to give a sword into their hand to slay us.'
texts.exo.5.22: And Moses turneth back unto Jehovah, and saith, `Lord, why hast Thou done evil to this people? why [is] this? -- Thou hast sent me!
texts.exo.5.23: and since I have come unto Pharaoh, to speak in Thy name, he hath done evil to this people, and Thou hast not at all delivered Thy people.'
texts.exo.6.1: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Now dost thou see that which I do to Pharaoh, for with a strong hand he doth send them away, yea, with a strong hand he doth cast them out of his land.'
texts.exo.6.2: And God speaketh unto Moses, and saith unto him, `I [am] Jehovah,
texts.exo.6.3: and I appear unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, as God Almighty; as to My name Jehovah, I have not been known to them;
texts.exo.6.4: and also I have established My covenant with them, to give to them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojournings, wherein they have sojourned;
texts.exo.6.5: and also I have heard the groaning of the sons of Israel, whom the Egyptians are causing to serve, and I remember My covenant.
texts.exo.6.6: `Therefore say to the sons of Israel, I [am] Jehovah, and I have brought you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and have delivered you from their service, and have redeemed you by a stretched-out arm, and by great judgments,
texts.exo.6.7: and have taken you to Me for a people, and I have been to you for God, and ye have known that I [am] Jehovah your God, who is bringing you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians;
texts.exo.6.8: and I have brought you in unto the land which I have lifted up My hand to give it to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, and have given it to you -- a possession; I [am] Jehovah.'
texts.exo.6.9: And Moses speaketh so unto the sons of Israel, and they hearkened not unto Moses, for anguish of spirit, and for harsh service.
texts.exo.6.10: And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
texts.exo.6.11: `Go in, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he doth send the sons of Israel out of his land;
texts.exo.6.12: and Moses speaketh before Jehovah, saying, `Lo, the sons of Israel have not hearkened unto me, and how doth Pharaoh hear me, and I of uncircumcised lips?'
texts.exo.6.13: And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, and unto Aaron, and chargeth them for the sons of Israel, and for Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring out the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.6.14: These [are] heads of the house of their fathers: Sons of Reuben first-born of Israel [are] Hanoch, and Phallu, Hezron, and Carmi: these [are] families of Reuben.
texts.exo.6.15: And sons of Simeon [are] Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul, son of the Canaanitess: these [are] families of Simeon.
texts.exo.6.16: And these [are] the names of the sons of Levi, as to their births: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari: and the years of the life of Levi [are] a hundred and thirty and seven years.
texts.exo.6.17: The sons of Gershon [are] Libni, and Shimi, as to their families.
texts.exo.6.18: And the sons of Kohath [are] Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel: and the years of the life of Kohath [are] a hundred and thirty and three years.
texts.exo.6.19: And the sons of Merari [are] Mahli and Mushi: these [are] families of Levi, as to their births.
texts.exo.6.20: And Amram taketh Jochebed his aunt to himself for a wife, and she beareth to him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram [are] a hundred and thirty and seven years.
texts.exo.6.21: And sons of Izhar [are] Korah, and Nepheg, and Zichri.
texts.exo.6.22: And sons of Uzziel [are] Mishael, and Elzaphan, and Sithri.
texts.exo.6.23: And Aaron taketh Elisheba daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to himself for a wife, and she beareth to him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
texts.exo.6.24: And sons of Korah [are] Assir, and Elkanah, and Abiasaph: these [are] families of the Korhite.
texts.exo.6.25: And Eleazar, Aaron's son, hath taken to him [one] of the daughters of Putiel for a wife to himself, and she beareth to him Phinehas: these [are] heads of the fathers of the Levites, as to their families.
texts.exo.6.26: This [is] Aaron -- and Moses -- to whom Jehovah said, `Bring ye out the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt, by their hosts;'
texts.exo.6.27: these are they who are speaking unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring out the sons of Israel from Egypt, this [is] Moses -- and Aaron.
texts.exo.6.28: And it cometh to pass in the day of Jehovah's speaking unto Moses in the land of Egypt,
texts.exo.6.29: that Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying, `I [am] Jehovah, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I am speaking unto thee.'
texts.exo.6.30: And Moses saith before Jehovah, `Lo, I [am] of uncircumcised lips, and how doth Pharaoh hearken unto me?'
texts.exo.7.1: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `See, I have given thee a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron thy brother is thy prophet;
texts.exo.7.2: thou -- thou dost speak all that I command thee, and Aaron thy brother doth speak unto Pharaoh, and he hath sent the sons of Israel out of his land.
texts.exo.7.3: `And I harden the heart of Pharaoh, and have multiplied My signs and My wonders in the land of Egypt,
texts.exo.7.4: and Pharaoh doth not hearken, and I have put My hand on Egypt, and have brought out My hosts, My people, the sons of Israel, from the land of Egypt by great judgments;
texts.exo.7.5: and the Egyptians have known that I [am] Jehovah, in My stretching out My hand against Egypt; and I have brought out the sons of Israel from their midst.'
texts.exo.7.6: And Moses doth -- Aaron also -- as Jehovah commanded them; so have they done;
texts.exo.7.7: and Moses [is] a son of eighty years, and Aaron [is] a son of eighty and three years, in their speaking unto Pharaoh.
texts.exo.7.8: And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,
texts.exo.7.9: `When Pharaoh speaketh unto you, saying, Give for yourselves a wonder; then thou hast said unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and cast before Pharaoh -- it becometh a monster.'
texts.exo.7.10: And Moses goeth in -- Aaron also -- unto Pharaoh, and they do so as Jehovah hath commanded; and Aaron casteth his rod before Pharaoh, and before his servants, and it becometh a monster.
texts.exo.7.11: And Pharaoh also calleth for wise men, and for sorcerers; and the scribes of Egypt, they also, with their flashings, do so,
texts.exo.7.12: and they cast down each his rod, and they become monsters, and the rod of Aaron swalloweth their rods;
texts.exo.7.13: and the heart of Pharaoh is strong, and he hath not hearkened unto them, as Jehovah hath spoken.
texts.exo.7.14: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `The heart of Pharaoh hath been hard, he hath refused to send the people away;
texts.exo.7.15: go unto Pharaoh in the morning, lo, he is going out to the water, and thou hast stood to meet him by the edge of the River, and the rod which was turned to a serpent thou dost take in thy hand,
texts.exo.7.16: and thou hast said unto him: Jehovah, God of the Hebrews, hath sent me unto thee, saying, Send My people away, and they serve Me in the wilderness; and lo, thou hast not hearkened hitherto.
texts.exo.7.17: `Thus said Jehovah: By this thou knowest that I [am] Jehovah; lo, I am smiting with the rod which [is] in my hand, on the waters which [are] in the River, and they have been turned to blood,
texts.exo.7.18: and the fish that [are] in the River die, and the River hath stank, and the Egyptians have been wearied of drinking waters from the River.'
texts.exo.7.19: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and stretch out thy hand against the waters of Egypt, against their streams, against their rivers, and against their ponds, and against all their collections of waters; and they are blood -- and there hath been blood in all the land of Egypt, both in [vessels of] wood, and in [those of] stone.'
texts.exo.7.20: And Moses and Aaron do so, as Jehovah hath commanded, and he lifteth up [his hand] with the rod, and smiteth the waters which [are] in the River, before the eyes of Pharaoh, and before the eyes of his servants, and all the waters which [are] in the River are turned to blood,
texts.exo.7.21: and the fish which [is] in the River hath died, and the River stinketh, and the Egyptians have not been able to drink water from the River; and the blood is in all the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.7.22: And the scribes of Egypt do so with their flashings, and the heart of Pharaoh is strong, and he hath not hearkened unto them, as Jehovah hath spoken,
texts.exo.7.23: and Pharaoh turneth and goeth in unto his house, and hath not set his heart even to this;
texts.exo.7.24: and all the Egyptians seek water round about the river to drink, for they have not been able to drink of the waters of the River.
texts.exo.7.25: And seven days are completed after Jehovah's smiting the River,
texts.exo.8.1: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Go in unto Pharaoh: and thou hast said unto him, Thus said Jehovah, Send My people away, and they serve Me;
texts.exo.8.2: and if thou art refusing to send away, lo, I am smiting all thy border with frogs;
texts.exo.8.3: and the River hath teemed [with] frogs, and they have gone up and gone into thy house, and into the inner-chamber of thy bed, and on thy couch, and into the house of thy servants, and among thy people, and into thine ovens, and into thy kneading-troughs;
texts.exo.8.4: yea, on thee, and on thy people, and on all thy servants do the frogs go up.'
texts.exo.8.5: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy hand, with thy rod, against the streams, against the rivers, and against the ponds, and cause the frogs to come up against the land of Egypt.'
texts.exo.8.6: And Aaron stretcheth out his hand against the waters of Egypt, and the frog cometh up, and covereth the land of Egypt;
texts.exo.8.7: and the scribes do so with their flashings, and cause the frogs to come up against the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.8.8: And Pharaoh calleth for Moses and for Aaron, and saith, `Make supplication unto Jehovah, that he turn aside the frogs from me, and from my people, and I send the people away, and they sacrifice to Jehovah.'
texts.exo.8.9: And Moses saith to Pharaoh, `Beautify thyself over me; when do I make supplication for thee, and for thy servants, and for thy people, to cut off the frogs from thee and from thy houses -- only in the River they do remain?'
texts.exo.8.10: and he saith, `To-morrow.' And he saith, According to thy word [it is], so that thou knowest that there is none like Jehovah our God,
texts.exo.8.11: and the frogs have turned aside from thee, and from thy houses, and from thy servants, and from thy people; only in the River they do remain.'
texts.exo.8.12: And Moses -- Aaron also -- goeth out from Pharaoh, and Moses crieth unto Jehovah, concerning the matter of the frogs which He hath set on Pharaoh;
texts.exo.8.13: and Jehovah doth according to the word of Moses, and the frogs die out of the houses, out of the courts, and out of the fields,
texts.exo.8.14: and they heap them up together, and the land stinketh.
texts.exo.8.15: And Pharaoh seeth that there hath been a respite, and he hath hardened his heart, and hath not hearkened unto them, as Jehovah hath spoken.
texts.exo.8.16: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy rod, and smite the dust of the land, and it hath become gnats in all the land of Egypt.'
texts.exo.8.17: And they do so, and Aaron stretcheth out his hand with his rod, and smiteth the dust of the land, and the gnats are on man and on beast; all the dust of the land hath been gnats in all the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.8.18: And the scribes do so with their flashings, to bring out the gnats, and they have not been able, and the gnats are on man and on beast;
texts.exo.8.19: and the scribes say unto Pharaoh, `It [is] the finger of God;' and the heart of Pharaoh is strong, and he hath not hearkened unto them, as Jehovah hath spoken.
texts.exo.8.20: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Rise early in the morning, and station thyself before Pharaoh, lo, he is going out to the waters, and thou hast said unto him, Thus said Jehovah, Send My people away, and they serve Me;
texts.exo.8.21: for, if thou art not sending My people away, lo, I am sending against thee, and against thy servants, and against thy people, and against thy houses, the beetle, and the houses of the Egyptians have been full of the beetle, and also the ground on which they are.
texts.exo.8.22: `And I have separated in that day the land of Goshen, in which My people are staying, that the beetle is not there, so that thou knowest that I [am] Jehovah in the midst of the land,
texts.exo.8.23: and I have put a division between My people and thy people: to-morrow is this sign.'
texts.exo.8.24: And Jehovah doth so, and the grievous beetle entereth the house of Pharaoh, and the house of his servants, and in all the land of Egypt the land is corrupted from the presence of the beetle.
texts.exo.8.25: And Pharaoh calleth unto Moses and to Aaron, and saith, `Go, sacrifice to your God in the land;'
texts.exo.8.26: and Moses saith, `Not right to do so, for the abomination of the Egyptians we do sacrifice to Jehovah our God; lo, we sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes -- and they do not stone us!
texts.exo.8.27: A journey of three days we go into the wilderness, and have sacrificed to Jehovah our God, as He saith unto us.'
texts.exo.8.28: And Pharaoh saith, `I send you away, and ye have sacrificed to Jehovah your God in the wilderness, only go not very far off; make ye supplication for me;'
texts.exo.8.29: and Moses saith, `Lo, I am going out from thee, and have made supplication unto Jehovah, and the beetle hath turned aside from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people -- to-morrow, only let not Pharaoh add to deceive -- in not sending the people away to sacrifice to Jehovah.'
texts.exo.8.30: And Moses goeth out from Pharaoh, and maketh supplication unto Jehovah,
texts.exo.8.31: and Jehovah doth according to the word of Moses, and turneth aside the beetle from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people -- there hath not been left one;
texts.exo.8.32: and Pharaoh hardeneth his heart also at this time, and hath not sent the people away.
texts.exo.9.1: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Go in unto Pharaoh, and thou hast spoken unto him, Thus said Jehovah, God of the Hebrews, Send My people away, and they serve me,
texts.exo.9.2: for, if thou art refusing to send away, and art still keeping hold upon them,
texts.exo.9.3: lo, the hand of Jehovah is on thy cattle which [are] in the field, on horses, on asses, on camels, on herd, and on flock -- a pestilence very grievous.
texts.exo.9.4: `And Jehovah hath separated between the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt, and there doth not die a thing of all the sons of Israel's;
texts.exo.9.5: and Jehovah setteth an appointed time, saying, To-morrow doth Jehovah do this thing in the land.'
texts.exo.9.6: And Jehovah doth this thing on the morrow, and all the cattle of Egypt die, and of the cattle of the sons of Israel not one hath died;
texts.exo.9.7: and Pharaoh sendeth, and lo, not even one of the cattle of Israel hath died, and the heart of Pharaoh is hard, and he hath not sent the people away.
texts.exo.9.8: And Jehovah saith unto Moses and unto Aaron, `Take to you the fulness of your hands [of] soot of a furnace, and Moses hath sprinkled it towards the heavens, before the eyes of Pharaoh,
texts.exo.9.9: and it hath become small dust over all the land of Egypt, and it hath become on man and on cattle a boil breaking forth [with] blains, in all the land of Egypt.'
texts.exo.9.10: And they take the soot of the furnace, and stand before Pharaoh, and Moses sprinkleth it towards the heavens, and it is a boil [with] blains, breaking forth, on man and on beast;
texts.exo.9.11: and the scribes have not been able to stand before Moses, because of the boil, for the boil hath been on the scribes, and on all the Egyptians.
texts.exo.9.12: And Jehovah strengtheneth the heart of Pharaoh, and he hath not hearkened unto them, as Jehovah hath spoken unto Moses.
texts.exo.9.13: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Rise early in the morning, and station thyself before Pharaoh, and thou hast said unto him, Thus said Jehovah, God of the Hebrews, Send My people away, and they serve Me,
texts.exo.9.14: for, at this time I am sending all My plagues unto thy heart, and on thy servants, and on thy people, so that thou knowest that there is none like Me in all the earth,
texts.exo.9.15: for now I have put forth My hand, and I smite thee, and thy people, with pestilence, and thou art hidden from the earth.
texts.exo.9.16: `And yet for this I have caused thee to stand, so as to show thee My power, and for the sake of declaring My Name in all the earth;
texts.exo.9.17: still thou art exalting thyself against My people -- so as not to send them away;
texts.exo.9.18: lo, I am raining about [this] time to-morrow hail very grievous, such as hath not been in Egypt, even from the day of its being founded, even until now.
texts.exo.9.19: `And, now, send, strengthen thy cattle and all that thou hast in the field; every man and beast which is found in the field, and is not gathered into the house -- come down on them hath the hail, and they have died.'
texts.exo.9.20: He who is fearing the word of Jehovah among the servants of Pharaoh hath caused his servants and his cattle to flee unto the houses;
texts.exo.9.21: and he who hath not set his heart unto the word of Jehovah leaveth his servants and his cattle in the field.
texts.exo.9.22: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Stretch forth thy hand towards the heavens, and there is hail in all the land of Egypt, on man, and on beast, and on every herb of the field in the land of Egypt.'
texts.exo.9.23: And Moses stretcheth out his rod towards the heavens, and Jehovah hath given voices and hail, and fire goeth towards the earth, and Jehovah raineth hail on the land of Egypt,
texts.exo.9.24: and there is hail, and fire catching itself in the midst of the hail, very grievous, such as hath not been in all the land of Egypt since it hath become a nation.
texts.exo.9.25: And the hail smiteth in all the land of Egypt all that [is] in the field, from man even unto beast, and every herb of the field hath the hail smitten, and every tree of the field it hath broken;
texts.exo.9.26: only in the land of Goshen, where the sons of Israel [are], there hath been no hail.
texts.exo.9.27: And Pharaoh sendeth, and calleth for Moses and for Aaron, and saith unto them, `I have sinned this time, Jehovah [is] the Righteous, and I and my people [are] the Wicked,
texts.exo.9.28: make ye supplication unto Jehovah, and plead that there be no voices of God and hail, and I send you away, and ye add not to remain.'
texts.exo.9.29: And Moses saith unto him, `At my going out of the city, I spread my palms unto Jehovah -- the voices cease, and the hail is not any more, so that thou knowest that the earth [is] Jehovah's;
texts.exo.9.30: but thou and thy servants -- I have known that ye are not yet afraid of the face of Jehovah God.'
texts.exo.9.31: And the flax and the barley have been smitten, for the barley [is] budding, and the flax forming flowers,
texts.exo.9.32: and the wheat and the rye have not been smitten, for they are late.
texts.exo.9.33: And Moses goeth out from Pharaoh, [from] the city, and spreadeth his hands unto Jehovah, and the voices and the hail cease, and rain hath not been poured out to the earth;
texts.exo.9.34: and Pharaoh seeth that the rain hath ceased, and the hail and the voices, and he continueth to sin, and hardeneth his heart, he and his servants;
texts.exo.9.35: and the heart of Pharaoh is strong, and he hath not sent the sons of Israel away, as Jehovah hath spoken by the hand of Moses.
texts.exo.10.1: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Go in unto Pharaoh, for I have declared hard his heart, and the heart of his servants, so that I set these My signs in their midst,
texts.exo.10.2: and so that thou recountest in the ears of thy son, and of thy son's son, that which I have done in Egypt, and My signs which I have set among them, and ye have known that I [am] Jehovah.'
texts.exo.10.3: And Moses cometh in -- Aaron also -- unto Pharaoh, and they say unto him, `Thus said Jehovah, God of the Hebrews, Until when hast thou refused to be humbled at My presence? send My people away, and they serve Me,
texts.exo.10.4: for if thou art refusing to send My people away, lo, I am bringing in to-morrow the locust into thy border,
texts.exo.10.5: and it hath covered the eye of the land, and none is able to see the land, and it hath eaten the remnant of that which is escaped, which is left to you from the hail, and it hath eaten every tree which is springing for you out of the field;
texts.exo.10.6: and they have filled thy houses, and the houses of all thy servants, and the houses of all the Egyptians, which neither thy fathers nor thy father's fathers have seen, since the day of their being on the ground unto this day,' -- and he turneth and goeth out from Pharaoh.
texts.exo.10.7: And the servants of Pharaoh say unto him, `Until when doth this [one] become a snare to us? send the men away, and they serve Jehovah their God; knowest thou not yet that Egypt hath perished?'
texts.exo.10.8: And Moses is brought back -- Aaron also -- unto Pharaoh, and he saith unto them, `Go, serve Jehovah your God; -- who and who [are] those going?'
texts.exo.10.9: And Moses saith, `With our young ones, and with our aged ones, we go, with our sons, and with our daughters, with our flock, and our herd, we go, for we have a festival to Jehovah.'
texts.exo.10.10: And he saith unto them, `Be it so, Jehovah [be] with you when I send you and your infants away; see -- for evil [is] before your faces;
texts.exo.10.11: not so! go now, ye who [are] men, and serve Jehovah, for that ye are seeking;' and [one] casteth them out from the presence of Pharaoh.
texts.exo.10.12: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Stretch out thy hand against the land of Egypt for the locust, and it goeth up against the land of Egypt, and doth eat every herb of the land -- all that the hail hath left.'
texts.exo.10.13: And Moses stretcheth out his rod against the land of Egypt, and Jehovah hath led an east wind over the land all that day, and all the night; the morning hath been, and the east wind hath lifted up the locust.
texts.exo.10.14: And the locust goeth up against all the land of Egypt, and resteth in all the border of Egypt -- very grievous: before it there hath not been such a locust as it, and after it there is none such;
texts.exo.10.15: and it covereth the eye of all the land, and the land is darkened; and it eateth every herb of the land, and all the fruit of the trees which the hail hath left, and there hath not been left any green thing in the trees, or in the herb of the field, in all the land of Egypt.'
texts.exo.10.16: And Pharaoh hasteth to call for Moses and for Aaron, and saith, `I have sinned against Jehovah your God, and against you,
texts.exo.10.17: and now, bear with, I pray you, my sin, only this time, and make ye supplication to Jehovah your God, that He turn aside from off me only this death.'
texts.exo.10.18: And he goeth out from Pharaoh, and maketh supplication unto Jehovah,
texts.exo.10.19: and Jehovah turneth a very strong sea wind, and it lifteth up the locust, and bloweth it into the Red Sea -- there hath not been left one locust in all the border of Egypt;
texts.exo.10.20: and Jehovah strengtheneth the heart of Pharaoh, and he hath not sent the sons of Israel away.
texts.exo.10.21: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Stretch out thy hand towards the heavens, and there is darkness over the land of Egypt, and the darkness is felt.'
texts.exo.10.22: And Moses stretcheth out his hand towards the heavens, and there is darkness -- thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days;
texts.exo.10.23: they have not seen one another, and none hath risen from his place three days; and to all the sons of Israel there hath been light in their dwellings.'
texts.exo.10.24: And Pharaoh calleth unto Moses and saith, `Go ye, serve Jehovah, only your flock and your herd are stayed, your infants also go with you;'
texts.exo.10.25: and Moses saith, `Thou also dost give in our hand sacrifices and burnt-offerings, and we have prepared for Jehovah our God;
texts.exo.10.26: and also our cattle doth go with us, there is not left a hoof, for from it we do take to serve Jehovah our God; and we -- we know not how we do serve Jehovah till our going thither.'
texts.exo.10.27: And Jehovah strengtheneth the heart of Pharaoh, and he hath not been willing to send them away;
texts.exo.10.28: and Pharaoh saith to him, `Go from me, take heed to thyself, add not to see my face, for in the day thou seest my face thou diest;'
texts.exo.10.29: and Moses saith, `Rightly hast thou spoken, I add not any more to see thy face.'
texts.exo.11.1: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `One plague more I do bring in on Pharaoh, and on Egypt, afterwards he doth send you away from this; when he is sending you away, he surely casteth you out altogether from this [place];
texts.exo.11.2: speak, I pray thee, in the ears of the people, and they ask -- each man from his neighbour, and each woman from her neighbour, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold.'
texts.exo.11.3: And Jehovah giveth the grace of the people in the eyes of the Egyptians; also the man Moses [is] very great in the land of Egypt, in the eyes of the servants of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of the people.
texts.exo.11.4: And Moses saith, `Thus said Jehovah, About midnight I am going out into the midst of Egypt,
texts.exo.11.5: and every first-born in the land of Egypt hath died, from the first-born of Pharaoh who is sitting on his throne, unto the first-born of the maid-servant who [is] behind the millstones, and all the first-born of beasts;
texts.exo.11.6: and there hath been a great cry in all the land of Egypt, such as there hath not been, and such as there is not again.
texts.exo.11.7: `And against all the sons of Israel a dog sharpeneth not its tongue, from man even unto beast, so that ye know that Jehovah doth make a separation between the Egyptians and Israel;
texts.exo.11.8: and all these thy servants have come down unto me, and bowed themselves to me, saying, Go out, thou and all the people who [are] at thy feet; and afterwards I do go out;' -- and he goeth out from Pharaoh in the heat of anger.
texts.exo.11.9: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Pharaoh doth not hearken unto you, so as to multiply My wonders in the land of Egypt;'
texts.exo.11.10: and Moses and Aaron have done all these wonders before Pharaoh, and Jehovah strengtheneth Pharaoh's heart, and he hath not sent the sons of Israel out of his land.
texts.exo.12.1: And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses and unto Aaron, in the land of Egypt, saying,
texts.exo.12.2: `This month [is] to you the chief of months -- it [is] the first to you of the months of the year;
texts.exo.12.3: speak ye unto all the company of Israel, saying, In the tenth of this month -- they take to them each man a lamb for the house of the fathers, a lamb for a house.
texts.exo.12.4: `(And if the household be too few for a lamb, then hath he taken, he and his neighbour who is near unto his house, for the number of persons, each according to his eating ye do count for the lamb,)
texts.exo.12.5: a lamb, a perfect one, a male, a son of a year, let be to you; from the sheep or from the goats ye do take [it].
texts.exo.12.6: `And it hath become a charge to you, until the fourteenth day of this month, and the whole assembly of the company of Israel have slaughtered it between the evenings;
texts.exo.12.7: and they have taken of the blood, and have put on the two side-posts, and on the lintel over the houses in which they eat it.
texts.exo.12.8: `And they have eaten the flesh in this night, roast with fire; with unleavened things and bitters they do eat it;
texts.exo.12.9: ye do not eat of it raw, or boiled at all in water, but roast with fire, its head with its legs, and with its inwards;
texts.exo.12.10: and ye do not leave of it till morning, and that which is remaining of it till morning with fire ye do burn.
texts.exo.12.11: `And thus ye do eat it: your loins girded, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand, and ye have eaten it in haste; it is Jehovah's passover,
texts.exo.12.12: and I have passed over through the land of Egypt during this night, and have smitten every first-born in the land of Egypt, from man even unto beast, and on all the gods of Egypt I do judgments; I [am] Jehovah.
texts.exo.12.13: `And the blood hath become a sign for you on the houses where ye [are], and I have seen the blood, and have passed over you, and a plague is not on you for destruction in My smiting in the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.12.14: `And this day hath become to you a memorial, and ye have kept it a feast to Jehovah to your generations; -- a statute age-during; ye keep it a feast.
texts.exo.12.15: Seven days ye eat unleavened things; only -- in the first day ye cause leaven to cease out of your houses; for any one eating anything fermented from the first day till the seventh day, even that person hath been cut off from Israel.
texts.exo.12.16: `And in the first day [is] a holy convocation, and in the seventh day ye have a holy convocation; any work is not done in them, only that which is eaten by any person -- it alone is done by you,
texts.exo.12.17: and ye have observed the unleavened things, for in this self-same day I have brought out your hosts from the land of Egypt, and ye have observed this day to your generations -- a statute age-during.
texts.exo.12.18: `In the first [month], in the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, ye do eat unleavened things until the one and twentieth day of the month, at evening;
texts.exo.12.19: seven days leaven is not found in your houses, for any [one] eating anything fermented -- that person hath been cut off from the company of Israel, among the sojourners or among the natives of the land;
texts.exo.12.20: anything fermented ye do not eat, in all your dwellings ye do eat unleavened things.'
texts.exo.12.21: And Moses calleth for all the elders of Israel, and saith unto them, `Draw out and take for yourselves [from] the flock, for your families, and slaughter the passover-sacrifice;
texts.exo.12.22: and ye have taken a bunch of hyssop, and have dipped [it] in the blood which [is] in the basin, and have struck [it] on the lintel, and on the two side-posts, from the blood which [is] in the basin, and ye, ye go not out each from the opening of his house till morning.
texts.exo.12.23: `And Jehovah hath passed on to smite the Egyptians, and hath seen the blood on the lintel, and on the two side-posts, and Jehovah hath passed over the opening, and doth not permit the destruction to come into your houses to smite.
texts.exo.12.24: `And ye have observed this thing, for a statute to thee, and to thy sons -- unto the age;
texts.exo.12.25: and it hath been, when ye come in unto the land which Jehovah giveth to you, as He hath spoken, that ye have kept this service;
texts.exo.12.26: and it hath come to pass when your sons say unto you, What [is] this service ye have?
texts.exo.12.27: that ye have said, A sacrifice of passover it [is] to Jehovah, who passed over the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt, in His smiting the Egyptians, and our houses He delivered.'
texts.exo.12.28: And the people bow and do obeisance, and the sons of Israel go and do as Jehovah commanded Moses and Aaron; so have they done.
texts.exo.12.29: And it cometh to pass, at midnight, that Jehovah hath smitten every first-born in the land of Egypt, from the first-born of Pharaoh who is sitting on his throne, unto the first-born of the captive who [is] in the prison-house, and every first-born of beasts.
texts.exo.12.30: And Pharaoh riseth by night, he and all his servants, and all the Egyptians, and there is a great cry in Egypt, for there is not a house where there is not [one] dead,
texts.exo.12.31: and he calleth for Moses and for Aaron by night, and saith, `Rise, go out from the midst of my people, both ye and the sons of Israel, and go, serve Jehovah according to your word;
texts.exo.12.32: both your flock and your herd take ye, as ye have spoken, and go; then ye have blessed also me.'
texts.exo.12.33: And the Egyptians are urgent on the people, hasting to send them away out of the land, for they said, `We are all dead;'
texts.exo.12.34: and the people taketh up its dough before it is fermented, their kneading-troughs [are] bound up in their garments on their shoulder.
texts.exo.12.35: And the sons of Israel have done according to the word of Moses, and they ask from the Egyptians vessels of silver and vessels of gold, and garments;
texts.exo.12.36: and Jehovah hath given the grace of the people in the eyes of the Egyptians, and they cause them to ask, and they spoil the Egyptians.
texts.exo.12.37: And the sons of Israel journey from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand men on foot, apart from infants;
texts.exo.12.38: and a great rabble also hath gone up with them, and flock and herd -- very much cattle.
texts.exo.12.39: And they bake with the dough which they have brought out from Egypt unleavened cakes, for it hath not fermented; for they have been cast out of Egypt, and have not been able to delay, and also provision they have not made for themselves.
texts.exo.12.40: And the dwelling of the sons of Israel which they have dwelt in Egypt [is] four hundred and thirty years;
texts.exo.12.41: and it cometh to pass, at the end of four hundred and thirty years -- yea, it cometh to pass in this self-same day -- all the hosts of Jehovah have gone out from the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.12.42: A night of watchings it [is] to Jehovah, to bring them out from the land of Egypt; it [is] this night to Jehovah of watchings to all the sons of Israel to their generations.
texts.exo.12.43: And Jehovah saith unto Moses and Aaron, `This [is] a statute of the passover; Any son of a stranger doth not eat of it;
texts.exo.12.44: and any man's servant, the purchase of money, when thou hast circumcised him -- then he doth eat of it;
texts.exo.12.45: a settler or hired servant doth not eat of it;
texts.exo.12.46: in one house it is eaten, thou dost not carry out of the house [any] of the flesh without, and a bone ye do not break of it;
texts.exo.12.47: all the company of Israel do keep it.
texts.exo.12.48: `And when a sojourner sojourneth with thee, and hath made a passover to Jehovah, every male of his [is] to be circumcised, and then he doth come near to keep it, and he hath been as a native of the land, but any uncircumcised one doth not eat of it;
texts.exo.12.49: one law is to a native, and to a sojourner who is sojourning in your midst.'
texts.exo.12.50: And all the sons of Israel do as Jehovah commanded Moses and Aaron; so have they done.
texts.exo.12.51: And it cometh to pass in this self-same day, Jehovah hath brought out the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt, by their hosts.
texts.exo.13.1: And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
texts.exo.13.2: `Sanctify to Me every first-born, opening any womb among the sons of Israel, among man and among beast; it [is] Mine.'
texts.exo.13.3: And Moses saith unto the people, `Remember this day [in] which ye have gone out from Egypt, from the house of servants, for by strength of hand hath Jehovah brought you out from this, and any thing fermented is not eaten;
texts.exo.13.4: To-day ye are going out, in the month of Abib.
texts.exo.13.5: `And it hath been, when Jehovah bringeth thee in unto the land of the Canaanite, and of the Hittite, and of the Amorite, and of the Hivite, and of the Jebusite, which He hath sworn to thy fathers to give to thee, a land flowing with milk and honey, that thou hast done this service in this month.
texts.exo.13.6: `Seven days thou dost eat unleavened things, and in the seventh day [is] a feast to Jehovah;
texts.exo.13.7: unleavened things are eaten the seven days, and any thing fermented is not seen with thee; yea, leaven is not seen with thee in all thy border.
texts.exo.13.8: `And thou hast declared to thy son in that day, saying, `[It is] because of what Jehovah did to me, in my going out from Egypt,
texts.exo.13.9: and it hath been to thee for a sign on thy hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes, so that the law of Jehovah is in thy mouth, for by a strong hand hath Jehovah brought thee out from Egypt;
texts.exo.13.10: and thou hast kept this statute at its appointed season from days to days.
texts.exo.13.11: `And it hath been, when Jehovah bringeth thee in unto the land of the Canaanite, as He hath sworn to thee and to thy fathers, and hath given it to thee,
texts.exo.13.12: that thou hast caused every one opening a womb to pass over to Jehovah, and every firstling -- the increase of beasts which thou hast: the males [are] Jehovah's.
texts.exo.13.13: `And every firstling of an ass thou dost ransom with a lamb, and if thou dost not ransom [it], then thou hast beheaded it: and every first-born of man among thy sons thou dost ransom.
texts.exo.13.14: `And it hath been, when thy son asketh thee hereafter, saying, What [is] this? that thou hast said unto him, By strength of hand hath Jehovah brought us out from Egypt, from a house of servants;
texts.exo.13.15: yea, it cometh to pass, when Pharaoh hath been pained to send us away, that Jehovah doth slay every first-born in the land of Egypt, from the first-born of man even unto the first-born of beast; therefore I am sacrificing to Jehovah all opening a womb who [are] males, and every first-born of my sons I ransom;
texts.exo.13.16: and it hath been for a token on thy hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes, for by strength of hand hath Jehovah brought us out of Egypt.'
texts.exo.13.17: And it cometh to pass in Pharaoh's sending the people away, that God hath not led them the way of the land of the Philistines, for it [is] near; for God said, `Lest the people repent in their seeing war, and have turned back towards Egypt;'
texts.exo.13.18: and God turneth round the people the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea, and by fifties have the sons of Israel gone up from the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.13.19: And Moses taketh the bones of Joseph with him, for he certainly caused the sons of Israel to swear, saying, `God doth certainly inspect you, and ye have brought up my bones from this with you.'
texts.exo.13.20: And they journey from Succoth, and encamp in Etham at the extremity of the wilderness,
texts.exo.13.21: and Jehovah is going before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them in the way, and by night in a pillar of fire, to give light to them, to go by day and by night;
texts.exo.13.22: He removeth not the pillar of the cloud by day, and the pillar of the fire by night, [from] before the people.
texts.exo.14.1: And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
texts.exo.14.2: `Speak unto the sons of Israel, and they turn back and encamp before Pi-Hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal-Zephon; over-against it ye do encamp by the sea,
texts.exo.14.3: and Pharaoh hath said of the sons of Israel, They are entangled in the land, the wilderness hath shut upon them;
texts.exo.14.4: and I have strengthened the heart of Pharaoh, and he hath pursued after them, and I am honoured on Pharaoh, and on all his force, and the Egyptians have known that I [am] Jehovah;' and they do so.
texts.exo.14.5: And it is declared to the king of Egypt that the people hath fled, and the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants is turned against the people, and they say, `What [is] this we have done? that we have sent Israel away from our service.'
texts.exo.14.6: And he harnesseth his chariot, and his people he hath taken with him,
texts.exo.14.7: and he taketh six hundred chosen chariots, even all the chariots of Egypt, and captains over them all;
texts.exo.14.8: and Jehovah strengtheneth the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursueth after the sons of Israel, and the sons of Israel are going out with a high hand,
texts.exo.14.9: and the Egyptians pursue after them, and all the chariot horses of Pharaoh, and his horsemen, and his force, overtake them, encamping by the sea, by Pi-Hahiroth, before Baal-Zephon.
texts.exo.14.10: And Pharaoh hath drawn near, and the sons of Israel lift up their eyes, and lo, the Egyptians are journeying after them, and they fear exceedingly, and the sons of Israel cry unto Jehovah.
texts.exo.14.11: And they say unto Moses, `Because there are no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in a wilderness? what is this thou hast done to us -- to bring us out from Egypt?
texts.exo.14.12: Is not this the word which we spake unto thee in Egypt, saying, Cease from us, and we serve the Egyptians; for better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in a wilderness?'
texts.exo.14.13: And Moses saith unto the people, `Fear not, station yourselves, and see the salvation of Jehovah, which He doth for you to-day; for, as ye have seen the Egyptians to-day, ye add no more to see them -- to the age;
texts.exo.14.14: Jehovah doth fight for you, and ye keep silent.'
texts.exo.14.15: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `What? thou criest unto Me -- speak unto the sons of Israel, and they journey;
texts.exo.14.16: and thou, lift up thy rod, and stretch out thy hand towards the sea, and cleave it, and the sons of Israel go into the midst of the sea on dry land.
texts.exo.14.17: `And I -- lo, I am strengthening the heart of the Egyptians, and they go in after them, and I am honoured on Pharaoh, and on all his force, on his chariots, and on his horsemen;
texts.exo.14.18: and the Egyptians have known that I [am] Jehovah, in My being honoured on Pharaoh, on his chariots, and on his horsemen.'
texts.exo.14.19: And the messenger of God, who is going before the camp of Israel, journeyeth and goeth at their rear; and the pillar of the cloud journeyeth from their front, and standeth at their rear,
texts.exo.14.20: and cometh in between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel, and the cloud and the darkness are, and he enlighteneth the night, and the one hath not drawn near unto the other all the night.
texts.exo.14.21: And Moses stretcheth out his hand towards the sea, and Jehovah causeth the sea to go on by a strong east wind all the night, and maketh the sea become dry ground, and the waters are cleaved,
texts.exo.14.22: and the sons of Israel go into the midst of the sea, on dry land, and the waters [are] to them a wall, on their right and on their left.
texts.exo.14.23: And the Egyptians pursue, and go in after them (all the horses of Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen) unto the midst of the sea,
texts.exo.14.24: and it cometh to pass, in the morning watch, that Jehovah looketh unto the camp of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and of the cloud, and troubleth the camp of the Egyptians,
texts.exo.14.25: and turneth aside the wheels of their chariots, and they lead them with difficulty, and the Egyptians say, `Let us flee from the face of Israel, for Jehovah is fighting for them against the Egyptians.'
texts.exo.14.26: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Stretch out thy hand toward the sea, and the waters turn back on the Egyptians, on their chariots, and on their horsemen.'
texts.exo.14.27: And Moses stretcheth out his hand towards the sea, and the sea turneth back, at the turning of the morning, to its perennial flow, and the Egyptians are fleeing at its coming, and Jehovah shaketh off the Egyptians in the midst of the sea,
texts.exo.14.28: and the waters turn back, and cover the chariots and the horsemen, even all the force of Pharaoh, who are coming in after them into the sea -- there hath not been left of them even one.
texts.exo.14.29: And the sons of Israel have gone on dry land in the midst of the sea, and the waters [are] to them a wall, on their right and on their left;
texts.exo.14.30: and Jehovah saveth Israel in that day out of the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel seeth the Egyptians dead on the sea-shore,
texts.exo.14.31: and Israel seeth the great hand with which Jehovah hath wrought against the Egyptians, and the people fear Jehovah, and remain stedfast in Jehovah, and in Moses His servant.
texts.exo.15.1: Then singeth Moses and the sons of Israel this song to Jehovah, and they speak, saying: -- `I sing to Jehovah, For triumphing He hath triumphed; The horse and its rider He hath thrown into the sea.
texts.exo.15.2: My strength and song is JAH, And He is become my salvation: This [is] my God, and I glorify Him; God of my father, and I exalt Him.
texts.exo.15.3: Jehovah [is] a man of battle; Jehovah [is] His name.
texts.exo.15.4: Chariots of Pharaoh and his force He hath cast into the sea; And the choice of his captains Have sunk in the Red Sea!
texts.exo.15.5: The depths do cover them; They went down into the depths as a stone.
texts.exo.15.6: Thy right hand, O Jehovah, Is become honourable in power; Thy right hand, O Jehovah, Doth crush an enemy.
texts.exo.15.7: And in the abundance of Thine excellency Thou throwest down Thy withstanders, Thou sendest forth Thy wrath -- It consumeth them as stubble.
texts.exo.15.8: And by the spirit of Thine anger Have waters been heaped together; Stood as a heap have flowings; Congealed have been depths In the heart of a sea.
texts.exo.15.9: The enemy said, I pursue, I overtake; I apportion spoil; Filled is my soul with them; I draw out my sword; My hand destroyeth them: --
texts.exo.15.10: Thou hast blown with Thy wind The sea hath covered them; They sank as lead in mighty waters.
texts.exo.15.11: Who [is] like Thee among the gods, O Jehovah? Who [is] like Thee -- honourable in holiness -- Fearful in praises -- doing wonders?
texts.exo.15.12: Thou hast stretched out Thy right hand -- Earth swalloweth them!
texts.exo.15.13: Thou hast led forth in Thy kindness The people whom Thou hast redeemed. Thou hast led on in Thy strength Unto Thy holy habitation.
texts.exo.15.14: Peoples have heard, they are troubled; Pain hath seized inhabitants of Philistia.
texts.exo.15.15: Then have chiefs of Edom been troubled: Mighty ones of Moab -- Trembling doth seize them! Melted have all inhabitants of Canaan!
texts.exo.15.16: Fall on them doth terror and dread; By the greatness of Thine arm They are still as a stone, Till Thy people pass over, O Jehovah; Till the people pass over Whom Thou hast purchased.
texts.exo.15.17: Thou dost bring them in, And dost plant them In a mountain of Thine inheritance, A fixed place for Thy dwelling Thou hast made, O Jehovah; A sanctuary, O Lord, Thy hands have established;
texts.exo.15.18: Jehovah reigneth -- to the age, and for ever!'
texts.exo.15.19: For the horse of Pharaoh hath gone in with his chariots and with his horsemen into the sea, and Jehovah turneth back on them the waters of the sea, and the sons of Israel have gone on dry land in the midst of the sea.
texts.exo.15.20: And Miriam the inspired one, sister of Aaron, taketh the timbrel in her hand, and all the women go out after her, with timbrels and with choruses;
texts.exo.15.21: and Miriam answereth to them: -- `Sing ye to Jehovah, For Triumphing He hath triumphed; The horse and its rider He hath thrown into the sea!'
texts.exo.15.22: And Moses causeth Israel to journey from the Red Sea, and they go out unto the wilderness of Shur, and they go three days in the wilderness, and have not found water,
texts.exo.15.23: and they come in to Marah, and have not been able to drink the waters of Marah, for they [are] bitter; therefore hath [one] called its name Marah.
texts.exo.15.24: And the people murmur against Moses, saying, `What do we drink?'
texts.exo.15.25: and he crieth unto Jehovah, and Jehovah sheweth him a tree, and he casteth unto the waters, and the waters become sweet. There He hath made for them a statute, and an ordinance, and there He hath tried them,
texts.exo.15.26: and He saith, `If thou dost really hearken to the voice of Jehovah thy God, and dost that which is right in His eyes, and hast hearkened to His commands, and kept all His statutes: none of the sickness which I laid on the Egyptians do I lay on thee, for I, Jehovah, am healing thee.
texts.exo.15.27: And they come to Elim, and there [are] twelve fountains of water, and seventy palm trees; and they encamp there by the waters.
texts.exo.16.1: And they journey from Elim, and all the company of the sons of Israel come in unto the wilderness of Sin, which [is] between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month of their going out from the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.16.2: And all the company of the sons of Israel murmur against Moses and against Aaron in the wilderness;
texts.exo.16.3: and the sons of Israel say unto them, `Oh that we had died by the hand of Jehovah in the land of Egypt, in our sitting by the flesh-pot, in our eating bread to satiety -- for ye have brought us out unto this wilderness to put all this assembly to death with hunger.'
texts.exo.16.4: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Lo, I am raining to you bread from the heavens -- and the people have gone out and gathered the matter of a day in its day -- so that I try them whether they walk in My law, or not;
texts.exo.16.5: and it hath been on the sixth day, that they have prepared that which they bring in, and it hath been double above that which they gather day [by] day.'
texts.exo.16.6: And Moses saith -- Aaron also -- unto all the sons of Israel, `Evening -- and ye have known that Jehovah hath brought you out from the land of Egypt;
texts.exo.16.7: and morning -- and ye have seen the honour of Jehovah, in His hearing your murmurings against Jehovah, and what [are] we, that ye murmur against us?'
texts.exo.16.8: And Moses saith, `In Jehovah's giving to you in the evening flesh to eat, and bread in the morning to satiety -- in Jehovah's hearing your murmurings, which ye are murmuring against Him, and what [are] we? your murmurings [are] not against us, but against Jehovah.'
texts.exo.16.9: And Moses saith unto Aaron, `Say unto all the company of the sons of Israel, Come ye near before Jehovah, for He hath heard your murmurings;'
texts.exo.16.10: and it cometh to pass, when Aaron is speaking unto all the company of the sons of Israel, that they turn towards the wilderness, and lo, the honour of Jehovah is seen in the cloud.
texts.exo.16.11: And Jehovah speaketh unto Moses, saying,
texts.exo.16.12: `I have heard the murmurings of the sons of Israel; speak unto them, saying, Between the evenings ye eat flesh, and in the morning ye are satisfied [with] bread, and ye have known that I [am] Jehovah your God.'
texts.exo.16.13: And it cometh to pass in the evening, that the quail cometh up, and covereth the camp, and in the morning there hath been the lying of dew round about the camp,
texts.exo.16.14: and the lying of the dew goeth up, and lo, on the face of the wilderness a thin, bare thing, thin as hoar-frost on the earth.
texts.exo.16.15: And the sons of Israel see, and say one unto another, `What [is] it?' for they have not known what it [is]; and Moses saith unto them, `It [is] the bread which Jehovah hath given to you for food.
texts.exo.16.16: `This [is] the thing which Jehovah hath commanded: Gather of it each according to his eating, an omer for a poll; and the number of your persons, take ye each for those in his tent.'
texts.exo.16.17: And the sons of Israel do so, and they gather, he who is [gathering] much, and he who is [gathering] little;
texts.exo.16.18: and they measure with an omer, and he who is [gathering] much hath nothing over, and he who is [gathering] little hath no lack, each according to his eating they have gathered.
texts.exo.16.19: And Moses saith unto them, `Let no man leave of it till morning;'
texts.exo.16.20: and they have not hearkened unto Moses, and some of them do leave of it till morning, and it bringeth up worms and stinketh; and Moses is wroth with them.
texts.exo.16.21: And they gather it morning by morning, each according to his eating; when the sun hath been warm, then it hath melted.
texts.exo.16.22: And it cometh to pass on the sixth day, they have gathered a second bread, two omers for one, and all the princes of the company come in, and declare to Moses.
texts.exo.16.23: And he saith unto them, `It [is] that which Jehovah hath spoken [of]; a rest -- a holy sabbath to Jehovah -- [is] to-morrow; that which ye bake, bake; and that which ye boil, boil; and all that is over, let rest for yourselves in charge till the morning.'
texts.exo.16.24: And they let it rest until the morning, as Moses hath commanded, and it hath not stank, and a worm hath not been in it.
texts.exo.16.25: And Moses saith, `Eat it to-day, for to-day [is] a sabbath to Jehovah; to-day ye find it not in the field:
texts.exo.16.26: six days ye do gather it, and in the seventh day -- the sabbath -- in it there is none.'
texts.exo.16.27: And it cometh to pass on the seventh day, some of the people have gone out to gather, and have not found.
texts.exo.16.28: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `How long have ye refused to keep My commands, and My laws?
texts.exo.16.29: see, because Jehovah hath given to you the sabbath, therefore He is giving to you on the sixth day bread of two days; abide ye each [in] his place, no one doth go out from his place on the seventh day.'
texts.exo.16.30: And the people rest on the seventh day,
texts.exo.16.31: and the house of Israel call its name Manna, and it [is] as coriander seed, white; and its taste [is] as a cake with honey.
texts.exo.16.32: And Moses saith, `This [is] the thing which Jehovah hath commanded: Fill the omer with it, for a charge for your generations, so that they see the bread which I have caused you to eat in the wilderness, in My bringing you out from the land of Egypt.'
texts.exo.16.33: And Moses saith unto Aaron, `Take one pot, and put there the fulness of the omer of manna, and let it rest before Jehovah, for a charge for your generations;'
texts.exo.16.34: as Jehovah hath given commandment unto Moses, so doth Aaron let it rest before the Testimony, for a charge.
texts.exo.16.35: And the sons of Israel have eaten the manna forty years, until their coming in unto the land to be inhabited; the manna they have eaten till their coming in unto the extremity of the land of Canaan.
texts.exo.16.36: and the omer is a tenth of the ephah.
texts.exo.17.1: And all the company of the sons of Israel journey from the wilderness of Sin, on their journeyings, by the command of Jehovah, and encamp in Rephidim, and there is no water for the people to drink;
texts.exo.17.2: and the people strive with Moses, and say, `Give us water, and we drink.' And Moses saith to them, `What? -- ye strive with me, what? -- ye try Jehovah?'
texts.exo.17.3: and the people thirst there for water, and the people murmur against Moses, and say, `Why [is] this? -- thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to put us to death, also our sons and our cattle, with thirst.'
texts.exo.17.4: And Moses crieth to Jehovah, saying, `What do I to this people? yet a little, and they have stoned me.'
texts.exo.17.5: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Pass over before the people, and take with thee of the elders of Israel, and thy rod with which thou hast smitten the River take in thy hand, and thou hast gone:
texts.exo.17.6: Lo, I am standing before thee there on the rock in Horeb, and thou hast smitten on the rock, and waters have come out from it, and the people have drunk.' And Moses doth so before the eyes of the elders of Israel,
texts.exo.17.7: and he calleth the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the `strife' of the sons of Israel, and because of their `trying' Jehovah, saying, `Is Jehovah in our midst or not?'
texts.exo.17.8: And Amalek cometh, and fighteth with Israel in Rephidim,
texts.exo.17.9: and Moses saith unto Joshua, `Choose for us men, and go out, fight with Amalek: to-morrow I am standing on the top of the hill, and the rod of God in my hand.'
texts.exo.17.10: And Joshua doth as Moses hath said to him, to fight with Amalek, and Moses, Aaron, and Hur, have gone up [to] the top of the height;
texts.exo.17.11: and it hath come to pass, when Moses lifteth up his hand, that Israel hath been mighty, and when he letteth his hands rest, that Amalek hath been mighty.
texts.exo.17.12: And the hands of Moses [are] heavy, and they take a stone, and set [it] under him, and he sitteth on it: and Aaron and Hur have taken hold on his hands, on this side one, and on that one, and his hands are stedfast till the going in of the sun;
texts.exo.17.13: and Joshua weakeneth Amalek and his people by the mouth of the sword.
texts.exo.17.14: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Write this, a memorial in a Book, and set [it] in the ears of Joshua, that I do utterly wipe away the remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens;'
texts.exo.17.15: and Moses buildeth an altar, and calleth its name Jehovah-Nissi,
texts.exo.17.16: and saith, `Because a hand [is] on the throne of Jah, war [is] to Jehovah with Amalek from generation -- generation.'
texts.exo.18.1: And Jethro priest of Midian, father-in-law of Moses, heareth all that God hath done for Moses, and for Israel his people, that Jehovah hath brought out Israel from Egypt,
texts.exo.18.2: and Jethro, father-in-law of Moses, taketh Zipporah, wife of Moses, besides her parents,
texts.exo.18.3: and her two sons, of whom the name of the one [is] Gershom, for he said, `a sojourner I have been in a strange land:'
texts.exo.18.4: and the name of the other [is] Eliezer, for, `the God of my father [is] for my help, and doth deliver me from the sword of Pharaoh.'
texts.exo.18.5: And Jethro, father-in-law of Moses, cometh, and his sons, and his wife, unto Moses, unto the wilderness where he is encamping -- the mount of God;
texts.exo.18.6: and he saith unto Moses, `I, thy father-in-law, Jethro, am coming unto thee, and thy wife, and her two sons with her.'
texts.exo.18.7: And Moses goeth out to meet his father-in-law, and boweth himself, and kisseth him, and they ask one at another of welfare, and come into the tent;
texts.exo.18.8: and Moses recounteth to his father-in-law all that Jehovah hath done to Pharaoh, and to the Egyptians, on account of Israel, all the travail which hath found them in the way, and Jehovah doth deliver them.
texts.exo.18.9: And Jethro rejoiceth for all the good which Jehovah hath done to Israel, whom He hath delivered from the hand of the Egyptians;
texts.exo.18.10: and Jethro saith, `Blessed [is] Jehovah, who hath delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians, and from the hand of Pharaoh -- who hath delivered this people from under the hand of the Egyptians;
texts.exo.18.11: now I have known that Jehovah [is] greater than all the gods, for in the thing they have acted proudly -- [He is] above them!'
texts.exo.18.12: And Jethro, father-in-law of Moses, taketh a burnt-offering and sacrifices for God; and Aaron cometh in, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with the father-in-law of Moses, before God.
texts.exo.18.13: And it cometh to pass on the morrow, that Moses sitteth to judge the people, and the people stand before Moses, from the morning unto the evening;
texts.exo.18.14: and the father-in-law of Moses seeth all that he is doing to the people, and saith, `What [is] this thing which thou art doing to the people? wherefore art thou sitting by thyself, and all the people standing by thee from morning till evening?'
texts.exo.18.15: And Moses saith to his father-in-law, `Because the people come unto me to seek God;
texts.exo.18.16: when they have a matter, it hath come unto me, and I have judged between a man and his neighbour, and made known the statutes of God, and His laws.'
texts.exo.18.17: And the father-in-law of Moses saith unto him, `The thing which thou art doing [is] not good;
texts.exo.18.18: thou dost surely wear away, both thou, and this people which [is] with thee, for the thing is too heavy for thee, thou art not able to do it by thyself.
texts.exo.18.19: `Now, hearken to my voice, I counsel thee, and God is with thee: be thou for the people over-against God, and thou hast brought in the things unto God;
texts.exo.18.20: and thou hast warned them [concerning] the statutes and the laws, and hast made known to them the way in which they go, and the work which they do.
texts.exo.18.21: `And thou -- thou dost provide out of all the people men of ability, fearing God, men of truth, hating dishonest gain, and hast placed [these] over them, heads of thousands, heads of hundreds, heads of fifties, and heads of tens,
texts.exo.18.22: and they have judged the people at all times; and it hath come to pass, every great matter they bring in unto thee, and every small matter they judge themselves; and lighten it from off thyself, and they have borne with thee.
texts.exo.18.23: If thou dost this thing, and God hath commanded thee, then thou hast been able to stand, and all this people also goeth in unto its place in peace.'
texts.exo.18.24: And Moses hearkeneth to the voice of his father-in-law, and doth all that he said,
texts.exo.18.25: and Moses chooseth men of ability out of all Israel, and maketh them chiefs over the people, heads of thousands, heads of hundreds, heads of fifties, and heads of tens,
texts.exo.18.26: and they have judged the people at all times; the hard matter they bring in unto Moses, and every small matter they judge themselves.
texts.exo.18.27: And Moses sendeth his father-in-law away, and he goeth away unto his own land.
texts.exo.19.1: In the third month of the going out of the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt, in this day they have come into the wilderness of Sinai,
texts.exo.19.2: and they journey from Rephidim, and enter the wilderness of Sinai, and encamp in the wilderness; and Israel encampeth there before the mount.
texts.exo.19.3: And Moses hath gone up unto God, and Jehovah calleth unto him out of the mount, saying, `Thus dost thou say to the house of Jacob, and declare to the sons of Israel,
texts.exo.19.4: Ye -- ye have seen that which I have done to the Egyptians, and I bear you on eagles' wings, and bring you in unto Myself.
texts.exo.19.5: `And now, if ye really hearken to My voice, then ye have kept My covenant, and been to Me a peculiar treasure more than all the peoples, for all the earth [is] Mine;
texts.exo.19.6: and ye -- ye are to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation: these [are] the words which thou dost speak unto the sons of Israel.'
texts.exo.19.7: And Moses cometh, and calleth for the elders of the people, and setteth before them all these words which Jehovah hath commanded him;
texts.exo.19.8: and all the people answer together and say, `All that Jehovah hath spoken we do;' and Moses returneth the words of the people unto Jehovah.
texts.exo.19.9: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Lo, I am coming unto thee in the thickness of the cloud, so that the people hear in My speaking with thee, and also believe in thee to the age;' and Moses declareth the words of the people unto Jehovah.
texts.exo.19.10: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Go unto the people; and thou hast sanctified them to-day and to-morrow, and they have washed their garments,
texts.exo.19.11: and have been prepared for the third day; for on the third day doth Jehovah come down before the eyes of all the people, on mount Sinai.
texts.exo.19.12: `And thou hast made a border [for] the people round about, saying, Take heed to yourselves, going up into the mount, or coming against its extremity; whoever is coming against the mount is certainly put to death;
texts.exo.19.13: a hand cometh not against him, for he is certainly stoned or shot through, whether beast or man it liveth not; in the drawing out of the jubilee cornet they go up into the mount.'
texts.exo.19.14: And Moses cometh down from the mount unto the people, and sanctifieth the people, and they wash their garments;
texts.exo.19.15: and he saith unto the people, `Be ye prepared for the third day, come not nigh unto a woman.'
texts.exo.19.16: And it cometh to pass, on the third day, while it is morning, that there are voices, and lightnings, and a heavy cloud, on the mount, and the sound of a trumpet very strong; and all the people who [are] in the camp do tremble.
texts.exo.19.17: And Moses bringeth out the people to meet God from the camp, and they station themselves at the lower part of the mount,
texts.exo.19.18: and mount Sinai [is] wholly a smoke from the presence of Jehovah, who hath come down on it in fire, and its smoke goeth up as smoke of the furnace, and the whole mount trembleth exceedingly;
texts.exo.19.19: and the sound of the trumpet is going on, and very strong; Moses speaketh, and God doth answer him with a voice.
texts.exo.19.20: And Jehovah cometh down on mount Sinai, unto the top of the mount, and Jehovah calleth for Moses unto the top of the mount, and Moses goeth up.
texts.exo.19.21: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Go down, protest to the people, lest they break through unto Jehovah to see, and many of them have fallen;
texts.exo.19.22: and also the priests who are coming nigh unto Jehovah do sanctify themselves, lest Jehovah break forth on them.'
texts.exo.19.23: And Moses saith unto Jehovah, `The people [is] unable to come up unto mount Sinai, for Thou -- Thou hast protested to us, saying, Make a border [for] the mount, then thou hast sanctified it.'
texts.exo.19.24: And Jehovah saith unto him, `Go, descend, then thou hast come up, thou, and Aaron with thee; and the priests and the people do not break through, to come up unto Jehovah, lest He break forth upon them.'
texts.exo.19.25: And Moses goeth down unto the people, and saith unto them: --
texts.exo.20.1: `And God speaketh all these words, saying,
texts.exo.20.2: I [am] Jehovah thy God, who hath brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of servants.
texts.exo.20.3: `Thou hast no other Gods before Me.
texts.exo.20.4: `Thou dost not make to thyself a graven image, or any likeness which [is] in the heavens above, or which [is] in the earth beneath, or which [is] in the waters under the earth.
texts.exo.20.5: Thou dost not bow thyself to them, nor serve them: for I, Jehovah thy God, [am] a zealous God, charging iniquity of fathers on sons, on the third [generation], and on the fourth, of those hating Me,
texts.exo.20.6: and doing kindness to thousands, of those loving Me and keeping My commands.
texts.exo.20.7: `Thou dost not take up the name of Jehovah thy God for a vain thing, for Jehovah acquitteth not him who taketh up His name for a vain thing.
texts.exo.20.9: six days thou dost labour, and hast done all thy work,
texts.exo.20.10: and the seventh day [is] a Sabbath to Jehovah thy God; thou dost not do any work, thou, and thy son, and thy daughter, thy man-servant, and thy handmaid, and thy cattle, and thy sojourner who is within thy gates, --
texts.exo.20.11: for six days hath Jehovah made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that [is] in them, and resteth in the seventh day; therefore hath Jehovah blessed the Sabbath-day, and doth sanctify it.
texts.exo.20.12: `Honour thy father and thy mother, so that thy days are prolonged on the ground which Jehovah thy God is giving to thee.
texts.exo.20.16: `Thou dost not answer against thy neighbour a false testimony.
texts.exo.20.17: `Thou dost not desire the house of thy neighbour, thou dost not desire the wife of thy neighbour, or his man-servant, or his handmaid, or his ox, or his ass, or anything which [is] thy neighbour's.'
texts.exo.20.18: And all the people are seeing the voices, and the flames, and the sound of the trumpet, and the mount smoking; and the people see, and move, and stand afar off,
texts.exo.20.19: and say unto Moses, `Speak thou with us, and we hear, and let not God speak with us, lest we die.'
texts.exo.20.20: And Moses saith unto the people, `Fear not, for to try you hath God come, and in order that His fear may be before your faces -- that ye sin not.'
texts.exo.20.21: And the people stand afar off, and Moses hath drawn nigh unto the thick darkness where God [is].
texts.exo.20.22: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, `Thus dost thou say unto the sons of Israel: Ye -- ye have seen that from the heavens I have spoken with you;
texts.exo.20.23: ye do not make with Me gods of silver, even gods of gold ye do not make to yourselves.
texts.exo.20.24: `An altar of earth thou dost make for Me, and thou hast sacrificed on it thy burnt-offerings and thy peace-offerings, thy flock and thy herd; in every place where I cause My name to be remembered I come in unto thee, and have blessed thee.
texts.exo.20.25: `And if an altar of stones thou dost make to Me, thou dost not build them of hewn work; when thy tool thou hast waved over it, then thou dost pollute it;
texts.exo.20.26: neither dost thou go up by steps on Mine altar, that thy nakedness be not revealed upon it.
texts.exo.21.1: `And these [are] the judgments which thou dost set before them:
texts.exo.21.2: `When thou buyest a Hebrew servant -- six years he doth serve, and in the seventh he goeth out as a freeman for nought;
texts.exo.21.3: if by himself he cometh in, by himself he goeth out; if he [is] owner of a wife, then his wife hath gone out with him;
texts.exo.21.4: if his lord give to him a wife, and she hath borne to him sons or daughters -- the wife and her children are her lord's, and he goeth out by himself.
texts.exo.21.5: `And if the servant really say: I have loved my lord, my wife, and my sons -- I do not go out free;
texts.exo.21.6: then hath his lord brought him nigh unto God, and hath brought him nigh unto the door, or unto the side-post, and his lord hath bored his ear with an awl, and he hath served him -- to the age.
texts.exo.21.7: `And when a man selleth his daughter for a handmaid, she doth not go out according to the going out of the men-servants;
texts.exo.21.8: if evil in the eyes of her lord, so that he hath not betrothed her, then he hath let her be ransomed; to a strange people he hath not power to sell her, in his dealing treacherously with her.
texts.exo.21.9: `And if to his son he betroth her, according to the right of daughters he doth to her.
texts.exo.21.10: `If another [woman] he take for him, her food, her covering, and her habitation, he doth not withdraw;
texts.exo.21.11: and if these three he do not to her, then she hath gone out for nought, without money.
texts.exo.21.12: `He who smiteth a man so that he hath died, is certainly put to death;
texts.exo.21.13: as to him who hath not laid wait, and God hath brought to his hand, I have even set for thee a place whither he doth flee.
texts.exo.21.14: `And when a man doth presume against his neighbour to slay him with subtilty, from Mine altar thou dost take him to die.
texts.exo.21.15: `And he who smiteth his father or his mother is certainly put to death.
texts.exo.21.16: `And he who stealeth a man, and hath sold him, and he hath been found in his hand, is certainly put to death.
texts.exo.21.17: `And he who is reviling his father or his mother is certainly put to death.
texts.exo.21.18: `And when men contend, and a man hath smitten his neighbour with a stone, or with the fist, and he die not, but hath fallen on the bed;
texts.exo.21.19: if he rise, and hath gone up and down without on his staff, then hath the smiter been acquitted; only his cessation he giveth, and he is thoroughly healed.
texts.exo.21.20: `And when a man smiteth his man-servant or his handmaid, with a rod, and he hath died under his hand -- he is certainly avenged;
texts.exo.21.21: only if he remain a day, or two days, he is not avenged, for he [is] his money.
texts.exo.21.22: `And when men strive, and have smitten a pregnant woman, and her children have come out, and there is no mischief, he is certainly fined, as the husband of the woman doth lay upon him, and he hath given through the judges;
texts.exo.21.23: and if there is mischief, then thou hast given life for life,
texts.exo.21.24: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
texts.exo.21.25: burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.
texts.exo.21.26: `And when a man smiteth the eye of his man-servant, or the eye of his handmaid, and hath destroyed it, as a freeman he doth send him away for his eye;
texts.exo.21.27: and if a tooth of his man-servant or a tooth of his handmaid he knock out, as a freeman he doth send him away for his tooth.
texts.exo.21.28: `And when an ox doth gore man or woman, and they have died, the ox is certainly stoned, and his flesh is not eaten, and the owner of the ox [is] acquitted;
texts.exo.21.29: and if the ox is [one] accustomed to gore heretofore, and it hath been testified to its owner, and he doth not watch it, and it hath put to death a man or woman, the ox is stoned, and its owner also is put to death.
texts.exo.21.30: `If atonement is laid upon him, then he hath given the ransom of his life, according to all that is laid upon him;
texts.exo.21.31: whether it gore a son or gore a daughter, according to this judgment it is done to him.
texts.exo.21.32: `If the ox gore a man-servant or a handmaid, thirty silver shekels he doth give to their lord, and the ox is stoned.
texts.exo.21.33: `And when a man doth open a pit, or when a man doth dig a pit, and doth not cover it, and an ox or ass hath fallen thither, --
texts.exo.21.34: the owner of the pit doth repay, money he doth give back to its owner, and the dead is his.
texts.exo.21.35: `And when a man's ox doth smite the ox of his neighbour, and it hath died, then they have sold the living ox, and halved its money, and also the dead one they do halve;
texts.exo.21.36: or, it hath been known that the ox is [one] accustomed to gore heretofore, and its owner doth not watch it, he certainly repayeth ox for ox, and the dead is his.
texts.exo.22.1: `When a man doth steal an ox or sheep, and hath slaughtered it or sold it, five of the herd he doth repay for the ox, and four of the flock for the sheep.
texts.exo.22.2: `If in the breaking through, the thief is found, and he hath been smitten, and hath died, there is no blood for him;
texts.exo.22.3: if the sun hath risen upon him, blood [is] for him, he doth certainly repay; if he have nothing, then he hath been sold for his theft;
texts.exo.22.4: if the theft is certainly found in his hand alive, whether ox, or ass, or sheep -- double he repayeth.
texts.exo.22.5: `When a man depastureth a field or vineyard, and hath sent out his beast, and it hath pastured in the field of another, [of] the best of his field, and the best of his vineyard, he doth repay.
texts.exo.22.6: `When fire goeth forth, and hath found thorns, and a stack, or the standing corn, or the field, hath been consumed, he who causeth the burning doth certainly repay.
texts.exo.22.7: `When a man doth give unto his neighbour silver, or vessels to keep, and it hath been stolen out of the man's house; if the thief is found, he repayeth double.
texts.exo.22.8: `If the thief is not found, then the master of the house hath been brought near unto God, whether he hath not put forth his hand against the work of his neighbour;
texts.exo.22.9: for every matter of transgression, for ox, for ass, for sheep, for raiment, for any lost thing of which it is said that it is his; unto God cometh the matter of them both; he whom God doth condemn, he repayeth double to his neighbour.
texts.exo.22.10: `When a man doth give unto his neighbour an ass, or ox, or sheep, or any beast to keep, and it hath died, or hath been hurt, or taken captive, none seeing --
texts.exo.22.11: an oath of Jehovah is between them both, that he hath not put forth his hand against the work of his neighbour, and its owner hath accepted, and he doth not repay;
texts.exo.22.12: but if it is certainly stolen from him, he doth repay to its owner;
texts.exo.22.13: if it is certainly torn, he bringeth it in -- a witness; the torn thing he doth not repay.
texts.exo.22.14: `And when a man doth ask [anything] from his neighbour, and it hath been hurt or hath died -- its owner not being with it -- he doth certainly repay;
texts.exo.22.15: if its owner [is] with it, he doth not repay, -- if it [is] a hired thing, it hath come for its hire.
texts.exo.22.16: `And when a man doth entice a virgin who [is] not betrothed, and hath lain with her, he doth certainly endow her to himself for a wife;
texts.exo.22.17: if her father utterly refuse to give her to him, money he doth weigh out according to the dowry of virgins.
texts.exo.22.18: `A witch thou dost not keep alive.
texts.exo.22.19: `Whoever lieth with a beast is certainly put to death.
texts.exo.22.20: `He who is sacrificing to a god, save to Jehovah alone, is devoted.
texts.exo.22.21: `And a sojourner thou dost not oppress, nor crush him, for sojourners ye have been in the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.22.22: `Any widow or orphan ye do not afflict;
texts.exo.22.23: if thou dost really afflict him, surely if he at all cry unto Me, I certainly hear his cry;
texts.exo.22.24: and Mine anger hath burned, and I have slain you by the sword, and your wives have been widows, and your sons orphans.
texts.exo.22.25: `If thou dost lend My poor people with thee money, thou art not to him as a usurer; thou dost not lay on him usury;
