texts.exo.36.3: Y tomaron de delante de Moisés toda la ofrenda que los hijos de Israel habían traído para la obra del servicio del santuario para hacerla, y ellos le traían aun ofrenda voluntaria cada mañana.
texts.exo.36.4: Y vinieron todos los maestros que hacían toda la obra del santuario, cada uno de la obra que hacía,
texts.exo.36.5: Y hablaron a Moisés, diciendo: El pueblo trae mucho más de lo que es menester para hacer la obra para el ministerio, que Jehová ha mandado que se haga.
texts.exo.36.6: Entonces Moisés mandó pregonar por el campo, diciendo: Ningún hombre ni mujer hagan más obra para ofrecer al santuario. Y así fue el pueblo prohibido de ofrecer.
texts.exo.36.7: Y tenían hacienda abasto para hacer toda la obra, y sobraba.
texts.exo.36.8: ¶ Y todos los sabios de corazón entre los que hacían la obra, hicieron el tabernáculo de diez cortinas, de lino torcido, y de cárdeno, y de púrpura, y de carmesí, las cuales hicieron de obra de artífice con querubines.
texts.exo.36.9: La longura de la una cortina era de veinte y ocho codos, y la anchura de cuatro codos, todas las cortinas tenían una misma medida.
texts.exo.36.10: Y juntó las cinco cortinas la una con la otra, y las otras cinco cortinas juntó la una con la otra.
texts.exo.36.11: E hizo las lazadas de cárdeno en la orilla de la una cortina, en el cabo a la juntura y así hizo en la orilla en el cabo de la segunda cortina, en la juntura.
texts.exo.36.12: Cincuenta lazadas hizo en la una cortina, y otras cincuenta en la segunda cortina, en el cabo, en la juntura, las unas lazadas en frente de las otras.
texts.exo.36.13: Hizo también cincuenta corchetes de oro con los cuales juntó las cortinas la una con la otra, e hízose un tabernáculo.
texts.exo.36.14: Hizo asimismo cortinas de pelos de cabras para la tienda sobre el tabernáculo, e hízolas once.
texts.exo.36.15: La longura de la una cortina era de treinta codos, y la anchura de cuatro codos, las once cortinas tenían una misma medida.
texts.exo.36.16: Y juntó por sí las cinco cortinas, y las seis cortinas por sí.
texts.exo.36.17: E hizo cincuenta lazadas en la orilla de la postrera cortina en la juntura, y otras cincuenta lazadas en la orilla de la otra cortina en la juntura.
texts.exo.36.18: Hizo también cincuenta corchetes de metal para juntar la tienda que fuese una.
texts.exo.36.19: E hizo un cobertor para la tienda de cueros rojos de carnero, y otro cobertor encima de cueros de tejones.
texts.exo.36.20: ¶ E hizo las tablas para el tabernáculo de madera de cedro estantes.
texts.exo.36.21: La longura de cada tabla de diez codos, y de codo y medio la anchura.
texts.exo.36.22: Cada tabla tenía dos quicios enclavijados el uno delante del otro, así hizo todas las tablas del tabernáculo.
texts.exo.36.23: E hizo las tablas para el tabernáculo, veinte tablas al lado del austro, al mediodía.
texts.exo.36.24: Hizo también las cuarenta basas de plata debajo de las veinte tablas; dos basas debajo de la una tabla para sus dos quicios, y otras dos basas debajo de la otra tabla para sus dos quicios.
texts.exo.36.25: Y en el otro lado del tabernáculo, en el lado del aquilón, hizo otras veinte tablas,
texts.exo.36.26: Con sus cuarenta basas de plata, dos basas debajo de la una tabla, y otras dos basas debajo de la otra tabla.
texts.exo.36.27: Y en el lado occidental del tabernáculo hizo seis tablas.
texts.exo.36.28: A las esquinas del tabernáculo en los dos lados hizo dos tablas.
texts.exo.36.29: Las cuales se juntaban por abajo, y asimismo por arriba a una sortija; y así hizo a la una y a la otra en las dos esquinas.
texts.exo.36.30: Y así eran ocho tablas, y sus basas de plata diez y seis, dos basas debajo de cada tabla.
texts.exo.36.31: E hizo las barras de madera de cedro, cinco para las tablas del un lado del tabernáculo,
texts.exo.36.32: Y otras cinco barras para las tablas del otro lado del tabernáculo, y otras cinco barras para las tablas del lado del tabernáculo a las esquinas del occidente.
texts.exo.36.33: E hizo que la barra del medio pasase por medio de las tablas del un cabo al otro.
texts.exo.36.34: Y cubrió las tablas de oro, e hizo de oro las sortijas de ellas por donde pasasen las barras, y cubrió de oro las barras.
texts.exo.36.35: ¶ Hizo asimismo el velo de cárdeno, y púrpura, y carmesí, y lino torcido, el cual hizo de obra de artífice con querubines.
texts.exo.36.36: E hizo para él cuatro columnas de cedro, y cubriólas de oro, los capiteles de las cuales eran de oro, e hizo para ellas cuatro basas de plata de fundición.
texts.exo.36.37: ¶ Hizo asimismo el velo para la puerta del tabernáculo de cárdeno, y púrpura, y carmesí, y lino torcido, de obra de recamador;
texts.exo.36.38: Con sus cinco columnas y sus capiteles, y cubrió las cabezas de ellas y sus molduras de oro, y sus cinco basas hizo de metal.
texts.exo.37.1: Hizo también Beseleel el arca de madera de cedro, su longura era de dos codos y medio, y de codo y medio su anchura, y su altura de otro codo y medio.
texts.exo.37.2: Y cubrióla de oro puro por de dentro y por de fuera, e hízole una corona de oro al rededor.
texts.exo.37.3: Y fundióle cuatro sortijas de oro a sus cuatro esquinas, en el un lado dos sortijas, y en el otro lado otras dos sortijas.
texts.exo.37.4: Hizo también las barras de madera de cedro, y cubriólas de oro.
texts.exo.37.5: Y metió las barras por las sortijas a los lados del arca para llevar el arca.
texts.exo.37.6: ¶ Hizo asimismo la cubierta de oro puro: su longura de dos codos y medio, y su anchura de codo y medio.
texts.exo.37.7: Ítem, hizo los dos querubines de oro, los cuales hizo de martillo, a los dos cabos de la cubierta.
texts.exo.37.8: El un querubín de esta parte al un cabo, y el otro querubín de la otra parte al otro cabo de la cubierta: hizo los querubines a sus dos cabos.
texts.exo.37.9: Y los querubines extendían sus alas por encima cubriendo con sus alas la cubierta; y sus rostros el uno contra el otro, los rostros de los querubines a la cubierta.
texts.exo.37.10: ¶ Hizo también la mesa de madera de cedro, su longura de dos codos, y su anchura de un codo, y de codo y medio su altura.
texts.exo.37.11: Y cubrióla de oro puro, e hízole una corona de oro al derredor.
texts.exo.37.12: Hízole también una moldura de anchura de una mano al rededor, a la cual moldura hizo la corona de oro al derredor.
texts.exo.37.13: Hízole también de fundición cuatro sortijas de oro, y púsolas a las cuatro esquinas, que estaban a los cuatro pies de ella.
texts.exo.37.14: Delante de la moldura estaban las sortijas, por las cuales se metiesen las barras para llevar la mesa.
texts.exo.37.15: Hizo también las barras de madera de cedro para llevar la mesa, y cubriólas de oro.
texts.exo.37.16: Ítem, hizo los vasos que habían de estar sobre la mesa, sus platos, y sus cucharones, y sus cubiertas, y sus tazones con que se había de cubrir el pan, de oro fino.
texts.exo.37.17: ¶ Hizo asimismo el candelero de oro puro, el cual hizo de martillo: su pie, y su caña, sus copas, sus manzanas, y sus flores eran de lo mismo.
texts.exo.37.18: De sus lados salían seis cañas, las tres cañas del un lado del candelero, y las otras tres cañas del otro lado del candelero.
texts.exo.37.19: En la una caña había tres copas almendradas, una manzana, y una flor: y en la otra caña otras tres copas almendradas, otra manzana y otra flor: y así en todas las seis cañas que salían del candelero.
texts.exo.37.20: Y en el mismo candelero había cuatro copas almendradas, sus manzanas, y sus flores.
texts.exo.37.21: Y una manzana debajo de las unas dos cañas de lo mismo, y otra manzana debajo de las otras dos cañas de lo mismo, y otra manzana debajo de las otras dos cañas de lo mismo, por las seis cañas que salían de él.
texts.exo.37.22: Sus manzanas y sus cañas eran de lo mismo, todo era una pieza de martillo de oro puro.
texts.exo.37.23: Hizo asimismo sus candilejas siete, y sus despabiladeras, y sus paletas de oro puro.
texts.exo.37.24: De un talento de oro puro lo hizo a él y a todos sus vasos.
texts.exo.37.25: ¶ Hizo también el altar del perfume de madera de cedro: un codo su longura, y otro codo su anchura, cuadrado: y dos codos su altura, y sus cuernos eran de la misma pieza.
texts.exo.37.26: Y cubriólo de oro puro, su mesa y sus paredes al rededor, y sus cuernos: e hízole una corona de oro al derredor.
texts.exo.37.27: Hízole también dos sortijas de oro debajo de la corona en las dos esquinas a los dos lados, para pasar por ellas las barras con que había de ser llevado.
texts.exo.37.28: Y las barras hizo de madera de cedro, y cubriólas de oro.
texts.exo.37.29: ¶ Hizo asimismo el aceite de la unción santo, y el perfume aromático fino, de obra de perfumador.
texts.exo.38.1: E hizo el altar del holocausto de madera de cedro, su longura de cinco codos, y su anchura de otros cinco codos, cuadrado, y de tres codos su altura.
texts.exo.38.2: E hízole sus cuernos a sus cuatro esquinas, los cuales eran de la misma pieza, y cubriólo de metal.
texts.exo.38.3: Hizo asimismo todos los vasos del altar, calderones, y badiles, y lebrillos, y garfios, y palas: todos sus vasos hizo de metal.
texts.exo.38.4: E hizo la criba para el altar de hechura de red de metal, en su cerco debajo hasta el medio de él.
texts.exo.38.5: E hizo de fundición cuatro sortijas para la criba de metal a los cuatro cabos para meter las barras.
texts.exo.38.6: E hizo las barras de madera de cedro, y cubriólas de metal.
texts.exo.38.7: Y metió las barras por las sortijas a los lados del altar para llevarlo con ellas, el cual hizo hueco de tablas.
texts.exo.38.8: ¶ Ítem, hizo la fuente de metal y su basa de metal de los espejos de las que velaban a la puerta del tabernáculo del testimonio.
texts.exo.38.9: ¶ Ítem, hizo el patio a la parte del mediodía austral; las cortinas del patio eran de cien codos de lino torcido.
texts.exo.38.10: Sus columnas veinte, y las basas de ellas veinte de metal: los capiteles de las columnas y sus molduras de plata.
texts.exo.38.11: Y a la parte del aquilón cortinas de cien codos: sus columnas veinte, y las basas de ellas veinte, de metal: los capiteles de las columnas y sus molduras de plata.
texts.exo.38.12: A la parte del occidente cortinas de cincuenta codos: sus columnas diez, y las basas de ellas diez: los capiteles de las columnas y sus molduras de plata.
texts.exo.38.13: Y a la parte oriental al oriente, cortinas de cincuenta codos.
texts.exo.38.14: Al un lado cortinas de quince codos, sus tres columnas con sus tres basas.
texts.exo.38.15: Al otro lado de la una parte y de la otra de la puerta del patio, cortinas de a quince codos, sus tres columnas, con sus tres basas.
texts.exo.38.16: Todas las cortinas del patio al derredor eran de lino torcido.
texts.exo.38.17: Y las basas de las columnas, de metal: los capiteles de las columnas y sus molduras, de plata. Y las cubiertas de las cabezas de ellas, de plata, asimismo todas las columnas del patio tenían molduras de plata.
texts.exo.38.18: ¶ Y el pabellón de la puerta del patio de obra de recamado de cárdeno, y púrpura, y carmesí, y lino torcido: la longura de veinte codos, y la altura en la anchura de cinco codos y conforme a las cortinas del patio.
texts.exo.38.19: Y sus columnas cuatro con sus basas cuatro de metal, y sus corchetes de plata, y las cubiertas de los capiteles de ellas, y sus molduras, de plata.
texts.exo.38.20: Y todas las estacas del tabernáculo y del patio al rededor de metal.
texts.exo.38.21: Estas son las cuentas del tabernáculo, del tabernáculo del testimonio, lo cual fue contado por dicho de Moisés por mano de Itamar hijo de Aarón, sacerdote, para el ministerio de los Levitas.
texts.exo.38.22: Y Beseleel, hijo de Uri, hijo de Jur, de la tribu de Judá, hizo todas las cosas que Jehová mandó a Moisés.
texts.exo.38.23: Y con él Ooliab, hijo de Aquisamec, de la tribu de Dan, maestro e ingeniero, y recamador en cárdeno, y púrpura, y carmesí, y lino fino.
texts.exo.38.24: ¶ Todo el oro gastado en la obra, en toda la obra del santuario, el cual fue oro de ofrenda, fue veinte y nueve talentos, y sietecientos y treinta siclos, al siclo del santuario.
texts.exo.38.25: Y la plata de los contados de la congregación fue cien talentos, y mil y sietecientos y setenta y cinco siclos, al siclo del santuario.
texts.exo.38.26: Medio por cabeza, medio siclo, al siclo del santuario, a todos los que pasaron por cuenta de edad de veinte años y arriba, que fueron seiscientos y tres mil y quinientos y cincuenta.
texts.exo.38.27: Hubo además cien talentos de plata para hacer de fundición las basas del santuario, y las basas del velo, en cien basas cien talentos, a talento por basa.
texts.exo.38.28: Y de mil y siete cientos y setenta y cinco siclos hizo los capiteles de las columnas, y cubrió los capiteles de ellas, y las ciñó.
texts.exo.38.29: Y el metal de la ofrenda fue setenta talentos, y dos mil y cuatrocientos siclos.
texts.exo.38.30: Del cual hizo las basas de la puerta del tabernáculo del testimonio, y el altar de metal, y su criba de metal, y todos los vasos del altar.
texts.exo.38.31: Y las basas del patio al derredor, y las basas de la puerta del patio, y todas las estacas del tabernáculo, y todas las estacas del patio al rededor.
texts.exo.39.1: Y del cárdeno, y púrpura, y carmesí, hicieron las vestiduras del ministerio para ministrar en el santuario; y asimismo hicieron las santas vestiduras que eran para Aarón, como Jehová lo mandó a Moisés.
texts.exo.39.2: Hizo también el efod de oro, cárdeno, y púrpura, y carmesí, y lino torcido.
texts.exo.39.3: Y extendieron las planchas de oro, y cortaron los hilos para tejer entre el cárdeno, y entre la púrpura, y entre el carmesí, y entre el lino, por obra de artífice.
texts.exo.39.4: Hiciéronle los espaldares que se juntasen, y juntábanse en sus dos lados.
texts.exo.39.5: Y el cinto del efod, que estaba sobre él, era de lo mismo, conforme a su obra de oro, cárdeno, y púrpura, y carmesí, y lino torcido, como Jehová lo había mandado a Moisés.
texts.exo.39.6: Y labraron las piedras oniquinas cercadas de engastes de oro, grabadas de grabadura de sello con los nombres de los hijos de Israel:
texts.exo.39.7: Y púsolas sobre las hombreras del efod, por piedras de memoria a los hijos de Israel, como Jehová lo había mandado a Moisés.
texts.exo.39.8: Hizo también el pectoral de obra de artífice, como la obra del efod, de oro, cárdeno, y púrpura, y carmesí, y lino torcido.
texts.exo.39.9: Era cuadrado: doblado hicieron el pectoral, su longura era de un palmo, y de otro palmo su anchura, doblado.
texts.exo.39.10: Y engastaron en él cuatro ordenes de piedras. El orden era un rubí, una esmeralda, y una crisólita, el primer orden.
texts.exo.39.11: El segundo orden, un carbunclo, un zafiro, y un diamante.
texts.exo.39.12: El tercer orden, un topacio, una turquesa, y un ametisto.
texts.exo.39.13: Y el cuarto orden, un tarsis, un ónix, y un jaspe, cercadas y engastadas en sus engastes de oro.
texts.exo.39.14: Las cuales piedras eran conforme a los nombres de los hijos de Israel doce, conforme a los nombres de ellos, de grabadura de sello, cada una conforme a su nombre, según las doce tribus.
texts.exo.39.15: Hicieron también sobre el pectoral las cadenas pequeñas de hechura de trenza, de oro puro.
texts.exo.39.16: Hicieron asimismo los dos engastes, y las dos sortijas de oro, las cuales dos sortijas de oro pusieron en los dos cabos del pectoral.
texts.exo.39.17: Y pusieron las dos trenzas de oro en aquellas dos sortijas en los cabos del pectoral.
texts.exo.39.18: Y los dos cabos de las dos trenzas pusieron en los dos engastes, los cuales pusieron sobre las hombreras del efod en la parte delantera de él.
texts.exo.39.19: E hicieron otras dos sortijas de oro, que pusieron en los dos cabos del pectoral en su orilla a la parte baja del efod.
texts.exo.39.20: Hicieron más otras dos sortijas de oro, las cuales pusieron en las dos hombreras del efod abajo en la parte delantera, delante de su juntura sobre el cinto del efod.
texts.exo.39.21: Y ataron el pectoral de sus sortijas a las sortijas del mismo efod con un cordón de cárdeno, para que estuviese sobre el cinto del mismo efod, y el pectoral no se apartase del efod, como Jehová lo había mandado a Moisés.
texts.exo.39.22: Hizo también el manto del efod de obra de tejedor todo de cárdeno.
texts.exo.39.23: Con su collar en medio de él, como el collar de un coselete, con un borde al rededor del collar, porque no se rompiese.
texts.exo.39.24: E hicieron en las orillas del manto las granadas de cárdeno, y púrpura, y carmesí, y lino torcido.
texts.exo.39.25: Hicieron también las campanillas de oro puro, las cuales campanillas pusieron entre las granadas por las orillas del manto al derredor, entre las granadas.
texts.exo.39.26: Una campanilla y una granada, una campanilla y una granada, en las orillas del manto, al rededor, para ministrar, como Jehová lo mandó a Moisés.
texts.exo.39.27: E hicieron las túnicas de lino fino de obra de tejedor para Aarón, y para sus hijos.
texts.exo.39.28: Asimismo la mitra de lino fino, y las orladuras de los chapeos de lino fino, y los pañetes de lino, de lino torcido.
texts.exo.39.29: Ítem, el cinto de lino torcido, y de cárdeno, y púrpura, y carmesí, de obra de recamador, como Jehová lo mandó a Moisés.
texts.exo.39.30: Ítem, hicieron la plancha, la corona de la santidad, de oro puro, y escribieron en ella de grabadura de sello el rotulo, Santidad a Jehová.
texts.exo.39.31: Y pusieron sobre ella un cordón de cárdeno para ponerla sobre la mitra encima, como Jehová lo había mandado a Moisés.
texts.exo.39.32: ¶ Y fue acabada toda la obra del tabernáculo, del tabernáculo del testimonio. E hicieron los hijos de Israel como Jehová lo había mandado a Moisés: así lo hicieron.
texts.exo.39.33: Y trajeron el tabernáculo a Moisés; el tabernáculo y todos sus vasos, sus corchetes, sus tablas, sus barras, y sus columnas y sus basas,
texts.exo.39.34: Y la cobertura de pieles rojas de carneros, y la cobertura de pieles de tejones, y el velo del pabellón,
texts.exo.39.35: El arca del testimonio, y sus barras, y la cubierta,
texts.exo.39.36: La mesa, todos sus vasos, y el pan de la proposición,
texts.exo.39.37: El candelero limpio, sus candilejas, las candilejas de la ordenanza, y todos sus vasos, y el aceite de la luminaria,
texts.exo.39.38: Y el altar de oro, y el aceite de la unción, y el perfume aromático, y el pabellón para la puerta del tabernáculo,
texts.exo.39.39: El altar de metal, y su criba de metal, sus barras, y todos sus vasos, y la fuente y su basa,
texts.exo.39.40: Las cortinas del patio, y sus columnas y sus basas, y el pabellón para la puerta del patio, y sus cuerdas, y sus estacas, y todos los vasos del servicio del tabernáculo, del tabernáculo del testimonio,
texts.exo.39.41: Las vestiduras del servicio para ministrar en el santuario, las santas vestiduras para Aarón el sacerdote, y las vestiduras de sus hijos para ministrar en el sacerdocio.
texts.exo.39.42: Conforme a todas las cosas que Jehová había mandado a Moisés, así hicieron los hijos de Israel toda la obra.
texts.exo.39.43: Y vio Moisés toda la obra, y he aquí que la habían hecho como Jehová había mandado; y bendíjolos.
texts.exo.40.1: Y Jehová habló a Moisés, diciendo:
texts.exo.40.2: En el día del mes primero, el primero del mes harás levantar el tabernáculo, el tabernáculo del testimonio.
texts.exo.40.3: Y pondrás en él el arca del testimonio, y cubrirla has con el velo.
texts.exo.40.4: Y meterás la mesa, y ponerla has en orden: y meterás el candelero, y encenderás sus lámparas.
texts.exo.40.5: Y pondrás el altar de oro para el perfume delante del arca del testimonio: y pondrás el pabellón de la puerta del tabernáculo.
texts.exo.40.6: Después pondrás el altar del holocausto delante de la puerta del tabernáculo, del tabernáculo del testimonio.
texts.exo.40.7: Luego pondrás la fuente entre el tabernáculo del testimonio y el altar: y pondrás agua en ella.
texts.exo.40.8: Finalmente pondrás el patio al rededor, y el pabellón de la puerta del patio.
texts.exo.40.9: Y tomarás el aceite de la unción, y ungirás el tabernáculo, y todo lo que estará en él, y santificarlo has con todos sus vasos, y será santo.
texts.exo.40.10: Y ungirás también el altar del holocausto, y todos sus vasos: y santificarás el altar, y será el altar santidad de santidades.
texts.exo.40.11: Asimismo ungirás la fuente y su basa, y santificarla has.
texts.exo.40.12: Y harás llegar a Aarón y a sus hijos a la puerta del tabernáculo del testimonio, y lavarlos has con agua.
texts.exo.40.13: Y harás vestir a Aarón las santas vestiduras, y ungirle has, y consagrarle has, para que sea mi sacerdote.
texts.exo.40.14: Después harás llegar sus hijos, y vestirles has las túnicas.
texts.exo.40.15: Y ungirles has como ungiste a su padre, y serán mis sacerdotes: y será, que su unción les será por sacerdocio perpetuo por sus generaciones.
texts.exo.40.16: E hizo Moisés conforme a todo lo que Jehová le mandó: así lo hizo.
texts.exo.40.17: Así en el mes primero, en el segundo año al primero del mes, el tabernáculo fue levantado.
texts.exo.40.18: E hizo Moisés levantar el tabernáculo, y puso sus basas, y puso sus tablas, y puso sus barras, e hizo alzar sus columnas.
texts.exo.40.19: Y tendió la tienda sobre el tabernáculo, y puso el cobertor sobre el tabernáculo encima, como Jehová había mandado a Moisés.
texts.exo.40.20: Y tomó, y puso el testimonio en el arca; y puso las barras sobre el arca: y la cubierta sobre el arca encima.
texts.exo.40.21: Y metió el arca en el tabernáculo: y puso el velo de la tienda, y cubrió el arca del testimonio, como Jehová había mandado a Moisés.
texts.exo.40.22: Y puso la mesa en el tabernáculo del testimonio al lado del aquilón del pabellón fuera del velo.
texts.exo.40.23: Y sobre ella puso por orden los panes delante de Jehová, como Jehová había mandado a Moisés.
texts.exo.40.24: Y puso el candelero en el tabernáculo del testimonio en frente de la mesa, al lado del mediodía del pabellón.
texts.exo.40.25: Y encendió las lámparas delante de Jehová, como Jehová había mandado a Moisés.
texts.exo.40.26: Puso también el altar de oro en el tabernáculo del testimonio, delante del velo.
texts.exo.40.27: Y encendió sobre él el perfume aromático, como Jehová había mandado a Moisés.
texts.exo.40.28: Puso asimismo el pabellón de la puerta del tabernáculo.
texts.exo.40.29: Y puso el altar del holocausto a la puerta del tabernáculo, del tabernáculo del testimonio: y ofreció sobre el holocausto y presente, como Jehová había mandado a Moisés.
texts.exo.40.30: Y puso la fuente entre el tabernáculo del testimonio y el altar: y puso en ella agua para lavar.
texts.exo.40.31: Y lavaban en ella Moisés, y Aarón, y sus hijos sus manos y sus pies.
texts.exo.40.32: Cuando entraban en el tabernáculo del testimonio, y cuando se llegaban al altar se lavaban, como Jehová había mandado a Moisés.
texts.exo.40.33: Finalmente levantó el patio en derredor del tabernáculo y del altar, y puso el pabellón de la puerta del patio: y así acabó Moisés la obra.
texts.exo.40.34: ¶ Entonces una nube cubrió el tabernáculo del testimonio, y la gloria de Jehová hinchió el tabernáculo.
texts.exo.40.35: Y no podía Moisés entrar en el tabernáculo del testimonio, porque la nube estaba sobre él, y la gloria de Jehová lo tenía lleno.
texts.exo.40.36: Y cuando la nube se alzaba del tabernáculo, los hijos de Israel se movían en todas sus partidas.
texts.exo.40.37: Y si la nube no se alzaba, no se partían, hasta el día que ella se alzaba.
texts.exo.40.38: Porque la nube de Jehová estaba de día sobre el tabernáculo, y el fuego estaba de noche en él, en ojos de toda la casa de Israel en todas sus partidas.

texts.exo.1.1: Now, these, are the names of the Sons of Israel, who came into Egypt, with Jacob, did each man and his household come in:—
texts.exo.1.4: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
texts.exo.1.5: And it came to pass that all the persons who were descended from Jacob were seventy souls,—but, Joseph, was already in Egypt.
texts.exo.1.6: So then Joseph died and all his brethren, and all that generation.
texts.exo.1.7: But the sons of Israel, were fruitful and swarmed and multiplied and waxed mighty, with exceeding vigour,—so that the land was filled with them.
texts.exo.1.8: Then arose a new king over Egypt,—who had not known Joseph.
texts.exo.1.9: So he said, unto his people, Lo! the people of the sons of Israel are too many and mighty for us!
texts.exo.1.10: Come on! let us shew ourselves wise with regard to them, lest they so multiply that it shall come to pass when war befalleth us, that they also, shall join themselves unto them who hate us, and shall make war upon us. and then go up out of the land.
texts.exo.1.11: So they set over them chiefs of tribute, to the end they might humiliate them with their burdens,—and they built store-cities for Pharaoh, even Pithom and Raamses.
texts.exo.1.12: But the more they were humiliating them, the more, were they multiplying, and, the more, were they breaking forth, so they were filled with alarm because of the sons of Israel.
texts.exo.1.13: And the Egyptians rigorously made the sons of Israel serve;
texts.exo.1.14: and embittered their lives with harsh service, in clay and in bricks, and in all manner of service in the field,—all their service, wherein they rigorously made them serve.
texts.exo.1.15: Then said the king of Egypt to the Hebrew midwives,—of whom, the name of the one was, Shiphrah, and, the name of the other Puah;—
texts.exo.1.16: then he said—When ye act as midwives unto the Hebrew women, then shall ye look out for the sex,—If it is, a son, then shall ye kill it, But, if it is, a daughter, then shall it live.
texts.exo.1.17: But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt spake unto them,—but suffered the male children to live.
texts.exo.1.18: Then called the king of Egypt for the midwives, and said to them—Wherefore have ye done this thing, that ye should let the male children live?
texts.exo.1.19: And the midwives said unto Pharaoh. Because not like the Egyptian women, are the Hebrew women, for they are full of life, ere yet the midwife can come in unto them, they have given birth,
texts.exo.1.20: So then God dealt well with the midwives,—and the people multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty.
texts.exo.1.21: And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made for them households.
texts.exo.1.22: Then gave Pharaoh command to all his people saying—Every son that is born to the Hebrews, into the river, shall ye cast him; But every daughter, shall ye suffer to live.
texts.exo.2.1: And there went a man of the house of Levi,—and took a daughter of Levi.
texts.exo.2.2: And the woman conceived and bare a son,—and she saw him, that he was a goodly child, so she hid him three months.
texts.exo.2.3: And when she could no longer hide him, she took for him an ark of paper-reed, and covered it over with bitumen, and with pitch,—and put therein the child, and laid it among the rushes upon the bank of the river.
texts.exo.2.4: Then did his sister station herself at a distance,—to see what would be done to him.
texts.exo.2.5: So then the daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe by the river, and her, maidens, were walking by the side of the river,—when she saw the ark in the midst of the rushes, and sent her handmaid, and fetched it.
texts.exo.2.6: And she opened and beheld it—even the child, and lo! a boy weeping,—so she took pity on him, and said, Of the children of the Hebrews, is this.
texts.exo.2.7: Then said his sister unto Pharaoh’s daughter, Shall I go and call thee a nurse, of the Hebrew women,—that she may nurse for thee the child?
texts.exo.2.8: And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her—Go. So the maid went, and called the mother of the child.
texts.exo.2.9: And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her—Take this child, and nurse it for me, and, I, will give thee thy wages. So the woman took the child, and nursed it.
texts.exo.2.10: And the child grew, and she brought him in to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses, and said—For out of the water, I drew him.
texts.exo.2.11: And it came to pass in those days when Moses grew up, that he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens,—and saw, an Egyptian smiting a Hebrew—of his brethren,
texts.exo.2.12: So he turned this way and that, and when he saw that there was no man, he smote the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.
texts.exo.2.13: And he went out on the second day, and lo! two Hebrews, striving together,—so he said to him that did the wrong, Wherefore shouldest thou smite thy fellow?
texts.exo.2.14: And he said—Who hath set thee for a chief and a judge over us? To slay me, art thou thinking, as thou didst slay the Egyptian? Then was Moses afraid, and said—Surely the thing is, known!
texts.exo.2.15: So Pharaoh heard this thing, and sought to slay Moses,—and Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian and sat down by the well.
texts.exo.2.16: Now, the priest of Midian, had seven daughters,—and they came and drew and filled the troughs, to water their fathers flock.
texts.exo.2.17: Then came the shepherds, and drave them away,—so Moses rose up, and succoured them, and watered their flock,
texts.exo.2.18: Then came they in unto Reuel their father,—and he said, Wherefore have ye so early come in to-day?
texts.exo.2.19: And they said, An Egyptian, delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds,—Moreover also he drew, for us, and watered the flock.
texts.exo.2.20: And he said unto his daughters—And where is he? wherefore is it that ye left the man? Call him that he may eat bread.
texts.exo.2.21: And Moses was well-pleased to dwell with the man,—and he gave Zipporah his daughter to Moses.
texts.exo.2.22: And she bare a son, and he called his name Gershom,—for he said, A, sojourner, I am, in a strange land.
texts.exo.2.23: And it came to pass, during those many days, that the king of Egypt died, and the sons of Israel sighed by reason of the servitude and lamented,—and their cry for help went up to God, by reason of the servitude.
texts.exo.2.24: And God heard their groaning,—and God remembered his covenant, with Abraham, with Isaac and with Jacob;
texts.exo.2.25: so then, God looked upon the sons of Israel,—and God regarded.
texts.exo.3.1: Now, Moses, was shepherding the flock of Jethro his father-in-law priest of Midian,—so he led forth the flock behind the desert, and came in unto the mountain of God to Horeb.
texts.exo.3.2: Then appeared the messenger of Yahweh unto him, in a flame of fire from the midst of the thorn-bush,—so he looked and lo! the thorn-bush burning with fire and yet the thorn-bush, was not consumed.
texts.exo.3.3: And, Moses said, Let me turn aside, pray, and see this great sight,—why the thorn-bush, doth not burn up.
texts.exo.3.4: And Yahweh saw, that he turned aside to see,—so God called unto him out of the midst of the thorn-bush, and said—Moses! Moses! And he said—Behold me!
texts.exo.3.5: And he said—Do not draw nigh hither,—put off thy sandals from thy feet, for, the place whereon thou art standing is holy ground.
texts.exo.3.6: And he said—I, am the God of thy father, God of Abraham, God of Isaac and God of Jacob. And Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look upon God.
texts.exo.3.7: Then said Yahweh, I have, seen, the humiliation of my people, who are in Egypt,—and their outcry, have I heard, by reason of their task-masters, for I know their pains;
texts.exo.3.8: therefore have I come down to deliver them from the hand of the Egyptians, and to take them up out of that land, into a land good and large, into a land flowing with milk and honey,—into the place of the Canaanite and the Hittite, and the Amorite and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
texts.exo.3.9: Now, therefore, lo! the outcry of the sons of Israel, hath come in unto me,—moreover also, I have seen the oppression, wherewith the Egyptians are oppressing them.
texts.exo.3.10: Now, therefore, come thou! that I may send thee unto Pharaoh,—and bring thou forth my people—the sons of Israel—out of Egypt.
texts.exo.3.11: And Moses said unto God, Who am, I, that I should go unto Pharaoh,—and that I should bring forth the sons of Israel out of Egypt?
texts.exo.3.12: And he said—I will be with thee, and, this, to thee, [shall be] the sign, that, I have sent thee,—When thou bringest forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall do service unto God, upon this mountain.
texts.exo.3.13: And Moses said unto God—Lo! as surely as, I, go in unto the sons of Israel, and say unto them, The God of your fathers, hath sent me unto you, So surely will they say unto me—What is his name? What shall I say unto them?
texts.exo.3.14: And God said unto Moses, I Will Become whatsoever I please, And he said—Thus, shalt thou say to the sons of Israel, I Will Become hath sent me unto you.
texts.exo.3.15: And God said yet further unto Moses—Thus shalt thou say unto the sons of Israel, Yahweh God of your fathers. God of Abraham God of Isaac and God of Jacob, hath sent me unto you. This, is my name to times age-abiding, And, this, my memorial to generation after generation.
texts.exo.3.16: Go—and thou shalt gather together the elders of Israel and shalt say unto them-Yahweh God of your fathers, hath appeared unto me, the God of Abraham Isaac, and Jacob saying,—I am, concerned, for you, and for what is done to you in Egypt;
texts.exo.3.17: therefore do I say—I will bring you up out of the humiliation of Egypt, into the land of the Canaanite and the Hittite, and the Amorite and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite,—into a land flowing with milk and honey.
texts.exo.3.18: So will they hearken to thy voice,—and thou shalt go in—thou, and the elders of Israel, unto the king of Egypt and ye shall say unto him—Yahweh, God of the Hebrews, hath fallen in with us, Now, therefore let us go, we pray thee, a journey of three days into the desert, that we may sacrifice to Yahweh, our God.
texts.exo.3.19: But, I, know, that the king of Egypt will not suffer you to go,—not even by a firm hand.
texts.exo.3.20: So then I will put forth my hand and smite Egypt, with all my wonders, which I will do in the midst thereof,—and, after that, he will send you forth.
texts.exo.3.21: Thus will I give favour to this people in the eyes of the Egyptians,—so shall it come to pass that when ye do go, ye shall not go empty;
texts.exo.3.22: but every woman shall ask of her neighbour, and of her that sojourneth in her house, jewels of silver, and jewels of gold and mantles,—and ye shall put them upon your sons and upon your daughters, so shall ye spoil the Egyptians.
texts.exo.4.1: Then responded Moses, and said, And lo! they will not believe me, neither hearken to my voice,—for they will say, Yahweh, hath not appeared unto thee.
texts.exo.4.2: And Yahweh said unto him—What is this in thy hand? And he said—A staff.
texts.exo.4.3: Then said he—Cast it to the earth. And he cast it to the earth, and it became a serpent,—and Moses fled from the face thereof.
texts.exo.4.4: And Yahweh said unto Moses, Put forth thy hand, and take it by its tail: So he put forth his hand, and laid hold of it, and it became a staff in his hand:—
texts.exo.4.5: that they may believe that Yahweh, God of their fathers,—God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob hath appeared unto thee.
texts.exo.4.6: Then said Yahweh unto him, yet again—Bring, I pray thee, thy hand, into thy bosom. So he brought his hand, into his bosom,—and then took it out, and lo! his hand, was leprous,—like snow,
texts.exo.4.7: And he said—Put back thy hand into thy bosom: So he put back his hand into his bosom,—and then took it out of his bosom, and lo it had come again like his own flesh:
texts.exo.4.8: thus shall it come to pass, if they will not believe thee, nor hearken to the voice of the first sign, then will they believe the voice of the next sign;
texts.exo.4.9: and it shall come to pass if they will not believe even these two signs nor hearken to thy voice, then shalt thou take of the water of the river, and pour it out on the dry land,—so shall the water which thou hast taken from the river, become, yea it shall become, blood, on the dry land.
texts.exo.4.10: And Moses said unto Yahweh—Pardon, O My Lord! not a man of words, am I, neither heretofore, nor since thou hast spoken unto thy servant,—for heavy of mouth and heavy of tongue, I am.
texts.exo.4.11: Then Yahweh said unto him—Who appointed a mouth for man, or who appointeth him to be dumb, or deaf, or seeing or blind? Is it not I, Yahweh,?
texts.exo.4.12: Now, therefore go,—and, I, will be with thy mouth, so will I direct thee, what thou shalt speak.
texts.exo.4.13: And he said—Pardon, O My Lord! send, I pray thee by the hand of him whom thou wilt send—
texts.exo.4.14: Then was kindled the anger of Yahweh against Moses, and he said—Is there not Aaron, thy brother, the Levite? I know that he, can speak. Moreover also lo! he himself is coming forth to meet thee, as surely as he seeth thee, so surely will he rejoice in his heart.
texts.exo.4.15: Then shalt thou speak unto him, and shalt put the words in his mouth,—and, I, will be with thy mouth and with his mouth, so will I direct you what ye shall do.
texts.exo.4.16: And, he, shall speak for thee unto the people,—so shall it come to pass that he shall become thy mouth, and thou shalt become to him as God.
texts.exo.4.17: And this staff, take thou in thy hand,—wherewith thou shalt do the signs.
texts.exo.4.18: So Moses went and returned unto Jethro his father-in-law and said to him—Let me go, I pray thee, and return unto my brethren who are in Egypt, that I may see whether they are yet alive. And Jethro said to Moses: Go and prosper.
texts.exo.4.19: Then said Yahweh unto Moses in Midian, Go, return to Egypt,—for all the men are dead who were seeking thy life.
texts.exo.4.20: So Moses took his wife and his sons, and caused them to ride upon the ass, and he returned to the land of Egypt,—and Moses took the staff of God in his hand.
texts.exo.4.21: And Yahweh said unto Moses, When thou goest to return to Egypt, see as touching all the wonders which I have put in thy hand, that thou do them before Pharaoh—but, I, will let his heart wax bold, and he will not suffer the people to go.
texts.exo.4.22: Then shalt thou say unto Pharaoh, Thus, saith Yahweh—My son—my firstborn, is Israel;
texts.exo.4.23: Therefore I say unto thee, Let my son go, that he may serve me, But if thou refuse to let him go, behold, I, am going to slay, thy son, thy firstborn.
texts.exo.4.24: And it came to pass, on the way, in the resting-place for the night, that Yahweh fell upon him, and sought to kill him.
texts.exo.4.25: So Zipporah took a sharp stone and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it down at his feet,—and said—Surely, a bridegroom by rites of blood, art thou to me!
texts.exo.4.26: So he let him go, Then, it was that she said, A bridegroom by rites of blood—with regard to the rites of circumcision.
texts.exo.4.27: And Yahweh said unto Aaron, Go thy way to meet Moses, towards the desert. So he went his way, and fell in with him in the mountain of God and kissed him.
texts.exo.4.28: And Moses told Aaron, all the words of Yahweh wherewith he had sent him,—and all the signs wherewith he had charged him.
texts.exo.4.29: So Moses and Aaron went their way,—and gathered together all the elders of the sons of Israel.
texts.exo.4.30: And Aaron spake all the words which Yahweh had spoken unto Moses,—and did the signs before the eyes of the people,
texts.exo.4.31: And the people believed,—and when they heard that Yahweh had concerned himself for the sons of Israel, and that he had looked upon their humiliation, then bent they their heads and bowed themselves down.
texts.exo.5.1: And afterwards, Moses and Aaron went in and said unto Pharaoh,—Thus, saith Yahweh God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a festival to me in the desert.
texts.exo.5.2: Then said Pharaoh, Who is Yahweh that I should hearken to his voice, to let Israel go? I know not Yahweh, and certainly. Israel, will I not let go!
texts.exo.5.3: And they said, the God of the Hebrews, hath met with us,—let us go, we pray thee, a journey of three days into the desert and sacrifice to Yahweh our God, lest he fall upon us with pestilence or with sword.
texts.exo.5.4: And the king of Egypt said unto them, Wherefore O Moses and Aaron should ye loose the people from their works? Get you to your burdens.
texts.exo.5.5: And Pharaoh said, Lo! many—now, are the people of the land,—and are ye to make them rest from their burdens?
texts.exo.5.6: So then Pharaoh gave command on that day, unto the taskmasters over the people and unto their overseers—saying:
texts.exo.5.7: Ye shall no more give straw unto the people, for making the bricks as heretofore: Let them, go, themselves, so shall they gather for themselves straw:
texts.exo.5.8: Nevertheless, the fixed number of bricks, which they have been making heretofore, shall ye lay upon them, ye shall not diminish therefrom,—for idle, they are, on this account, it is that they are making an outcry, saying, We must go our way, we must sacrifice to our God.
texts.exo.5.9: The service must be made heavy on the men that they may labour on it,—and let them not pay regard to words of falsehood.
texts.exo.5.10: Then went forth the taskmasters of the people and their overseers, and spake unto the people,—saying,—Thus, saith Pharaoh, I am not going to give you straw,
texts.exo.5.11: Ye yourselves go fetch you straw, of any ye can find,—yet hath there not been diminished from your service a single thing.
texts.exo.5.12: So the people dispersed themselves throughout all the land of Egypt,—to gather stubble for straw:
texts.exo.5.13: the taskmasters, meanwhile, being urgent saying,—Complete your works, The task of a day, in its day, as when the straw was provided.
texts.exo.5.14: Then were beaten the overseers of the sons of Israel, whom the taskmasters of Pharaoh had set over them saying: Wherefore have ye not completed your task for making bricks, as heretofore, so also, yesterday and, to-day?
texts.exo.5.15: Then came in the overseers of the sons of Israel, and made outcry unto Pharaoh, saying, Wherefore shouldst thou do thus to thy servants?
texts.exo.5.16: No straw, is given to thy servants, yet bricks,—they keep saying to us—make ye! And lo, thy servants, are beaten—thou dost, therefore, wrong thy people.
texts.exo.5.17: But he said: Idle, ye are—idle, on this account, are, ye, saying, We must take our journey, we must sacrifice to Yahweh.
texts.exo.5.18: Now, therefore, go labour, but, straw, shall not be given you,—yet the tale of bricks, shall ye render.
texts.exo.5.19: Then did the overseers of the sons of Israel see themselves to be in an evil case, when it was said,—Ye shall not diminish from your bricks—the task of a day, in its day
texts.exo.5.20: So they fell upon Moses and upon Aaron, stationing themselves to meet them,—as they came forth from Pharaoh;
texts.exo.5.21: and they said unto them, Yahweh look upon you and judge,—in that ye have made us odious in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants, putting a sword into their hand to slay us.
texts.exo.5.22: And Moses returned unto Yahweh and said,—O My Lord wherefore hast thou caused harm to this people? Wherefore now didst thou send me?
texts.exo.5.23: seeing that from what time I came in unto Pharaoh to speak in thy name, he hath done harm to this people, and thou hast not delivered, thy people,
texts.exo.6.1: Then said Yahweh unto Moses, Now, shalt thou see, what I will do to Pharaoh, for with a strong hand, shall he let them go, and with a strong hand, shall he drive them out from his land.
texts.exo.6.2: And God spake unto Moses,—and said unto him, I, am Yahweh:
texts.exo.6.3: I appeared, therefore, unto Abraham unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, as GOD Almighty,—although, by my name Yahweh was I not made known to them;
texts.exo.6.4: Moreover also I established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan,—even the land of their sojournings wherein they sojourned.
texts.exo.6.5: Moreover also, I heard the groaning of the sons of Israel, whom the Egyptians, were holding in servitude, So then I remembered my covenant.
texts.exo.6.6: Therefore say thou to the sons of Israel-I, am Yahweh, Therefore will I bring you forth from under the burdens of Egypt, And will deliver you out of their service, And will redeem you with a stretched-out arm, and with great judgments;
texts.exo.6.7: And will take you to myself for a people, And will become your God,—And ye shall know that, I Yahweh, am your God, who brought you forth from under the burdens of Egypt:
texts.exo.6.8: And I will bring you into the land as to which I uplifted my hand to give it to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob,—and will give it to you as an inheritance: I, am Yahweh.
texts.exo.6.9: And Moses spake thus unto the sons of Israel, but they hearkened not unto Moses, through shortness of spirit, and through hard service.
texts.exo.6.10: And Yahweh spake unto Moses saying:
texts.exo.6.11: Go in speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, that he let the sons of Israel go out of his land.
texts.exo.6.12: And Moses spake before Yahweh, saying,—Lo! the sons of Israel have not hearkened unto me, how then shall Pharaoh, hear, I, also being of uncircumcised lips.
texts.exo.6.13: Thus then did Yahweh speak unto Moses and unto Aaron, yea he gave them a charge unto the sons of Israel, and unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, for the bringing forth of the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.6.14: These, are the heads of their ancestral house: The sons of Reuben the first-born of Israel, Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi. These are the families of, Reuben.
texts.exo.6.15: And, the sons of Simeon, Jemuel and Jamin and Ohad and Jachin and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitess. These, are the families of, Simeon.
texts.exo.6.16: And, these, are the names of the sons of Levi by their generations, Gershon, and Kohath and Merari, And, the years of the life of Levi, were a hundred and thirty-seven years.
texts.exo.6.17: The sons of Gershon, Libni and Shimei by their families.
texts.exo.6.18: And the sons of Kohath, Amram and Izhar, and Hebron and Uzziel. And the years of the life of Kohath, were a hundred and thirty-three years.
texts.exo.6.19: And the sons of Merari, Mahli and Mushi. These, are the families of the Levites by their generations.
texts.exo.6.20: So then, Amram took Jochebed, his father’s sister to himself to wife, and she bare to him—Aaron and Moses. And, the years of the life of Amram, were a hundred and thirty-seven.
texts.exo.6.21: And the sons of Izhar, Korah and Nepheg, and Zichri.
texts.exo.6.22: And the sons of Uzziel, Mishael and Elzaphan, and Sithri.
texts.exo.6.23: And Aaron took Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Nahshon, to himself to wife,—and she bare to him—Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
texts.exo.6.24: And the sons of Korah, Assir and Elkanah, and Abiasaph. These are the families of the Korahites.
texts.exo.6.25: And Eleazar, son of Aaron took to himself [one] of the daughters of Putiel, to himself to wife, and she bare to him Phinehas. These, are the heads of the fathers of the Levites by their families.
texts.exo.6.26: The same, Aaron and Moses,—to whom said Yahweh, Bring ye forth the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt, according to their hosts:
texts.exo.6.27: They who were to speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring forth the sons of Israel out of Egypt: The same, Moses and Aaron.
texts.exo.6.28: Thus came it to pass, that on a certain day, Yahweh spake unto Moses in the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.6.29: So then Yahweh spake unto Moses, saying—I, am Yahweh: Speak thou unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, all that, I, am speaking unto thee.
texts.exo.6.30: And Moses said before Yahweh,—Lo! I, am of uncircumcised lips, how then will Pharaoh hearken unto me?
texts.exo.7.1: Then said Yahweh unto Moses—See! I have appointed thee to be God unto Pharaoh,—and, Aaron thy brother, shall be thy prophet!
texts.exo.7.2: Thou, shalt speak all that which I may command thee, and, Aaron thy brother, shall speak unto Pharaoh, and he shall let the sons of Israel go out of his land.
texts.exo.7.3: But, I, will suffer Pharaoh to harden his heart,—so will I multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.7.4: And Pharaoh will not hearken unto you, so will I lay my hand on Egypt,—and bring forth my hosts—my people the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt, with great judgments.
texts.exo.7.5: And the Egyptians shall know that I, am Yahweh, when I have stretched forth my hand over Egypt,—and brought forth the sons of Israel out of their midst.
texts.exo.7.6: And Moses and Aaron did [so],—as Yahweh commanded them, so, did they.
texts.exo.7.7: Now Moses, was eighty years old, and, Aaron, eighty-three years old,—when they spake unto Pharaoh.
texts.exo.7.8: And Yahweh spake unto Moses and unto Aaron saying:
texts.exo.7.9: When Pharaoh shall speak unto you saying, Shew for yourselves a wonder, then shalt thou say unto Aaron, Take thy staff, and cast it down before Pharaoh let it become a sea-serpent.
texts.exo.7.10: So Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharaoh, and did so as Yahweh had commanded,—and Aaron cast down his staff before Pharaoh and before his servants and it became a sea-serpent,
texts.exo.7.11: Then called Pharaoh also for the wise men and for the magicians,—and they too, the sacred scribes of Egypt with their secret arts, did in like manner;
texts.exo.7.12: yea they cast down each man his staff, and they became sea-serpents,—but Aaron’s staff swallowed up their staves.
texts.exo.7.13: Then waxed bold the heart of Pharaoh, and he hearkened not unto them,—as spake Yahweh.
texts.exo.7.14: Then said Yahweh unto Moses, Dull, is the heart of Pharaoh,—he hath refused to let the people go.
texts.exo.7.15: Get thee unto Pharaoh in the morning—lo! he is coming out to the waters, therefore shalt thou station thyself to meet him on the bank of the river,—and the staff which was turned into a serpent, shalt thou take in thy hand.
texts.exo.7.16: Then shalt thou say unto him—Yahweh God of the Hebrews hath sent me unto thee saying,—Let my people go, that they may serve me in the desert,—And lo! thou hast not hearkened hitherto.
texts.exo.7.17: Thus, saith Yahweh, Hereby, shalt thou know that, I, am Yahweh,—Lo! I, am smiting with the staff that is in my hand upon the waters that are in the river and they shall be turned to blood;
texts.exo.7.18: and, the fish that is in the river shall die and the river shall be loathsome,—and the Egyptians, shall disdain, to drink water out of the river.
texts.exo.7.19: And Yahweh said unto Moses,—Say unto Aaron—Take thy staff, and stretch forth thy hand over the waters of Egypt, over their streams over their rivers, and over their pools and over all their collections of water—that they may become blood,—so shall there be blood in all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood and in vessels of stone.
texts.exo.7.20: And Moses and Aaron, did so, as Yahweh commanded, and he lifted high the staff, and smote the waters which were in the river, before the eyes of Pharaoh, and before the eyes of his servants,—and all the waters which were in the river were turned to blood;
texts.exo.7.21: and the fish that was in the river, died and the river became loathsome, so that the Egyptians could not drink water out of the river,—thus came it to pass that blood was in all the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.7.22: And the sacred scribes of Egypt did in like manner with their secret arts,—so the heart of Pharaoh waxed bold and he hearkened not unto them, as spake Yahweh.
texts.exo.7.23: Then Pharaoh, turned away, and entered into his house—neither applied he his heart, even to this.
texts.exo.7.24: And all the Egyptians digged round about the river for water to drink,—for they could not drink of the water of the river.
texts.exo.7.25: And seven days were fulfilled,—after Yahweh had smitten the river.
texts.exo.8.1: Then said Yahweh unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh,—then shalt thou say unto him—Thus, saith Yahweh,—Let my people go, that they may serve me.
texts.exo.8.2: But if thou art, refusing, to let them go, lo! I, am plaguing all thy boundaries with frogs;
texts.exo.8.3: so shall the river swarm with frogs, and they shall come up, and enter into thy house, and into thy bedchamber and upon thy couch,—and into the house of thy servants and among thy people, and into thine ovens and into thy kneading-troughs:
texts.exo.8.4: both against thee, and against thy people, and against all thy servants, shall come up the frogs.
texts.exo.8.5: Then said Yahweh unto Moses, Say unto Aaron—Stretch forth thy hand with thy staff, over the streams over the rivers and over the pools,—and bring up the frogs, over the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.8.6: So Aaron stretched forth his hand, over the waters of Egypt,—and the frog came up, and covered the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.8.7: And the sacred scribes did in like manner, with their secret arts,—and brought up frogs over the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.8.8: Then called Pharaoh for Moses and for Aaron and said—Make entreaty unto Yahweh, that he take away the frogs from me and from my people,—and I must let the people go that they may sacrifice to Yahweh.
texts.exo.8.9: And Moses said to Pharaoh—Explain thyself unto me: For what time, shall I make entreaty for thee and for thy servants and for thy people, to cause the frogs to be cut off, from thee and from thy houses,—only in the river, shall they remain?
texts.exo.8.10: And he said—For to-morrow. And he said—According to thy word! that thou mayest know that there is none like Yahweh, our God:
texts.exo.8.11: so the frogs shall depart—from thee and from thy houses and from thy servants and from thy people,—only in the river, shall they remain.
texts.exo.8.12: Then went forth Moses and Aaron from Pharaoh,—and Moses made outcry unto Yahweh, over the matter of the frogs which he had appointed for Pharaoh.
texts.exo.8.13: And Yahweh did according to the word of Moses,—and the frogs died, out of the houses and out of the yards, and out of the fields;
texts.exo.8.14: and they piled them up, heaps—heaps,—and the land became loathsome.
texts.exo.8.15: But when Pharaoh saw that there had come a respite, then made he his heart dull and hearkened not unto them,—as spake Yahweh.
texts.exo.8.16: Then said Yahweh unto Moses, Say unto Aaron—Stretch forth thy staff, and smite the dust of the land,—so shall it become gnats in all the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.8.17: And they did so, and Aaron stretched forth his hand with his staff and smote the dust of the land, and there canto to be gnats, among men and among beasts,—all the dust of the land, became gnats, in all the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.8.18: And the sacred scribes did in like manner with their secret arts, to bring forth the gnats, but they could not. So there came to be gnats, among men and among beasts.
texts.exo.8.19: Then said the sacred scribes unto Pharaoh, The finger of God, it is! But the heart of Pharaoh waxed bold and he hearkened not unto them, as spake Yahweh.
texts.exo.8.20: Then said Yahweh unto Moses—Rise thou early in the morning, and station thyself before Pharaoh, lo! he is coming forth to the waters,—then shalt thou say unto him—Thus, saith Yahweh: Let my people go, that they may serve me.
texts.exo.8.21: But if thou art not letting my people go, behold me! sending forth—against thee, and against thy servants, and against thy people, and against thy houses the gad-fly,—and the houses of the Egyptians shall be full of the gad-fly, moreover also the ground whereon, they are:
texts.exo.8.22: then will I make to differ on that day, the land of Goshen wherein my people do dwell, so that there shall not be there a gad-fly! in order that thou mayest know, that I, Yahweh, am in the midst of the land;
texts.exo.8.23: so will I put a separation betwixt my people and thy people. By to-morrow, shall come to pass this sign.
texts.exo.8.24: And Yahweh did so, and brought a grievous gad-fly unto the house of Pharaoh and the houses of his servants and in all the land of Egypt, and the land was laid waste by reason of the gad-fly.
texts.exo.8.25: Then did Pharaoh cry out—unto Moses and to Aaron,—and said-Go your way, sacrifice to your God, in the land.
texts.exo.8.26: And Moses said: Not meet, is it, to do thus, for, an abomination to the Egyptians, we should sacrifice to Yahweh our God. Lo! could we sacrifice that which is an abomination to the Egyptians before their eyes and they not stone us?
texts.exo.8.27: A journey of three days, must we go, in the desert,—then will we sacrifice to Yahweh our God, as, Yahweh, hath said unto us.
texts.exo.8.28: Then said Pharaoh: I, will let you go—so shall ye sacrifice to Yahweh your God in the desert, only ye shall not go a, very long, journey,—make ye entreaty for me.
texts.exo.8.29: And Moses said: Lo! I, am going out from thee and will make entreaty unto Yahweh, so will he take away the gad-fly—from Pharaoh from his servants, and from his people tomorrow,—only let not Pharaoh again deceive, in not letting the people go, to sacrifice to Yahweh.
texts.exo.8.30: So Moses went out from Pharaoh,—and made entreaty unto Yahweh.
texts.exo.8.31: And Yahweh did according to the word of Moses, and took away the gad-fly, from Pharaoh from his servants and from his people,—there remained not, one.
texts.exo.8.32: And Pharaoh made his heart dull, this time also,—and did not let the people go.
texts.exo.9.1: Then said Yahweh unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh,—then shalt thou say unto him—Thus, saith Yahweh, God of the Hebrews, Let my people go, that they may serve me.
texts.exo.9.2: But, if, refusing, thou art to let them go,—and still art holding them fast,
texts.exo.9.3: lo! the hand of Yahweh, is coming on thy cattle which are in the field, on the horses, on the asses on the camels, on the herds and on the flocks,—a very grievous pestilence;
texts.exo.9.4: and Yahweh will make a difference between the cattle of Israel and the cattle of the Egyptians,—so that there shall not die from among all that pertaineth to the sons of Israel, a thing!
texts.exo.9.5: And Yahweh appointed a set time—saying, To-morrow, will Yahweh do this thing, in the land.
texts.exo.9.6: So Yahweh did this thing, on the morrow, and all the cattle of the Egyptians died,—but of the cattle of the sons of Israel, died not one.
texts.exo.9.7: And Pharaoh sent, and lo! there had not died of the cattle of Israel, so much as one. But Pharaoh’s heart became dull, and he did not let the people go.
texts.exo.9.8: Then said Yahweh unto Moses and unto Aaron, Take you your hands full of the ashes of an oven,—and Moses shall scatter them towards the heavens, before the eyes of Pharaoh:
texts.exo.9.9: then shall they become fine dust, over all the land of Egypt,—and shall become on man and on beast, a burning sore, breaking out in pustules in all the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.9.10: So they took the ashes of an oven and stood before Pharaoh, and Moses scattered them towards the heavens,—and it came to pass that there was a burning sore in pustules breaking out, among men, and among beasts;
texts.exo.9.11: and the sacred scribes could not stand before Moses, because of the burning sore,—for the burning sore had come on the sacred scribes, and on all the Egyptians.
texts.exo.9.12: But Yahweh let the heart of Pharaoh wax bold, and he hearkened not unto them,—as spake Yahweh unto Moses.
texts.exo.9.13: Then said Yahweh unto Moses, Rise thou early in the morning, and station thyself before Pharaoh,—then shalt thou say unto him—Thus, saith Yahweh, God of the Hebrews, Let my people go that they may serve me;
texts.exo.9.14: for this time, am I, sending all my plagues unto thy heart, and amongst thy servants and amongst thy people,—to the intent thou mayest get to know, that there is none like me in all the earth.
texts.exo.9.15: For now, might I have put forth my hand, and smitten thee and thy people with pestilence,—and thou shouldst have secretly disappeared from the earth;
texts.exo.9.16: but, in very deed for this purpose, have I let thee remain, for the purpose of showing thee my might,—and that my name may be celebrated in all the earth.
texts.exo.9.17: Even yet, art thou exalting thyself over my people—in not letting them go?
texts.exo.9.18: Behold me! raining down, about this time to-morrow, an exceeding heavy hail,—such as hath not been in Egypt, from the day it was founded, even unto the present time.
texts.exo.9.19: Now, therefore, send—bring into safety thy cattle, and all that thou hast in the field,—as touching all men and beasts which shall be found in the field and shall not be withdrawn into shelter, the hail shall come down upon them and they shall die.
texts.exo.9.20: He that feared the word of Yahweh, among the servants of Pharaoh, made his servants and his cattle flee, under shelter:
texts.exo.9.21: but, whoso applied not his heart unto the word of Yahweh, left his servants and his cattle in the field.
texts.exo.9.22: Then said Yahweh unto Moses—Stretch forth thy hand over the heavens, that there may be hail in all the land of Egypt,—on man and on beast, and on every herb of the field in the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.9.23: So Moses stretched forth his staff over the heavens, and, Yahweh, gave forth thunderings and hail, and there came fire towards the earth,—and Yahweh rained down hail, on the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.9.24: So there came to be hail, and fire catching hold of itself, in the midst of the hail,—exceeding heavy, such as had not been in all the land of Egypt, from the very time it became a nation.
texts.exo.9.25: And the hail smote in all the land of Egypt all that was in the field, both man and beast,—and every herb of the field, did the hail smite, and every tree of the field, did it shiver.
texts.exo.9.26: Only in the land of Goshen, where were the sons of Israel, was there no hail.
texts.exo.9.27: Then sent Pharaoh, and called for Moses and for Aaron, and said unto them—I have sinned this time,—Yahweh, is the righteous one, and, I and my people, are the wrong-doers.
texts.exo.9.28: Make ye request unto Yahweh, and it shall be enough without there being any more thunderings of God, and hail,—and I must a let you go, and not again shall ye delay.
texts.exo.9.29: And Moses said unto him, As soon as I am gone out of the city, will I spread out my hands unto Yahweh,—the thunderings, shall cease, and, the hail, shall come no more,—that thou mayest know, that to Yahweh, belongeth the earth.
texts.exo.9.30: But as touching thee and thy servants, I know that not yet will ye stand in awe of Yahweh Elohim.
texts.exo.9.31: Now, the flax and the barley, were smitten,—for the barley, was in the ear, and, the flax, was in flower;
texts.exo.9.32: but the wheat and the spelt, were not smitten,—for they were, not ripe.
texts.exo.9.33: So Moses went away from Pharaoh out of the city, and spread out his hands unto Yahweh,—then did the thunderings and the hail cease, and, rain, was not poured out on the earth.
texts.exo.9.34: And when Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunderings had ceased, he again sinned,—and made his heart dull, he, and his servants.
texts.exo.9.35: And the heart of Pharaoh waxed bold, and he did not let the sons of Israel go,—as spake Yahweh by the hand of Moses.
texts.exo.10.1: Then said Yahweh unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh,—for, I, have suffered his heart to be dull and the heart of his servants, that I may show these my signs, in their midst;
texts.exo.10.2: and that thou mayest recount in the ears of thy son and thy sons’ son, what I did in derision of the Egyptians, and my signs which I displayed among them,—so shall ye know that I, am Yahweh.
texts.exo.10.3: And Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharaoh, and said unto him—Thus, saith Yahweh, God of the Hebrews, How long hast thou refused to humble thyself before me? Let my people go that they may serve me.
texts.exo.10.4: But if, refusing, thou art to let my people go, behold me bringing in tomorrow a locust within thy bounds;
texts.exo.10.5: and it shall cover the eye of the land, so that one shall not be able to see the land,—and it shall eat the residue that hath escaped, that is left you from the hail, and shall eat up all the trees that sprout for you out of the field;
texts.exo.10.6: and they shall fill thy houses, and the houses of all thy servants and the houses of all the Egyptians, such as thy fathers and thy fathers’ fathers have never seen, from the day they came to be on the ground, until this day. And he turned away, and came out from the presence of Pharaoh.
texts.exo.10.7: Then said the servants of Pharaoh unto him, How long shall this [man] become to us a snare? Let the men go, that they may serve Yahweh their God. Not yet, knowest thou, that Egypt is, ruined?
texts.exo.10.8: So Moses and Aaron were brought back unto pharaoh, and he said unto them—Go, serve Yahweh your God,—who, are they that are going?
texts.exo.10.9: And Moses said, With our young and with our old, will we go,—with our sons and with our daughters with our flocks and with our herds, will we go,—for, the festival of Yahweh, is ours.
texts.exo.10.10: Then he said unto them: Let Yahweh, so, be with you, when I let go you and your little ones! Look out for, harm, is straight before your faces.
texts.exo.10.11: Not so! Go, I pray you, ye grown men and serve Yahweh, for, that, is what, ye, were seeking. And they were driven out from the presence of Pharaoh.
texts.exo.10.12: Then said Yahweh unto Moses—Stretch forth thy hand over the land of Egypt for the locust, that it may come up over the land of Egypt,—and may eat up every herb of the land, all that the hail hath left.
texts.exo.10.13: And Moses stretched forth his staff over the land of Egypt, and, Yahweh, caused an east wind to drive through the land, all that day, and all the night,—when the morning, had come, the east wind, had brought the locust.
texts.exo.10.14: And the locust came up over all the land of Egypt, and settled in all the bounds of Egypt,—very grievous, before it, had not been such a locust as that, neither after it, should be one like it.
texts.exo.10.15: So it covered the eye of all the land and the land was darkened, and it did eat every herb of the land and all the fruit of the trees, which the hail had left remaining,—so that there was not left remaining any green sprout in the trees or in the herb of the field in all the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.10.16: Then hastened Pharaoh, to call for Moses and for Aaron,—and said—I have sinned against Yahweh your God, and against you.
texts.exo.10.17: Now, therefore, forgive I pray you my sin—only this time, and make entreaty to Yahweh your God,—that he may take away from me, at least, this death.
texts.exo.10.18: So he came out from Pharaoh,—and made entreaty unto Yahweh;
texts.exo.10.19: and Yahweh turned back a west wind strong exceedingly, and carried away the locust and cast it into the Red Sea,—there was not left a single locust in all the bounds of Egypt.
texts.exo.10.20: But Yahweh suffered the heart of Pharaoh to wax bold,—and he did not let the sons of Israel go.
texts.exo.10.21: Then said Yahweh unto Moses: Stretch forth thy hand over the heavens, that there may be darkness, over the land of Egypt,—and that one may feel the darkness.
texts.exo.10.22: So Moses stretched forth his hand over the heavens,—and there was thick darkness in all the land of Egypt for three days;
texts.exo.10.23: they saw not one another neither rose any man from his couch for three days,—but all the sons of Israel, had light in their dwellings.
texts.exo.10.24: Then Pharaoh called out unto Moses and said—Go serve Yahweh, only, your flocks and your herds, shall be left,—even your little ones shall go with you.
texts.exo.10.25: And Moses said, Even thou thyself, shalt give into our hands sacrifices and ascending-offerings,—so shall we present offerings to Yahweh our God.
texts.exo.10.26: Moreover also, our own cattle, shall go with us—there shall not be left behind, a hoof, for thereof, must we take, to serve Yahweh our God,—even we ourselves, cannot know wherewith we must serve Yahweh, until we have come in thither.
texts.exo.10.27: And Yahweh let the heart of Pharaoh wax bold,—and he was not willing to let them go.
texts.exo.10.28: So Pharaoh said to him—Get thee from me,—take heed to thyself—do not any more! see my face, for in the day thou dost see my face, thou shalt die.
texts.exo.10.29: And Moses said—Well hast thou spoken,—no more again to see thy face.
texts.exo.11.1: Then said Yahweh unto Moses—Yet one plague, will I bring in upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt, after that, he will let you go from hence,—when he doth let you go, he will, altogether drive, you out from hence.
texts.exo.11.2: Speak, I pray you, in the ears of the people,—and let them ask—every man of his neighbour, and every woman of her neighbour, articles of silver and articles of gold.
texts.exo.11.3: And Yahweh gave the people favour, in the eyes of the Egyptians,—even the man Moses himself, was exceeding great in the land of Egypt,—in the eyes of Pharaoh’s servants and in the eyes of the people.
texts.exo.11.4: And Moses said, Thus saith Yahweh,—About midnight, am, I, going forth in the midst of Egypt;
texts.exo.11.5: then shall every firstborn in the land of Egypt die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who is sitting on his throne, unto the firstborn of the handmaid who is behind the two millstones,—and every firstborn of beasts;
texts.exo.11.6: then shall there be a great outcry, in all the land of Egypt,—such, as never was and, such, as shall not be again.
texts.exo.11.7: But against none of the sons of Israel, shall a dog sharpen his tongue, neither against man nor beast,—that ye may know that Yahweh maketh a difference between Egypt and Israel.
texts.exo.11.8: So shall all these thy servants come down unto me and bow themselves down to me saying—Go forth, thou and all the people who are in thy footsteps, and after that, will I go forth. And he went forth from Pharaoh, in a heat of anger.
texts.exo.11.9: And Yahweh had said unto Moses, Pharaoh will not hearken unto you,—that my wonders may be multiplied in the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.11.10: So then, Moses and Aaron, did all these wonders before Pharaoh,—but Yahweh let Pharaoh’s heart wax bold, and he did not let the sons of Israel go out of his land.
texts.exo.12.1: Then spake Yahweh, unto Moses and unto Aaron, in the land of Egypt saying—
texts.exo.12.2: This month, is, to you, a beginning of months,—the first, it is, to you, of the months of the year.
texts.exo.12.3: Speak ye unto all the assembly of Israel, saying, On the tenth of this month, then let them take to them, each man a lamb for his ancestral household, a lamb for a household.
texts.exo.12.4: But if the household be too small for a lamb, then shall he and his neighbour that is near unto his house take one, according to the number of souls,—each man according to his eating, shall ye number for the lamb.
texts.exo.12.5: A lamb without defect a male a year old, shall yours be,—from the sheep or from the goats, shall ye take it.
texts.exo.12.6: So shall it be yours, to keep, until the fourteenth day of this month,—then shall all the convocation of the assembly of Israel slay it between the two evenings.
texts.exo.12.7: And they shall take of the blood, and put upon the two door-posts and upon the upper-beam,—upon the houses wherein they are to eat it.
texts.exo.12.8: Then shall they eat the flesh, in the same night,—roast with fire, and with unleavened cakes, with bitter herbs, shall they eat it.
texts.exo.12.9: Do not eat of it underdone, nor cooked by boiling in water,—but roast with fire, its head with its legs, and with its inward parts.
texts.exo.12.10: And ye shall let nothing thereof remain until morning,—but that which is left remaining until morning, in the fire shall ye consume.
texts.exo.12.11: And, thus, shall ye eat it,—your loins, girded, your sandals, on your feet, and, your staff, in your hand,—so shall ye eat it in haste, it is Yahweh’s, passing over.
texts.exo.12.12: I will pass along, therefore, throughout the land of Egypt this night, and will smite every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from man even to beast,—and against all the gods of Egypt, will I execute judgments—I, Yahweh.
texts.exo.12.13: Then shall the blood serve you for a sign, on the houses wherein ye are, then will I behold the blood, and will pass over you,—and there shall be among you no plague to destroy, when I smite the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.12.14: So shall this day serve you for a memorial, and ye shall celebrate it, as a festival to Yahweh,—to your generations—as an age-abiding statute, shall ye celebrate it.
texts.exo.12.15: Seven days, unleavened cakes, shall ye eat, surely, on the first day, shall ye put away leaven, out of your houses,—for whosoever eateth what is leavened, then shall that soul be cut off out of Israel, from the first day, unto the seventh day.
texts.exo.12.16: Both on the first day, a holy convocation, and on the seventh day—a holy convocation, shall there be to you,—no work, shall be done therein, save only what must be eaten by every soul, that alone, shall be done by you.
texts.exo.12.17: So then ye shall observe the unleavened cakes, because on this self-same day, brought I forth your hosts out of the land of Egypt,—so then ye shall observe this day to your generations, as a statute age-abiding,
texts.exo.12.18: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month in the evening, shall ye eat unleavened cakes,—until the one-and-twentieth day of the month in the evening,
texts.exo.12.19: For seven days, leaven, shall not be found in your houses,—for, whosoever eateth what is leavened, then shall that soul be cut off out of the assembly of Israel, whether sojourner or native of the land.
texts.exo.12.20: Nothing leavened, shall ye eat,—in all your dwellings, shall ye eat unleavened cakes.
texts.exo.12.21: So then Moses called for all the elders of Israel, and said unto them,—Proceed and take for yourselves one of the flock according to your families, and slay the passover.
texts.exo.12.22: Then shall ye take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood which is in the basin, and strike the upper beam and the two door-posts, with the blood which is in the basin,—and, ye, shall not go forth any man out of the entrance of his house, until morning,
texts.exo.12.23: And Yahweh will pass along to plague the Egyptians, and when he beholdeth the blood upon the upper beam and upon the two door-posts, then will Yahweh pass over the entrance, and not suffer the destroyer to enter into your houses to inflict on you the plague.
texts.exo.12.24: And ye shall observe this thing,—for a statute to thee and to thy sons unto times age-abiding.
texts.exo.12.25: And so it shall come to pass when ye shall enter into the land which Yahweh will give you as he hath spoken,—and ye shall observe this service;
texts.exo.12.26: and it shall come to pass that your sons shall say unto you,—What is this your service?
texts.exo.12.27: Then shall ye say—A passover sacrifice, it is to Yahweh, who passed-over the houses of the sons of Israel, in Egypt, when he plagued the Egyptians but our houses, he delivered. Then did the people bend their heads and bow themselves down.
texts.exo.12.28: And the sons of Israel went their way and did,—as Yahweh had commanded Moses and Aaron, so, did they.
texts.exo.12.29: And it came to pass, at midnight, that Yahweh, smote every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat upon his throne, unto the firstborn of the captive who was in the pit of his prison,—and every firstborn of beasts.
texts.exo.12.30: Then rose up Pharaoh by night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians, and there arose a great outcry throughout Egypt,—for there was not a house, where there was not one dead.
texts.exo.12.31: So he called for Moses and for Aaron by night and said—Rise ye, go forth out of the midst of my people, both ye and the sons of Israel,—and go serve Yahweh according to your word;
texts.exo.12.32: also, your flocks and your herds, take ye, as ye spake and go your way,—so shall ye bless, even me.
texts.exo.12.33: And the Egyptians became urgent with the people, to send them in haste out of the land,—for they said—We all, are dying.
texts.exo.12.34: So the people took up their dough, ere yet it was leavened,—with their kneading-bowls, bound up in their mantles on their shoulders,
texts.exo.12.35: And the sons of Israel, did according to the word of Moses,—and asked of the Egyptians, articles of silver and articles of gold and mantles.
texts.exo.12.36: And Yahweh, gave the people favour in the eyes of the Egyptians and they gave them gladly,—so they spoiled the Egyptians.
texts.exo.12.37: Then did the sons of Israel break up from Rameses, towards Succoth,—about six hundred thousand foot of men grown, besides little ones.
texts.exo.12.38: Moreover also, a mixed multitude, came up with them,—flocks also, and herds, exceeding much cattle,
texts.exo.12.39: Then baked they the dough which they had brought out of Egypt—into round unleavened cakes for it had not been leavened,—for they had been driven out of Egypt and could not tarry, and indeed no provisions, had they made ready for themselves.
texts.exo.12.40: Now, the time during which the sons of Israel dwelt in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years.
texts.exo.12.41: And it came to pass at the end of four hundred and thirty years, yea it came to pass, on this self-same day, that all the hosts of Yahweh had come forth out of the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.12.42: A night of solemn observances, it is unto Yahweh, for bringing them forth out of the land of Egypt,—this same night, pertaineth to Yahweh, for solemn observances by all the sons of Israel to their generations.
texts.exo.12.43: And Yahweh said unto Moses and Aaron: This, is the statute of the passover,—No stranger, shall eat thereof;
texts.exo.12.44: but, every man’s servant bought with silver,—when thou hast circumcised him, then, shall he eat thereof:
texts.exo.12.45: An alien or a hireling, shall not eat thereof.
texts.exo.12.46: In one house, shall it be eaten, thou shalt not take forth out of the house any of the flesh outside; and a, bone thereof, shalt thou not break.
texts.exo.12.47: All the assembly of Israel, shall keep it.
texts.exo.12.48: And when there may sojourn with thee a sojourner who may wish to keep a passover to Yahweh, there must be circumcised to him every male and then, may he draw near to keep it, so shall he be as a native of the land,—but no uncircumcised male, shall eat thereof.
texts.exo.12.49: One law, shall there be for the native, and for the sojourner that sojourneth in your midst.
texts.exo.12.50: Thus did all the sons of Israel,—as Yahweh had commanded Moses and Aaron, so, did they.
texts.exo.12.51: And it came to pass, on this self-same day, that Yahweh brought forth the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt, by their hosts.
texts.exo.13.1: And Yahweh spake unto Moses, saying:
texts.exo.13.2: Hallow to me every firstborn, that which any female first beareth among the sons of Israel, among men and among beasts,—mine! it is.
texts.exo.13.3: And Moses said unto the people—[Ye are] to remember this day, on which ye came forth out of Egypt out of the house of slaves, that with strength of hand, did Yahweh bring you forth from hence,—there shall not, therefore be eaten anything leavened.
texts.exo.13.4: To-day, are, ye, coming forth,—in the month Abib.
