texts.exo.13.5: And it shall be, when Yahweh shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Amorite, and the Hivite and the Jebusite, which he sware to thy fathers to give thee, a land flowing with milk and honey, then shalt thou serve with this service, in this month.
texts.exo.13.6: Seven days, shalt thou eat unleavened cakes,—and on the seventh day, [shall be] a festival to Yahweh.
texts.exo.13.7: Unleavened cakes, shall be eaten for the seven days,—neither shall there be seen with thee anything leavened, nor shall there be seen with thee leaven, within any of thy bounds,
texts.exo.13.8: And thou shalt tell thy son, on that day, saying,—[This is] because, of that which Yahweh did for me, when he brought me forth out of Egypt.
texts.exo.13.9: And it shall be to thee for a sign upon thy hand and for a memorial between thine eyes, in order that the law of Yahweh may be in thy mouth,—for with a strong hand, did Yahweh bring thee forth out of Egypt.
texts.exo.13.10: So shalt thou observe this statute in its appointed time,—from year to year.
texts.exo.13.11: And it shall be when Yahweh shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanite, as he sware to thee and to thy fathers,—and shalt give it thee,
texts.exo.13.12: that thou shalt set apart whatsoever is born first, to Yahweh; and, of all firstlings of beasts which thou shalt have, the males, shall pertain to Yahweh.
texts.exo.13.13: But every firstling of an ass, shalt thou redeem with a lamb or if thou wilt not redeem it, then thou shalt break its neck,—but every firstborn of men among thy sons, shalt thou redeem.
texts.exo.13.14: And it shall be when thy son shall ask thee in time to come, saying, What is this? Then shalt thou say unto him: With strength of hand, did Yahweh bring us forth out of Egypt out of the house of slaves.
texts.exo.13.15: And it came to pass when Pharaoh had shown himself too hardened to let us go, then did Yahweh slay every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of men even unto the firstborn of beasts. For this cause, am, I, sacrificing to Yahweh whatsoever is born first, of the males, and every firstborn of my sons, must I redeem.
texts.exo.13.16: And it shall be for a sign upon thy hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes,—that, with strength of hand, did Yahweh bring us forth out of Egypt.
texts.exo.13.17: And it came to pass when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God did not lead by the land-way of the Philistines, although it was near,—for God said—Lest the people be dismayed when they see war and turn back to Egypt.
texts.exo.13.18: So God took the people round the desert-way of the Red Sea,—and the sons of Israel went up armed, out of the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.13.19: And Moses took the bones of Joseph, with him,—for he had, taken an oath, of the sons of Israel saying, God will, surely visit, you, so then ye shall carry up my bones from hence with you.
texts.exo.13.20: And they brake up from Succoth,—and encamped in Etham, at the edge of the desert.
texts.exo.13.21: Now, Yahweh, was going before them—by day, in a pillar of cloud to lead them the way, and by night, in a pillar of fire to give them light,—that they might journey day and night:
texts.exo.13.22: the pillar of cloud by day ceased not, nor the pillar of fire by night,—from before the people.
texts.exo.14.1: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying:
texts.exo.14.2: Speak unto the sons of Israel, that they turn back and encamp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea,—before Baal-zephon, over against it, shall ye encamp, by the sea.
texts.exo.14.3: Then will Pharaoh say, of the sons of Israel, Entangled, they are in the land,—the desert hath closed in upon them.
texts.exo.14.4: So will I let the heart of Pharaoh wax bold, and he will pursue them, that I may get me honour over Pharaoh, and over all his forces, and the Egyptians shall know, that I, am Yahweh. And they did so.
texts.exo.14.5: And it was told the king of Egypt, that the people had fled,—and the heart of Pharaoh and his servants was turned against the people, and they said—What is this we have done, that we have let Israel go from serving us?
texts.exo.14.6: So he yoked his chariot,—and his people, took he with him.
texts.exo.14.7: And he took six hundred chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Egypt,—with warriors in every one.
texts.exo.14.8: And Yahweh let the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt wax bold, and he pursued the sons of Israel,—when the sons of Israel, were going out with a high hand.
texts.exo.14.9: So the Egyptians pursued them and overtook them, encamping by the sea—all the horses and chariots of Pharaoh, and his horsemen, and his forces,—by Pi-hahiroth, before Baal-zephon.
texts.exo.14.10: Now when, Pharaoh, had drawn near, the sons of Israel lifted up their eyes, and lo! the Egyptians, moving along after them and they feared greatly, and the sons of Israel made outcry unto Yahweh.
texts.exo.14.11: Then said they unto Moses, Was it because there were no graves in Egypt, that thou didst fetch us to die in the desert? What is this thou hast done to us, bringing us forth out of Egypt?
texts.exo.14.12: Is not this the word which we spake unto thee in Egypt, saying, Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians,—for it is better for us, to serve the Egyptians, than to die in the desert?
texts.exo.14.13: And Moses said unto the people—Do not fear, stand still and see the salvation of Yahweh, which he will work for you to-day,—for as for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to-day, ye shall not again see them any more to times age-abiding.
texts.exo.14.14: Yahweh, will fight for you,—and, ye, shall forbear.
texts.exo.14.15: And Yahweh said unto Moses, What outcry wouldst thou make unto me? Speak unto the sons of Israel, that they go forward;
texts.exo.14.16: and, thou, lift high thy staff and stretch forth thy hand over the sea and cleave it asunder,—that the sons of Israel may enter into the midst of the sea on dry ground;
texts.exo.14.17: and, I, behold me letting the heart of the Egyptians wax bold, that they may enter after them,—that I may get me honour over Pharaoh and over his forces, over his chariots, and over his horsemen,
texts.exo.14.18: And the Egyptians shall know, that, I, am Yahweh,—when I have gotten me honour over Pharaoh, over his chariots and over his horsemen.
texts.exo.14.19: And the messenger of God who was going on before the camp of Israel removed, and came on behind them,—and the pillar of cloud removed from before them, and stood behind them;
texts.exo.14.20: so it came in between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel, so it became a cloud and darkness, and yet lighted up the night,—so that the one came not near unto the other, all the night.
texts.exo.14.21: And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and Yahweh carried away the sea by a mighty east wind all the night, and turned the sea into dry land,—and the waters were cloven asunder.
texts.exo.14.22: Then went the sons of Israel into the midst of the sea on the dry ground,—and, the waters, to them, were a wall, on their right hand and on their left.
texts.exo.14.23: And the Egyptians pursued, and entered after them—all the horses of Pharaoh his chariots and his horsemen,—into the midst of the sea.
texts.exo.14.24: And it came to pass in the morning watch, that Yahweh looked down into the camp of the Egyptians, through the pillar of fire and cloud, and confused the camp of the Egyptians;
texts.exo.14.25: and he took off the wheels of their chariots, and made them drive heavily,—so that the Egyptians said—We must flee from the face of Israel, for Yahweh, is fighting for them against the Egyptians.
texts.exo.14.26: Then said Yahweh unto Moses, Stretch forth thy hand over the sea,—that the waters may return upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots, and upon their horsemen.
texts.exo.14.27: So Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea and the sea returned, towards morning, to its steady flow, when the Egyptians, were fleeing to meet it,—thus Yahweh shook off the Egyptians into the midst of the sea;
texts.exo.14.28: thus the waters returned and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, even all the forces of Pharaoh that were entering after them into the sea,—there was not left remaining among them so much as one.
texts.exo.14.29: But the sons of Israel, had gone their way on dry ground in the saidst of the sea,—and the waters had been to them a wall, on their right hand and on their left.
texts.exo.14.30: Thus did Yahweh, on that day, save Israel, out of the hand of the Egyptians,—and Israel saw the Egyptians, dead on the shore of the sea.
texts.exo.14.31: And when Israel saw the mighty hand wherewith Yahweh had wrought against the Egyptians, then did the people revere Yahweh,—and they put their trust in Yahweh, and in Moses, his servant.
texts.exo.15.1: Then, sang Moses, and the sons of Israel, this song unto Yahweh, and they spake, saying,—I will sing to Yahweh, for he is exalted, exalted,—The horse and his rider, hath he cast into the sea.
texts.exo.15.2: My might and melody, is Yah, And he became mine, by salvation,—This, is my GOD, and I will glorify him, The God of my father and I will set him on high.
texts.exo.15.3: Yahweh is a warlike one,—Yahweh, is his name.
texts.exo.15.4: The chariots of Pharaoh and his train, hath he cast into the sea,—Yea, the choice of his warriors, were sunk in the Sedgy Sea.
texts.exo.15.5: Roaring deeps, covered them,—They went down in the raging depths like a stone.
texts.exo.15.6: Thy right hand, O Yahweh is splendid in power,—Thy right hand, O Yahweh dasheth in pieces a foe;
texts.exo.15.7: And in the greatness of thine exaltation, dost thou tear down thine opposers,—Thou dost send forth thy wrath, it consumeth them as straw;
texts.exo.15.8: And with the blast of thy nostrils, heaped up are the waters, Upreared like a mound, are the flowing waves,—Roaring deeps are congealed in the heart of the sea.
texts.exo.15.9: Said the foe—I will pursue—overtake divide spoil,—Take her fill of them—shall my soul, I will bare my sword, root them out—shall my hand.
texts.exo.15.10: Thou didst blow with thy wind they were covered by the sea,—They rolled like lead, into the waters so wide.
texts.exo.15.11: Who is, like unto thee, among the mighty O Yahweh? Who is, like unto thee, Majestic in holiness,—To be revered in praises, Doing a marvellous thing?
texts.exo.15.12: Thou didst stretch forth thy right hand, earth swallowed them up.
texts.exo.15.13: Thou hast led forth in thy lovingkindness, the people which thou hast redeemed,—Thou hast guided them in thy might into the home of thy holiness.
texts.exo.15.14: Peoples have heard they tremble,—A pang, hath seized the dwellers of Philistia:
texts.exo.15.15: Then, were amazed the chiefs of Edom, The mighty ones of Moab, there seizeth them, a trembling,—Melted away, have all the dwellers of Canaan:
texts.exo.15.16: There falleth upon them a terror and dread, With the greatness of thine arm, are they struck dumb as a stone,—Till thy people pass over O Yahweh, Till the people pass over, which thou hast made thine own:—
texts.exo.15.17: Thou bringest them in and plantest them, In the mountain of thine inheritance, Thy dwelling-place to abide in which thou hast made, O Yahweh,—A hallowed place O My Lord which thy hands have established.
texts.exo.15.18: Yahweh, shall reign unto times age-abiding and beyond.
texts.exo.15.19: For the horses of Pharaoh, with his chariots and his horsemen, entered into the sea, Then did Yahweh bring back upon them the waters of the sea,—But the sons of Israel, had gone their way on the dry ground through the midst of the sea.
texts.exo.15.20: Then took Miriam the prophetess, sister of Aaron the timbrel in her hand,—and all the women came forth after her with timbrels and dances,
texts.exo.15.21: And Miriam responded to the men, Sing to Yahweh for he is exalted—exalted, The horse and his rider, hath he cast into the sea.
texts.exo.15.22: And Moses caused Israel to break up from the Red Sea, and they went out into the desert of Shur,—and journeyed three days in the desert and found no water;
texts.exo.15.23: and, when they came in towards Marah they could not drink the waters of Marah, for they were bitter,—for this cause, was the name thereof called Marah.
texts.exo.15.24: So the people murmured against Moses—saying, What are we to drink?
texts.exo.15.25: And he made outcry unto Yahweh, and Yahweh pointed out a tree, and he cast it into the waters, and the waters became sweet,—There, he appointed him a statute and regulation And, there, he put him to the proof.
texts.exo.15.26: And he said: If thou, wilt indeed hearken, to the voice of Yahweh thy God, And the thing that is right in his eyes, thou wilt do, And so give ear to his commandments, And keep all his statutes, None of the sicknesses which I laid on the Egyptians, will I lay upon thee, For, I, am Yahweh, thy physician.
texts.exo.15.27: Then came they in to Elim, and there, were twelve fountains of water and seventy palm-trees,—so they encamped there, by the waters.
texts.exo.16.1: Then moved they on from Elim, and all the assembly of the sons of Israel entered into the desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month, by their coming forth out of the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.16.2: Then did all the assembly of the sons of Israel murmur against Moses and against Aaron in the desert;
texts.exo.16.3: and the sons of Israel said unto them—Oh that we had died by the hand of Yahweh, in the land of Egypt, when we remained by the pot of flesh, when we did eat bread to the full,—for ye have brought us forth into this desert, to cause all this multitude to die by famine.
texts.exo.16.4: Then said Yahweh unto Moses, Behold me! raining down for you bread out of heaven,—and the people shall go out and gather the portion for a day, on its day, that I may prove them whether they will walk in my law, or not.
texts.exo.16.5: And it shall come to pass on the sixth day, that they shall settle what they shall bring in,—and it shall be twice as much as they gather day by day.
texts.exo.16.6: So Moses and Aaron said unto all the sons of Israel,—At eventide, then shall ye know that it was, Yahweh, who brought you forth, out of the land of Egypt;
texts.exo.16.7: and, in the morning, then shall ye see the glory of Yahweh, in that he hath heard your murmurings against Yahweh,—what then are, we, that ye should murmur against, us?
texts.exo.16.8: And Moses said—In that Yahweh giveth you in the evening flesh to eat, and bread in the morning, to the full, in that Yahweh heareth your murmurings wherewith ye are murmuring against him, what then are, we? Not against us, do ye murmur but against Yahweh.
texts.exo.16.9: And Moses said unto Aaron, Say unto all the assembly of the sons of Israel, Draw near, before Yahweh,—for he hath heard your murmurings.
texts.exo.16.10: And it came to pass, when Aaron spake unto all the assembly of the sons of Israel, then turned they towards the desert,—and lo! the glory of Yahweh, had appeared in the cloud,
texts.exo.16.12: I have heard the murmurings of the sons of Israel,—speak unto them, saying—Between the two evenings, shall ye eat flesh, and in the morning, shall ye be filled with bread,—so shall ye know that I Yahweh am your God.
texts.exo.16.13: And it came to pass, in the evening, that there came up quail, and covered the camp,—and in the morning was the outpouring of dew, round about the camp;
texts.exo.16.14: and when the outpouring of dew went up, then lo! on the face of the desert, a thin flake, thin as hoar-frost on the earth,
texts.exo.16.15: And when the sons of Israel saw it they said one to another—What is that? For they knew not what "that" was. Then said Moses unto them, "That" is the bread which Yahweh hath given you to eat.
texts.exo.16.16: This, is the thing which Yahweh hath commanded, Gather ye thereof, each man what he needeth for eating,—an omer a head, by the number of your souls, each man—for them who are in his tent, shall ye take.
texts.exo.16.17: And the sons of Israel did so,—and gathered, [some] more, and [some] less;
texts.exo.16.18: and when they measured it with the omer, he who had gathered more had nothing over, and he who had gathered less had no lack: each man what he needed for eating, did they gather.
texts.exo.16.19: And Moses said unto them,—Let, no man leave thereof, until morning.
texts.exo.16.20: But they hearkened not unto Moses, but certain men left thereof until morning, and it swarmed with worms and become loathsome,—and Moses was wroth with them.
texts.exo.16.21: Thus then they gathered it morning by morning, each man what he needed for eating, and as soon as the sun waxed hot, so soon it melted.
texts.exo.16.22: And it came to pass on the sixth day, that they gathered food twice as much, two omers for each one,—so all the princes of the assembly came in, and told Moses.
texts.exo.16.23: And he said unto them—That is what Yahweh spake. The observance of a holy sabbath to Yahweh, is to-morrow,—what ye would bake, bake and what ye would boil, boil, and all that is left over, put by you to keep until the morning.
texts.exo.16.24: So they put it by until the morning, as Moses had commanded,—and it gave no unpleasant odour, neither was there a worm, therein.
texts.exo.16.25: Then said Moses—Eat ye it to-day, for a sabbath, is to-day, unto Yahweh,—to-day, ye shall not find it in the field.
texts.exo.16.26: Six days, shall ye gather it,—but on the seventh day, a sabbath, it shall not be therein.
texts.exo.16.27: And it came to pass on the seventh day, that there went forth some of the people to gather,—but they found not.
texts.exo.16.28: Then said Yahweh unto Moses,—How long have ye refused to keep my commandments and my laws?
texts.exo.16.29: See because Yahweh hath given you the sabbath, for this cause, is, he, giving you on the sixth day, food for two days,—abide ye every man in his place, let no man go forth from his dwelling, on the seventh day,
texts.exo.16.30: So the people rested on the seventh day.
texts.exo.16.31: And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna,—and the same, was like coriander seed white, and the taste thereof, like flat-cake with honey,
texts.exo.16.32: And Moses said—This, is the thing which Yahweh hath commanded, Fill an omer therefrom as a thing to be preserved to your generations,—that they may see the bread wherewith I fed you in the desert, when I brought you forth out of the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.16.33: So Moses said unto Aaron—Take a single basket, and put therein an omer-full of manna,—and set it down before Yahweh, as a thing to be preserved to your generations.
texts.exo.16.34: As Yahweh gave command unto Moses, so did Aaron set it down before the testimony, as a thing to be preserved,
texts.exo.16.35: And, the sons of Israel did eat the manna forty years, until they entered into the land wherein they were to dwell,—the manna, they did eat until they entered into the bounds of the land of Canaan.
texts.exo.16.36: Now, an omer, is, the tenth of the ephah.
texts.exo.17.1: And all the assembly of the sons of Israel set forward out of the desert of Sin, by their removings, at the bidding of Yahweh,—and encamped in Rephidim, and there was no water for the people to drink.
texts.exo.17.2: And the people found fault with Moses, and said—Give us water, that we may drink. And Moses said to them, Why should ye find fault with me? Why should ye put Yahweh to the proof?
texts.exo.17.3: So the people thirsted, there for water, and the people murmured against Moses,—and said—Wherefore is it that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill me and my sons and my cattle, with thirst?
texts.exo.17.4: And Moses made outcry unto Yahweh saying, What am I to do, with this people? Yet a little, and they will stone me.
texts.exo.17.5: Then said Yahweh unto Moses—Pass over before the people, and take with thee some of the elders of Israel,—thy staff also wherewith thou didst smite the river, take thou in thy hand, so shalt thou go thy way.
texts.exo.17.6: Behold me! standing before thee, there upon the rock in Horeb, then shalt thou smite the rock and there shall come forth therefrom water, and the people shall drink. And Moses did so, in the sight of the elders of Israel.
texts.exo.17.7: So he called the name of the place, Massah, and Meribah,—because of the fault-finding of the sons of Israel, and because of their putting Yahweh to the proof, saying, Is Yahweh in our midst or is he not?
texts.exo.17.8: Then came in Amalek,—and fought with Israel, in Rephidim.
texts.exo.17.9: And Moses said unto Joshua—Choose for us men, and go forth, fight with Amalek,—to-morrow, am, I, stationing myself upon the top of the hill, with the staff of God in my hand.
texts.exo.17.10: So Joshua did as Moses had said to him, to fight with Amalek,—and Moses, Aaron and Hur, went up to the top of the hill.
texts.exo.17.11: And it shall be when Moses shall lift on high his hands, then shall Israel prevail, but when he shall let down his hands, then shall Amalek prevail.
texts.exo.17.12: But, the hands of Moses, were weary, so they took a stone, and put under him, and he sat thereupon,—and, Aaron and Hur, upheld his hands—on this side, one and on that side, one, and so his hands became steady, until the going in of the sun.
texts.exo.17.13: So Joshua overthrew Amalek and his people, with the edge of the sword.
texts.exo.17.14: Then said Yahweh unto Moses—Write this as a remembrancer in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua—that I will, wipe out, the remembrance of Amalek, from under the heavens.
texts.exo.17.15: And Moses built an altar,—and called the name thereof, Yahweh-nissi.
texts.exo.17.16: And he said—Because of a hand against the throne of Yah, Yahweh hath war with Amalek,—from generation to generation!
texts.exo.18.1: And Jethro, priest of Midian, father-in-law of Moses, heard all that God had done for Moses, and for Israel his people,—in that Yahweh had brought forth Israel out of Egypt.
texts.exo.18.2: So Jethro, Moses father-in-law, took Zipporah, Moses wife,—after she had been sent home;
texts.exo.18.3: and her two sons,—of whom, the name of the one, was Gershom, for, said he, A sojourner, am I in a strange land,
texts.exo.18.4: and, the name of the other, Eliezer, for the God of my father, was my help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.
texts.exo.18.5: And Jethro, Moses father-in-law, came in, with his two sons and his wife, unto Moses,—into the desert where, he, was encamping, the mountain of God;
texts.exo.18.6: and said unto Moses, I, thy father-in-law, Jethro, am coming in unto thee,—and thy wife, and her two sons, with her.
texts.exo.18.7: So Moses went forth to meet his father-in-law, and bowed himself down to him and kissed him, and they asked each other of their welfare,—and came into the tent.
texts.exo.18.8: Then Moses recounted to his father-in-law, all that Yahweh had done to Pharaoh and to the Egyptians, for Israel’s sake,—all the hardship which had befallen them by the way, and how Yahweh had delivered them.
texts.exo.18.9: Then did Jethro rejoice, for all the good which Yahweh had done to Israel,—whom he had delivered out of the hand of the Egyptians.
texts.exo.18.10: And Jethro said—Blessed be Yahweh, who hath delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians and out of the hand of Pharaoh,—Who hath delivered the people from under the hand of the Egyptians:
texts.exo.18.11: Now, I know, that, greater, is Yahweh than all the gods,—Even in the thing wherein they were arrogant over them.
texts.exo.18.12: Then took Jethro father-in-law of Moses, an ascending-offering and sacrifices to God,—and Aaron and all the elders of Israel came in to eat bread with the father-in-law of Moses before God.
texts.exo.18.13: Now it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses sat, to judge the people,—and the people stood by Moses, from the morning, until the evening.
texts.exo.18.14: And when Moses father-in-law saw all that he, was doing for the people, he said—What is this thing which, thou, art doing for the people? Wherefore art, thou, sitting alone, with all the people, stationed by thee, from morning until evening?
texts.exo.18.15: And Moses said to his father-in-law,—Because the people come in unto me to seek God:
texts.exo.18.16: When they have a matter, they come in unto me, then do I judge between a man and his neighbour,—and make known the statutes of God and his laws.
texts.exo.18.17: Then said Moses’ father-in-law unto him,—Not good, is the thing that thou art doing.
texts.exo.18.18: Thou wilt get quite worn out, both thou and this people that is with thee,—for the thing is too heavy for thee, thou canst not do it, alone.
texts.exo.18.19: Now, hearken thou to my voice—let me counsel thee, and may God be with thee: Be, thou, for the people, in front of God, so shalt, thou, bring the matters unto God;
texts.exo.18.20: and shalt cause to shine upon them, the statutes and the laws,—and make known to them the way wherein they should go, and the work they should do.
texts.exo.18.21: Thou thyself, therefore shalt look out, from among all the people—men of ability, reverers of God, men of fidelity, haters of extortion,—and place them over [them] as rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.
texts.exo.18.22: So shall they judge the people at any time, and it shall be, all the great matters, shall they bring in unto thee, but all the small matters, shall, they themselves, judge,—so, lighten thou the burden for thyself, and let them bear it with thee.
texts.exo.18.23: If, this thing, thou wilt do, and God shall command thee, then shalt thou be able to endure,—yea, moreover, all this people, shall go in, unto their dwellings, contented.
texts.exo.18.24: So Moses hearkened to the voice of his father-in-law, and did all that he had said;
texts.exo.18.25: and Moses chose men of ability out of all Israel, and set them to be heads over the people,—rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.
texts.exo.18.26: And they shall judge the people, at any time,—the hard matters, shall they bring in unto Moses, but all the small matters, shall, they themselves, judge.
texts.exo.18.27: And Moses sent forth his father-in-law,—and he went his way by himself unto his own land.
texts.exo.19.1: In the third month, by the coming forth of the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt, on this day, came they into the desert of Sinai:
texts.exo.19.2: then was it that they brake up out of Rephidim and came into the desert of Sinai, and encamped in the desert,—yea Israel encamped there before the mountain.
texts.exo.19.3: And when Moses, had gone up unto God, then called Yahweh unto him out of the mountain saying, Thus, shalt thou say to the house of Jacob, And tell the sons of Israel:
texts.exo.19.4: Ye, have seen what I did unto the Egyptians,—And how I bare you upon wings of eagles, And brought you in unto myself:—
texts.exo.19.5: Now, therefore, if ye will, indeed hearken, to my voice, And keep my covenant, Then shall ye be mine as a treasure beyond all the peoples, For, mine, is all the earth;
texts.exo.19.6: But, ye, shall be mine, As a kingdom of priests, And a holy nation. These, are the words, which thou shalt speak unto the sons of Israel.
texts.exo.19.7: Then came Moses, and called for the elders of the people,—and put before them all these words which Yahweh had commanded him.
texts.exo.19.8: And all the people responded together and said, All that Yahweh hath spoken, will we do. And Moses took back the words of the people, unto Yahweh.
texts.exo.19.9: Then said Yahweh unto Moses: Lo! I, am coming unto thee in the veiling of cloud, in order that the people may hear when I speak with thee, moreover also, that, in thee, they may trust to times age-abiding. Then told Moses the words of the people unto Yahweh.
texts.exo.19.10: And Yahweh said unto Moses—Go unto the people, and thou shalt hallow them to-day, and to-morrow,—and they shall wash their clothes;
texts.exo.19.11: and shall be ready, by the third day,—for on the third day, will Yahweh come down in the sight of all the people upon Mount Sinai.
texts.exo.19.12: So then thou shalt set bounds for the people round about saying, Take heed to yourselves—that ye go not up into the mountain, nor touch the boundary thereof, whosoever toucheth the mountain, shall, surely die.
texts.exo.19.13: No hand shall touch it but he shall be, surely stoned, or be, surely shot, whether beast or man, he shall not live,—When the ram’s horn soundeth, they themselves, shall come up within the mount,
texts.exo.19.14: Then Moses went down out of the mount, unto the people,—and hallowed the people, and they washed their clothes.
texts.exo.19.15: And he said unto the people, Be ready, by the third day,—do not approach a woman.
texts.exo.19.16: And it came to pass on the third day, when the morning had come, that there were thunderings and lightnings, and a heavy cloud upon the mount, and the sound of a horn, loud exceedingly,—and all the people who were in the camp trembled.
texts.exo.19.17: And Moses brought forth the people, to meet God out of the camp,—and they stationed themselves in the lower part of the mount,
texts.exo.19.18: And Mount Sinai, smoked, all over, because Yahweh had come down thereon in fire,—and the smoke thereof went up as the smoke of a furnace, and all the mountain trembled exceedingly.
texts.exo.19.19: And as oft as the sound of the horn went on and became exceeding loud, Moses, spake and, God, responded to him with a voice.
texts.exo.19.20: Thus came Yahweh down upon Mount Sinai unto the top of the mount,—and Yahweh called Moses unto the top of the mount, and Moses went up.
texts.exo.19.21: Then said Yahweh unto Moses, Go down, adjure the people,—lest they press through unto Yahweh to see, and so there fall from among them a multitude.
texts.exo.19.22: Yea, even the priests who do approach unto Yahweh, must hallow themselves,—lest Yahweh break in upon them.
texts.exo.19.23: And Moses said unto Yahweh, The people cannot come up into Mount Sinai,—for, thou thyself, hast adjured us saying: Set bounds to the mountain and hallow it.
texts.exo.19.24: And Yahweh said unto him—Away, down, then shalt thou come up, thou and Aaron with thee,—but as for the priests and the people, let it not be that they press through to come up unto Yahweh lest he break in upon them.
texts.exo.19.25: So Moses went down unto the people,—and said [these things] unto them.
texts.exo.20.1: And God spake all these words saying:—
texts.exo.20.2: I, am Yahweh thy God,—who have brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of servants:—
texts.exo.20.3: Thou shalt not have other gods besides me.
texts.exo.20.4: Thou shalt not make to thee an image, or any form, that is in the heavens above,—or that is in the earth beneath,—or that is in the waters beneath the earth:
texts.exo.20.5: thou shalt not bow thyself down to them nor be led to serve them—For, I, Yahweh, thy God, am a jealous GOD, visiting the iniquity of fathers upon sons, unto three [generations] and, unto four, of them that hate me;
texts.exo.20.6: but shewing lovingkindness unto thousands [of generations],—of them who love me, and keep my commandments.
texts.exo.20.7: Thou shalt not utter the name of Yahweh thy God for falsehood, for Yahweh will not let him go unpunished who uttereth his name for falsehood.
texts.exo.20.8: Remember the sabbath day, to hallow it:
texts.exo.20.9: Six days, shalt thou labour, and do all thy work;
texts.exo.20.10: but, the seventh day, is a sabbath unto Yahweh thy God,—thou shalt do no work, thou nor thy son nor thy daughter nor thy servant, nor thy handmaid, nor thy beast, nor thy sojourner who is within thy gates,
texts.exo.20.11: For, in six days, did Yahweh make the heavens and the earth, [and] the sea—and all that in them is, and rested on the seventh day,—for this cause, Yahweh blessed the sabbath day and hallowed it.
texts.exo.20.12: Honour thy father, and thy mother,—that thy days may be prolonged upon the soil, which Yahweh thy God is about to give unto thee.
texts.exo.20.16: Thou shalt not testify against thy neighbour, with a witness of falsehood.
texts.exo.20.17: Thou shalt not covet, thy neighbour’s house,—thou shalt not covet, thy neighbour’s wife nor his servant nor his handmaid nor his ox, nor his ass, nor anything which belongeth unto thy neighbour.
texts.exo.20.18: And, all the people, were witnessing the voices and the torches, and the sound of the horn, and the mountain smoking,—so then the people were struck with awe and shrank back, and stood afar off.
texts.exo.20.19: And they said unto Moses, Speak, thou, with us, and we will hear,—but let not God speak with us lest we die.
texts.exo.20.20: And Moses said unto the people—Do not fear, for to the end he may prove you, hath God come,—and to the end the reverence of him may be upon your faces that ye sin not.
texts.exo.20.21: So then the people stood afar off, and, Moses, approached unto the thick gloom, where God was.
texts.exo.20.22: Then said Yahweh unto Moses, Thus, shalt thou say, unto the sons of Israel,—Ye yourselves, have seen that out of the heavens, have I spoken with you.
texts.exo.20.23: Ye shall not make [aught] beside me,—neither gods of silver, nor gods of gold, shall ye make to yourselves.
texts.exo.20.24: An altar of earth, shalt thou make to me, then shalt thou offer thereupon thine ascending-sacrifices and thy peace-offerings, thy sheep, and thine oxen. In every place where I may mention my name, will I come in unto thee and will bless thee.
texts.exo.20.25: But if, an altar of stones, thou wilt make to me, thou shalt not build them hewn,—for as soon as thou hast lifted, thy sharp tool, thereupon, thou hast profaned it;
texts.exo.20.26: neither shalt thou go up, by steps unto mine altar,—lest by any means thy shame be discovered thereupon.
texts.exo.21.1: Now, these are the regulations which thou shalt put before them.
texts.exo.21.2: When thou shalt acquire a servant who is a Hebrew, six years, shall he serve,—but in the seventh shall he go out freely—for nought.
texts.exo.21.3: If, by himself, he came in, by himself, shall he go out,—if he was married, then shall his wife go out with him.
texts.exo.21.4: If his lord gave him a wife, and she have borne him sons or daughters, the wife and her children shall be her lords, and, he shall go out by himself.
texts.exo.21.5: But, if the servant shall plainly say, I love my lord, and my wife and my sons,—I will not go out free,
texts.exo.21.6: then shall his lord bring him near unto God, and shall bring him near unto the door, or unto the door-post,—and his lord shall pierce his ear with an awl, so shall he serve him all his life.
texts.exo.21.7: And when a man shall sell his daughter to be a handmaid, she shall not go out according to the out-going of the men-servants,
texts.exo.21.8: If she is uncomely in the eyes of her lord, who hath not assigned her in marriage, then shall he suffer her to be redeemed: to a strange people, shall he not have power to sell her in that he hath dealt treacherously with her.
texts.exo.21.9: And if, to his son, he assign her, according to the custom for daughters, shall he do for her.
texts.exo.21.10: If he take to himself another, her food her clothing, and her marriage-right, shall he not withdraw.
texts.exo.21.11: But if these three, he will not do for her, then shall she go out for nought, without silver.
texts.exo.21.12: He that smiteth a man, so that he die, shall surely be put to death.
texts.exo.21.13: But he who hath not lain in wait, but, God, hath occasioned him to come to his hand, then will I appoint for thee a place, whither he may flee.
texts.exo.21.14: But, when a man shall act presumptuously against his neighbour to slay him with guile, from mine altar, shalt thou take him to die.
texts.exo.21.15: And, he that smiteth his father or his mother, shall, surely be put to death.
texts.exo.21.16: And, he that stealeth a man of the sons of Israel, and selleth him, or he be found in his hand, shall, surely be put to death.
texts.exo.21.17: And he who revileth his father or his mother, shall, surely be put to death.
texts.exo.21.18: And when men strive together, and one shall smite the other, with a stone or with his fist,—and he die not, but shall fall to his bed;—
texts.exo.21.19: if he rise and shall walk abroad on his staff, then shall he that smote him be acquitted,—only, for his loss of time, he shall pay, and, shall surely heal, him.
texts.exo.21.20: And when a man shall smite his servant or his handmaid with a rod, and he die under his hand, he shall, surely be avenged;
texts.exo.21.21: nevertheless if, for a day or for two days, he continue, he shall not be avenged, for, his silver, he is.
texts.exo.21.22: And when men strive together and push against a woman with child, and she miscarry, but there is no other mischief, he shall, surely be fined, according as the woman’s husband shall lay upon him, but he shall give it through judges.
texts.exo.21.23: But, if mischief follow, then shalt thou give life for life;
texts.exo.21.24: eye for eye, tooth for tooth,—hand for hand, foot for foot,
texts.exo.21.25: brand for brand, wound for wound,—stripe for stripe.
texts.exo.21.26: And, when a man smiteth the eye of his servant, or the eye of his handmaid, and destroyeth it, he shall send him forth, free, for his eye;
texts.exo.21.27: or, if, the tooth of his servant or the tooth of his handmaid, he knock out, he shall send him forth, free, for his tooth.
texts.exo.21.28: And when an ox goreth a man or a woman, and death ensueth, the ox shall, surely be stoned and his flesh shall not be eaten, and the owner of the ox, shall be quit.
texts.exo.21.29: But, if, the ox, was wont to gore before that time and it hath been attested to his owner, and he hath not proceeded to put him under guard, and he causeth the death of man or woman, the ox, shall be stoned, and, his owner also, shall be put to death.
texts.exo.21.30: If, a sin-covering, be laid on him, then shall he give a ransom for his life, according to whatsoever may be laid on him:
texts.exo.21.31: if, a son, he gore or, a daughter, he gore, according to this regulation, shall it be done to him;
texts.exo.21.32: if, a servant the ox gore, or a handmaid, thirty shekels of silver, shall he give to his lord, and, the ox, shall be stoned.
texts.exo.21.33: And when a man openeth a pit, or when a man diggeth a pit, and doth not cover it,—and there falleth thereinto an ox or an ass,
texts.exo.21.34: the owner of the pit, shall make it good, silver, shall he pay back to the owner thereof,—and the dead beast, shall be his.
texts.exo.21.35: And when the ox of one man thrusteth the ox of his neighbour so that it dieth, then shall they sell the live ox and divide the silver thereof, and the dead ox also, shall they divide,
texts.exo.21.36: Or if it was known that, an ox, was, wont to gore, before that time, and his owner proceeded not to put him under guard, he shall surely make good,—an ox for the ox, and, the dead one, shall be his.
texts.exo.22.1: When a man stealeth an ox or a sheep, and slayeth it, or selleth it, with five of the herd, shall he make good—for the ox, or with four of the flock, for the sheep.
texts.exo.22.2: If, in the place of breaking in, the thief be found and he is smitten so that he dieth, there is due for him no shedding of blood:
texts.exo.22.3: should the sun have arisen upon him, there would be shedding of blood due for him,—he is surely to make restitution, if he hath nothing, then is he to be sold, for his theft.
texts.exo.22.4: If the thing stolen is found in his hand—whether ox or ass or sheep, alive, with two, shall he make restitution.
texts.exo.22.5: When a man causeth a field or a vineyard to be depastured, or hath sent in his own cattle and stripped the field of another, he shall, surely make restitution, out of his own field, according to the yield thereof; or if, all the field, he depasture, with the best of his own field, or with the best of his own vineyard, shall he make restitution.
texts.exo.22.6: When a fire breaketh out and hath come upon thorns and so there is consumed a stack of sheaves, or the standing corn, or the field, he that kindled the fire, shall surely make restitution.
texts.exo.22.7: When a man giveth unto his neighbour silver or jewelry, to keep, and it is stolen out of the house of the man:
texts.exo.22.8: if the thief be found, he shall give in restitution double, if the thief be not found, then shall the owner of the house be brought near unto God to swear that he hath not laid his hand on the property of his neighbour.
texts.exo.22.9: For any affair of trespass—for an ox, for an ass, for a sheep, for a mantle for anything lost as to which one could say—This is it, unto God, shall come the affair of them both,—he whom God shall condemn, shall make restitution of double to his neighbour.
texts.exo.22.10: When a man delivereth unto his neighbour, an ass, or an ox or a sheep, or any beast, to keep,—and it dieth or is fractured, or is driven away, no one beholding,
texts.exo.22.11: the oath of Yahweh, shall come between them both, That he hath not laid his hand on the property of his neighbour,—then shall the owner thereof accept it and he shall not make restitution.
texts.exo.22.12: But, if it be verily stolen, from him, he shall make restitution to the owner thereof.
texts.exo.22.13: If it be, verily torn in pieces, he shall bring it in as a witness—for that which was torn, he shall not make restitution.
texts.exo.22.14: And when a man asketh aught of his neighbour, and it is fractured or dieth, its owner, not being with it, he shall, surely make restitution.
texts.exo.22.15: If, its owner, was with it, he shall not make restitution,—if it is, hired, it cometh into its hire.
texts.exo.22.16: And, when a man enticeth a virgin who is not betrothed, and lieth with her, he shall, surely pay a purchase-price, that she may be his wife.
texts.exo.22.17: If her father utterly refuse, to give her to him, silver, shall he weigh out, according to the purchase-price of virgins.
texts.exo.22.18: A sorceress, shalt thou not suffer to live.
texts.exo.22.19: Whosoever lieth with a beast shall surely be put to death.
texts.exo.22.20: He that sacrificeth to the gods shall be devoted to destruction,—except [he sacrificeth] to Yahweh alone.
texts.exo.22.21: And, a sojourner, shalt thou not tread down neither shalt thou drive him away,—for sojourners, ye became in the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.22.22: Neither widow nor fatherless, shalt thou humiliate:
texts.exo.22.23: if thou, do humiliate, him, when he in anywise crieth out unto me, I will, surely hear, his outcry:
texts.exo.22.24: so shall kindle mine anger, and I will slay you with the sword,—and your wives, shall become widows, and your, sons fatherless.
texts.exo.22.25: If, silver, thou wilt lend unto my people—unto the humbled one by thee, thou shalt not be to him like one that lendeth on interest,—thou shalt not lay upon him interest.
texts.exo.22.26: If thou, do take in pledge, the mantle of thy neighbour, by the going in of the sun, shalt thou restore it to him;
texts.exo.22.27: for that is his only covering, that, is his mantle, for his skin,—wherein shall he sleep? and it shall come to pass when he maketh outcry unto me, then will I hear because, gracious, I am.
texts.exo.22.28: God, shalt thou not revile,—and a prince among thy people, shalt thou not curse.
texts.exo.22.29: Thy fulness and thine outflow, shalt thou not delay,—the firstborn of thy sons, shalt thou give to me.
texts.exo.22.30: Thus, shalt thou do with thine ox with thy sheep,—seven days, shall it be with its dam, on the eighth day, shalt thou give it to me.
texts.exo.22.31: Holy men, therefore shall ye truly become to me,—and flesh in the field torn to pieces, shall ye not eat, to the dogs, shall ye cast it.
texts.exo.23.1: Thou shalt not utter a false report. Do not lay thy hand with a lawless man, to become a witness helping forward violence and wrong.
texts.exo.23.2: Thou shalt not follow multitudes to commit wickedness,—neither shalt thou answer in a quarrel, so as to turn away after multitudes to mislead,
texts.exo.23.3: Even a poor man, shalt thou not prefer in his quarrel.
texts.exo.23.4: When thou meetest the ox of thine enemy, or his ass, going astray, thou shalt, surely bring it back, to him.
texts.exo.23.5: When thou seest the ass of him that hateth thee sinking down under his burden, and mightest have foreborne to unload him, thou shalt surely help him to unload,
texts.exo.23.6: Thou shalt not pervert the vindication of thy needy one in his quarrel.
texts.exo.23.7: From a matter of falsehood, thou shalt keep far away,—and the innocent one and the righteous, do not thou slay, for I will not justify a lawless man.
texts.exo.23.8: And, a bribe, shalt thou not take,—for the bribe, blindeth the clear-sighted, and perverteth the words of the righteous.
texts.exo.23.9: And a sojourner, shalt thou not drive away,—seeing that, ye yourselves, know the, soul of a sojourner; for sojourners, became ye in the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.23.10: And six years, shalt thou sow thy land,—and shalt gather the yield thereof;
texts.exo.23.11: but the seventh year, shalt thou let it rest and be still so shall the needy of thy people eat, and what they leave, shall the wild-beast of the field eat,—in like manner, shalt thou deal with thy vineyard with thine oliveyard.
texts.exo.23.12: Six days, shalt thou do thy work, but on the seventh day, shalt thou keep sabbath,—that thine ox may rest and thine ass, and that the son of thy handmaid and the sojourner may be refreshed.
texts.exo.23.13: And, in all that I have said unto thee, shalt thou take heed to thyself,—and the name of other gods, shalt thou not mention, it shall not be heard upon thy mouth.
texts.exo.23.14: Three times, shalt thou keep festival to me, in the year.
texts.exo.23.15: The festival of unleavened cakes, shalt thou keep,—seven days, shalt thou eat unleavened cakes, as I commanded thee at the appointed time of the month Abib; for, therein, camest thou forth out of Egypt,—and they shall not see my face, empty-handed.
texts.exo.23.16: And the festival of harvest with the firstfruits of thy labours, which thou shalt sow in the field, And the festival of ingathering—at the outgoing of the year, when thou hast gathered in thy labours out of the field.
texts.exo.23.17: Three times in the year, shall all thy males see the face of the Lord, Yahweh.
texts.exo.23.18: Thou shalt not offer with anything leavened, the blood of my sacrifice,—neither shall the fat of my festival-sacrifice remain until morning.
texts.exo.23.19: The beginning of the firstfruits of thy ground, shalt thou bring into the house of Yahweh thy God. Thou shalt not boil a kid in the milk of its dam.
texts.exo.23.20: Lo! I, am sending a messenger before thee, to guard thee in the way,—and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared.
texts.exo.23.21: Take thou heed of his presence, and hearken to his voice—do not vex him,-for he will not pardon your transgression, for, my name, is within him.
texts.exo.23.22: But if thou wilt indeed hearken, to his voice, and so wilt do all that I may speak, then will I be an enemy to thine enemies, and an adversary to thine adversaries;
texts.exo.23.23: for my messenger shall go before thee, and bring thee in—unto the Amorite and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Canaanite, the Hivite and the Jebusite,—so will I destroy them.
texts.exo.23.24: Thou shalt not bow thyself down to their gods neither shalt thou be led to serve them, neither shalt thou do according to their works,—but thou shalt, verily overthrow, them, and, completely break in pieces, their pillars.
texts.exo.23.25: So shall ye serve Yahweh your God, and he will bless thy bread and thy water,—and I will take away sickness out of thy midst.
texts.exo.23.26: There shall be nothing casting its young or barren in thy land,—the number of thy days, will I make full.
texts.exo.23.27: My terror, will I send before thee, and will confound all the people amongst whom thou shalt come, and will deliver up all thine enemies unto thee as they flee.
texts.exo.23.28: And I will send the hornet, before thee,—and it shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee.
texts.exo.23.29: I will not drive them out from before thee, in one year,—lest the land should become a desolation, so would the wild-beast of the field multiply over thee.
texts.exo.23.30: Little by little, will I drive them out from before thee. until thou become fruitful, then shalt thou take possession of the land.
texts.exo.23.31: So will I set thy bounds from the Red Sea even unto the sea of the Philistines and from the desert unto the River (Euphrates),—for I will deliver into your hand the inhabitants of the land, so shalt thou drive them out from before thee.
texts.exo.23.32: Thou shalt not make with them or with their gods, a covenant:
texts.exo.23.33: they shall not dwell in thy land, lest they cause thee to sin against me,—for thou mightest serve their gods, verily! it would become to thee a snare!
texts.exo.24.1: And unto Moses, he said—Come up unto Yahweh—thou, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel, so shall ye bow yourselves down from afar.
texts.exo.24.2: And Moses alone shall draw near unto Yahweh, but, they shall not draw near, and, the people, shall not come up with him.
texts.exo.24.3: So Moses came, and recounted to the people all the words of Yahweh, and all the regulations, and all the people responded with one voice and said, All the words which Yahweh hath spoken, will we do.
texts.exo.24.4: Then wrote Moses all the words of Yahweh, and rose up early in the morning, and builded an altar, under the mountain, and twelve pillars, for the twelve tribes of Israel:
texts.exo.24.5: and he sent young men of the sons of Israel, and they caused to go up, ascending-sacrifices,—and slew peace-offerings to Yahweh, of oxen.
texts.exo.24.6: Then took Moses half of the blood, and put it in basins, and half of the blood, dashed he over the altar:
texts.exo.24.7: then took he the book of the covenant, and read in the ears of the people. And they said, All that Yahweh hath spoken, will we do, and will hearken,
texts.exo.24.8: Then Moses took the blood, and dashed over the people, and said, Lo! the blood of the covenant which Yahweh hath solemnised with you, over all these words.
texts.exo.24.9: Then went up Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel;
texts.exo.24.10: and they saw the God of Israel,—and under his feet, like a pavement of sapphire, and like the very heavens for brightness; and
texts.exo.24.11: against the nobles of the sons of Israel, put he not forth his hand,—so then they had vision of God, and did eat and drink,
texts.exo.24.12: Then said Yahweh unto Moses—Come thou up unto me in the mountain and remain thou there,—for I must give thee tables of stone and the law and the commandment, which I have written to direct them.
texts.exo.24.13: And Moses rose up, and Joshua his attendant, and Moses went up into the mountain of God;
texts.exo.24.14: but, unto the elders, he said—Tarry for us here, until we return unto you. And lo! Aaron and Hur, are with you, he that hath a cause, let him draw near unto them.
texts.exo.24.15: So then Moses wont up into the mountain,—and the cloud covered the mountain.
texts.exo.24.16: And the glory of Yahweh rested upon Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days,—then called he unto Moses on the seventh day, out of the midst of the cloud.
texts.exo.24.17: And the appearance of the glory of Yahweh was like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain,—in the sight of the sons of Israel.
texts.exo.24.18: And Moses entered into the midst of the cloud and ascended into the mountain. And it came to pass that Moses was in the mountain forty days and forty nights.
texts.exo.25.1: And Yahweh spake unto Moses, saying:
texts.exo.25.2: Speak unto the sons of Israel, that they take for me a heave-offering,—of every man whose heart urgeth him, shall ye take my heave-offering.
texts.exo.25.3: And, this is the heave-offering which ye shall take of them,—gold and silver and bronze;
texts.exo.25.4: and blue, and purple, and crimson and fine linen, and goat’s hair;
texts.exo.25.5: and rams’ skins dyed red, and badgers’ skins and acacia wood;
texts.exo.25.6: oil for giving light,—perfumes for the anointing oil, and for fragrant incense;
texts.exo.25.7: onyx stones, and setting stones,—for the ephod and for the breastpiece:
texts.exo.25.8: So shall they make for me a sanctuary,—and I will make my habitation in their midst:
texts.exo.25.9: according to all that, I, am shewing thee, the pattern of the habitation, and the pattern of all the furnishings thereof, even so, shall ye make it.
texts.exo.25.10: And they shall make an ark of acacia wood,-two cubits and a half, the length thereof and, a cubit and a half, the breadth thereof, and, a cubit and a half, the height thereof.
texts.exo.25.11: And thou shalt overlay it with pure gold, within and without, shalt thou overlay it,—and thou shalt make thereon a rim of gold, round about.
texts.exo.25.12: And thou shalt cast for it four rings of gold, and shalt put them on the four feet thereof,—even two rings on the one side thereof, and two rings on the other side thereof.
texts.exo.25.13: And thou shalt make staves, of acacia wood,—and shalt overlay them with gold.
texts.exo.25.14: And thou shalt bring in the staves into the rings, on the sides of the ark,—to bear the ark therewith,
texts.exo.25.15: In the rings of the ark, shall remain the staves,—they shall not be removed therefrom.
texts.exo.25.16: And thou shalt put into the ark,—the testimony which I will give unto thee.
texts.exo.25.17: And thou shalt make a propitiatory, of pure gold,—two cubits and a half, the length thereof, and, a cubit and a half, the breadth thereof,
texts.exo.25.18: And thou shalt make two cherubim of gold,—of beaten work, shalt thou make them, out of the two ends of the propitiatory.
texts.exo.25.19: And make thou one cherub out of this end, and the other cherub out of that end,—out of the propitiatory, shall ye make the cherubim upon the two ends thereof.
texts.exo.25.20: And the cherubim shall be spreading out two wings on high—making a shelter with their wings over the propitiatory, with their faces one towards the other,—towards the propitiatory, shall be the faces of the cherubim.
texts.exo.25.21: And thou shalt put the propitiatory upon the ark above,—and in the ark, shalt thou put the testimony, which I will give unto thee.
texts.exo.25.22: And I will meet with thee there, and will speak with thee from off the propitiatory, from between the two cherubim, which are upon the ark of the testimony,—whatsoever I may give thee in charge, for the sons of Israel.
texts.exo.25.23: And thou shalt make a table, of acacia wood, two cubits, the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof.
texts.exo.25.24: and thou shalt overlay it with pure gold,—and shalt make thereto a rim of gold, round about;
texts.exo.25.25: and thou shalt make thereto a border of a handbreadth, round about,—and shalt make a rim of gold to the border thereof, round about;
texts.exo.25.26: and thou shalt make to it four rings of gold,—and shalt place the rings on the four corners which pertain to the four feet thereof:
texts.exo.25.27: adjoining the border, shall be the rings,—as receptacles for the staves, for lifting the table;
texts.exo.25.28: and thou shalt make the staves of acacia wood, and shalt overlay them with gold,—and the table shall be lifted there, with;
texts.exo.25.29: and thou shalt make its dishes and its pans and its basins and its bowls, for pouring out therewith,—of pure gold, shalt thou make them.
texts.exo.25.30: And thou shalt place upon the table Presence-bread, before me continually.
texts.exo.25.31: And thou shalt make a lampstand of pure gold, of beaten work, shall the lampstand be made, even its base and its shaft its cups, its apples, and its blossoms of the same, shall be:
texts.exo.25.32: with, six branches, coming out of its sides, three branches of the lampstand, out the one side thereof, and three branches of the lampstand, out of the other side thereof:
texts.exo.25.33: three cups like almond-flowers, in the one branch apple and blossom, and, three cups like almond-flowers, in the other branch apple and blossom, so, for the six branches, coming out of the lampstand.
texts.exo.25.34: And in the lampstand itself, four cups,—like almond-flowers—its apples, and its blossoms;
texts.exo.25.35: and an apple under two branches of the same, and, another apple, under two other branches of the same, and another apple under two other branches, of the same,—for the six branches, coming out of the lampstand:
texts.exo.25.36: their apples and their branches, of the same, shall be,—all of it, of one beaten work, of pure gold.
texts.exo.25.37: And thou shalt make the lamps thereof seven, and one shall light up its lamps, and it shall give light, over against the face thereof.
texts.exo.25.38: And, its snuffers, and its snuff-trays of pure gold.
texts.exo.25.39: With a talent of pure gold, shall he make it, with all these vessels,
texts.exo.25.40: And see thou and make them, by the pattern of them, which thou wast caused to behold in the mount
texts.exo.26.1: Also the habitation shalt thou make, with ten curtains, of twined linen, and blue, and purple, and crimson, with cherubim, the work of a skilful weaver, shalt thou make them.
texts.exo.26.2: The length of each curtain twenty-eight cubits, and, the breadth four cubits, of each curtain, one measure, for all the curtains.
texts.exo.26.3: The five curtains, shall be joined, one to another, and, the other five curtains, joined, one to another.
texts.exo.26.4: And thou shalt make loops of blue on the border of each curtain, at the edge of the set,—and, thus, shalt thou do in the border of the curtain, that is outmost in the second set:
texts.exo.26.5: fifty loops, shalt thou make, in the one curtain, and fifty loops, shalt thou make in the edge of the curtain which is in the second set, the loops being opposite, one to another.
texts.exo.26.6: And thou shalt make fifty clasps of gold,—so shalt thou join the curtains one to another, with the clasps, and thus shall the habitation be one.
texts.exo.26.7: And thou shalt make curtains of goat’s hair, for a tent, over the habitation—eleven curtains, shalt thou make them.
texts.exo.26.8: The length of each curtain, thirty cubits, and the breadth, four cubits, of each curtain,—one measure, to the eleven curtains.
texts.exo.26.9: And thou shalt join the five curtains by themselves, and the six curtains by themselves, and thou shalt fold back the sixth curtain, in the forefront of the tent.
texts.exo.26.10: And thou shalt make fifty loops on the border of the one curtain, that is outmost in the set, and fifty loops on the border of the curtain, of the second set.
texts.exo.26.11: And thou shalt make fifty clasps of bronze, and bring the clasps into the loops, so shalt thou join the tent, and it shall be one.
texts.exo.26.12: And the overplus that remaineth in the curtains of the tent,—the half curtain that remaineth, shall hang over at the back of the habitation.
texts.exo.26.13: And, the cubit on the one side, and the cubit on the other side of that which remaineth, in the length of the curtains of the tent shall be hung over the sides of the habitation on this side and on that side to make a covering.
texts.exo.26.14: And thou shalt make a covering, for the tent, of rams’ skins dyed red,—and a covering of badger’s skins, above.
texts.exo.26.15: And thou shalt make boards for the habitation,—of acacia wood to stand up:
texts.exo.26.16: ten cubits, the length of the board, and a cubit and a half cubit the breadth of each board:
texts.exo.26.17: two tenons, to each board, united one to another,—thus, shalt thou make, for all the boards of the habitation,
texts.exo.26.18: So then thou shalt make the boards for the habitation, twenty boards, on the south side southwards.
texts.exo.26.19: And forty sockets of silver, shalt thou make under the twenty boards,—two sockets under the one board for its two tenons, and two sockets, under the next board, for its two tenons.
texts.exo.26.20: And on the second side of the habitation, towards the north, twenty boards;
texts.exo.26.21: and their forty sockets of silver,—two sockets, under the one board, and, two sockets, under the next board.
texts.exo.26.22: And for the hinderpart of the habitation, westward, shalt thou make six boards.
texts.exo.26.23: And, two boards, shalt thou make, for the corners of the habitation,—in the hinderpart:
texts.exo.26.24: that they may be double beneath, and at the same time, they shall be entire on the top thereof, into each ring,—thus, shall it be for them both, for the two corners, shall they be.
texts.exo.26.25: So shall they be eight boards, and, their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets,—two sockets, under the one board, and, two sockets, under the next board.
texts.exo.26.26: And thou shalt make bars, of acacia wood,—five, for the boards of the one side of the habitation,
texts.exo.26.27: and five bars, for the boards of the other side of the habitation, and five bars, for the boards of the side of the habitation, at the hinderpart westward;
texts.exo.26.28: with the middle bar in the midst of the boards,—running along from end to end.
texts.exo.26.29: And the boards, shalt thou overlay with gold, and their rings, shalt thou make of gold, as receptacles for the bars,—and thou shalt overlay the bars with gold.
texts.exo.26.30: So shalt thou rear up the habitation, according to the fashion thereof, which thou wast caused to see in the mount.
texts.exo.26.31: And thou shalt make a veil, of blue and purple, and crimson and fine-twined linen,—of the work of a skilful weaver, shall it be made, with cherubim;
texts.exo.26.32: and thou shalt hang it upon four pillars of acacia overlaid with gold, with their hooks of gold,—upon four sockets of silver,
texts.exo.26.33: And thou shalt hang up the veil under the clasps,—and shalt bring in thither, within the veil the ark of the testimony; and the veil shall make a division for you between the holy [place] and the most holy.
texts.exo.26.34: And thou shalt place the propitiatory, upon the ark of the testimony,—in the most holy [place].
texts.exo.26.35: And thou shalt set the table outside the veil, and the lampstand over against the table, on the side of the habitation, southward,—and the table, shalt thou place on the north side.
texts.exo.26.36: And thou shalt make a screen for the opening of the tent, of blue, and purple and crimson, and fine-twined linen,—the work of an embroiderer.
texts.exo.26.37: And thou shalt make for the screen five pillars of acacia, and shalt overlay them with gold, and their hooks [shall be] of gold,—and thou shalt cast for them five sockets of bronze.
texts.exo.27.1: And thou shalt make the altar of acacia wood,—of five cubits length and five cubits breadth four square, shall the altar be, and three cubits the height thereof.
texts.exo.27.2: And thou shalt make its horns upon its four corners, of the same, shall be its horns,—and thou shalt overlay it with copper.
texts.exo.27.3: And thou shalt make its pans for removing its ashes, and its shovels and its sprinkling bowls, and its flesh-hooks and its fire-pans,—all its vessels, shalt thou make of bronze.
texts.exo.27.4: And thou shalt make to it a grating, a network of bronze,—and thou shalt make upon the network, four rings of bronze, upon the four corners thereof.
texts.exo.27.5: And thou shalt place it under the margin of the altar beneath,—so shall the network reach unto the midst of the altar.
texts.exo.27.6: And thou shalt make staves for the altar, staves of acacia wood,—and shalt overlay them with copper.
texts.exo.27.7: And the staves shall be brought into the rings,—so shall the staves be on the two sides of the altar in lifting it:
texts.exo.27.8: Hollow with boards, shalt thou make it,—as it was showed thee in the mount, so, shall they make it.
texts.exo.27.9: And thou shalt make the court of the habitation,—on the south side southward, hangings for the court of fine-twined linen, a hundred cubits in length to the one side;
texts.exo.27.10: and the pillars thereof twenty, with their sockets twenty, of bronze,—and the hooks of the pillars and their cross-rods of silver.
texts.exo.27.11: And, so, for the north side in length, hangings a hundred cubits,—and the pillars thereof twenty, and their sockets twenty. of bronze, and the hooks of the pillars and their cross-rods of silver.
texts.exo.27.12: And, the breadth of the court on the west side, hangings fifty cubits,—their pillars ten, and their sockets ten.
texts.exo.27.13: And, the breadth of the court on the east side eastward, fifty cubits;
texts.exo.27.14: and fifteen cubits the hangings for the side-piece,—their pillars three, and their sockets three;
texts.exo.27.15: and, for the second side-piece, fifteen hangings,—their pillars three, and their sockets three,
texts.exo.27.16: And for the gate of the court, a screen of twenty cubits, of blue, and purple and crimson and fine-twined linen, the work of an embroiderer,—their pillars four, and their sockets four.
texts.exo.27.17: All the pillars of the court round about, to be joined with cross-rods of silver, and their hooks of silver,—and their sockets of bronze,
texts.exo.27.18: The length of the court, a hundred cubits and the breadth fifty throughout and the height five cubits of fine-twined linen,—and their sockets, of bronze.
texts.exo.27.19: All the utensils of the habitation, throughout all the service thereof,—and all the pins thereof, and all the pins of the court, of bronze.
texts.exo.27.20: Thou thyself, therefore, shalt command the sons of Israel that they bring unto thee—pure, beaten olive-oil, for giving light,—that the lamp may lift up its flame continually.
texts.exo.27.21: In the tent of meeting, outside the veil which is by the testimony, shall Aaron and his sons order it from evening until morning, before Yahweh,—a statute age-abiding, to their generations, from the sons of Israel.
texts.exo.28.1: Thou thyself, therefore bring near unto thee—Aaron thy brother and his sons with him out of the midst of the sons of Israel, that they may minister as priests unto me,—Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar sons of Aaron.
texts.exo.28.2: And thou shalt make holy garments for Aaron thy brother,—for glory and for beauty.
texts.exo.28.3: Thou thyself, therefore, shalt speak unto all the wise-hearted, whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom,—and they shall make Aaron’s garments, to hallow him for ministering as priest unto me.
texts.exo.28.4: These, therefore are the garments which they shall make—a breastpiece, and an ephod and a robe, and a tunic of checker work, a turban and a girdle,—so shall they make holy garments for Aaron thy brother and for his sons, for ministering as priests unto me.
texts.exo.28.5: They themselves, therefore, shall take the gold, and the blue and the purple,—and the crimson, and the fine linen.
texts.exo.28.6: And they shall make the ephod,—of gold, blue and purple crimson and fine-twined linen, the work of a skilful weaver.
texts.exo.28.7: Two joining shoulderpieces, shall there be to it upon the two extremities thereof that it may be joined together,
texts.exo.28.8: And the curious band for fastening it, that is upon it, like the work thereof of the same, shall it be,—of gold blue and purple and crimson and fine-twined linen,
texts.exo.28.9: And thou shalt take two onyx stones,—and engrave upon them the names of the sons of Israel:
texts.exo.28.10: six of their names, on the one stone,—and the names of the six that remain, on the second stone according to their births:
texts.exo.28.11: with the work of a stone engraver, like seal-ring engravings, shalt thou engrave the two stones, after the names of the sons of Israel,—to be encircled with settings of gold, shalt thou make them.
texts.exo.28.12: And thou shalt put the two stones upon the shoulderpieces of the ephod, as stones of memorial for the sons of Israel,—so shall Aaron bear their names before Yahweh upon his two shoulders, for a memorial.
texts.exo.28.13: And thou shalt make ouches of gold;
texts.exo.28.14: and two chains of pure gold, like cord, shalt thou make them, of wreathen work, and thou shalt put the wreathen chains on the ouches.
texts.exo.28.15: And thou shalt make a breastpiece for giving sentence the work of a skilful weaver, like the work of the ephod, shalt thou make it, of gold, blue, and purple and crimson and fine-twined linen, shalt thou make it.
texts.exo.28.16: Four-square, shall it be double,—a span the length thereof and a span the breadth thereof.
texts.exo.28.17: And thou shalt set therein a setting of stones, four rows of stones,—one row—a sardius, a topaz and an emerald, the first row;
texts.exo.28.18: and the second row a carbuncle a sapphire and a diamond;
texts.exo.28.19: and the third row an opal, an agate, and an amethyst;
texts.exo.28.20: and the fourth row, a Tarshish stone, a sardonyx, and a jasper,—enclosed with gold, shall they be when they are set.
texts.exo.28.21: And the stones shall be after the names of the sons of Israel—twelve, after their names,—as the engravings of a seal-ring everyone after his name, shall they be, for the twelve tribes,
texts.exo.28.22: And thou shalt make, upon the breastpiece, chains like cords of wreathen work,—of pure gold.
texts.exo.28.23: And thou shalt make, upon the breastpiece, two rings of gold,—and thou shalt place the two rings, upon the two ends of the breastpiece.
texts.exo.28.24: And thou shalt hang the two wreathen chains of gold upon the two rings,—upon the ends of the breastpiece;
texts.exo.28.25: and the other two ends of the two wreathen chains, shalt thou fasten upon the two ouches, so shalt thou hang them upon the shoulderpieces of the ephod, in the forefront thereof.
texts.exo.28.26: And thou shalt make two rings of gold, and put them on the two ends of the breastpiece upon the border thereof, which is on the side of the ephod inwards.
texts.exo.28.27: And thou shalt make two rings of gold, and place them upon the two shoulderpieces of the ephod beneath, on the front of the face thereof, over against its joining, above the curious band of the ephod:
texts.exo.28.28: that they may bind the breastpiece by the rings thereof unto the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue, so that it may remain upon the curious band of the ephod, and the breastpiece not be removed from of the ephod.
texts.exo.28.29: So shall Aaron bear the names of the sons of Israel in the breastpiece for giving sentence upon his heart when he goeth into the holy place,—for a memorial before Yahweh continually.
texts.exo.28.30: Thus shalt thou place, in the breastpiece for giving sentence, the lights and the perfections, so shall they be upon the heart of Aaron when he goeth in before Yahweh,—so shall Aaron bear the sentence of the sons of Israel, upon his heart before Yahweh continually.
texts.exo.28.31: And thou shalt make the robe of the ephod wholly of blue;
texts.exo.28.32: and the opening for his head shall be in the midst thereof,—a border, shall there be to the opening thereof round about the work of a weaver, like the opening of a coat of mail, shall there be to it, it must not be rent.
texts.exo.28.33: And thou shalt make upon the skirts thereof pomegranates of blue and purple and crimson, upon the skirts thereof round about—and bells of gold in the midst of them round about:
texts.exo.28.34: a bell of gold and a pomegranate, a bell of gold, and a pomegranate,—upon the skirts of the robe, round about.
texts.exo.28.35: And it shall be upon Aaron, for ministering,—so shall be heard the sound of him—when he goeth into the holy place, before Yahweh, and cometh out, and dieth not.
texts.exo.28.36: And thou shalt make a burnished plate, of pure gold,—and shalt engrave thereupon, like the engravings of a seal-ring, Holiness to Yahweh.
texts.exo.28.37: And thou shalt put it upon a cord of blue, so shall it be upon the turban,—upon the forefront of the turban, shall it be.
texts.exo.28.38: So shall it be upon the forehead of Aaron, and Aaron shall bear the iniquity of the hallowed things, which the sons of Israel shall hallow, for all their hallowed gift,—and it shall be upon his forehead continually, that there may be acceptance for them before Yahweh.
texts.exo.28.39: And thou shalt weave, in checker work the tunic of fine linen, and shalt make a turban of fine linen,—and, a girdle, shalt thou make the work of an embroiderer.
texts.exo.28.40: And, for the sons of Aaron, shalt thou make tunics, and shalt make for them girdles,—and caps, shalt thou make for them, for glory and for beauty.
texts.exo.28.41: And thou shalt clothe therewith Aaron thy brother, and his sons, with him,—and shalt anoint them and install them, and hallow them, so shall they minister as priests unto me.
texts.exo.28.42: And thou shalt make for them breeches of linen, to cover their unseemliness, from the loins even unto the thighs, shall they be;
texts.exo.28.43: so shall they be upon Aaron and upon his sons, when they go into the tent of meeting, or when they approach unto the altar, to minister in the holy place, lest they bear iniquity, and die,—a statute age-abiding, to him and to his seed after him.
texts.exo.29.1: And, this, is the thing which thou shalt do to them to hallow them, that they may minister as priests unto me,—Take one young bullock and two rams without defect;
texts.exo.29.2: and bread unleavened and cakes unleavened with oil poured over, and wafers unleavened anointed with oil,—of fine wheaten meal, shalt thou make them;
texts.exo.29.3: and thou shalt place them in one basket, and bring them near in the basket,—and the bullock, and the two rams.
texts.exo.29.4: And Aaron and his sons, shalt thou bring near, unto the opening of the tent of meeting,—and shalt bathe them in water.
texts.exo.29.5: And thou shalt take the garments and clothe Aaron—with the tunic, and with the robe of the ephod, and with the ephod, and with the breastpiece,—and shalt gird him with the curious band of the ephod;
texts.exo.29.6: and shalt put the turban upon his head,—and place the holy crown upon the turban.
texts.exo.29.7: Then shalt thou take the anointing oil, and pour upon his head,—so shalt thou anoint him.
texts.exo.29.8: His sons also, shalt thou bring near,—and clothe them with tunics;
texts.exo.29.9: and thou shalt gird them with girdles, Aaron and his sons, and twist round for them caps, so shall they have priesthood by a statute age-abiding,—so shalt thou install, Aaron and his sons.
texts.exo.29.10: And thou shalt bring near the bullock, before the tent of meeting,—and Aaron and his sons shall lean their hands upon the head of the bullock;
texts.exo.29.11: then shalt thou slay the bullock before Yahweh,—at the opening of the tent of meeting:
texts.exo.29.12: and thou shalt take of the blood of the bullock, and place upon the horns of the altar, with thy finger,—and all the remaining blood, shalt thou pour out at the foundation of the altar;
texts.exo.29.13: and thou shalt take all the fat that covereth the inner part, and the caul upon the liver, and the two kidneys, with the fat which is upon them, and burn as incense on the altar:
texts.exo.29.14: but the flesh of the bullock and its skin, and its dung, shalt thou burn up with fire, outside the camp,—a sin-bearer, it is.
texts.exo.29.15: One ram also, shalt thou take, and Aaron and his sons shall lean their hands, upon the head of the ram;
texts.exo.29.16: then shalt thou slay the ram,—and take its blood, and dash upon the altar round about;
texts.exo.29.17: but the ram itself, shalt thou cut up into its pieces,—and shalt bathe its inner part, and its legs, and lay upon its pieces and upon its head;
texts.exo.29.18: and shalt burn the whole ram as incense on the altar, an ascending-sacrifice, it is to Yahweh,—a satisfying odour, an altar-flame to Yahweh, it is.
texts.exo.29.19: Then shalt thou take the second ram,—and Aaron and his sons shall lean their hands upon the head of the ram;
texts.exo.29.20: then shalt thou slay the ram, and take of its blood, and place upon the tip of the ear of Aaron and upon the tip of the ear of his sons—the right ear, and upon the thumb of their right hand, and upon the great toe of their right foot,—and shalt dash the blood upon the altar round about.
texts.exo.29.21: Then shalt thou take of the blood that is upon the altar and of the anointing oil, and sprinkle upon Aaron and upon his garments, and upon his sons and upon the garments of his sons with him,—so shall he be hallowed—he, and his garments, and his sons and the garments of his sons, with him.
texts.exo.29.22: Then shalt thou take from the ram—the fat and the fat-tail and the fat that covereth the inner part and the caul of the liver and the two kidneys with the fat that is upon them, and the right shoulder,—for, a ram of installation, it is,—
texts.exo.29.23: and one round-cake of bread, and one cake of oiled bread, and one wafer,—out of the basket of unleavened cakes, which is before Yahweh;
texts.exo.29.24: and shalt lay the whole upon the heads of Aaron, and upon the hands of his sons,—then shalt thou wave them to and fro as a wave-offering, before Yahweh;
texts.exo.29.25: and shalt take them from their hand, and burn them as incense on the altar upon the ascending-sacrifice,—as a satisfying odour, before Yahweh, an altar-flame, it is to Yahweh.
texts.exo.29.26: Then shalt thou take the breast from the ram of installation which is for Aaron, and shalt wave it as a wave-offering, before Yahweh,—so shall it be thy share,
texts.exo.29.27: And thou shalt hallow the breast of the wave-offering, and the shoulder of the heave-offering, which is waved to and fro, and which is heaved up, from the ram of installation, from that which is for Aaron, and from that which is for his sons;
texts.exo.29.28: so shall it belong to Aaron and to his sons for an age-abiding statute from the sons of Israel, for a heave-offering, it is,—and, a heave-offering, shall it remain, from the sons of Israel out of their peace-offerings, their heave-offering to Yahweh.
texts.exo.29.29: And, the holy garments which belong to Aaron, shall belong to his sons, after him,-to be anointed therein, and to be installed therein,
texts.exo.29.30: Seven days, shall they be put on by him from among his sons who is priest in his stead,—by him who goeth into the tent of meeting, to minister in the holy place.
texts.exo.29.31: And, the ram of installation, shalt thou take,—and shalt boil its flesh, in a holy place;
texts.exo.29.32: and Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram, and the bread that is in the basket,—at the opening of the tent of meeting:
texts.exo.29.33: thus shall they eat those things wherewith a propitiatory-covering hath been made, to install them, to hallow them, but, a stranger, shall not eat, for holy, they are.
texts.exo.29.34: And, if there be left over of the flesh of installation, or of the bread until the morning, then shalt thou burn up what is left over, in the fire, it shall not be eaten for holy, it is.
texts.exo.29.35: So then thou shalt do for Aaron and for his sons, in this manner, according to all which I have commanded, thee,—seven days, shalt thou install them.
