texts.exo.29.36: And a sin-bearing bullock, shalt thou offer daily, for them who are to be covered by propitiation, and shalt make a sin-cleansing for the altar, when thou puttest a propitiatory-covering thereon,—and shalt anoint it to hallow it.
texts.exo.29.37: Seven days, shalt thou put a propitiatory-covering over the altar, and so shalt hallow it, thus shall the altar become most holy; whosoever toucheth the altar, must be holy.
texts.exo.29.38: This, moreover, is what thou shalt offer upon the altar, two lambs of a year old day by day, continually:
texts.exo.29.39: The one lamb, shalt thou offer in the morning, and the second lamb, shalt thou offer between the evenings;
texts.exo.29.40: and a tenth part of fine meal mingled with a fourth part of the hin of beaten oil, and, as a drink-offering, a fourth part of the hin of wine,—with the one lamb.
texts.exo.29.41: And the second lamb, shalt thou offer between the evenings,-according to the meal-offering of the morning, and according to the drink-offering thereof, shalt thou offer with it, for a satisfying odour, an altar-flame, to Yahweh:
texts.exo.29.42: a continual ascending-sacrifice to your generations, at the opening of the tent of meeting, before Yahweh, where will meet with you, to speak unto thee there.
texts.exo.29.43: So will I meet there with the sons of Israel, and it shall be hallowed by my glory.
texts.exo.29.44: Thus will I hallow the tent of meeting, and the altar,—and, Aaron and his sons, will I hallow, to minister as priests unto me.
texts.exo.29.45: Thus will I make my habitation in the midst of the sons of Israel, and will be their God;
texts.exo.29.46: and they shall know that, I—Yahweh, am their God, who brought them forth out of the land of Egypt that I might make my habitation in their midst, I—Yahweh, their God.
texts.exo.30.1: And thou shalt make an altar, for burning incense, of acacia wood, shalt thou make it:
texts.exo.30.2: a cubit, the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof four square, shall it be,—and two cubits, the height thereof, of the same, [shall be] the horns thereof,
texts.exo.30.3: And thou shalt overlay it with pure gold the top thereof, and the sides thereof round about, and the horns thereof,-and thou shalt make to it a border of gold round about.
texts.exo.30.4: And, two rings of gold, shalt thou make to it, under the border thereof upon the two corners thereof, shalt thou make them on the two sides thereof,—so shall they become receptacles for the staves, to lift it therewith.
texts.exo.30.5: And thou shalt make the staves of acacia wood,—and overlay them with gold.
texts.exo.30.6: And thou shalt place it before the veil, which is by the ark of the testimony,—before the propitiatory which is upon the testimony, where I will meet thee.
texts.exo.30.7: And Aaron shall burn thereon fragrant incense,—morning by morning, when he trimmeth the lamps, shall he burn it;
texts.exo.30.8: and, when Aaron lighteth the lamps, between the evenings, shall he burn it,—a continual incense before Yahweh, to your generations.
texts.exo.30.9: Ye shall not cause to ascend thereupon strange incense, nor an ascending-sacrifice, nor a meal-offering,—and a drink offering, shall ye not pour out thereupon.
texts.exo.30.10: But Aaron shall put a propitiatory-covering upon the horns thereof, once in the year: of the blood of the sin-bearer for propitiatory-coverings, once in the year, shall he put a propitiatory-covering thereupon to your generations, most holy, it is to Yahweh.
texts.exo.30.11: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying—
texts.exo.30.12: When thou takest the sum of the sons of Israel, by their numberings, then shall they give every man a propitiatory-covering for his soul to Yahweh, when they are numbered,—that there may be among them no plague when they are numbered.
texts.exo.30.13: This, shall they give—every one that passeth over to them that have been numbered—a half-shekel by the shekel of the sanctuary,—the shekel is twenty gerahs—the half-shekel, shall be a heave-offering to Yahweh.
texts.exo.30.14: All who pass over to the numbered, from twenty years old and upwards, shall give the heave-offering of Yahweh.
texts.exo.30.15: The rich, shall not give more, and the poor, shall not give less, than the half-shekel,—when they give the heave-offering of Yahweh, to put a propitiatory-covering over your souls.
texts.exo.30.16: So then thou shalt take the silver for the propitiatory-coverings from the sons of Israel, and shalt expend it upon the service of the tent of meeting,—thus shall it be for the sons of Israel as a memorial before Yahweh, to put a propitiatory-covering over your souls.
texts.exo.30.17: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying—
texts.exo.30.18: And thou shalt make a laver of bronze, and its stand of bronze for bathing,—and thou shalt place it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and shalt put therein water.
texts.exo.30.19: So shall Aaron and his sons bathe thereat,—their hands, and their feet.
texts.exo.30.20: When they enter the tent of meeting, they shall bathe with water so shall they not die,—or when they approach unto the altar to minister, to burn as incense an altar-flame to Yahweh:
texts.exo.30.21: so then they shall bathe their hands and their feet and shall not die,—and it shall be to them an age-abiding statute, to him and to his seed to their generations.
texts.exo.30.22: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying—
texts.exo.30.23: Thou, therefore, take to thee—principal spices,—self-flowing myrrh, five hundred, and fragrant cinnamon, half as much, two hundred and fifty, and, fragrant cane, two hundred and fifty;
texts.exo.30.24: and, cassia, five hundred, by the shekel of the sanctuary,—and, oil olive, a hin.
texts.exo.30.25: And thou shalt make it an oil for holy anointing, a compounded perfume the work of a perfumer,—an oil for holy anointing, shall it be.
texts.exo.30.26: And thou shalt anoint therewith the tent of meeting,—and the ark of the testimony;
texts.exo.30.27: and the table and all its utensils, and the lampstand, and its utensils,—and the incense altar,
texts.exo.30.28: and the altar for the ascending-sacrifice, and all its utensils,-and the laver, and its stand.
texts.exo.30.29: So shalt thou hallow them, and they shall be most holy,—whosoever toucheth them, shall be holy.
texts.exo.30.30: Aaron also, and his sons, shalt thou anoint,—so shalt thou hallow them to minister as priests unto me.
texts.exo.30.31: And unto the sons of Israel, shalt thou speak, saying, An oil for holy anointing, shall this be to me, to your generations.
texts.exo.30.32: Upon the flesh of a common man, shall it not be poured, and according to the proportions thereof, shall ye not make any like it,—holy, it is, holy, shall it be to you.
texts.exo.30.33: Whosoever compoundeth any like it, and whosoever bestoweth thereof upon a stranger, shall be cut off from among his people.
texts.exo.30.34: Then said Yahweh unto Moses—Take to thee aromatic spices stacte and onycha, and galbanum,—aromatic spices, and pure frankincense,—weight for weight, shall it be.
texts.exo.30.35: And thou shalt make of it an incense, a perfume the work of a perfumer,—salted, pure, holy.
texts.exo.30.36: And thou shalt beat some of it to powder, and place thereof before the testimony, in the tent of meeting, where I am to meet with thee,—most holy, shall it be to you.
texts.exo.30.37: And the incense which thou shalt make, according to the proportions thereof, ye shall not make for yourselves,—holy, shall it be to thee, to Yahweh.
texts.exo.30.38: Whosoever shall make like it, to smell of it shall be cut off from among his people.
texts.exo.31.1: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying:
texts.exo.31.2: See, I have called by name, Bezaleel, son of Uri, son of Hur of the tribe of Judah;
texts.exo.31.3: and have filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom and in understanding, and in knowledge and in all manner of workmanship;
texts.exo.31.4: to devise skilful designs, to work in gold and in silver, and in bronze;
texts.exo.31.5: and in the cutting of stones for setting, and in the carving of wood,—to work in all manner of workmanship,
texts.exo.31.6: I myself, therefore, lo! I have given with him Oholiab, son of Ahisamach of the tribe of Dan, and in the heart of every one that is wise-hearted, have I put wisdom,—so shall they make all that I have commanded thee—
texts.exo.31.7: the tent of meeting, and the ark of the testimony; and the propitiatory which is thereupon, and all the utensils of the tent;
texts.exo.31.8: and the table, and its utensils, and the pure lampstand, and all its utensils,—and the incense altar;
texts.exo.31.9: and the altar for the ascending-sacrifice, and all its utensils, and the laver, and its stand;
texts.exo.31.10: and the cloths of variegated stuff, and the holy garments, for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, for ministering as priests;
texts.exo.31.11: and the anointing oil and the fragrant incense for the holy place, according to all which I have commanded thee, shall they do.
texts.exo.31.12: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses saying—
texts.exo.31.13: Thou thyself, therefore, speak unto the sons of Israel, saying, Surely, my sabbaths, shall ye keep, for, a sign it is betwixt me and you to your generations, that ye may know that I Yahweh do hallow you.
texts.exo.31.14: Therefore shall ye keep the sabbath, for holy, it is unto you, he that profaneth it shall be surely put to death; verily whosoever doeth therein any work that soul shall be cut off from the midst of its people:
texts.exo.31.15: Six days, shall work be done, but on the seventh day, is a holy sabbath-keeping of rest unto Yahweh,—whosoever doeth work on the sabbath day, shall be, surely put to death.
texts.exo.31.16: Therefore shall the sons of Israel keep the sabbath,—by making it a Day of Rest to your generations, as an age-abiding covenant:
texts.exo.31.17: between me and the sons of Israel, a sign it is unto times age-abiding,—for in six days, did Yahweh make the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day, he rested, and was refreshed.
texts.exo.31.18: Then gave he unto Moses, as he finished speaking with him in Mount Sinai, the two tables of the testimony,—tables of stone, written with the finger of God,
texts.exo.32.1: And, when the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron, and said unto him—Up, make for us gods, who shall go before us, for, as for this Moses—the man who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we know not what hath befallen him.
texts.exo.32.2: And Aaron said unto them, Break off the rings of gold, which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons and of your daughters,—and bring them unto me.
texts.exo.32.3: And all the people of themselves brake off the rings of gold which were in their ears, and brought them unto Aaron.
texts.exo.32.4: And he received [the gold] at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, and made it a molten calf, and they said—These, are thy gods, O Israel, who brought thee up, out of the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.32.5: And when Aaron saw it, he built an altar before it. And Aaron made proclamation, and said, A festival to Yahweh, to-morrow!
texts.exo.32.6: So they rose up early, on the morrow, and offered ascending-sacrifices, and brought near peace-offerings, and the people sat down, to eat and to drink, and then rose up—to make sport!
texts.exo.32.7: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses—Go get thee down, for thy people whom thou hast brought up out of the land of Egypt have corrupted themselves.
texts.exo.32.8: They have turned aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them, they have made for themselves—a molten calf, and have bowed themselves down thereto and have sacrificed thereto, and have said. These, are thy gods, O Israel, who have brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
texts.exo.32.9: So then Yahweh said unto Moses,—I have looked on this people, and lo! a stiff-necked people, it is.
texts.exo.32.10: Now, therefore, let me alone, that mine anger may kindle upon them and that I may consume them, and may make of thee a great nation.
texts.exo.32.11: And Moses besought the face of Yahweh his God,—and said—Wherefore, O Yahweh, should thine anger kindle upon thy people, whom thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great might and with a firm hand?
texts.exo.32.12: Wherefore should the Egyptians speak saying—For mischief, hath he taken them forth to slay them among the mountains, and to make an end of them from off the face of the ground? Turn thou from the kindling of thine anger, and be grieved over the calamity to thy people,
texts.exo.32.13: Have remembrance of Abraham, of Isaac and of Israel thy servants to whom thou didst swear by thyself, and didst speak unto them saying, I will multiply your seed, as the stars of the heavens,—and, all this land of which I have spoken, will I give to your seed, and they shall inherit it to times age-abiding.
texts.exo.32.14: So then Yahweh was grieved,—over the calamity—which he had spoken of inflicting on his people.
texts.exo.32.15: And Moses turned and went down out of the mount, with the two tables of testimony in his hand,—tables written upon on both sides of them, on this and on that, were they written.
texts.exo.32.16: Now as for, the tables, the work of God, they were,—and, as for the writing, the writing of God, it was, graven upon the tables.
texts.exo.32.17: And Joshua heard the noise of the people as they shouted,—so he said unto Moses—The noise of war, in the camp!
texts.exo.32.18: But he said—Not the noise of the cry of heroism, nor yet the noise of the cry of defeat,—the noise of alternate song, do I hear.
texts.exo.32.19: And it came to pass when he drew near unto the camp, and saw the calf, and the dancings, that the anger of Moses kindled, and he cast out of his hands the tables, and brake them in pieces at the foot of the mountain.
texts.exo.32.20: Then took he the calf which they had made and burned it in the fire, and ground it till it became powder, and strewed it on the face of the waters, and made the sons of Israel drink.
texts.exo.32.21: And Moses said unto Aaron, What had this people done to thee,—that thou shouldst have brought upon them a great sin?
texts.exo.32.22: And Aaron said, Let not the anger of my lord kindle,—thou thyself, knowest the people, that ready for mischief, they are.
texts.exo.32.23: So they said to me—Make for us gods, who shall go before us,—for, as for this, Moses—the man who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we know not what hath befallen him.
texts.exo.32.24: And I said to them—Whosoever hath gold let them break it off, So they gave it to me,—and I cast it into the fire, and there came out—this calf.
texts.exo.32.25: And Moses saw the people, that unbridled, they were,—for Aaron had given them the rein, for a whispering, among their enemies.
texts.exo.32.26: So Moses took his stand in the gate of the camp, and said—Who is for Yahweh? …To me! Then gathered unto him all the sons of Levi,
texts.exo.32.27: And he said to them—Thus, saith Yahweh, God of Israel, Put ye every man his sword upon his thigh,—pass through and return from gate to gate in the camp, and slay ye every man his brother and every man his friend and every man his neighbour.
texts.exo.32.28: So the sons of Levi did, according to the word of Moses,—and there fell from among the people on that day, about three thousand men.
texts.exo.32.29: And Moses said—Install yourselves to-day, unto Yahweh, yea every man for his son and for his brother,—so will he bestow upon you to-day, a blessing.
texts.exo.32.30: And it came to pass, on the morrow, that Moses said unto the people, Ye, have sinned a great sin,—Now, therefore, I must go up unto Yahweh, Peradventure, I may make a propitiatory-covering for your sin.
texts.exo.32.31: So Moses returned unto Yahweh, and said,—Oh now, this people hath sinned a great sin, and they have made for themselves—gods of gold.
texts.exo.32.32: Now, therefore, if thou wilt forgive their sin, …but if not, blot me I pray thee out of thy book, which thou hast written,
texts.exo.32.33: And Yahweh said unto Moses,—Him who hath sinned against me, must I blot out of my book.
texts.exo.32.34: Now, therefore, go lead the people to the place of which I spake to thee, lo! my messenger, shall go before thee,—But, in the day when I do visit, then will I visit upon them their sin.
texts.exo.32.35: And Yahweh plagued the people,—for what they had done with the calf, which Aaron made.
texts.exo.33.1: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses—Get thee away, go up from hence, thou, and the people whom thou hast brought up out of the land of Egypt,—into the land of which I sware to Abraham to Isaac and to Jacob, saying, To thy seed, will I give it;
texts.exo.33.2: And I will send before thee a messenger,-and will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite;
texts.exo.33.3: into a land flowing with milk and honey,—for I will not go up in thy midst in that a stiff-necked people, thou art, lest I consume thee in the way.
texts.exo.33.4: And when the people heard these evil tidings, they afflicted themselves,—and they put not, any man, his ornaments upon him.
texts.exo.33.5: Then said Yahweh unto Moses—Say unto the sons of Israel, Ye, are a stiff-necked people, in one moment—if I should go up in thy midst, should I make an end of thee,—Now, therefore lay down thine ornaments from off thee, that I may see what I must do with thee.
texts.exo.33.6: So then the sons of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments, [and moved on] from Mount Horeb.
texts.exo.33.7: And, Moses, proceeded to take a tent, and pitch it by itself outside the camp, afar off from the camp, and he called it, The Tent of Meeting,—and so it came to pass that whosoever was seeking Yahweh went out unto the tent of meeting, which was on the outside of the camp.
texts.exo.33.8: And it came about, that, when Moses went out unto the tent, all the people used to rise up, and station themselves every man at the opening of his tent,—and they watched Moses, until he entered the tent.
texts.exo.33.9: And it came to pass that when Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud came down, and stood at the opening of the tent,—and spake with Moses.
texts.exo.33.10: And when all the people beheld the pillar of cloud, standing at the opening of the tent, then all the people rose up and bowed themselves down, every man at the entrance of his tent.
texts.exo.33.11: Thus Yahweh used to speak unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend,—and when he returned unto the camp, his attendant Joshua son of Nun, a young man, moved not from the midst of the tent.
texts.exo.33.12: Then said Moses, unto Yahweh, See! thou art saying unto me—Take up this people, and yet thou hast no let me know whom thou wilt send with me,—though thou thyself, didst say—I acknowledge thee by name, Yea, moreover, thou hast found favour in mine eyes.
texts.exo.33.13: Now, therefore, if, I pray thee, I have found favour in thine eyes, let me know, I beseech thee, thy way, that I may acknowledge thee, to the intent I may find favour in thine eyes,—see thou, therefore, that this nation is thine own people.
texts.exo.33.14: So then he said,—Mine own presence, shall go on thus will I give thee rest.
texts.exo.33.15: And he said unto him, If thy presence is not going on, do not take us up from hence.
texts.exo.33.16: Whereby, indeed, shall it be known then that I have found favour in thine eyes, I, and thy people? Shall it not be, by thy going on with us? So shall we be more distinguished, I, and thy people, than any people that are on the face of the ground.
texts.exo.33.17: Then said Yahweh unto Moses: Even this thing, which thou hast spoken, will I do—For thou hast found favour in mine eyes, And I have acknowledged thee by name.
texts.exo.33.18: And he said,—Show me, I pray thee, thy glory.
texts.exo.33.19: And he said,—I, will cause all my goodness to pass before thee. And will proclaim myself by the name Yahweh, before thee, And will show favour, unto whom I may show favour, And will have compassion on whom I may have compassion.
texts.exo.33.20: But he said—Thou canst not see my face, For no son of earth can see me, and live
texts.exo.33.21: And Yahweh, said, Lo! a place near me,—So then thou shalt station thyself upon the rock:
texts.exo.33.22: And it shall be while my glory passeth by, I will put thee in the cleft of the rock,—and will cover thee with my hand while I pass by:
texts.exo.33.23: Then will I take away my hand, and thou shalt see behind me, But, my face, must not be seen.
texts.exo.34.1: And Yahweh said unto Moses—Hew thee two tables of stone, like the first,—and I will write upon the tables the words which were upon the first tables which thou didst break in pieces;
texts.exo.34.2: and be thou ready by the morning,—and thou shalt come up. in the morning, into Mount Sinai; then shalt thou station thyself for me there upon the top of the mount;
texts.exo.34.3: and, no man, may come up with thee, and let no man so much as be seen in all the mount,—and let not even the flocks or the herds, feed in front of that mountain.
texts.exo.34.4: So he hewed two tables of stone like the first and Moses rose up early in the morning, and went up into Mount Sinai, as Yahweh had commanded him,—and took in his hand two tables of stone.
texts.exo.34.5: And Yahweh descended in the cloud, and took his station with him there,—and proclaimed himself by the name Yahweh.
texts.exo.34.6: So Yahweh passed before him, and proclaimed,—Yahweh, Yahweh, A God of compassion and favour,—Slow to anger and abundant in lovingkindness and faithfulness:
texts.exo.34.7: Keeping lovingkindness to a thousand generations, Forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, Though he leave not, utterly unpunished, Visiting the iniquity of fathers, Upon sons, And upon sons’ sons, Unto a third and unto a fourth generation.
texts.exo.34.8: Then Moses made haste,—and bent his head towards the earth and bowed himself down;
texts.exo.34.9: and said—If, I pray thee, I have found favour in thine eyes, O My Lord, I pray thee let My Lord go on in our midst,—although a stiff-necked people, it is, so wilt thou pardon our iniquity and our sin and take us as thine own.
texts.exo.34.10: And he said—Lo! I, am about to solemnise a covenant,-in presence of all thy people, will I do marvellous things, which have not been created in any part of the earth nor among any of the nations,—so shall all the people in whose midst thou, art see the work of Yahweh for a fearful thing, it is, which I, am doing with thee.
texts.exo.34.11: Take thou heed what, I, am commanding thee this day,—behold me! driving out from before thee—the Amorite, and the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
texts.exo.34.12: Take heed to thyself, Lest thou solemnise a covenant with the inhabitant of the land, whereupon, thou, art about to enter,—Lest he become a snare in thy midst;
texts.exo.34.13: For their altars, shall ye smash, And their pillars, shall ye shiver,—And their sacred-stems, shall ye fell.
texts.exo.34.14: For thou shalt not bow thyself down to another GOD,—For as for Yahweh, Jealous, is his name, A jealous GOD, he is:
texts.exo.34.15: Lest thou solemnise a covenant with the inhabitant of the land,—And then as surely as they go unchastely after their gods and sacrifice to their gods, So surely will he invite thee, And thou wilt eat of his sacrifice;
texts.exo.34.16: And thou wilt take of his daughters for thy sons,—And his daughters will go unchastely after their gods, And will cause thy sons to go unchastely after their gods.
texts.exo.34.17: Molten gods, shalt thou not make to thee.
texts.exo.34.18: The festival of unleavened cakes, shalt thou keep, seven days, shalt thou eat unleavened cakes, which I commanded thee, at the set time, in the month Abib,—for in the month Abib, camest thou forth out of Egypt.
texts.exo.34.19: Every one that is the first to be born, is mine,—and every one of thy cattle that is born a male, firstling of oxen or sheep.
texts.exo.34.20: But the firstling of an ass, thou mayst redeem with a lamb, and if thou wilt not redeem it, then shalt thou break its neck. Every firstborn of thy sons, shalt thou redeem, and he must not see my face, with empty hand.
texts.exo.34.21: Six days, shalt thou labour, but on the seventh day, shalt thou rest,—in plowing time and in harvest, shalt thou rest.
texts.exo.34.22: And the festival of weeks, shalt thou make to thee, the firstfruits of the wheat harvest,—and the festival of ingathering, at the closing in of the year:
texts.exo.34.23: three times in the year, shall every one of thy males see the face of the Lord Yahweh the God of Israel.
texts.exo.34.24: For I will root out nations from before thee, and will enlarge thy borders,—and no man shall covet thy land, when thou goes up to see the face of Yahweh thy God, three times in the year.
texts.exo.34.25: Thou shalt not slay, along with anything leavened, the blood of my sacrifice,—neither shall remain to the morning, the sacrifice of the festival of the passover.
texts.exo.34.26: The beginning of the firstfruits of thy ground, shalt thou bring into the house of Yahweh, thy God, Thou shalt not boil a kid, in the milk of its dam.
texts.exo.34.27: And Yahweh said unto Moses, Write for thyself these words, for according to the tenor of these words, have I solemnized with thee, a covenant, and with Israel.
texts.exo.34.28: So then he was there, with Yahweh, forty days and forty nights, bread, did he not eat and, water, did he not drink, and he wrote upon the tables, the words of the covenant, the ten words.
texts.exo.34.29: And it came to pass, when Moses came down out of Mount Sinai, with the two tables of testimony in the hand of Moses, when he came down out of the mount, that, Moses, knew not that the skin of his face shone, through his having spoken with him.
texts.exo.34.30: And Aaron and all the sons of Israel saw Moses, and lo! the skin of his face shone, and they stood in awe of drawing nigh unto him.
texts.exo.34.31: So then Moses called unto them, and Aaron and all the princes in the assembly returned unto him,—and Moses spake unto them.
texts.exo.34.32: And afterwards, came nigh, all the sons of Israel, and he gave them in commandment all that Yahweh had spoken with him in Mount Sinai.
texts.exo.34.33: And when Moses had made an end of speaking with them, he put over his face a veil:
texts.exo.34.34: but, as often as Moses went in before Yahweh to speak with him, he put aside the veil until he came out,—and, as often as he came out and spake unto the sons of Israel, that which he had been commanded,
texts.exo.34.35: the sons of Israel saw the face of Moses, that the skin of Moses face shone,—so Moses again put the veil over his face, until he went in to speak with him.
texts.exo.35.1: And Moses called together all the assembly of the sons of Israel and said unto them,—These are the things which Yahweh hath commanded to do them.
texts.exo.35.2: Six days, shall work be done, but on the seventh day, shall there be to you a holy sabbath-keeping, unto Yahweh, whosoever doeth work therein shall be put to death.
texts.exo.35.3: Ye shall not kindle a fire, in any of your dwellings,—on the sabbath day.
texts.exo.35.4: And Moses spake unto all the assembly of the sons of Israel, saying, This, is the thing which Yahweh hath commanded, saying,
texts.exo.35.5: Take ye from among you, a heave-offering to Yahweh, every one whose heart is willing shall bring it in, even the heave-offering of Yahweh, gold and silver and bronze:
texts.exo.35.6: and blue and purple and crimson and fine linen and goat’s-hair;
texts.exo.35.7: and rams’ skins dyed red, and badgers’ skins, and acacia wood;
texts.exo.35.8: and oil for giving light, and aromatic spices for the anointing oil, and for fragrant incense;
texts.exo.35.9: and onyx stones and setting stones, for the ephod, and for the breastpiece.
texts.exo.35.10: And, all the wise-hearted among you, shall come in, that they may make, all that which Yahweh hath commanded:—
texts.exo.35.11: the habitation, its tent, and its covering,—its clasps its boards, and its bars its pillars, and its sockets:
texts.exo.35.12: the ark with its staves the propitiatory, and the screening veil;
texts.exo.35.13: the table with its staves and all its utensils, and the Presence-bread:
texts.exo.35.14: the lampstand for giving light, with its utensils, and its lamps, and the oil for giving light;
texts.exo.35.15: and the incense altar, with its staves, and the anointing oil, and the fragrant incense,—and the entrance screen, for the entrance of the habitation;
texts.exo.35.16: the altar for the ascending-sacrifice, and the bronze grating which pertaineth thereto, its staves and all its utensils, the laver and its stand;
texts.exo.35.17: the hangings for the court, its pillars and its sockets,—and the screen for the gate of the court:
texts.exo.35.18: the pins of the habitation, and the pins of the court, and their cords;
texts.exo.35.19: the cloths of variegated stuff for ministering in the sanctuary,—the sacred garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for ministering as priests.
texts.exo.35.20: So all the assembly of the sons of Israel went forth from the presence of Moses;
texts.exo.35.21: and they brought in—every man whose heart lifted him up,—and, every one whose spirit made him willing, brought in the heave-offering of Yahweh, for the construction of the tent of meeting, and for all its service, and for the holy garments.
texts.exo.35.22: Yea they brought in—the men with the women,—all who were willing-hearted, brought in—bracelets and nose-ornaments and rings, and buckles, all manner of jewels of gold, even every man who waved a wave-offering of gold unto Yahweh.
texts.exo.35.23: And, every man with whom was found blue and purple and crimson and fine linen and goat’s-hair,—and rams’ skins dyed red and badgers’ skins brought them in.
texts.exo.35.24: Every one who would heave a heave-offering of silver or bronze, brought in the heave-offering of Yahweh,—and, every one with whom was found acacia wood for any construction for the service, brought it in.
texts.exo.35.25: And, all the women who were wise-hearted, with their hands, did spin,—and brought in that which they had spun—the blue, and the purple, the crimson, and the fine linen.
texts.exo.35.26: And, all the women whose hearts lifted them up with wisdom, span the goat’s-hair.
texts.exo.35.27: And the princes, brought in the onyx stones and the setting stones,—for the ephod and for the breastpiece;
texts.exo.35.28: and the aromatic spices, and the oil,—for giving light, and for anointing oil, and for the fragrant incense.
texts.exo.35.29: [In the case of], every male and woman whose heart, made them willing, to bring in for any construction which, Yahweh had commanded them to make, by the hand of Moses, [in their case] did the sons of Israel bring in a free-will offering unto Yahweh.
texts.exo.35.30: And Moses said unto the sons of Israel—See! Yahweh hath called by name,—Bezaleel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah;
texts.exo.35.31: and filled him with the spirit of God,—in, wisdom in understanding and in knowledge, and in all manner of execution;
texts.exo.35.32: to devise skilful designs,—to work in gold and in silver and in bronze;
texts.exo.35.33: and in the cutting of stones for setting, and in the cutting of wood,—to work in any manner of skilful workmanship,
texts.exo.35.34: To teach also, hath he put in his heart, [the heart of] him, and of Oholiab—son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan;
texts.exo.35.35: hath filled them with wisdom of heart to work all manner of workmanship of cutter, and deviser and embroiderer, in blue and in purple, in crimson and in fine linen and of the weaver,—workers of any manner of workmanship, and devisers of skilful designs.
texts.exo.36.1: Thus shall Bezaleel and Oholiab work, and every man that is wise-hearted, in whom Yahweh hath put wisdom and understanding, to know how to work any manner of workmanship for the holy service,—according to all that Yahweh hath commanded.
texts.exo.36.2: So then Moses called upon Bezaleel, and upon Oholiab, and upon every man that was wise-hearted, in whose heart Yahweh had put wisdom,—every one whose heart lifted him up, to draw near unto the work, to do it.
texts.exo.36.3: And they took, from the presence of Moses, all the heave-offering which the sons of Israel had brought in for the work of the holy service to do it,—howbeit, they, brought in unto him yet more free-will offerings, morning by morning.
texts.exo.36.4: Then came in all the wise men who were doing all the holy work,—man by man from his work which, they, were doing;
texts.exo.36.5: and spake unto Moses, saying, More than enough, are the people bringing in,—[more] than is needed for the service pertaining to the work; which Yahweh hath commanded to be done.
texts.exo.36.6: So Moses gave commandment and they passed a proclamation throughout the camp, saying, Let, neither man nor woman, make any more material for the holy heave-offering. So the people were restrained from bringing in.
texts.exo.36.7: For the material was enough for all the work, to make it,—and to spare.
texts.exo.36.8: Then did all the wise-hearted among the workers of the material make the habitation of ten curtains, of fine-twined linen, and blue and purple and crimson, with cherubim the work of the skilful weaver, did he make them.
texts.exo.36.9: The length of each curtain, was twenty-eight cubits, and the breadth four cubits, for each curtain,—one measure, had all the curtains.
texts.exo.36.10: And he joined the [first] five curtains, one to another,—and the [other] five curtains, joined he one to another,
texts.exo.36.11: And he made loops of blue upon the border of the first curtain, at the edge of the set,—thus, made he in the border of the other curtain at the edge of the second set:
texts.exo.36.12: Fifty loops, made he in the first curtain, and fifty loops, made he in the edge of the curtain that was in the second set,—the loops being, opposite, one to another.
texts.exo.36.13: And he made fifty clasps of gold,—and joined the curtains one to another with the clasps, and so the habitation became, one.
texts.exo.36.14: And he made curtains of goat’s-hair, for the tent over the habitation, eleven curtains, did he make them:
texts.exo.36.15: the length of each curtain, was thirty cubits, and, four cubits, was the breath of each curtain,—one measure, had the eleven curtains.
texts.exo.36.16: And he joined five of the curtains by themselves,—and the six curtains, by themselves.
texts.exo.36.17: And he made fifty loops upon the border of the curtain that was outmost in the one set and fifty loops, made he upon the border of the curtain of the second set.
texts.exo.36.18: And he made fifty clasps of bronze,—to join together the tent, that it might become one.
texts.exo.36.19: And he made a covering to the tent, of rams’ skins dyed red,—and a covering of badgers’ skins, above.
texts.exo.36.20: And he made the boards for the habitation, of acacia wood, for standing up:
texts.exo.36.21: ten cubits, the length of each board, and a cubit and a half the breadth of each board:
texts.exo.36.22: two tenons to each board, united one to another,—thus, made he for all the boards of the habitation.
texts.exo.36.23: And he made the boards for the habitation, twenty boards, for the south side southwards;
texts.exo.36.24: and, forty sockets of silver, made he, under the twenty boards, two sockets, under the first board, for its two tenons, and, two sockets, under the next board for its two tenons.
texts.exo.36.25: And for the second side of the habitation to the north quarter, made he twenty boards;
texts.exo.36.26: and their forty sockets of silver, two sockets, under the first board, and, two sockets, under the next board.
texts.exo.36.27: And, for the hinder part of the habitation westward, made he six boards;
texts.exo.36.28: and two boards, made he for the corners of the habitation,—in the hinderpart.
texts.exo.36.29: Thus were they to be double beneath, and at the same time, should they be entire, at the top thereof, into each ring, thus, did he for them both, for the two corners.
texts.exo.36.30: Thus were there to be eight boards, and, their sockets of silver, were sixteen sockets, two sockets apiece under each board.
texts.exo.36.31: And he made bars of acacia wood,—five, for the boards of the first side of the habitation,
texts.exo.36.32: and five bars, for the boards of the other side of the habitation, and, five bars, for the boards of the habitation at the hinderpart westward.
texts.exo.36.33: And he made the middle bar,—to run along in the midst of the boards, from end to end.
texts.exo.36.34: And the boards, overlaid he with gold and their rings, made he of gold, as receptacles for the bars, and he overlaid the bars with gold.
texts.exo.36.35: And he made the veil, of blue and purple and crimson and fine-twined linen,—of the work of a skilful weaver, made he it, with cherubim.
texts.exo.36.36: And he made for it four pillars of acacia, and overlaid them with gold their hooks of gold, and cast for them, four sockets of silver.
texts.exo.36.37: And he made a screen for the opening of the tent, of blue and purple and crimson and fine twined linen, the work of an embroiderer;
texts.exo.36.38: and the five pillars thereof and their hooks, and he overlaid their capitals and their cross-rods, with gold, but, their five sockets, were of bronze.
texts.exo.37.1: And Bezaleel made the ark, of acacia wood, two cubits and a half, the length thereof and, a cubit and a half, the breadth thereof, and, a cubit and a half, the height thereof;
texts.exo.37.2: and he overlaid it with pure gold within and without,-and made for it a rim of gold, round about;
texts.exo.37.3: and he cast for it four rings of gold, upon the four feet thereof,—even, two rings, on the one side thereof and, two rings, on the other side thereof;
texts.exo.37.4: and he made staves of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold;
texts.exo.37.5: and he brought the staves into the rings, upon the sides of the ark, for lifting the ark.
texts.exo.37.6: And he made a propitiatory of pure gold,—two cubits and a half, the length thereof, and, a cubit and a half, the breadth thereof:
texts.exo.37.7: and he made two cherubim, of gold, of beaten work, did he make them, out of the two ends of the propitiatory:
texts.exo.37.8: one cherub, out of this end, and, one cherub, out of that end, out of the propitiatory itself, made he the cherubim, out of the two ends thereof:
texts.exo.37.9: and the cherubim were spreading out their wings on high making a shelter with their wings over the propitiatory, with, their faces, one towards the other, towards the propitiatory, were the faces of the cherubim,
texts.exo.37.10: And he made the table of acacia wood, two cubits, the length thereof and, a cubit, the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof,
texts.exo.37.11: And he overlaid it with pure gold,—and he made thereto a rim of gold round about:
texts.exo.37.12: and he mane thereto a border of a handbreadth, round about, and he made a rim of gold to the border thereof round about:
texts.exo.37.13: and he cast for it, four rings of gold, and placed the rings upon the four corners, which pertained to the four feet thereof:
texts.exo.37.14: near to the border, were the rings, as receptacles for the staves, for lifting the table;
texts.exo.37.15: and he made the staves of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold,—for lifting the table;
texts.exo.37.16: and he made the utensils which were to be upon the table, its dishes and its pans and its bowls, and its basins for pouring out therewith, of pure gold.
texts.exo.37.17: And he made the lampstand, of pure gold, of beaten work, made he the lampstand, its base and its shafts, its cups, its apples and its blossoms were, of the same;
texts.exo.37.18: with, six branches coming out of its sides,—three branches of the lampstand out of its one side and three branches of the lampstand out of its other side:
texts.exo.37.19: three cups like almond-flowers in the one branch—apple and blossom, and, three cups like almond-flowers, in the next branch, apple and blossom, so for the six branches coming out of the lampstand;
texts.exo.37.20: and in the lampstand itself, four cups, like almond-flowers, its apples and its blossoms:
texts.exo.37.21: with, an apple, under the two branches of the same, and, an apple, under the next two branches of the same, and, an apple, under the next two branches of the same, for the six branches coming out of the same:
texts.exo.37.22: their apples and their brunches were of the same, all of it one beaten work, of pure gold.
texts.exo.37.23: And he made the lamps thereof seven,—with its snuffers and its snuff-trays, of pure gold.
texts.exo.37.24: Of a talent of pure gold, made he it,—and all the utensils thereof.
texts.exo.37.25: And he made the incense altar, of acacia wood,—a cubit, the length thereof, and, a cubit, the breadth thereof, foursquare, and two cubits the height thereof, of the same, were the horns thereof.
texts.exo.37.26: And he overlaid it with pure gold—the top thereof and the sides thereof round about, and the horns thereof,-and he made thereto a rim of gold, round about.
texts.exo.37.27: And two rings of gold, made he thereto—beneath the rim thereof, upon the two corners thereof, upon the two sides thereof,—as receptacles for the staves, to lift it therewith.
texts.exo.37.28: And he made the staves of acacia wood,—and overlaid them with gold.
texts.exo.37.29: And he made the holy anointing oil, and the pure fragrant incense,—the work of a perfumer.
texts.exo.38.1: And he made the altar for the ascending-sacrifice of acacia wood,—five cubits, the length thereof and, five cubits, the breadth thereof foursquare, and, three cubits, the height thereof.
texts.exo.38.2: And he made the horns thereof, upon the four corners thereof, of the same, were the horns thereof,—and he overlaid it with bronze.
texts.exo.38.3: And he made all the utensils of the altar—the pans and the shovels, and the sprinkling bowls, the flesh-hooks and the fire-pans,—all the utensils thereof, made he of bronze.
texts.exo.38.4: And he made to the altar a grating, of network of bronze,—under the margin thereof beneath as far as the midst thereof.
texts.exo.38.5: And he cast four rings in the four corners to the grating of bronze,—as receptacles for the staves,
texts.exo.38.6: And he made the staves of acacia wood,—and overlaid them with bronze.
texts.exo.38.7: And he brought the staves into the rings, upon the sides of the altar, to lift it therewith,—hollow with boards, did he make it.
texts.exo.38.8: And he made the laver of bronze, and the stand thereof of bronze,—with the mirrors of the female hosts who did service at the opening of the tent of meeting.
texts.exo.38.9: And he made the court,—on the south side southward, the hangings of the court of fine twined linen, a hundred cubits;
texts.exo.38.10: their pillars, twenty, and their sockets twenty, of bronze,—the hooks of the pillars and their connecting-rods, of silver:
texts.exo.38.11: and, on the north side, a hundred cubits, their pillars, twenty, and, their sockets twenty, of bronze,—the hooks of the pillars and their connecting-rods, of silver.
texts.exo.38.12: And on the west side, hangings, fifty cubits, their pillars, ten, and, their sockets, ten,—and, the hooks of the pillars and their connecting-rods, of silver.
texts.exo.38.13: And on the east side towards the dawn, fifty cubits:
texts.exo.38.14: hangings, fifteen cubits, for the side-piece,—their pillars, three, and, their sockets three;
texts.exo.38.15: and, for the second sidepiece on this side and on that of the gate of the court, hangings, fifteen cubits,—their pillars three, and their sockets, three.
texts.exo.38.16: All the hangings of the court round about were of fine twined linen.
texts.exo.38.17: And, the sockets for the pillars, were of bronze, the hooks of the pillars and their connecting-rods of silver,—and the overlaying of their capitals, was silver,—and, they themselves, were filleted with silver, even all the pillars of the court,
texts.exo.38.18: And, the screen of the gate of the court was the work of an embroiderer, blue and purple and crimson, and fine-twined linen,—and, twenty cubits, in length, and the height, according to the breadth, of five cubits, to match the curtains of the court;
texts.exo.38.19: and, their pillars, were four, and, their sockets, four, of bronze,—their hooks, of silver, and the overlaying of their capitals and their connecting-rods, of silver.
texts.exo.38.20: And, all the pins for the habitation, and for the court round about, of bronze.
texts.exo.38.21: These, are the details of the habitation—the habitation of testimony, which were detailed at the bidding of Moses,—the service of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.
texts.exo.38.22: So then Bezaleel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made all that Yahweh had commanded Moses.
texts.exo.38.23: And, with him, was Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an artificer and skilful weaver,—and an embroiderer—in blue, and in purple and in crimson and in fine linen.
texts.exo.38.24: As for all the gold that was used for, the work, in all the construction of the sanctuary, it came to pass that the gold of the wave-offering was nine-and-twenty talents, and seven hundred and thirty shekels by the shekel of the sanctuary.
texts.exo.38.25: And, the silver of them who were numbered of the assembly, was one hundred talents,—and one thousand, seven hundred and seventy-five shekels by the shekel of the sanctuary;
texts.exo.38.26: a bekah per head, that is a half shekel, by the shekel of the sanctuary, for all that passed over to them who had been numbered, from twenty years old and upwards, for six hundred and three thousand, and five hundred and fifty.
texts.exo.38.27: And it came to pass that the hundred talents of silver were used for casting the sockets of the sanctuary, and the sockets of the veil,—one hundred sockets with the hundred talents a talent for a socket.
texts.exo.38.28: And with the thousand, seven hundred and seventy-five, made the hooks for the pillars,—and overlaid their capitals and united them with connecting-rods.
texts.exo.38.29: And the bronze of the wave-offering, was seventy talents,—and two thousand and four hundred shekels.
texts.exo.38.30: And he made therewith, the sockets for the opening of the tent of meeting, and the altar of bronze and the grating of bronze which pertained thereto,—and all the utensils of the altar,
texts.exo.38.31: and the sockets for the court round about, and the sockets for the gate of the court,—and all the pins for the habitation and all the pins for the court round about.
texts.exo.39.1: And of the blue and the purple, and the crimson, made they cloths of variegated stuff for ministering in the sanctuary,—and they made the holy garments which were for Aaron,—As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.exo.39.2: So he made the ephod,—of gold, blue, and purple, and crimson, and fine twined linen,
texts.exo.39.3: And they did beat out the plates of gold and he proceeded to cut them into threads, to work into the midst of the blue and into the midst of the purple and into the midst of the crimson, and into the midst of the fine linen,—with the work of a skilful weaver.
texts.exo.39.4: Shoulder-pieces, made they thereto, for joining,—at its two edges, was it joined.
texts.exo.39.5: And as for the curious fastening girdle which was thereon, of the same, it was according to the working thereof, gold blue, and purple, and crimson and fine twined linen,—As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.exo.39.6: And they wrought the onyx stones, enclosed in ouches of gold,—graven with the engravings of a seal-ring, after the names of the sons of Israel.
texts.exo.39.7: And he put them on the shoulderpieces of the ephod, as stones of memorial for the sons of Israel,—As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.exo.39.8: And he made the breastpiece the work of a skilful weaver like the work of the ephod,—of gold blue and purple and crimson, and fine twined linen.
texts.exo.39.9: Foursquare, it was doubled, made they the breastpiece,—a span, was the length thereof, and, a span, the breadth thereof, doubled.
texts.exo.39.10: And they set therein four rows of stones,—one row a sardius, a topaz and an emerald, the first row;
texts.exo.39.11: and the second row,—a carbuncle a sapphire, and a diamond;
texts.exo.39.12: and the third row,—an opal an agate and an amethyst;
texts.exo.39.13: and the fourth row, a Tarshish stone, a sardonyx, and a jasper,—enclosed in ouches of gold, when they were set
texts.exo.39.14: And as for the stones, after the names of the sons of Israel, they were twelve, after their names,—with the engravings of a seal-ring, each one, after his name, for the twelve tribes,
texts.exo.39.15: And they made, upon the breastpiece, chains like cords of wreathen work,—of pure gold.
texts.exo.39.16: And they made two ouches of gold, and two rings of gold,—and they placed the two rings upon the two ends of the breastpiece;
texts.exo.39.17: and they placed the two wreathen chains of gold upon the two rings,-upon the ends of the breastpiece;
texts.exo.39.18: and the other two ends of the two wreathen chains, placed they upon the two ouches,—and placed them upon the shoulder-pieces of the ephod in the forefront thereof.
texts.exo.39.19: And they made two rings of gold, and put on the two ends of the breastpiece, upon the border thereof, which is towards the ephod, inwards.
texts.exo.39.20: And they made two other rings of gold, and placed them upon the two shoulder-pieces of the ephod below on the front of the face thereof, to match the joining thereof.—above the curious girdle of the ephod,
texts.exo.39.21: And they bound the breastpiece by the rings thereof into the rings of the ephod, with a cord of blue that it might remain upon the curious girdle of the ephod, and the breastpiece not be removed from upon the ephod,—As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.exo.39.22: And he made the robe of the ephod, the work of a weaver, wholly of blue;
texts.exo.39.23: with the opening of the robe in the midst thereof, like the opening of a coat of mail,—a border to the opening thereof round about it might not be rent open.
texts.exo.39.24: And they made upon the skirts of the robe, pomegranates—of blue and purple and crimson,—twined.
texts.exo.39.25: And they made bells of pure gold, and placed the bells in the midst of the pomegranates upon the skirts of the robe, roundabout, in the midst of the pomegranates:
texts.exo.39.26: a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, upon the skirts of the robe, round about, to minister in—As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.exo.39.27: And they made the tunics of fine linen the work of a weaver, for Aaron and for his sons:
texts.exo.39.28: and the turban of fine linen, and the ornamental caps of fine linen,—and the linen drawers, of fine twined linen:
texts.exo.39.29: and the girdle of fine twined linen, and blue and purple and crimson the work of an embroiderer,—As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.exo.39.30: And they made the burnished plate of the holy crown of pure gold, and wrote thereupon a writing, with the engravings of a seal-ring Holy unto Yahweh.
texts.exo.39.31: And they placed there, upon a cord of blue, to fasten it upon the turban up above, As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.exo.39.32: Thus was finished all the work of the habitation of the tent of meeting,—thus did the sons of Israel, according to all that Yahweh commanded Moses, so, did they.
texts.exo.39.33: And they brought in the habitation unto Moses, the tent, and all its furniture,—its clasps, its boards, its bars, and its pillars and its sockets;
texts.exo.39.34: and the covering of rams’ skins dyed red, and the covering of badgers’ skins, and the screening veil;
texts.exo.39.35: the ark of the testimony, with its staves,—and the propitiatory;
texts.exo.39.36: the table all its utensils, and the Presence-bread;
texts.exo.39.37: the pure lampstand the lamps thereof the lamps to be put in order, and all the utensils thereof,—and the oil for giving light;
texts.exo.39.38: and the altar of gold, and the oil of anointing, and the fragrant incense,—and the screen for the opening of the tent;
texts.exo.39.39: the altar of bronze and the grating of bronze which pertaineth thereto, the staves thereof, and all the utensils thereof,—the laver, and its stand,
texts.exo.39.40: the hangings of the court its pillars and its sockets, and the screen for the gate of the court, its cords and its pins,—and all the utensils for the service of the habitation for the tent of meeting;
texts.exo.39.41: them cloths of variegated stuff, for ministering in the sanctuary,—the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for ministering as priests.
texts.exo.39.42: According to all that Yahweh commanded Moses, so, did the sons of Israel make all the work.
texts.exo.39.43: And Moses looked upon all the structure and lo! they had made it, as Yahweh had commanded, so, had they made it,—and Moses blessed them.
texts.exo.40.1: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying—
texts.exo.40.2: On the first day of the month, in the first month, shalt thou rear the habitation, of the tent of meeting;
texts.exo.40.3: and thou shalt put therein, the ark of the testimony,—and shalt screen the ark with the veil;
texts.exo.40.4: and thou shalt bring in the table, and set in order what is to be arranged thereupon,—and thou shalt bring in the lampstand, and mount the lamps thereof;
texts.exo.40.5: and thou shalt place the altar of gold for incense, before the ark of the testimony,—and put up the screen for the opening of the habitation;
texts.exo.40.6: and thou shalt place the altar for the ascending-sacrifice,—before the opening of the habitation of the tent of meeting;
texts.exo.40.7: and thou shalt place the laver between the tent of meeting, and the altar, and shalt put therein water,
texts.exo.40.8: And thou shalt put up the court round about, and hang up the screen of the gate of the court.
texts.exo.40.9: And thou shalt take the oil of anointing, and anoint the habitation and all that is therein,—and shalt hallow it. and all the furniture thereof so shall it be holy.
texts.exo.40.10: And thou shalt anoint the altar of ascending sacrifice, and all its utensils,—and hallow the altar, so shall the altar be most holy:
texts.exo.40.11: and thou shalt anoint the laver and its stand,—and shalt hallow it.
texts.exo.40.12: And thou shalt bring near Aaron and his sons, unto the opening of the tent of meeting,—and shalt bathe them in the water;
texts.exo.40.13: and thou shalt clothe Aaron with the holy garments,—and shalt anoint him and hallow him so shall he minister as priest unto me.
texts.exo.40.14: His sons also, shalt thou bring near,—and shalt clothe them with tunics;
texts.exo.40.15: and shalt anoint them as thou didst anoint their father, and they shall minister as priests unto me,—so shall their anointing remain to them for an age-abiding priesthood, to their generations.
texts.exo.40.16: And Moses did,—according to all that Yahweh had commanded him, so did he.
texts.exo.40.17: Thus came it to pass, in the first month, in the second year, on the first of the month, that the habitation was reared.
texts.exo.40.18: Yea Moses reared the habitation, and placed its sockets, and fixed its boards, and fastened its bars,—and reared its pillars.
texts.exo.40.19: Then spread he abroad the tent upon the habitation, and put the covering of the tent upon it, above,—As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.exo.40.20: And he took and placed the testimony within the ark, and put the staves upon the ark,—and placed the propitiatory upon the ark, above;
texts.exo.40.21: and brought in the ark into the habitation, and put up the screening veil, and screened over the ark of the testimony,—As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.exo.40.22: And he placed the table in the tent of meeting,—on the side of the habitation northward,—outside the veil;
texts.exo.40.23: and set in order thereupon the arrangement of bread before Yahweh,—As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.exo.40.24: And he put the lampstand, in the tent of meeting, over against the table,—on the side of the habitation southward;
texts.exo.40.25: and mounted the lamps before Yahweh,—As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.exo.40.26: And he put the altar of gold in the tent of meeting,—before the veil;
texts.exo.40.27: and burned thereupon the fragrant incense,—As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.exo.40.28: And he put up the screen of the entrance pertaining to the habitation;
texts.exo.40.29: and, the altar of ascending-sacrifice, put he at the entrance of the habitation of the tent of meeting,—and he caused to ascend thereupon the ascending-sacrifice, and the meal-offering,—As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.exo.40.30: And he put the laver, between the tent of meeting, and the altar,—and put therein water for bathing;
texts.exo.40.31: and Moses and Aaron and his sons thenceforth bathed thereat,—their hands and their feet;
texts.exo.40.32: when they were entering into the tent of meeting, and when they were drawing near unto the altar, then used they to bathe,—As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.exo.40.33: And he reared the court round about to the habitation and to the altar, and put up the screen of the gate of the court,—and Moses finished the work.
texts.exo.40.34: Then did the cloud cover the tent of meeting,—and, the glory of Yahweh, filled the habitation;
texts.exo.40.35: and Moses was not able to enter into the tent of meeting, because the cloud had made its habitation thereupon,—and the glory of Yahweh, filled the habitation.
texts.exo.40.36: And whensoever the cloud ascended from off the habitation, then did the sons of Israel set forward, in all their journeyings;
texts.exo.40.37: but if the cloud did not ascend, then did they not set forward—until the day when it did ascend.
texts.exo.40.38: For, the cloud of Yahweh, was upon the habitation by day, and, a fire, came to be by night therein,—in the sight of all the house of Israel in all their journeyings.

texts.exo.1.1: Estos son los nombres de los hijos de Israel que vinieron a Egipto (cada hombre y su familia vinieron con Jacob):
texts.exo.1.4: Dan y Neftalí, Gad y Aser.
texts.exo.1.5: Todas las almas que salieron del cuerpo de Jacob fueron setenta almas, y José ya estaba en Egipto.
texts.exo.1.6: José murió, al igual que todos sus hermanos y toda aquella generación.
texts.exo.1.7: Los hijos de Israel fructificaron, se multiplicaron y se hicieron muy poderosos, y la tierra se llenó de ellos.
texts.exo.1.8: Se levantó un nuevo rey sobre Egipto, que no conocía a José.
texts.exo.1.9: Dijo a su pueblo: “He aquí, el pueblo de los hijos de Israel es más y más poderoso que nosotros.
texts.exo.1.10: Venid, actuemos con astucia con ellos, no sea que se multipliquen, y suceda que cuando estalle alguna guerra, ellos también se unan a nuestros enemigos, luchen contra nosotros y escapen del país.”
texts.exo.1.11: Por lo tanto, pusieron sobre ellos capataces para que los afligieran con sus cargas. Construyeron ciudades de almacenaje para el faraón: Pitón y Ramsés.
texts.exo.1.12: Pero cuanto más los afligían, más se multiplicaban y más se extendían. Comenzaron a temer a los hijos de Israel.
texts.exo.1.13: Los egipcios hicieron servir sin piedad a los hijos de Israel,
texts.exo.1.14: y les amargaron la vida con un duro servicio en la argamasa y en el ladrillo, y en todo tipo de servicio en el campo, todo su servicio, en el que los hicieron servir sin piedad.
texts.exo.1.15: El rey de Egipto habló con las parteras hebreas, de las cuales una se llamaba Sifra y la otra Fúa,
texts.exo.1.16: y les dijo: “Cuando cumpláis con el deber de partera para las mujeres hebreas y las veáis en la silla de parto, si es un hijo, lo mataréis; pero si es una hija, vivirá.”
texts.exo.1.17: Pero las parteras temían a Dios, y no hicieron lo que el rey de Egipto les ordenaba, sino que salvaron la vida a los niños.
texts.exo.1.18: El rey de Egipto llamó a las parteras y les dijo: «¿Por qué habéis hecho esto y habéis salvado la vida a los niños?»
texts.exo.1.19: Las parteras dijeron al faraón: “Porque las mujeres hebreas no son como las egipcias, pues son vigorosas y dan a luz antes de que la partera llegue a ellas.”
texts.exo.1.20: Dios trató bien a las parteras, y el pueblo se multiplicó y se hizo muy poderoso.
texts.exo.1.21: Como las parteras temían a Dios, él les dio familias.
texts.exo.1.22: El faraón ordenó a todo su pueblo, diciendo: “Echaréis al río a todo hijo que nazca, y a toda hija la salvaréis con vida.”
texts.exo.2.1: Un hombre de la casa de Leví fue y tomó como esposa a una hija de Leví.
texts.exo.2.2: La mujer concibió y dio a luz un hijo. Al ver que era un buen niño, lo escondió durante tres meses.
texts.exo.2.3: Cuando ya no pudo esconderlo, tomó una arquilla de papiro para él, y la cubrió con asfalto y brea. Puso al niño en ella y la depositó en los juncos de la orilla del río.
texts.exo.2.4: Su hermana se quedó lejos, para ver qué se hacía con él.
texts.exo.2.5: La hija del faraón bajó a bañarse en el río. Sus doncellas se paseaban por la orilla del río. Vio la arquilla entre los juncos y envió a su criada a buscarla.
texts.exo.2.6: La abrió y vio al niño, y he aquí que el niño lloraba. Se compadeció de él y dijo: «Este es uno de los hijos de los hebreos».
texts.exo.2.7: Entonces su hermana dijo a la hija del faraón: «¿Debo ir a llamar a una nodriza de las mujeres hebreas para que te amamante al niño?»
texts.exo.2.8: La hija del faraón le dijo: «Ve». La joven fue y llamó a la madre del niño.
texts.exo.2.9: La hija del faraón le dijo: «Llévate a este niño y cuídalo por mí, y te daré tu salario». La mujer tomó al niño y lo amamantó.
texts.exo.2.10: El niño creció, lo llevó a la hija del faraón y se convirtió en su hijo. Ella le puso el nombre de Moisés, y dijo: «Porque lo saqué del agua».
texts.exo.2.11: En aquellos días, cuando Moisés había crecido, salió a ver a sus hermanos y vio sus cargas. Vio que un egipcio golpeaba a un hebreo, uno de sus hermanos.
texts.exo.2.12: Miró a un lado y a otro, y al ver que no había nadie, mató al egipcio y lo escondió en la arena.
texts.exo.2.13: Salió al día siguiente, y he aquí que dos hombres de los hebreos estaban peleando entre sí. Le dijo al que había hecho el mal: «¿Por qué golpeas a tu compañero?».
texts.exo.2.14: Él dijo: «¿Quién te ha puesto como príncipe y juez sobre nosotros? ¿Piensas matarme, como mataste al egipcio?» Moisés tuvo miedo y dijo: «Ciertamente esto se sabe».
texts.exo.2.15: Cuando el faraón se enteró de esto, trató de matar a Moisés. Pero Moisés huyó de la presencia del faraón, habitó en la tierra de Madián, y se sentó junto a un pozo.
texts.exo.2.16: El sacerdote de Madián tenía siete hijas. Ellas vinieron y sacaron agua, y llenaron los abrevaderos para dar de beber al rebaño de su padre.
texts.exo.2.17: Los pastores vinieron y las ahuyentaron; pero Moisés se levantó, las ayudó y dio de beber a su rebaño.
texts.exo.2.18: Cuando llegaron a Reuel, su padre, este les dijo: «¿Cómo es que habéis vuelto hoy tan temprano?»
texts.exo.2.19: Dijeron: “Un egipcio nos libró de la mano de los pastores, y además nos sacó agua y dio de beber al rebaño.”
texts.exo.2.20: Dijo a sus hijas: “¿Dónde está? ¿Por qué habéis dejado al hombre? Llamadle, para que coma pan”.
texts.exo.2.21: Moisés accedió a habitar con aquel hombre. Él le dio a Moisés a Séfora, su hija.
texts.exo.2.22: Ella dio a luz un hijo, y él le puso el nombre de Gersón, porque dijo: «He vivido como forastero en tierra extranjera».
texts.exo.2.23: En el transcurso de esos muchos días, el rey de Egipto murió, y los hijos de Israel suspiraron a causa de la esclavitud, y clamaron, y su clamor subió a Dios a causa de la esclavitud.
texts.exo.2.24: Dios oyó su gemido, y se acordó de su pacto con Abraham, con Isaac y con Jacob.
texts.exo.2.25: Dios miró a los hijos de Israel, y Dios los tuvo en cuenta.
texts.exo.3.1: Moisés apacentaba el rebaño de Jetro, su suegro, el sacerdote de Madián, y condujo el rebaño más allá del desierto, y llegó al monte de Dios, a Horeb.
texts.exo.3.2: El ángel de Yahvé se le apareció en una llama de fuego en medio de una zarza. Miró, y he aquí que la zarza ardía en fuego, y la zarza no se consumía.
texts.exo.3.3: Moisés dijo: «Iré ahora a ver esta gran visión, por qué la zarza no se quema».
texts.exo.3.4: Cuando Yahvé vio que se acercaba a ver, Dios le llamó desde el medio de la zarza y le dijo: «¡Moisés! ¡Moisés!» Dijo: «Aquí estoy».
texts.exo.3.5: Él dijo: «No te acerques. Quítate las sandalias, porque el lugar que pisas es tierra santa».
texts.exo.3.6: Además, dijo: «Yo soy el Dios de tu padre, el Dios de Abraham, el Dios de Isaac y el Dios de Jacob». Moisés ocultó su rostro porque tenía miedo de mirar a Dios.
texts.exo.3.7: Yahvé dijo: «Ciertamente he visto la aflicción de mi pueblo que está en Egipto, y he oído su clamor a causa de sus capataces, pues conozco sus sufrimientos.
texts.exo.3.8: He descendido para librarlos de la mano de los egipcios, y para hacerlos subir de esa tierra a una tierra buena y ancha, a una tierra que mana leche y miel; al lugar del cananeo, del hitita, del amorreo, del ferezeo, del heveo y del jebuseo.
texts.exo.3.9: Ahora bien, he aquí que el clamor de los hijos de Israel ha llegado hasta mí. Además, he visto la opresión con que los egipcios los oprimen.
texts.exo.3.10: Ven, pues, ahora y te enviaré al faraón para que saques a mi pueblo, los hijos de Israel, de Egipto».
texts.exo.3.11: Moisés dijo a Dios: «¿Quién soy yo para ir al faraón y sacar a los hijos de Israel de Egipto?»
texts.exo.3.12: Dijo: “Ciertamente yo estaré contigo. Esta será la señal para ti de que te he enviado: cuando hayas sacado al pueblo de Egipto, serviréis a Dios en este monte.”
texts.exo.3.13: Moisés dijo a Dios: “He aquí que cuando llegue a los hijos de Israel y les diga: El Dios de vuestros padres me ha enviado a vosotros, y ellos me pregunten: ¿Cuál es su nombre?, ¿qué debo decirles?”
texts.exo.3.14: Dios dijo a Moisés: «YO SOY EL QUE SOY», y añadió: «Dirás a los hijos de Israel esto: YO SOY me ha enviado a vosotros».
texts.exo.3.15: Dios dijo además a Moisés: «Dirás a los hijos de Israel esto: Yahvé, el Dios de vuestros padres, el Dios de Abraham, el Dios de Isaac y el Dios de Jacob, me ha enviado a vosotros. Este es mi nombre para siempre, y este es mi memorial para todas las generaciones.
texts.exo.3.16: Ve y reúne a los ancianos de Israel y diles: Yahvé, el Dios de vuestros padres, el Dios de Abraham, de Isaac y de Jacob, se me ha aparecido diciendo: Ciertamente os he visitado y he visto lo que os han hecho en Egipto.
texts.exo.3.17: He dicho que os haré subir de la aflicción de Egipto a la tierra del cananeo, del hitita, del amorreo, del ferezeo, del heveo y del jebuseo, a una tierra que mana leche y miel.
texts.exo.3.18: Ellos escucharán tu voz. Vendrás, tú y los ancianos de Israel, al rey de Egipto, y le diréis: Yahvé, el Dios de los hebreos, se ha encontrado con nosotros. Ahora, por favor, permítenos ir tres días de camino al desierto, para que ofrezcamos sacrificios a Yahvé, nuestro Dios.
texts.exo.3.19: Yo sé que el rey de Egipto no os dará permiso para ir, si no es por una mano poderosa.
texts.exo.3.20: Extenderé mi mano y golpearé a Egipto con todas mis maravillas que haré entre ellos, y después de eso os dejará ir.
texts.exo.3.21: Yo le daré a este pueblo gracia a los ojos de los egipcios, y sucederá que cuando os vayáis, no os iréis con las manos vacías.
texts.exo.3.22: Sino que cada mujer pedirá a su vecina, y a la que habite en su casa, alhajas de plata, alhajas de oro y vestidos. Los pondréis sobre vuestros hijos y sobre vuestras hijas. Saquearéis a los egipcios».
texts.exo.4.1: Moisés respondió: «Pero he aquí que no me creerán ni escucharán mi voz, porque dirán: Yahvé no se te ha aparecido».
texts.exo.4.2: Yahvé le dijo: «¿Qué es eso que tienes en la mano?» Dijo: «Una vara».
texts.exo.4.3: Dijo: «Tírala al suelo». La arrojó al suelo, y se convirtió en una serpiente; y Moisés huyó de ella.
texts.exo.4.4: Yahvé dijo a Moisés: «Extiende tu mano y tómala por la cola». Extendió la mano y la agarró, y se convirtió en una vara en su mano.
texts.exo.4.5: «Esto es para que crean que Yahvé, el Dios de sus padres, el Dios de Abraham, el Dios de Isaac y el Dios de Jacob, se te ha aparecido».
texts.exo.4.6: Yahvé le dijo además: «Ahora mete tu mano en tu seno». Metió la mano en su seno, y cuando la sacó, he aquí que su mano estaba leprosa, blanca como la nieve.
texts.exo.4.7: Dijo: «Vuelve a meter la mano en tu seno». Volvió a meter la mano en su seno, y cuando la sacó, he aquí que se había vuelto de nuevo como el resto de su carne.
texts.exo.4.8: «Sucederá que si no te creen ni escuchan la voz de la primera señal, creerán la voz de la segunda señal.
texts.exo.4.9: Sucederá, si no creen ni siquiera a estas dos señales ni escuchan tu voz, que tomarás del agua del río y la derramarás sobre la tierra seca. El agua que saques del río se convertirá en sangre sobre la tierra seca».
texts.exo.4.10: Moisés dijo a Yahvé: «¡Ay, Señor! Nunca he sido elocuente, ni antes, ni desde que has hablado a tu siervo; porque soy tardo de palabra y torpe de lengua.»
texts.exo.4.11: Yahvé le dijo: “¿Quién dio la boca al hombre? ¿O quién hace que uno sea mudo, o sordo, o que vea, o que sea ciego? ¿No soy yo, Yahvé?
texts.exo.4.12: Ahora, pues, ve, y yo estaré con tu boca y te enseñaré lo que debes hablar”.
texts.exo.4.13: Moisés dijo: “¡Ay, Señor! Por favor, envía a otro”.
texts.exo.4.14: La ira de Yahvé se encendió contra Moisés y le dijo: “¿No está Aarón, tu hermano, el levita? Sé que él sabe hablar bien. Además, he aquí que él sale a recibirte. Cuando te vea, se alegrará en su corazón.
texts.exo.4.15: Tú le hablarás y pondrás las palabras en su boca. Yo estaré con tu boca y con la suya, y os enseñaré lo que debéis hacer.
texts.exo.4.16: Él será tu portavoz ante el pueblo. Sucederá que él será para ti como boca, y tú serás para él como Dios.
texts.exo.4.17: Tomarás esta vara en tu mano, con la cual harás las señales”.
texts.exo.4.18: Moisés fue y regresó a Jetro, su suegro, y le dijo: “Por favor, déjame ir y regresar a mis hermanos que están en Egipto, para ver si todavía están vivos.” Jetro dijo a Moisés: «Ve en paz».
texts.exo.4.19: Yahvé dijo a Moisés en Madián: «Ve, vuelve a Egipto, porque todos los hombres que buscaban tu vida han muerto».
texts.exo.4.20: Moisés tomó a su mujer y a sus hijos, los montó en un asno y volvió a la tierra de Egipto. Moisés tomó la vara de Dios en su mano.
texts.exo.4.21: Yahvé le dijo a Moisés: «Cuando vuelvas a Egipto, asegúrate de hacer ante el faraón todas las maravillas que he puesto en tu mano, pero yo endureceré su corazón y no dejará ir al pueblo.
texts.exo.4.22: Le dirás al faraón: Yahvé dice: Israel es mi hijo, mi primogénito,
texts.exo.4.23: y yo te he dicho: Deja ir a mi hijo para que me sirva, y tú te has negado a dejarlo ir. He aquí que voy a matar a tu hijo primogénito».
texts.exo.4.24: En el camino, en una posada, Yahvé le salió al encuentro a Moisés y quiso matarlo.
texts.exo.4.25: Entonces Séfora tomó un cuchillo de pedernal, cortó el prepucio de su hijo y lo arrojó a sus pies, y dijo: «Ciertamente eres un esposo de sangre para mí».
texts.exo.4.26: Así que lo dejó en paz. Entonces ella dijo: «Eres un esposo de sangre», a causa de la circuncisión.
texts.exo.4.27: Yahvé dijo a Aarón: «Ve al desierto a recibir a Moisés». Fue, y se encontró con él en el monte de Dios, y lo besó.
texts.exo.4.28: Moisés le contó a Aarón todas las palabras de Yahvé con las que lo había enviado, y todas las señales que le había mandado hacer.
texts.exo.4.29: Moisés y Aarón fueron y reunieron a todos los ancianos de los hijos de Israel.
texts.exo.4.30: Aarón pronunció todas las palabras que Yahvé había dicho a Moisés, e hizo las señales a la vista del pueblo.
texts.exo.4.31: El pueblo creyó, y al oír que Yahvé había visitado a los hijos de Israel y que había visto su aflicción, inclinaron la cabeza y adoraron.
texts.exo.5.1: Después vinieron Moisés y Aarón y le dijeron al faraón: “Esto es lo que dice Yahvé, el Dios de Israel: ‘Deja ir a mi pueblo para que me celebre una fiesta en el desierto’”.
texts.exo.5.2: El faraón dijo: “¿Quién es Yahvé, para que yo escuche su voz y deje ir a Israel? No conozco a Yahvé, y además no dejaré ir a Israel”.
texts.exo.5.3: Dijeron: “El Dios de los hebreos se ha encontrado con nosotros. Por favor, permítenos ir tres días de camino al desierto para ofrecer sacrificios a Yahvé, nuestro Dios, no sea que nos castigue con peste o con espada.”
texts.exo.5.4: El rey de Egipto les dijo: “¿Por qué vosotros, Moisés y Aarón, apartáis al pueblo de su trabajo? Volved a vuestras tareas”.
texts.exo.5.5: El faraón añadió: «He aquí que el pueblo de la tierra es ahora numeroso, y vosotros hacéis que descansen de sus tareas».
texts.exo.5.6: Ese mismo día el faraón ordenó a los capataces del pueblo y a sus oficiales, diciendo:
texts.exo.5.7: “Ya no daréis al pueblo paja para hacer ladrillos, como hacíais antes. Que vayan a recoger paja por sí mismos.
texts.exo.5.8: Pero les exigiréis la misma cantidad de ladrillos que hacían antes. No disminuiréis nada de ella, porque están ociosos. Por eso claman diciendo: ‘Vamos a ofrecer sacrificios a nuestro Dios’.
texts.exo.5.9: Que el trabajo más pesado recaiga sobre estos hombres, para que se ocupen en él y no presten atención a palabras mentirosas”.
texts.exo.5.10: Los capataces del pueblo salieron con sus oficiales y hablaron al pueblo diciendo: “Esto es lo que dice el faraón: ‘No os daré paja.
texts.exo.5.11: Id vosotros mismos y conseguid paja donde podáis encontrarla, porque no se disminuirá nada de vuestro trabajo’”.
texts.exo.5.12: Así que el pueblo se dispersó por toda la tierra de Egipto para recoger rastrojos en lugar de paja.
texts.exo.5.13: Los capataces los apremiaban diciendo: «¡Cumplid vuestra cuota de trabajo diaria, como cuando teníais paja!»
texts.exo.5.14: Los oficiales de los hijos de Israel, a quienes los capataces del faraón habían puesto sobre ellos, fueron golpeados y se les preguntó: «¿Por qué no habéis cumplido vuestra cuota de hacer ladrillos, ni ayer ni hoy, como antes?»
texts.exo.5.15: Entonces los oficiales de los hijos de Israel vinieron y clamaron al faraón, diciendo: “¿Por qué tratas así a tus siervos?
texts.exo.5.16: No se nos da paja a tus siervos, y sin embargo nos dicen: ‘¡Haced ladrillos!’ Y he aquí que tus siervos son golpeados, pero la culpa es de tu propio pueblo.”
texts.exo.5.17: Pero el faraón dijo: “¡Estáis ociosos! ¡Estáis ociosos! Por eso decís: ‘Vamos a ofrecer sacrificios a Yahvé’.
texts.exo.5.18: ¡Id, pues, ahora y trabajad! No se os dará paja, pero tendréis que entregar la misma cantidad de ladrillos.”
texts.exo.5.19: Los oficiales de los hijos de Israel vieron que estaban en graves apuros cuando se les dijo: «¡No disminuiréis nada de vuestra cuota diaria de ladrillos!»
texts.exo.5.20: Al salir de la presencia del faraón, se encontraron con Moisés y Aarón, que los estaban esperando en el camino.
texts.exo.5.21: Y les dijeron: «¡Que Yahvé os mire y os juzgue, porque nos habéis hecho odiosos a los ojos del faraón y a los ojos de sus siervos, poniéndoles una espada en la mano para matarnos!»
texts.exo.5.22: Moisés se volvió a Yahvé y le dijo: «Señor, ¿por qué has traído este mal sobre este pueblo? ¿Por qué me has enviado?
texts.exo.5.23: Porque desde que me presenté al faraón para hablar en tu nombre, él ha maltratado a este pueblo, y tú no has librado a tu pueblo en absoluto».
texts.exo.6.1: Yahvé dijo a Moisés: “Ahora verás lo que haré con el faraón, porque obligado por una mano fuerte los dejará ir, y con mano fuerte los expulsará de su tierra.”
texts.exo.6.2: Dios habló a Moisés y le dijo: “Yo soy Yahvé.
texts.exo.6.3: Me apareci a Abraham, a Isaac y a Jacob como Dios Todopoderoso; pero por mi nombre Yahvé no me di a conocer a ellos.
texts.exo.6.4: También establecí mi pacto con ellos, para darles la tierra de Canaán, la tierra de sus peregrinaciones, en la que vivieron como forasteros.
texts.exo.6.5: Además, he oído el gemido de los hijos de Israel, a quienes los egipcios mantienen en esclavitud, y me he acordado de mi pacto.
texts.exo.6.6: Por tanto, di a los hijos de Israel: ‘Yo soy Yahvé, y os sacaré de las pesadas tareas de los egipcios, os libraré de su esclavitud, y os redimiré con brazo extendido y con grandes juicios.
texts.exo.6.7: Os tomaré para mí como pueblo. Yo seré vuestro Dios; y sabréis que yo soy Yahvé, vuestro Dios, que os saca de las pesadas tareas de los egipcios.
texts.exo.6.8: Os llevaré a la tierra que juré dar a Abraham, a Isaac y a Jacob, y os la daré en heredad: yo soy Yahvé’”.
texts.exo.6.9: Moisés habló así a los hijos de Israel, pero ellos no escucharon a Moisés debido a su angustia de espíritu y a la dura esclavitud.
texts.exo.6.11: “Entra y habla con el faraón, rey de Egipto, para que deje salir de su tierra a los hijos de Israel.”
texts.exo.6.12: Moisés respondió ante Yahvé diciendo: “He aquí que los hijos de Israel no me han escuchado. ¿Cómo, pues, me va a escuchar el faraón, si soy torpe de labios?”
texts.exo.6.13: Yahvé habló a Moisés y a Aarón y les dio órdenes para los hijos de Israel y para el faraón, rey de Egipto, a fin de sacar a los hijos de Israel de la tierra de Egipto.
texts.exo.6.14: Estos son los jefes de las casas paternas. Los hijos de Rubén, primogénito de Israel: Hanoc, Falú, Hezrón y Carmí; estas son las familias de Rubén.
texts.exo.6.15: Los hijos de Simeón: Jemuel, Jamín, Ohad, Jaquín, Zohar y Saúl, hijo de una cananea; estas son las familias de Simeón.
texts.exo.6.16: Estos son los nombres de los hijos de Leví según sus generaciones: Gersón, Coat y Merari; y los años de la vida de Leví fueron ciento treinta y siete años.
texts.exo.6.17: Los hijos de Gersón: Libní y Simeí, según sus familias.
texts.exo.6.18: Los hijos de Coat: Amram, Izhar, Hebrón y Uziel; y los años de la vida de Coat fueron ciento treinta y tres años.
texts.exo.6.19: Los hijos de Merari: Mahlí y Musí. Estas son las familias de los levitas según sus generaciones.
texts.exo.6.20: Amram tomó por esposa a Jocabed, tía suya, y ella le dio a luz a Aarón y a Moisés. Los años de la vida de Amram fueron ciento treinta y siete años.
texts.exo.6.21: Los hijos de Izhar: Coré, Néfeg y Zicrí.
texts.exo.6.22: Los hijos de Uziel: Misael, Elzafán y Sitrí.
texts.exo.6.23: Aarón tomó por esposa a Eliseba, hija de Aminadab, hermana de Naasón, y ella le dio a luz a Nadab, Abiú, Eleazar e Itamar.
texts.exo.6.24: Los hijos de Coré: Asir, Elcaná y Abiasaf; estas son las familias de los coreítas.
texts.exo.6.25: Eleazar, hijo de Aarón, tomó por mujer a una de las hijas de Putiel, y ella le dio a luz a Finees. Estos son los jefes de las casas paternas de los levitas según sus familias.
texts.exo.6.26: Estos son aquel Aarón y aquel Moisés a quienes Yahvé dijo: “Sacad a los hijos de Israel de la tierra de Egipto según sus ejércitos.”
texts.exo.6.27: Estos son los que hablaron con el faraón, rey de Egipto, para sacar a los hijos de Israel de Egipto. Estos son Moisés y Aarón.
texts.exo.6.28: El día en que Yahvé habló con Moisés en la tierra de Egipto,
texts.exo.6.29: Yahvé dijo a Moisés: «Yo soy Yahvé. Dile al faraón, rey de Egipto, todo lo que te digo».
